title: Micah Parsons may not be ready to play until November
summary: The Packers aren't expecting linebacker Micah Parsons back on the field any time soon.
full_text: '' The Packers aren't expecting linebacker Micah Parsons back on the field any time soon. Parsons was ruled out for the first four games of the season as soon as the Packers put him on the physically unable to perform list, but there was previously some optimism he'd be good to go soon after he was eligible to return to the active roster — perhaps as soon as next week. Now, it looks like it's going to be a while. Parsons is not expected to practice next week and might not be ready to play in a game until November , according to Tom Pelissero. Although Parsons hasn't had a setback in recovery from the torn ACL he suffered in Week 15 of last season, those injuries can take close to a year to heal, and Parsons is still less than 10 months out. It's going to take him some more time. When the Packers pulled off the blockbuster trade to acquire Parsons, they thought they could be adding the last piece for a Super Bowl contender. Instead, last year they were bounced out of the first round of the playoffs, and now they're 1-2, with big questions about whether they'll be playoff contenders this year, with or without Parsons.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Deshaun Watson seeks redemption without genuine remorse
summary: Thursday night's broadcast of Steelers-Browns on Prime Video featured plenty of tiptoeing around the elephant that Deshaun Watson dragged into the room with his own actions.
full_text: ' Thursday night's broadcast of Steelers-Browns on Prime Video featured plenty of tiptoeing around the elephant that Deshaun Watson dragged into the room with his own actions. From the sit-down interview with Taylor Rooks to the periodic vague references from Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit to Watson's past issues, there was never a direct mention of the self-created adversity Watson has experienced since 2021. It meshes with Watson's broader approach to the situation. He has never shown true, consistent remorse for more than 25 civil lawsuits alleging sexual misconduct during massage therapy sessions. Although a grand jury declined to indict him in any of the cases that landed in the criminal system, the NFL's in-house judicial process resulted in an 11-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy. After twice saying he has "no regrets" regarding the situation in 2022, Watson finally apologized in August of that year. "I want to say that I’m truly sorry to all of the women that I have impacted in this situation," Watson said at the time. "The decisions that I made in my life that put me in this position I would definitely like to have back, but I want to continue to move forward and grow and learn and show that I am a true person of character and I am going to keep pushing forward." The apology happened after Judge Sue L. Robinson suspended Watson six games — but before the situation was settled on appeal with an 11-game suspension and a $5 million fine . (The settlement happened because the league wanted a suspension much longer than six games.) Watson arguably walked back his apology in August 2026, when he made a sweeping statement in response to the specific question of whether he regrets joining the Browns. "I don’t regret anything in my life," Watson told reporters after the preseason game during which he was relentlessly booed. "I think the Lord put me through situations for a reason, so I don’t regret anything at all." Watson had another chance to express true and complete remorse in his interview with Prime Video . He didn't. He referred to the impact of "the world kind of flipping against me" on his "mental state." As to the fans who continue to boo Watson "because of who they believe you are as a person," Watson was asked whether the "skepticism" is fair. "Fair?" Watson said. "Of course, to me I'm going to say, 'No.' But life isn't fair and I understand. I can accept my responsibilities and everything that I went through and feel and move forward." He then acknowledged that he can understand the "apprehension" fans may have. Through it all, there was no mention of the specific reasons for the apprehension or the skepticism. Rooks referred generally to his past as "unresolved." Michaels glossed over the incidents that contributed to the world "flipping against" Watson. Herbstreit seemed to search for the right words before referring to Watson as "much-maligned." On one hand, it's a four-year-old story. On the other hand, the effects of it continue to linger. Thursday night's handling of Watson felt like a deliberate effort to boost his redemption story. But redemption can't come without genuine remorse. And the full scope of his limited comments about the incidents that derailed his career show that he has never expressed true and full and unequivocal remorse. That's the question that remains unanswered. Does he believe he was in the wrong, or does he believe it was a misunderstanding or perhaps a mass conspiracy? It's a question that won't be going away. Even as he thrives as Cleveland's unlikely starting quarterback in the final year of his fully-guaranteed, $230 million contract, plenty of Browns fans will never embrace him. He can believe it's not fair, he can characterize it as another test from above. Or he can accept the reasons for the resistance and try to finally say and do something to prove that he understands what he did, that he realizes why it was wrong, and that he'll use his platform and profile to help make a meaningful difference. At this point, Watson may not feel compelled to do any of that. His redemption story is being written without the need for genuine remorse, thanks in large part to the way his past behavior was whitewashed on Thursday night.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones on Joey Porter Jr. trade: "It's important to think big"
summary: The Steelers decided to move on from cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
full_text: '' The Steelers decided to move on from cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The Cowboys were ready to pounce. " It’s important to think big ," Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, "and this is over in that big thought area about what we can do to help our defense." As to whether other moves will be made this year, Jones said "it's always fluid" and "you can't sit still." "If you look at the overall picture, I frankly decided a couple of years ago to get in the business of reworking what we are defensively," Jones said. The Porter trade is about winning now. The question is whether one player will make a big difference. The Cowboys have seen their cornerback play dip since trading linebacker Micah Parsons, and it's not a coincidence. It's easier to cover receivers if the quarterback is rushing to throw — or not throwing at all. Porter isn't Deion Sanders. (Then again, no one is.) The issue in Pittsburgh was that the two sides had a dramatically different viewpoint as to his value. And the eventual price that Cowboys paid (a sixih-round pick in 2027 and a second-round pick in 2028, with the possibility of a third-round compensatory pick in 2028 if he leave in free agency after this season) reflects the Steelers' assessment of Porter as a player. Porter's value to the Cowboys remains to be seen. But all signs are pointing to Porter getting his first chance to show what he can do for his new team on Sunday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Liam Coen on Travis Hunter's usage: "He cares about winning"
summary: Questions have persisted regarding whether the Jaguars are getting the most out of cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter, the second overall pick in the 2025 draft.
full_text: Questions have persisted regarding whether the Jaguars are getting the most out of cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter, the second overall pick in the 2025 draft. Coach Liam Coen addressed the situation in simple terms on Friday. " He cares about winning ," Coen said, "That's what he cares about. Like, and all the other stuff, the reps, where we picked him, does that — I don't give two Fs about value. And neither does he. We care about winning. And that's it." That's not what Hunter said in an August appearance on The Pivot podcast. He said he wants to play both sides of the ball, on a full-time basis. “If I’m trying to be the best — how are you gonna be the best, if you ain’t trying to be the best?" Hunter said at the time. "If you ain’t trying to compete and do the best to be the best? So my main focus is be the best. So I’m gonna do everything I can do to be the best. I don’t want to be the best at one position. There’s a lot of people that’s the best at one position. Ain’t nobody yet been the best at both , full-time. . . . "I cannot sit on the sideline. I don’t think nobody’s noticed that yet. I hate the sidelines. I do not wanna sit there. I can’t sit there and just watch football. I’ve got to be on the field.” The fact that the Jaguars are winning makes it harder for Hunter to gripe about his usage, which is increasing on the defensive side of the ball but which continues to be cameo appearances, at best, on offense. But he's on the record with his wishes. And, yes, it's fair to ask about value. Especially given the glowing remarks G.M. James Gladstone made after the Jaguars traded up from No. 5 to No. 2 to get him. “This is something I’m uniquely positioned to navigate," Gladstone said in April 2025. "We ended up bringing Travis Hunter to Jacksonville, and with that, he is somebody who is deserving of a first-round draft pick as a wide receiver, and he is worthy of a first-round draft pick as a corner. Certainly, look forward to each of those elements showing themselves over the next few years while he is under his rookie contract." While the Jaguars have emerged as an elite team, the stated vision for Hunter has yet to come to fruition. And it seems that no one wants that to happen more than him.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams don't have a timeline on Myles Garrett's return
summary: Despite a report that Rams defensive end Myles Garrett would miss about six weeks with his knee injury, head coach Sean McVay says the team isn't working on a timeline that specific.
full_text: Despite a report that Rams defensive end Myles Garrett would miss about six weeks with his knee injury, head coach Sean McVay says the team isn't working on a timeline that specific. Asked how Garrett is doing after knee surgery, McVay said Garrett is doing well but told reporters the team does not have any time frame for when he will actually be back on the field. "Myles is good. I've seen him in there, he physically looks good," McVay said. "He's got a good look in his eye. It's been good having him in and out of a lot of the meetings while he's attacking his rehab. He's making good progress, but as far as a specific timeline, I'm not ready to give you guys that. As soon as I have those things I'll give you guys updates." After sitting out practice with a knee injury in training camp and struggling to play on his injured knee in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers, Garrett had surgery and was placed on injured reserve. By rule, players on injured reserve have to miss at least four weeks, but it appears that Garrett will be out longer than that. How much longer, the Rams still don't know.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Maxx Crosby: Vegas is a different type of city, we have to earn home-field advantage
summary: "We're new to this city and we have to win. The fans come out, they want to see a winner. We have to earn that," Crosby said.
full_text: The Raiders haven't had a lot of success since moving to Las Vegas in 2020, but things may be changing. The Raiders are 3-0, on Sunday they host the 3-0 Chiefs, and Maxx Crosby says now is the time to show what kind of home-field advantage Allegiant Stadium can provide. Crosby said that unlike Oakland and Los Angeles, where the rabid fans of the Black Hole were legendary, Vegas is a city where the Raiders are going to need to develop a fan base that isn't yet so invested in the team. " We’re gonna need the fans at full effect, and that's all season," Crosby said. "We have to earn our stadium, and having the fans here. In Oakland it's built in, fans are going to show up, it's going to be Silver and Black. L.A. is the same thing. But Vegas is a different type of city. We're new to this city and we have to win. The fans come out, they want to see a winner. We have to earn that." Crosby thinks winning comes first and the home-field advantage follows. "We take it one day at a time and keep earning the respect, and love and passion for the fans. We know the fans have it, to fill that stadium every Sunday with Silver and Black, we've got to continue winning and keep putting a great product out there for the fans," Crosby said. If the Raiders beat the Chiefs on Sunday, a whole lot of Las Vegas fans will be buying in.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean McVay: I don't like it that the Rams are 1-2, but we grow through adversity
summary: "It's a challenge for me: What kind of leader do I want to be for this group?" McVay said.
full_text: Rams coach Sean McVay isn't happy with his team's 1-2 start this season, but he isn't losing confidence in the long-term plan, and he even thinks the Rams might be better in January for what they went through in September. "Do I love the fact that we've played three games and came up short in a couple of them? No, of course not," McVay said. "But what I also know is this: There's been other moments that it seems like you're in some storms, but this too shall pass, and let's do the next right thing. Let's lean in. What kind of lens do we want to see this through? Do we want to see this as, this is happening to me or for me, and how can I learn from it, how can I grow? It's a challenge for me: What kind of leader do I want to be for this group?" McVay said he believes in growing through adversity, even if it doesn't feel good at the time. "Do I want to go through that adversity? No, but this is what we're going through," McVay said. "That's what makes it meaningful. When things come easy, sometimes when you have success you become less resilient. I do not like it but I do know that's where the real growth occurs." McVay said he thinks when this season is over, his team might be more proud of its accomplishments because of the early struggles. "Sometimes it doesn't go down for you and I always think about the people I respect the most are the ones that handle the tough times the best," McVay said. "Tough times don't last. Tough people do. The most growth that's ever occurred for me by far is when we've been in those adverse moments when you don't like it when you're in them, but then you look back and say you're proud of the person you became from them." Up next for the Rams is a game at Philadelphia on Sunday, and McVay acknowledged his own struggles against the Eagles . "I'm excited to swing and compete again with this group. This story is not yet written. There are people who feel otherwise, but we've got a lot of ball ahead of us," McVay said. "We've got a great challenge. This is an excellent place to play at, great fan base. We're not going to run away from that we haven't gotten the results when we've gone up there. Last year was a gut-wrenching one but I'm not afraid to put it out there again." For the Rams, who were heavy preseason favorites to win the Super Bowl, falling to 1-3 would be a massive letdown. But McVay continues to believe that his team won't stay down.
author: Michael David Smith

title: YouTube believes NFL could "deconstruct" Sunday Ticket in next broadcast deals
summary: Come 2030, out-of-market games could be seen without plunking down an extra $400.
full_text: The next wave of NFL broadcast deals could include plenty of changes. One change could be the end of the out-of-market package of games. Via Alex Sherman of CNBC, YouTube believes that the NFL could “deconstruct” Sunday Ticket . The league first launched Sunday Ticket in 1994, marketing it as a way for fans to watch games not televised in the markets where they reside. DirecTV owned the package for years, before YouTube acquired the rights in 2023. The current Sunday Ticket deal with YouTube, for which the company pays $2 billion per year, remains the subject of a federal class action that is pending on appeal in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, The case could still result in a massive liability for the NFL (in excess of $14 billion). It also could generate a court order compelling the NFL to end the longstanding device for allowing fans to watch all games played in the Sunday afternoon windows. The NFL lost at trial in 2024. The jury found that the NFL's pricing of the package, which was intended to be high enough to persuade many viewers to choose to watch the CBS and Fox games available in their local markets, violated the antitrust laws. The judge didn't throw out the entire verdict; he dismissed the damages award. The finding of an antitrust violation remains in place — and it continues. At some point, there likely will be a reckoning. And the league has already explored the possibility of making the games available through other platforms, simulating a college football viewing experience that has a wide variety of games on various cable and broadcast platforms. Quite possibly, the league could make as much or more money by selling in-market games to a pair of broadcast networks, with the out-of-market games sprinkled throughout the various other channels on the dial. Regardless of the revenue potential, the league will have no choice, if a court compels them to dismantle Sunday Ticket. And it would allow fans to watch games on networks to which they already have access, without paying nearly $400 per year for it. Ditching Sunday Ticket would also address concerns that the league has devalued it by putting more and more games into non-Sunday windows. And it would give the NFL the freedom to more aggressively schedule games for Wednesday nights and, eventually, Tuesday nights.
author: Mike Florio

title: Quarterbacks who didn't start in Week 1 are 6-0
summary: It's the year of the backup quarterback, so far.
full_text: '' It's the year of the backup quarterback, so far. Through three weeks, six quarterbacks who didn't start in Week 1 have since started six games. They're collectively 6-0. Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz started and won at Chicago in Week 2. Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock started and won at Arizona in Week 2. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. started and won at Green Bay in Week 3. Giants quarterback Jameis Winston started and won vs. the Titans in Week 3. Washington quarterback Marcus Mariota started and won vs. the Seahawks in Week 6. And Bears quarterback Case Keenum started and won vs. the Eagles in Week 3. In Week 4, two more quarterbacks who didn't start in Week 1 are expected to start their first games of the season: Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent vs. the Jets and Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels vs. the Packers. The situation shows the importance of having two, if not three, quarterbacks who can be counted on to play, and play well. A game here or a game there in the absence of the starting quarterback could eventually make the difference between making the playoffs or missing the bus.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay is 0-4 against Nick Sirianni
summary: Rams coach Sean McVay has had tremendous success since becoming a head coach in 2017.
full_text: Rams coach Sean McVay has had tremendous success since becoming a head coach in 2017. Against one specific coach, McVay has struggled. Via NBC Sports research, McVay has an 0-4 record against Eagles coach Nick Sirianni. McVay gets his next chance to get his first win over Sirianni on Sunday in Philadelphia. The 1-2 Rams desperately need to avoid falling to 1-3. In 2023, the Eagles and Sirianni beat the Rams and McVay in L.A., 23-14. The next year, the Eagles won again in L.A., 37-20. In the 2024 playoffs, the Eagles escaped an upset bid in the divisional round, 28-22. Last season, a blocked field goal in the final seconds (returned for a touchdown) gave the Eagles a 33-26 win. Overall, McVay is 1-6 against the Eagles. And Philly has won 10 of the last 11 games played between the two teams. The Rams are nevertheless favored by 3.5 points over the Eagles. The game starts at 1:00 p.m. ET on Sunday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Five teams face an 0-4 start — and only one 0-4 team has ever made the playoffs
summary: Week 4 is here, and five teams are still looking for their first victory of 2026.
full_text: Week 4 is here, and five teams are still looking for their first victory of 2026. The Dolphins, Texans, Titans, Chargers, and Buccaneers are all 0-3. Only seven teams (most recently, the 2025 Texans) have made the playoffs after an 0-3 start. None of the five teams play each other this weekend, which means all five could still be winless come Monday. Any that land at 0-4 will be facing a steep climb to the postseason. Only one team in NFL history has qualified for the playoffs after starting 0-4. In 1992, the Chargers under first-year coach Bobby Ross turned it around and secured the AFC West crown. The Chargers won 11 of their 12 final games of the season. The Chargers advanced through the wild-card round with a 17-0 win over the Chiefs, who had swept the Chargers during the regular season. The next week, the Dolphins eliminated the Chargers with a 31-0 blowout. With 17 games and seven playoff spots per conference, it's easier than ever for a team to turn it around after an 0-4 start. Still, many 0-4 teams start that way for a reason; they're not very good. The 1992 Chargers were much better than their early-season record indicated, and they made it all the way to the final eight.
author: Mike Florio

title: New Bears stadium in Illinois could be publicly owned
summary: The Bears claim to be focused on building a new stadium in Indiana.
full_text: The Bears claim to be focused on building a new stadium in Indiana. And yet they're still talking to Illinois. Via Danny Ecker of Crain's Chicago Business , the possible construction in Arlington Heights could entail a publicly-owned venue . Per the report, recent discussions between the Bears and Illinois officials have focused on a public model. Thursday's meeting between, Commissioner Roger Goodell, Bears minority owner Pat Ryan, Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, and state legislative leaders, has renewed hope that the Bears won't cross the border for their next home. Ecker also points out that Bears president and CEO Kevin Warren and primary owner George McCaskey were "notably absent" from Thursday's meeting. Public ownership would solve the property-tax question that has stalled the team's ability to convert the Arlington Park site, which the Bears own, into a new stadium. The goal is to craft legislation that would pass both houses of the Illinois Legislature. The Bears originally intended to own, and to privately finance, the new stadium. That strategy hasn't gained sufficient footing. The leverage that comes from the Indiana option has spurred the powers-that-be in Illinois to explore a different strategy that would keep the team from leaving the state. The best outcome would be, in our view, a new stadium in Chicago. If that's not doable, it's far better for the Bears to stay in Illinois than to move to another state. Still, the Indiana option has always seemed to be aimed at getting the attention of Illinois. That apparently has worked. The next question is whether they can get a deal done to build a new stadium in Illinois. Until then, the Bears will continue to play at Soldier Field. Enjoy the open-air experience while it lasts.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vinod Khosla on a potential Seahawks move: "Never say never"
summary: New owner keeps saying things that won't make the fan base happy.
full_text: Q: What's the best way to get the Seahawks' fan base to forget that the new owner is a Steelers fan who still watches all of their games ? A: Fail to unequivocally rule out the possibility of moving the team to a new city. " I will never say never ," new owner Vinod Khosla told Dan Primack of Axios . "Will this team be in Seattle 500 years from now? But I have no current plans to change anything about the team, including the coach, president, operation or Lumen Field. It all functions well." The 500-year question is far less relevant than the six-year question. The team's lease at Lumen Field expires in 2032. Khosla may simply be playing the game of stadium politics. In order to get someone else to pay for major renovations or a new stadium, leverage must exist. If nothing else, "never say never" helps set the stage for an infusion of significant taxpayer money. Besides, Khosla is still learning the ropes of being an owner. "Three months ago I wasn't even thinking about buying an NFL team," Khosla said. "Now I ended up with a Super Bowl-winning team with one of the most amazing fan bases. But I know very little about running a team. I don't think I'll do anything but learn for a while." One thing Khosla may realize the hard way is a lesson that plenty of other anonymous billionaires turned NFL owners have learned: The only thing better than being rich and famous is being rich. Khosla's comments will make the fan base leery about the future. How can they not be? But they don't deserve to be caught in the crossfire of the billion-dollar gamesmanship over who'll pay for the next Seahawks stadium.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL fines Quinn Meinerz $14,926 for a celebratory dice roll
summary: Broncos right guard Quinn Meinerz celebrated with Jaylen Waddle after the wide receiver's 2-point conversion on Sunday.
full_text: '' Broncos right guard Quinn Meinerz celebrated with Jaylen Waddle after the wide receiver's 2-point conversion on Sunday. He playfully "waddled" over to offer his congratulations, and the teammates then pantomimed a dice roll. “ I got fined ,’’ Meinerz told Mike Klis of 9News. “We were playing Yahtzee. They didn’t like we were playing Yahtzee.” In 2017, the NFL announced that it had no problem with celebratory dice rolls. A spokesperson at the time said the league "isn't in a place to determine" whether players were referring to Yahtzee or backgammon. The league fined Meinerz $14,926 for what the league deemed an illegal celebration. It seems likely the NFL fined Waddle the same amount. Meinerz said he will appeal. After the Broncos' second 2-point conversion, Meinerz lifted Pat Bryant II off the ground with a two-arm, elbow-locked shiver. “It’s fun to be back to who I am and I can breathe. I can see, I’m feeling good about life and where things are at,’’ Meinerz said. “So when I have the opportunity to use more of that energy to go celebrate with my teammates, why not? It’s hard to score, have fun with it.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Chiefs DB Chamarri Conner set to make his season debut
summary: Chiefs defensive back Chamarri Conner is set to make his 2026 debut on Sunday.
full_text: Chiefs defensive back Chamarri Conner is set to make his 2026 debut on Sunday. Conner missed the first three games with a knee injury. He led the team in defensive snap percentage last season and is a favorite of defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. Conner can play nickel or safety. “It seems like every year he’s been here — and we’ve done cut-ups at the end of the season and we’re looking through the film — 27 keeps showing up , making plays,” Spagnuolo said, via Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star . “Hopefully, we can get him back there doing that. I think he’s a really good tackler and a good football player. “We’ll fit him in there, whether it’s a safety or nickel in certain packages. And I like having him on the field, and I’m hoping we get him for this game.” Jaden Hicks and Alohi Gilman have started at safety in Conner's absence, and Hicks has played every snap. Starting left tackle Josh Simmons will miss his fourth consecutive game to start the season. He has a bulging disc in his lower back. Undrafted rookie Khalil Benson has started in Simmons' stead.
author: Charean Williams

title: Keenan Allen misses Friday's practice, questionable to play Sunday
summary: The Colts did not rule out any players for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London, but they do have a pair of wide receivers listed as questionable.
full_text: The Colts did not rule out any players for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London, but they do have a pair of wide receivers listed as questionable. Keenan Allen was listed as a non-participant in Friday's practice due to a groin injury. Allen was a limited participant in the team's first two practices of the week. Ashton Dulin missed the last two games with an ankle injury and did not practice on Wednesday, but has been a full participant in the last two practices. If either wideout is ruled out on Sunday or if the Colts want more insurance, they could have Darius Slayton in the lineup for the first time since he signed with the team last month.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Evans is going to try to play through his injured ribs
summary: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Broncos after a limited practice Friday.
full_text: '' 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Broncos after a limited practice Friday. He is going to try to play with a built-in compression shirt with padding in it to protect his injured ribs. Coach Kyle Shanahan called Evans a "game-time decision." "I'm going to do my best [to play]," Evans said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. He has previously played through something similar. Evans said he isn't certain exactly when he injured his ribs, but it didn't feel good. "That shit hurt bad," Evans said. "It was like non-contact. It might have happened before, but when I ran a route, and I turned, I just felt it, like, 'Ah!' Felt like somebody stabbed me in my chest. "But it's cool. The training staff and doctors did a good job of getting me off the field and making sure I was good." Shanahan broke his ribs in a car wreck this summer, so he sympathizes with Evans. "Mine are good now, but it's been two months, and I would not be questionable," Shanahan said. "I would be out, without a doubt. But he's definitely a lot tougher than me, so hopefully we've got a shot." The 49ers ruled out defensive linemen Nick Bosa (knee/calf), James Thompson Jr. (ankle) and Mykel Williams (knee). Left tackle Trent Williams (neck) does not have an injury designation. Defensive end Keion White (hamstring), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (quad) and linebacker Jaden Dugger (shoulder) are questionable. Dugger was a new addition to the injury report Friday.
author: Charean Williams

title: Cardinals list Josh Sweat as questionable with a groin injury
summary: The Cardinals listed a key member of their defense as questionable to play in this Sunday's game against the Giants.
full_text: The Cardinals listed a key member of their defense as questionable to play in this Sunday's game against the Giants. Linebacker Josh Sweat landed in that category after a limited practice on Friday. Sweat was listed as limited on Thursday for a rest day, but the Cardinals added a groin injury to the report on Friday. Sweat has three tackles and a tackle for loss so far this season. Baron Browning, Zaven Collins, Jordan Burch, and Eku Leota are the other outside linebackers on the 53-man roster in Arizona. Safety Dadrion Taylor-Demerson has been ruled out for this weekend. Taylor-Demerson is dealing with a back injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Rams put TE Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve
summary: The Rams ruled tight end Terrance Ferguson out for Sunday's game against the Eagles and that won't be the last one that Ferguson misses.
full_text: The Rams ruled tight end Terrance Ferguson out for Sunday's game against the Eagles and that won't be the last one that Ferguson misses. The team announced that Ferguson has been placed on injured reserve on Friday. Ferguson has an ankle injury. Ferguson has seven catches for 63 yards and a touchdown on the season. He had 11 catches for 231 yards and two touchdowns last season. The Rams also announced that they have signed wide receiver Alex Bachman and defensive end Larrell Murchison to the active roster from the practice squad. Defensive tackle Aaron Donald (back) and cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) have also been ruled out for this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chargers list Derwin James, Ladd McConkey, Trey Lance as questionable
summary: The Chargers have ruled out four players and list five others as questionable.
full_text: '' The Chargers have ruled out four players and list five others as questionable. Safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring), quarterback Trey Lance (groin), wide receiver Ladd McConkey (foot), safety Elijah Molden (hamstring) and cornerback Donte Jackson (concussion) are questionable. Lance was active for the Week 3 game after being questionable. The Chargers have DJ Uiagalelei behind Lance on the depth chart. Lance, James, Molden and McConkey were limited participants Friday. Jackson was a full participant. The Chargers ruled out left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring). Running back Keaton Mitchell, who wore a walking boot this week, was a full participant Friday and has no injury designation.

title: Stephen Jones: Steelers' initial asking price for Joey Porter Jr. was "a little hefty"
summary: Cowboys Executive V.P.
full_text: '' Cowboys Executive V.P. Stephen Jones says the team spent significant time negotiating a trade with the Steelers for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. that made sense for the Cowboys — and made the trade only after the Steelers' price came down. Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that what the Steelers were initially asking for was more than the Cowboys were willing to give up, but they eventually got the Steelers to lower the price to a 2027 sixth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick. "Early on the price was a little hefty for us, then it got to a point where we could deal with it," Jones said. Jones said the Cowboys know there's a chance Porter will leave in free agency after this season, but they think if he does, they'll get a 2028 compensatory pick that largely makes up for losing the 2028 second-round pick. "We had to have that trade make sense if Joey left after this year," Jones said. "That's why the 2 in '28 matches up with a compensatory pick. If he did leave we'd probably get a 3 or a 4 for him and get that back for Joey in '28 when that 2 is in place. So it made a lot of sense. It protected us." Even if Porter proves to be only a rental for the rest of this season before going elsewhere, Jones thinks the price was right, once the Steelers lowered it.

title: NFL reminds teams that conversations on officiating are "confidential"
summary: The NFL routinely communicates with teams regarding concerns arising from calls made and not made in the most recent games.
full_text: The NFL routinely communicates with teams regarding concerns arising from calls made and not made in the most recent games. The league, with some express exceptions, does not want the teams talking publicly about the contents of the conversations. On Friday, the NFL sent a memo reminding all teams that such communications are " confidential ," and not for external disclosure. The memo is an obvious response to Rams coach Sean McVay's decision to spill the beans on his discussions with the league regarding the controversial defensive pass interference call at the end of Sunday night's game against the Broncos. While it's unknown whether McVay was fined for the infraction, the memo makes clear that the league doesn't want its coaches flipping the lid on Pandora’s box . As noted yesterday, what will the league do if it admits that such an important mistake (we still don't think it was a mistake) changed the outcome of a game? Refund all wagers on the Rams? Los Angeles closed as a 0.5-point favorite. All moneyline and spread wagers on the Rams that lost were, based on that admission, winners. It's just a matter of time before someone files a nationwide class action arising from losses that should have been wins due to avoidable officiating errors. The NFL's too-cozy relationship with gambling makes it inevitable. Having one of the coaches hold up the smoking gun and wave it around for all to see makes it easy.
author: Mike Florio

title: CBS, Tony Romo undoubtedly negotiated a contract settlement
summary: Friday's announcement that CBS and No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo have "mutually agreed to part ways" hardly means that the separation was a joint decision.
full_text: Friday's announcement that CBS and No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo have " mutually agreed to part ways " hardly means that the separation was a joint decision. Romo had vowed to return to CBS ; CBS clearly did not want him back. The mutual agreement comes from the paperwork. With Romo owed $72 million over four years, ending the relationship meant reaching an agreement on how much he'll be paid to walk away. Andrew Marchand of The Athletic writes that "CBS preferred to eat a good portion of the remaining money " to fighting with Romo over how much he'd get. Marchand notes that the "exact figure" is "unknown." As Marchand surmises, the fact that the situation was resolved without full-blown litigation or arbitration means it was not insignificant. Our guess (and it's just a guess) is that Romo will get anywhere from half to two-thirds of the money — $36 million to $48 million. While CBS may have had a silver bullet in the contract allowing for termination without pay for violation of a broad and vague "morals clause," it would have been difficult to make it stick based solely on an OWI arrest and ensuing no-contest plea. And the simple reality is that CBS used the situation as a way to pull the plug. If CBS felt the same way about Romo as it did when he signed his latest contract, they would have found a way to excuse the situation and move on. He was already on thin ice at CBS, based in incessant criticisms of his performances. The OWI arrest was tantamount to Romo jumping up and down on it. Romo still gets a sizable portion of the money. But he doesn't get all of it, and he also loses the status and the profile that comes with being the top NFL analyst at one of the few networks that televise NFL games watched by millions every week.
author: Mike Florio

title: Inside Drake Maye's alarming 2026 slump one year after Patriots QB was MVP runner-up
summary: New England's franchise quarterback has six interceptions and an NFL-worst 58.6 passer rating as opposing evaluators question his confidence and pocket poise
full_text:
Through the Patriots ' first 20 games last season -- a combination of the regular season and the three playoff games leading into the Super Bowl -- there wasn't a single game that Drake Maye finished with more than one interception. It was a breakthrough year that saw Maye finish as MVP runner-up and catapult himself onto the short list of the NFL's best young quarterbacks.
Eight months later, the 24-year old is now coming off his third multi-interception performance in New England's last four games dating back to that Super Bowl loss to Seahawks .
It's part of a maddening run for Maye and the Patriots, who are off to a 1-2 start just a season after advancing to the Super Bowl. A large part of that has been regression from Maye that's surprised many around the NFL, including (based on grades from Pro Football Focus) the worst game of his career last week during the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars . Maye finished with no touchdowns and two interceptions.
In all through the first three games of this season, the 2024 and 2025 Pro Bowl selection has six interceptions with just one touchdown, has yet to eclipse 208 passing yards in any individual game and has a QB rating (58.6) that ranks as the worst in the NFL among quarterbacks who've made more than two starts.
It's led to some in NFL coaching and front office circles starting to wonder whether Maye's confidence is on a downward spiral.
"When I when I studied him when he was coming out (of college), you saw the athletic ability and you saw the arm talent but, especially his last year at North Carolina, there were just a lot of the misses, and the missed throws were kind of alarming and some instinctual things too," a veteran NFL front office staffer told CBS Sports. "Then last year (in that second season in New England), he looked just a lot more comfortable and in command and like the game had slowed down for him. But now this year it almost looks like it's kind of sped up for him a little bit. And some of the misses, whether it be mis-read or missed throw, some of those things have just kind of popped up a little bit more and he's just not taking care of the ball all that well.
"He just doesn't look comfortable and confident out there right now, especially when he's in the pocket. You still see how much talent he has. It's just very up and down play in and play out."
Opposing team staffers also see teams having success generating pressuring on Maye and that impacting him.
In Super Bowl LX, the Seahawks had six sacks of Maye. Then in Week 1, Seattle again had success pressuring him, this time, as described by sources familiar with their gameplan, shifting to more zone blitzes instead of man-to-man pressures after the Patriots' offseason wide receiver additions. The Seahawks finished with three sacks and three interceptions.
The Steelers then had three sacks in Week 2 and the Jaguars followed that last week with three sacks too.
"He's a good quarterback obviously but we were able to pressure him early and I think that showed up later (impacting his play)," an opposing team staffer said.
Other opposing coaches have been critical of New England's offensive system as well and point to that as a primary issue. It also doesn't help that Maye and the Patriots have been without the team's main offseason acquisition, star wide receiver A.J. Brown, since Week 1 due to ankle injury. Without Brown, as one opposing defensive coach put it, "they don't have receivers that are getting open."
Either way, Maye and New England now head into a matchup against Josh Allen and the 3-0 Bills having yet to produce more than 13 offensive points in any of these first three games, a big dropoff in offensive success for the Patriots after ranking second in the NFL with an average of 28.8 points per game.
"He's got to be better at learning what defenses look like and where his relief's going to be, but the offensive system doesn't do him any favors in my opinion," an opposing coach, who's faced New England this season, said. "They only run a certain number of plays and it's the same plays they've been running for a long time. And if your quarterback's not Tom Brady, who's going to get you in the perfect call, or someone like Josh Allen who's (elite at) second-chance plays, that offensive system after a while starts to get real stale."
Last week, back when it was still unclear how much time Jayden Daniels would miss due to his injured left elbow, the Commanders star quarterback decided to get in front of his team and announce that he was going to bypass surgery and that he owed it to the team to get back as quickly as possible.
Within days, Daniels was already back doing light throwing. He then practiced this week on a limited basis. And while he won't play this week vs. the Colts in London, sources continue to classify him as truly being week-to-week.
Washington, which beat the Seahawks last week behind backup QB Marcus Mariota to move to 1-2, face the Giants next week and then play the 49ers .
For a second straight season already, the 49ers have had to deal with injuries to a number of key players.
There's some good news on that front, though, with a high level of confidence that 2025 first-round draft pick Mykel Williams , who's been out since an ACL injury last November, will be able to return to action and play next week when the 49ers face the Seahawks, sources tell CBS Sports.
The defensive end returned to practice this week after beginning the season on the PUP list. Williams, whom San Francisco selected with the No. 11 pick in last year's draft, started nine games for the 49ers last year before suffering the torn ACL.

title: NFL Week 4 injury report: Justin Jefferson out, Nico Collins in; Terry McLaurin suffers late-week injury
summary: Here's a look at each game designation for Week 4 in the NFL
full_text:
The NFL is about to turn the page on the first month of the regular season with Week 4 already underway. After the Cleveland Browns pulled off the home upset on Thursday night over the Pittsburgh Steelers , and coming off a Week 3 slate that tied an NFL record for one-score games, this upcoming crop of contests has a lot to live up to. Judging by what we've seen over the previous three weeks as a whole, Week 4 will be locked and loaded with storylines.
One of the unfortunate storylines that is a factor every week, however, is injuries. Already this season, the league has endured several high-profile injuries, and the bug continues to bite teams across the NFL with a number of notable names sidelined for Week 4. That includes receiver Justin Jefferson of the Vikings , Rams star defensive lineman Aaron Donald , and Patriots All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez , who have each been ruled out for this weekend due to injury. And that's just the tip of the iceberg.
With teams concluding their week of practice, they've released their final injury reports, which include game statuses for Week 4. Below, you can see a breakdown of each game's designations: who is in, who's out, and who still has their status up in the air.
Keenan Allen did not practice on Friday after logging back-to-back limited sessions. If he is unable to go, that would result in an even more concentrated target share for the likes of tight end Tyler Warren and wideout Josh Downs . Meanwhile, Dulin could also factor into that after practicing fully for the second straight day, despite that questionable designation.
Despite making the trip to London and practicing on a limited basis throughout the week, the Commanders have ruled out quarterback Jayden Daniels. That means Marcus Mariota will start for the second straight week. Outside of Daniels, the most noteworthy development on the injury report is the addition of Terry McLaurin. He was limited on Friday after suffering a hamstring injury.
New England will be without two key starters on defense as they've ruled out star corner Christian Gonzalez and defensive tackle Christian Barmore due to shoulder injuries. Neither was able to practice this week. On a more positive note, starting right tackle Morgan Moses has a chance to play Sunday, as he returned to practice Friday on a limited basis. He's questionable with a foot injury.
Buffalo could be without defensive lineman T.J. Sanders due to an illness. After not practicing on Wednesday, he was limited both Thursday and Friday, but is doubtful to play. As for Christian Benford, the corner is questionable despite not practicing at all this week with a toe injury.
The Jets will not have standout running back Breece Hall on Sunday due to a quad injury, so Braelon Allen will get the start out of the backfield. The offense will take another hit with Adonai Mitchell out and possibly not have Kenyon Sadiq, as the rookie tight end is questionable with a back injury. Sadiq practiced on a limited basis throughout the week.
Caleb Williams will not play this week as he continues to recover from his hamstring injury. That said, Ben Johnson has yet to make it clear who'll start in his place, with Tyson Bagent (who cleared concussion protocol last week) and Case Keenum as the top options. Whoever gets the nod will have D'Andre Swift in the backfield after he returned to practice as a full participant on Friday and carries no designation after missing Thursday's session with a knee injury.
Jacksonville is pretty healthy coming into this matchup, with no players ruled out. Regis, Brown and Braswell all practiced on a limited basis throughout the week.
B.J. Hill was able to return to practice on a limited basis for Cincinnati on Friday, which gives him a shot to play in Week 4. Meanwhile, Bozeman is trending in the opposite direction despite each sharing questionable designations. He did not participate in practice on Friday after being limited on Thursday.
Arizona is largely sitting pretty from an injury standpoint, listing just Dadrion Taylor-Demerson out for Week 4 after he did not practice this week due to a back injury. However, edge rusher Josh Sweat was downgraded to a limited participant on Friday due to a groin injury.

Aaron Donald will not be cleared to go for this NFC matchup against Philadelphia, as the standout defensive lineman is dealing with a back injury that held him out throughout the week of practice. On a more positive note, wideout Puka Nacua (hip) will make his return, as he has no injury designation.

title: Rams' Aaron Donald to miss Week 4 game vs. Eagles, Puka Nacua's status updated
summary: Donald will miss his second game of the season, but the Rams received some good news on Friday
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams won't have star defensive end Aaron Donald in their Week 4 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles , the team announced Friday, but wide receiver Puka Nacua is expected to return. Donald is dealing with a back injury and did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, while Nacua has been dealing with a hip injury and was limited in practice both days.
Donald has played in two games this year, while Nacua has played in one.
Donald unretired this offseason, returning to play for his former team after initially retiring in 2023. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year's return has not been as smooth as he or the team had hoped. He sat out the opener when the Rams fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, and Sunday will mark his second missed game of the season. Head coach Sean McVay said Donald felt soreness in his back after the team's Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos .
"He's working as hard as he can to get himself feeling as good as possible. And we're hopeful and optimistic that good days are ahead," McVay said.
When Donald is healthy, he is an offense's worst nightmare. The 35-year-old's resume includes a Super Bowl win, eight first-team All-Pro nods and 10 Pro Bowl selections. He has 547 tackles, 111 sacks, 24 forced fumbles and seven fumble recoveries over 11 seasons in his career.
However, this week, the Rams will now be without Donald and Myles Garrett , who is on injured reserve. Garrett underwent knee surgery after Week 1 and is expected to miss at least several more weeks.
Nacua has shown his dominance early, with two 1,000+ yard seasons in his four-year career. He's quickly become a staple in Matthew Stafford's offense, and his return should help a team that's struggled more than many expected this season.
McVay said that while Nacua will not have an injury designation, how much he will play is still to be determined. The head coach noted that his star wide receiver "looked sharp" on Thursday.
"Physically, he's getting in and out of his breaks, looks strong, looks sturdy, looks explosive," McVay said. "I think it'll really just be a feel for the overall conditioning. Hoping the magic of the jersey on Sundays, he's feeling really good there."
Nacua played in the team's season-opening loss in Australia, recording five catches for 74 yards, but he hasn't seen action in a game since.
L.A.'s offense has put up 26+ points the last two weeks, but it split those games. The offense is fourth in passing yards (885) and seventh in rushing yards (401), while the defense is second-best in passing yards allowed (522) and 11th in rushing yards allowed (304). However, the Rams have two checks in the loss column.
Turnovers are one thing slowing down the offense, with Stafford throwing two picks last week. Having his favorite receiver, who had the league's second-most receiving yards last year (1,715), back will add to his comfort level in creating better decision-making and fewer picks.
In his absence, Davante Adams has stepped up, recording 137 yards on seven receptions last week and eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns in the air.
The Rams sit at 1-2 as they get ready to face a 2-1 Eagles team that has also had their share of struggles this season as well.

title: NFL suspends 49ers owner Jed York six games, fines him $500,000 after Ohio arrest
summary: York accepted responsibility after the NFL suspended him for violating its Personal Conduct Policy, with three games he already missed counting toward the punishment
full_text:
The NFL suspended San Francisco 49ers principal owner Jed York for six regular-season games and fined him $500,000 for violating the Personal Conduct Policy, the league announced on Friday .
York, who was arrested in late August and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools , stayed away from the organization during the league's investigation. Those three missed games will count as time served, meaning he may be allowed to return to the team on Tuesday, Oct. 20, following San Francisco's Week 6 matchup on "Monday Night Football" against the Washington Commanders .
The first game he will be eligible to watch live will be Week 7, when the team visits the Atlanta Falcons , while the first home game he'll be permitted to attend will be Week 9, when San Francisco hosts the Las Vegas Raiders .
"Today, the NFL concluded its review, and I accept its decision in full," York said in a statement, via NFL Network . "To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry.
"This was an inexcusable mistake, and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one's failures, and that even our moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don't take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead."
Police arrested York in East Palestine, Ohio, on the weekend of August 22nd, specifically at Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community off State Route 170. After pleading no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools, he was sentenced to two days in the Columbiana County Jail, with credit for one day served, and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines. KRON4 obtained court documents that showed the disorderly conduct charge was amended from engaging in prostitution.
York, who has been the 49ers CEO since 2008, became the fifth principal owner of the franchise in March of 2024.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Watt is going on in Pittsburgh? Frustrations boil over on Steelers' sideline during loss to Browns
summary: Multiple Steelers players were seen sounding off during the divisional game on Thursday night
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers had a frustrating night on Thursday, and it showed. Numerous players were visibly upset, from quarterback Aaron Rodgers , to defensive stars T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward.
The Steelers were down 21-7 against the Cleveland Browns with less than two minutes to go in the first half, with their second-quarter drives reading "interceptions, punt, missed field goal" and the home team's resulting in "touchdown, touchdown, touchdown."
It was a tough showing for the offense and defense and one player decided to take things into his own hands.
Watt, a former Defensive Player of the Year and eight-time Pro Bowler, asked for a coach's headset so he could speak to those in the booth, including defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. I'm not a body language expert, but it certainly didn't look like a pleasant conversation.
T.J. Watt asked for the headset to speak to the coaching staff 😅 #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/AchzuDdQoP
It's certainly not typical for a player to do this, so Watt must have really felt strongly about how the game was called to step in.
Whatever Watt did seemed to work to some degree, as the Steelers came back to tie the game with just under two minutes to go, but ultimately lost 27-24 after a late field goal from the Browns.
"It's extremely frustrating," Watt said after the game. "To not sit here at 3-1 isn't acceptable. Obviously, it's a long season to go, but we just have to put it together."
He said there were situations in the game that they feel like they would want back or done better, and they'll watch film this week to see where those spots were.
Watt added that there is an urgent need to improve, saying, "We have to get better and get better quick."
When asked if he felt there was anything weighing the defense down, he gave a very immediate and strong, "No."
While total yards on offense (Browns 372 to 361), turnovers (2 per team), third down efficiency (Steelers: 4-of-13, Browns: 4-of 10) and red zone efficiency (Steelers: 2-of-3, Browns 2-of-2) were comparable, the Browns easily marched down the field when it mattered most. The former first overall pick took accountability for the defense's woes, while giving credit to his offense.
"We always have faith," Watt said on the near comeback. "Anytime we have 8 [Rodgers] at quarterback we've seen those guys move the ball up and down the field all the time so we're just trying to give those guys a chance and we didn't do it tonight."
He was far from the only Steeler to have a notable reaction during the game. Seven-time Pro Bowler Cam Heyward appeared to scream at another player, "That's f----ed up man. That's f---iing crazy!"
The cameras also caught Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy in a heated exchange , using colorful language other over play calls.
After the game, McCarthy unsurprisingly got questions about what was said and his response could also apply to Watt and Heyward.
"What's said on the field, the way I grew up in this game, usually stays on the field. That's not the case today. I understand that. Any negative communication on my part, I wish I wouldn't use those words," McCarthy said.
The Steelers now sit at 2-2, with their other loss coming in a blowout defeat against the struggling New England Patriots in Week 2. Next up for Pittsburgh is the Indianapolis Colts , who sit at 1-2 coming into Week 4.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Mike Tomlin gets roasted by former Super Bowl MVP, former Steelers star and others for Minecraft City
summary: Former players and coaches marveled at Tomlin's surprising hobby, while Cleveland used it to troll its division rival after a wild victory
full_text:
It's not easy to have a hobby when you're an NFL coach, but Mike Tomlin definitely had one and he unveiled it this week. During a YouTube stream Thursday , the former Steelers coach revealed that he secretly spent the past 12 years building an extremely detailed Minecraft City , and let's just say, there were a lot of people around the NFL who found it amusing that Tomlin spent so much time on something that wasn't related to football at all.
After unveiled his city, Tomlin got absolutely roasted by everyone from a former player to a former Super Bowl MVP to a former NFL head coach. There was even one NFL team that made fun of him, but let's start with Le'Veon Bell .
The three-time Pro Bowler spent five seasons with Tomlin in Pittsburgh and he was one of the first players to make fun of Tomlin for his city.
we were tryna win super bowls and coach T was on minecraft building cities 😭 https://t.co/iMyJ2Su3pm
Bell seems to be joking here, but there's certainly some truth to his tweet. Tomlin said he started building his Minecraft City in 2014, and over his 12 seasons of coaching, the Steelers didn't reach the Super Bowl a single time. They also didn't win a single playoff game during Tomlin's final nine seasons on the job.
Someone actually broke down how Tomlin coached before and after he started his Minecraft City, and, well, the numbers probably won't make Steelers fans very happy.
Mike Tomlin Minecraft splits Tomlin before Minecraft (7 seasons) 1 Super Bowl win 2 Super Bowl trips 5 playoff wins (5-3, 0.625) overall Tomlin with Minecraft (12 seasons) 0 Super Bowl wins 0 Super Bowl trips 3 playoff wins (3-9, 0.250) overall pic.twitter.com/zSfkCBridV
Of those three playoff wins that came after he started Minecraft, the final one came in the 2016 divisional round. After beating the Chiefs 18-16, that set up a game with New England in the AFC Championship. Former Super Bowl MVP Julian Edelman played in that January 2017 game and he made fun of Tomlin's preparation for the matchup.
we were tryna win super bowls and coach T was on minecraft building cities 😭 https://t.co/iMyJ2Su3pm
The Patriots ended up steamrolling the Steelers, 36-17, on their way to a Super Bowl title.
Being an NFL coach takes up a lot of your time, which is why most people were so surprised that Tomlin was able to build such a detailed city. Former Colts coach Chuck Pagano was asked about Tomlin's Minecraft habit and he was absolutely shocked that the former Steelers coach was able to construct anything so detailed while also coaching the Steelers at the same time.
"I don't know how one does it," Pagano said on the Pat McAfee Show .
Pagano admitted he also had a hobby during his coaching career, but it was one that let him do his job at the same time.
"You know I had a hobby? Right. The peloton," Pagano said. "I had it next to my desk. Like our buddy [Seahawks GM John Schneider] up in Seattle, multi-tasking, you can stick that in your office, you can jump on it, you can still watch tape, you can do a lot of things while you're just pedaling a bike, but I can't fathom. I don't have as big a brain as Coach Tomlin has -- granted he did a lot of great things, Super Bowl champ, all those great things -- but do try to find the time to create this extravagant."
According to Tomlin, building the city started as a way for him to connect with his young children, but after they grew up, he stayed with it because it was therapeutic.
"I'm not a big TV watcher," Tomlin said. "It allowed me to detach from the realities and the pressures of life."
Although Tomlin doesn't watch much TV, he was probably watching on Thursday night when the Browns stunned the Steelers with a wild 27-24 win in Cleveland. Tomlin obviously doesn't coach the Steelers anymore, but the Browns still decided to poke fun at him on social media following the game.
game over. pic.twitter.com/cbdDFZLDew
At this point, it's starting to feel like Tomlin might not ever live this down. If any other NFL coach is currently building a secret Minecraft City, you might want to keep that to yourself.
author: John Breech

title: Browns' Mason Graham to reportedly miss a few weeks with MCL sprain, ankle sprain
summary: The standout defensive tackle was injured during Pittsburgh's opening possession on Thursday night
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns saw one of their best players exit the field during the first quarter of Thursday night's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers . During Pittsburgh's first offensive drive, Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham exited the game after sustaining a left knee injury. He was initially labeled as questionable to return before he was ruled out of the game as the second half began.
Per NFL Network , Graham is expected to miss a few weeks with an MCL sprain and an ankle sprain.
Graham underwent an MRI on Friday, which revealed he is not believed to have suffered an injury that will keep him out long term.
Graham appeared to get tangled up with a Steelers offensive lineman before he fell to the ground. He quickly received attention from Cleveland's medical staff before walking off the field under his own power. He then went to the blue medical tent before walking into the locker room.
The fifth overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft , Graham has been enjoying a stellar season so far. He entered the game with 4.0 sacks, including at least one sack in each of the Browns' first three games. During Cleveland's Week 3 win over the Carolina Panthers , Graham filled the stat sheet with 2.0 sacks and seven tackles (three for loss).
Graham, 23, enjoyed a standout college career at Michigan from 2022-24. In 2023, he played a key role in Michigan's first national championship win since 1997. On Thursday night, his former college teammate, Steelers wideout Roman Wilson , capped off Pittsburgh's first drive with a touchdown run.
