(Photo by David Madison/Getty Images) | Getty Images Atlanta Falcons fans who endured the first two decades of this franchise’s existence were only occasionally rewarded with winning seasons, much less greatness. As has been the case for the Falcons throughout their 60 year history, it was up to individual stars to make this franchise feel special when the wins and losses didn’t feel special at all. So you watched Tommy Nobis, an underrated great who had the undying respect of his peers. You rooted hard for Claude Humphrey, who put together the first leg of a Hall of Fame career in Atlanta. You winced as Steve Bartkowski took big hits and cheered as he still delivered some of the franchise’s biggest passes. Later on, you watched William Andrews glide and dance through defenders and mourned the career he might have had if not for injury. But if you were a fan of this team all the way back to the 60s, mostly you watched Jeff Van Note. Maybe he didn’t jump out to you on a play-by-play basis, but you saw him every single game mauling some hapless defensive tackle, paving the way for a rotating cast of runners, and keeping everyone from Bob Berry to David Archer upright. You watched him suit up in rain and sunshine, for the worst and best squads the Falcons had to offer, surrounded by players and coaching staffs who continually turned over and changed. The constant was Van Note, with a bloody nose and an injured knee, with that mustache and his 57 jersey crouched over the ball for thousands upon thousands of snaps. He did it for 18 years, missing only four games with that aforementioned knee injury, and along the way Van Note became the greatest center in Falcons history and one of the finest centers the NFL produced in his era. The most remarkable part of that was that he was actually drafted as a linebacker in the 11th round and barely played his rookie season, but Norm Van Brocklin saw Van Note as a center and the rest is history. What made Jeff Van Note great—inspiring, even—was that consistency. He did something he loved and was good at tenaciously, professionally, and with little complaint, no matter how dark and dumb everything around him might have been or felt. He gave so much to this franchise as a player, a legend, and later a broadcaster that it was a no-brainer to make the six-time Pro Bowler a Ring of Honor inductee. The very best players and people the Falcons have offered us over these many years, from Van Note to Mike Kenn to Julio Jones to Grady Jarrett to Matt Ryan, have followed in his footsteps by coming to play, by leading in word and deed, and showing up on Sundays to try to drag this impossible franchise to greatness with everything they could give. It’s a wonder, and the work and the dignity and the consistency are something we can all admire and emulate in our own lives. Jeff Van Note has died , as the headline says, and we mourn the passing of a Falcons legend. But we also remember Jeff Van Note as a good man and a great player who gave so much to our favorite team, and we can and should kindle that memory for many, many years to come.

title: Ravens vs Cowboys Rookie Report
summary: After their first loss last week, the rookies and the Ravens bounced back to experience a once-in-a-decade type of win in just their third week of their careers. Baltimore’s youngsters played a key role in the team’s massive comeback win in first-ever NFL game in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. OG Vega Ioane Ioane had his […]
full_text: RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 27: Matthew Hibner #88 of the Baltimore Ravens scores a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images) | Getty Images After their first loss last week, the rookies and the Ravens bounced back to experience a once-in-a-decade type of win in just their third week of their careers. Baltimore’s youngsters played a key role in the team’s massive comeback win in first-ever NFL game in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. OG Vega Ioane Ioane had his best day as a pro in Brazil. He gave up zero pressures ( via Pro Football Focus ) and had moments where he moved some bodies in the run game in dominant fashion. But by far his biggest highlight of the day didn’t come at his normal position. After the Ravens lost both their starting center Jovaughn Gwyn and his backup Ethan Pocic, the Ravens turned to none other than the rookie in his third career game. Ioane hadn’t played center in a game since 2023 at Penn State. He proceeded to have zero snap mistakes and continue his perfect pass protection. For now, it seems the rookie will continue to play at center until a different solution is found. Vega Ioane getting NASTY in the run game. pic.twitter.com/ROs3emJ45m — Chris Cooper (@ChrisCooper_NFL) September 28, 2026 OLB Zion Young Young seems to be improving every week, and it’s encouraging how many snaps the coaching staff is giving him. Young played 26 snaps and ended up totaling three tackles with one run stop and a pressure, according to PFF. While the stats themselves aren’t anything electric, his PFF grades are rising, and the film shows development in the areas of his game that had questions while he leans into using his strength more comfortably. Zion Young had a great game vs the cowboys Stats may not reflect (1 pressure, 2 tackles, 1 tfl) but charged up hand usage and leveraging length at the POA. SOB vs the run Finally starting to show improved reaction time/ get off (watch rep 2). 50% win rate on true pass sets pic.twitter.com/Teqkmkfpw6 — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) September 28, 2026 WR Elijah Sarratt A week after Sarratt was mentioned by name as somebody who could find rhythm in the offense following the injuries to Zay Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane and then proceeded to get zero snaps against the Saints, Sarratt was on the inactive list as Flowers made his return. With Lane’s return coming soon and every other wide receiver seemingly ahead of him on the depth chart, Sarratt’s rookie year seems to be one that is going to be filled with limited snaps and lots of healthy scratches. TE Matt Hibner Hibner’s role continues to get bigger and bigger every week as the Ravens slowly get the explosive tight end more involved. Hibner finished with 32 snaps, just barely behind Durham Smythe (34) and Mark Andrews (33), who had a hand injury and left the game for a couple of snaps. Hibner caught two more passes for 23 yards. One was an explosive 21-yard reception, and the other was his first career touchdown that gave the Ravens the lead with a minute and a half remaining in the game. Outside of his receiving stats, PFF charted Hibner with eight routes ran, three pass-blocking snaps, and 21 run-blocking snaps. Hibner received a 59.5 run-blocking grade and a 73.1 pass-blocking grade with no pressures. CLUTCH TOUCHDOWN @MatthewHibner !!!!!!!! Tune in on @NFLonCBS and @ParamountPlus pic.twitter.com/Y1aPEOdTUz — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) September 27, 2026 TE Josh Cuevas Cuevas had his busiest day as a pro with 16 snaps, in large part due to Mark Andrews’ absence during his hand injury. Cuevas had his first career catch, a 14-yard play from a drag route off a chip-and-release that came with 11 yards after the catch. Cuevas ability to chip and then become a quarterback-friendly target immediately after was one of his most consistent traits and one of my favorite things from his college tape, and it’s something the Ravens should utilize more as the offensive line continues to build. Cuevas also had eight run-blocking snaps where PFF graded him at 58.1 CB Chandler Rivers Rivers is another Day 3 rookie whose role continues to grow exponentially right now as the Ravens figure some things out on the defensive side of the ball. Rivers finished with 32 total snaps and tallied two pressures on three pass-rush snaps, proving his effectiveness as a blitzer, something that was heavily noted on his college tape. Like much of the Ravens’ secondary, though, PFF was not kind to Rivers on his coverage. For now, we will hope that will improve as the rest of the secondary gets better in Jesse Minter’s scheme, as the head coach looks to elevate the unit as he does so well. P Ryan Eckley You are doing your job well as a rookie punter if nobody is thinking about you at the end of the game. For those who remember Jordan Stout’s rookie year, and a couple following it, Stout was often remembered, and not for the best reasons, before finally developing into the NFL’s best punter last season. For now, Eckley is getting his job done without mistakes, and that’s all you can ask for. Eckley had three punts against the Cowboys, averaging 49.7 per punt and having a long of 58 yards. Wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane and running back Adam Randall remain on injured reserve, with defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny on the practice squad. Ja’Kobi Lane on his IG: pic.twitter.com/CCGhIpuAIb — Ravens Nation 𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀 (@LiveRavenNation) September 29, 2026

title: Ravens vs Cowboys: the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
summary: In a potential game-of-the-year candidate, the Baltimore Ravens won a thriller in Rio against the Dallas Cowboys by a score 34-31. It wasn’t pretty, but it was a major victory that could hopefully help this team shrug off some of the demons they’ve had about closing games. There was plenty of good, bad and ugly […]
full_text: Baltimore Ravens' wide receiver #04 Zay Flowers runs with the ball during the NFL match between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on September 27, 2026. (Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images In a potential game-of-the-year candidate, the Baltimore Ravens won a thriller in Rio against the Dallas Cowboys by a score 34-31. It wasn’t pretty, but it was a major victory that could hopefully help this team shrug off some of the demons they’ve had about closing games. There was plenty of good, bad and ugly all across the board in an up-and-down performance so let’s get into it. The Good Redemption: The biggest storyline coming out of this game. Tyler Loop received a lot of hostility this offseason after his massive miss to end the Ravens’ season that triggered shockwaves for this organization. Then, after a rough preseason, he watched competition get signed to the roster and faced honest questions about how long he could keep this job started. He’s done nothing but be near perfect since then. Outside of a field goal that was blocked Week 2, he’s hit all of his kicks. And when the pressure was as high as it could be this early in the season, Loop hit a 56-yard bomb to win it for the Ravens. Suddenly, he has the trust of the fanbase back again – and Baltimore might have a new clutch kicker. Lamar Jackson crunch-time narratives: It’s always been a silly narrative. Since Lamar Jackson became a starter in 2019, he has 12 fourth-quarter comeback wins, tied for seventh with Aaron Rodgers. Now he’s done it again. It’s his first game-winning drive that started with less than a minute on the clock. It’s also the fastest game-winning drive in the Super Bowl-era. Jackson wasn’t perfect in this game and had some accuracy issues early, especially deep. But he got better as the game went on and was clutch when it was needed. Three-headed monster: After missing it for the second half of Week 1 and all of Week 2, the beast made its return in Week 3. Jackson completed 15 of his 20 passes for 186 yards and two touchdowns and a 136.7 passer rating He also added 50 yards on the ground in key moments, both to save himself and kickstart the offense when it was sputtering. Running back Derrick Henry had a down day by his standards with only 89 yards on 26 carries. He still managed a couple of explosives, including a long of 29 yards, and had two touchdowns. Zay Flowers’ return also had a massive impact. In a game many were nervous about the shifty wideout playing in due to the poor field conditions potentially worsening his hamstring injury, he was a vital to the win. Flowers had five catches for 84 yards including the massive 27 yard strike that set up the game winner. His efficiency this year has been the best in the league. It’s hard to argue that any other team has a better QB-RB-WR trio than the Ravens. Carson Vinson: While the offensive line unit itself is still a struggling unit trying to build and figure itself out, Vinson’s play on Sunday can’t be thrown out. With Ronnie Stanley down, Vinson made his first career start in his second season and did a commendable job. Pro Football Focus had him giving up zero pressures. He was a little hit-or-miss in the run game and still has plenty to work on. But right now, Vinson is exactly what you need as a backup left tackle: a guy you can plug in and not have to worry about, even if he won’t give you spectacular play. Hopefully with a little more development, the Ravens have their future left tackle on the roster. Vega Ioane: After a rough showing last week against the Saints where Ioane’s ability to process up the middle blitzes was put to the test, Ioane reasserted himself against the Cowboys. It wasn’t a flawless performance but Ioane was getting after in the run game moving bodies and help up in pass protection without a pressure according to PFF. The most impressive part was Ioane’s slide to center after the Ravens lost both Gwyn and Pocic to injury. Ioane became the snapper and finished the game without any snap issues and no pressures. It was a massive moment where the rookie stepped up in just his third career game and was prepared for the moment. Now, at least for now, Ioane is going to stick at center. We’ll have to wait and see if it’s a season-long change. The Bad Penalties: For the third week in a row, penalties are on this list. The Ravens committed nine for 78 yards on Sunday. Once again, a couple of them took away big plays for the Ravens and set them back into unfavorable situations. You can’t even blame it on the strange environment of playing internationally, as the crowd seemed almost Ravens heavy. There were more pre-snap, procedural penalties along the offensive line. It has to get fixed. Slow starts: The Ravens came out and went three-and-out on their first drive and then followed it up with a four-and-out on their next. The defense also allowed 10 points to open up the game on their first two drives. Both units proceeded to improve and flip the moment in the first half. But Baltimore’s coaching staff needs to figure out how to get off to better starts and put themselves ahead. The Ravens are going to start a gauntlet of a scheduled in a couple of weeks against tougher teams and will need more consistency to open games if they want better chances at winning. Sack conversions: The Ravens only managed one sack while hitting Dak Prescott eight times with 22 pressures. The pressures are a good sign, the conversion rate simply isn’t good enough and the defense needs to find more sacks. While I know some will panic about the lack of pass rush, both the success on blitzes and a four-man rush, I am not worried just yet. While they haven’t converted just yet, the pressure numbers for the Ravens defense is good, and when the secondary play does improve, more sacks should come with it. As Nnamdi Madubuike ramps up, those sack numbers should jump up as well too. Trey Hendrickson will convert more and I’ve liked the flashes I’ve seen from Mike Green and Zion Young when out in a position to utilize their skill sets. Secondary play: Considering Jesse Minter’s calling card was elevating secondary play in LA, it’s confusing how a more talented secondary in Baltimore is struggling so much. Especially after seeing the success the scheme had in the preseason. Marlon and Bate Wiggins had their struggles in this game, which is to be expected against a duo as talented as Lamb and Pickens. But both have made a handful of plays so far this season and overall have been better than last season. Wiggins came back with a lock down end to keep the Cowboys out of the end zone at the end of the game. But the safety room outside of Kyle Hamilton has been abysmal. They don’t do anything. Malaki Starks and Jaylin Hawkins struggles seem to have nothing to do with talent and everything do with looking lost. Both of them are playing like they are lost, jumping at random things and playing hesitant at times. I don’t know if they just aren’t comfortable in the scheme yet or don’t know what their roles are, but they are both capable of playing much better than this. At this point, I have to guess that Minter and the staff are aware of the lack of impact from their safeties and are working with those guys to get it fixed. I’m going to give it time because we know Minter is capable of elevating that part of a defense. But they don’t have long until a couple of powerhouse offenses are on deck. The Ugly Fourth-quarter collapses : I know the Ravens won. I know Lamar Jackson lead two drives at the end of the game to get the lead and win the game, and I know the defense forced a field goal at the end despite an awful pass interference call against them. I also know Loop finally hit his first clutch game winner in the NFL. That doesn’t mean the problems disappear. The offense was non-existent for most of the second half and the defense, once again, just seemingly…

title: Ravens rule out OLB Trey Hendrickson for Week 4 vs. Titans
summary: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday that outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson would not play in Sunday’s matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Hendrickson, 31, suffered multiple fractures in a finger on his right hand in Week 1. He missed multiple practices but continued to play with a cast and virtually no drop in […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Trey Hendrickson #91 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts against the New Orleans Saints prior to an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday that outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson would not play in Sunday’s matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Hendrickson, 31, suffered multiple fractures in a finger on his right hand in Week 1. He missed multiple practices but continued to play with a cast and virtually no drop in his production. This week, however, he missed all three practices while seeking a more permanent solution. “We were able to get the finger fixed,” Minter explained. “We think it’ll be very, very short term…think that’s going to be best for us moving forward, long-term.” “Trey Hendrickson will be out this week.” pic.twitter.com/p4kUkLQ3Jl — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) October 2, 2026 Hendrickson’s absence will open up more snaps on the blind side for second-year edge rusher Mike Green. The 2025 second-round pick flashed in Week 2 against the Saints but has otherwise been quiet to start what was expected to be a breakout sophomore campaign. Rookie Zion Young, another second-rounder, could also see more pass-rushing opportunities after showcasing his physical run defense to in his first three NFL games. Undrafted rookie Ethan Burke will also be brought into Minter’s game day plans for the first time this year. Injuries were among the top concerns when the Ravens gave Hendrickson $60 million in fully guaranteed money this spring. He was dominant when healthy in 2023 and 2024, but he missed time in every previous season and played just seven games last year before undergoing core muscle surgery. But even with a broken finger, Hendrickson has looked worth every penny. He has 14 pressures – four in Week 1 and 10 across the next two games with a cast on his right hand – which ranks sixth in the league, according to Pro Football Focus . His 16.3% pass rush win rate also leads Baltimore’s defensive line. Next Gen Stats ranks Hendrickson as the league’s fourth-best edge rusher in both categories, too. By getting surgery done now, Hendrickson is hoping that his finger can fully heal and not bother him down the stretch of the season. Minter’s specific wording indicates that the team needed some time to evaluate the fracture and determine the best long-term fix. The Ravens will release their final Week 4 injury report later this afternoon, which will provide information on the status of other players who could miss Sunday’s game like left tackle Ronnie Stanley.

title: How does double-dipping correlating to winning in the NFL?
summary: It’s time to answer another question from a comment on my comprehensive study on end-of-half scoring. Yesterday, I wrote an article to answer the first question from a Rumbler on whether or not end-of-half scoring correlates to wins. Turns out it does. Teams that outscore their opponents in the final two minutes of the half […]
full_text: It’s time to answer another question from a comment on my comprehensive study on end-of-half scoring. Yesterday, I wrote an article to answer the first question from a Rumbler on whether or not end-of-half scoring correlates to wins. Turns out it does. Teams that outscore their opponents in the final two minutes of the half won 65.6% of the time in the 25-year sample from 2001 – 2025. On this glorious Saturday in Western New York, let’s attack the next questions from Rumbler PaulieB here: To answer it the best way I could, that actually had a large enough sample to pull from, I extended the double-dip question on either side of the half to four minutes. I did that simply because there was a very small percentage of games with points in the final two minutes of the first half AND in the first two minutes of the second half. Also, I’ve regularly heard the double-dip window as “the middle eight” or the final four minutes at the end of the second quarter and first four of the third quarter. Does scoring in the double-dip window correlate to wins? See for yourself here in this table: Win percentage Double dip occurred: scored in both windows 73.7% Scored in neither window 37.3% That’s a pretty striking percentage on the double-dip win rate, especially when it’s compared to a team’s win percentage when they don’t score in either window. Of course, the double dip doesn’t happen super often, only 13.5% of the time in this study’s quarter-century sample. But when it does, the team accomplishing it is in darn-good shape to win that football game, which is why we’ve seen teams regularly chasing the double dip. That 73.7% in the table is not necessarily the “classic” double dip. All a team needed to do is have scored in both windows. I included that figure in the table it’s essentially the exact same as the classic double dip, which is scoring right before the half then getting the ball out of halftime and scoring within the first four minutes of the third quarter. The winning percentage for the classic version of the double dip was 73.3% in the sample. And remember those five-year timeframe segments from the original article (2001 – 2005, 2006 – 2010 etc.)? The double-dip winning percentage wasn’t buoyed by one segment in particular. In fact, that winning percentage has never dipped — pun intended — below 70% in any segment or climbed higher than 75%. It’s at 71.4% through Week 3 in the 2026 season. As for the Bills, they’ve only double dipped seven times — six occurrences in the regular season and one time in the playoffs — since the start of the 2020 campaign. Their record when doing so is 7-0. So, yes, teams should make a concerted effort to double dip. It correlates rather strongly with winning the football game.

title: NFL predictions: 3 bold takes for Bills-Patriots in Week 4
summary: The Buffalo Bills and New England Patriots renew their rivalry Sunday afternoon in a key Week 4 AFC East showdown. The Bills have an opportunity to improve to 4-0 while handing the Patriots another loss that further harms their chances of repeating as AFC Champions. Everyone knows well by now that the NFL is a […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - DECEMBER 14: Khalil Shakir #10 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball during the second quarter against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and New England Patriots renew their rivalry Sunday afternoon in a key Week 4 AFC East showdown. The Bills have an opportunity to improve to 4-0 while handing the Patriots another loss that further harms their chances of repeating as AFC Champions. Everyone knows well by now that the NFL is a week-to-week league, which means that it’s wise to consider teams 0-0 in a given matchup. Anything can happen, and to overlook New England despite their 1-2 record would be foolish. This is a team fresh off a Super Bowl appearance, after all. Many will recall that New England got off to a similar start last season. Yet the Patriots, as well the Bills, are not the same team from the 2025 campaign. What does all that mean for Sunday? There are quiet a few things that could happen, which include a few of my bold takes below. Josh Allen lays waste to Patriots’ defense Have you ever seen one of Josh Allen’s locked-in games? You know the type — most-often seen during playoff season. That’s what I’m channeling here for his work on Sunday. I don’t know that he’ll have an equal counterpart on the Patriots’ sideline akin to those matchups featuring co-star Patrick Mahomes, but I expect Allen ( and Joe Brady ) will be acutely prepared to make an example of Mike Vrabel’s team. Playing a factor here is his subpar performances in Week 3, but also something else… from last season. There’s no way Allen has forgotten that Drake Maye played in a Super Bowl eight months ago. If anything, that’s likely become a huge source of motivation for Allen. Step one is beating the Patriots in Week 4 (and ideally again in Week 13), then later finishing ahead of them to reclaim the AFC East. The only way the Bills knock off the Patriots is with Allen playing his best football. When all’s said and done, it’s probably going to take a season-long effort to do it. Is there a better player for the role than Allen? As Sean Murphy pointed out in his most recent edition of “5 Bills to Watch vs. the Patriots,” even amid last season’s down campaign, Allen put up 446 passing yards and five touchdown (1 INT) while completing 69% of his passes, and adding 20 rushes for 101 yards in two games versus a great New England defense. Here’s what I see happening on Sunday… He scores at least one touchdown as a rusher. Allen has scored a rushing touchdown in three straight games to begin the 2026 season, and Buffalo may need similar magic from him at the goal line in Week 4. Remember the last time New England came over to Highmark Stadium and Maye ran at-will against Buffalo’s defense? You know who else remembers it? Right. It understandably isn’t bold to say Allen scores more touchdowns, in any capacity. It’s also not all that he’s going to accomplish Sunday afternoon. But, it is a pretty solid bet with FanDuel Sportsbook , where a “2 leg Same Game Parlay” featuring Allen and running back James Cook III as anytime touchdown scorers is at +249 (as of publishing). FanDuel also lists odds featuring Allen seven separate times as part of an “Either Player — First Touchdown Scorer” scenario. A key for Allen will be eliminating turnovers. Buffalo was lucky to escape with a win against the Los Angeles Chargers after Allen turned the ball over three times. New England’s defense is quite a bit better than the Chargers’ group, with the Patriots currently ranked fifth overall in total defense (LAC ranked 23). The Patriots have given up a total of six touchdowns through three games — matchups featuring quarterbacks Sam Darnold, Aaron Rodgers, and Trevor Lawrence. Despite what happened to Allen in Week 3, I see him rising to the challenge New England presents defensively. They’re a thorn in his side now thanks to last season, and I wouldn’t put it past Allen throwing for more yards alone than New England allows total on average (278.4 yards per game). Thanks in large part to Maye’s recent struggles and the Patriots’ injury concerns in the secondary, oddsmakers at FanDuel see Allen as likely to finish with the most passing yards (-136). But how many yards makes for a bold prediction? Allen’s current over/under is set at O/U 242.2 (-114 at FanDuel), and I like him to flirt with over 100 more, as in 350 passing yards. That equates to the second-worst odds at present with FanDuel, where oddsmakers have Allen throwing for 350+ yards at +880. Football revenge is a dish well-complemented by plenty of yards. Allen will also throw for at least two touchdowns, because one thing we all know is that football revenge is best served by touchdowns. Khalil Shakir leads all WRs in Week 4 There was a time not so long ago when Khalil Shakir was Allen’s favorite target. It’s perhaps an era much of Bills Mafia would prefer leaving in the past due to the lack of options beyond Shakir at that point. However, Shakir helps lock Allen in early. This season, Shakir has taken a backseat in terms of primary targets, but he’s been utilized more as a downfield receiver. It’s almost as though Shakir has become a forgotten man in the offense. His production and efficiency rate are down, with him making just eight catches on 15 targets for 94 yards and no touchdowns (per Pro Football Reference ). Last season through three games, Shakir caught 11 passes on 15 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown. He’s not that far off of last season’s pace, but I believe the longer pass plays to him have lowered Shakir’s production against outside defenders. They’ve also eaten into his targets between the down-and-distance markers. To counter the trouble that happened in Week 3, I see Brady looking to get Allen and Shakir on the same page once again. That means some bubble screens and short passes to him in the slot, spaces where Shakir creates YAC thanks to his magical work in space. To keep the Patriots honest on defense, I expect the Bills to utilize Shakir at all levels of the field on Sunday (but hopefully not as a backfield runner in suboptimal situations). The Chargers did well taking the Allen-to-Shakir bread & butter plays away, but look for them to return this weekend. In general, there should also be plenty of opportunity for some deep shots since New England will be without cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder injury), and I see that benefiting Shakir both directly (downfield) and indirectly (classic Shakir plays). Trust me, it’s a bold take. As of publishing, FanDuel has Shakir’s over/under set at O/U 38.5 (-114). That’s a relatively low threshold, representative of his start to the season beginning with a high of 50 yards (Week 1), then 38 yards (Week 2), and just six yards (Week 3). In two games against the Patriots last season, Shakir totaled 11 catches (14 targets) for 110 yards. Could he find his way to that type of production in the latest matchup alone? Consider the options for “Most Receiving Yards” in Bills-Patriots currently with FanDuel Sportsbook , where Shakir has only the fifth-best odds (+700) behind teammates Moore (+320), Kincaid (+360), plus New England wideouts Mack Hollins (+460) and Romeo Doubs (+550). Then remember that Moore is managing an AC-joint sprain, that Kincaid was hurt in some capacity in Week 3, and that the guy throwing footballs for New England looks broken. Shakir helps bring out the best in Allen, and that’s what should happen Sunday with him finishing as the game’s best receiver. Overall, it’s an enticing bet to make for any of the listed players, who all boast plus odds with FanDuel: Greg Rousseau ties or sets new PB for sacks/season in Week 4 In the midst of a Renaissance season, the newly minted AFC Defensive Player of the Month for September has been reinvented under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. I truly love…

summary: Joe Brady spoke to media after the Buffalo Bills finished up their Friday practice. Brady’s statement is a little surprising since the cornerback left last week’s game early, was seen in a […]
full_text: Joe Brady spoke to media after the Buffalo Bills finished up their Friday practice. The first year head coach said that Christian Benford will officially be listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots. Brady’s statement is a little surprising since the cornerback left last week’s game early, was seen in a walking boot after, and hasn’t been seen at a single practice since. Is Brady being coy or is her legitimately hopeful that the only veteran outside corner on the roster will be able to run on Sunday? It’s very likely that the Bills will elevate a DB from the practice squad before tomorrow’s deadline. Buffalo has Te’Cory Couch, Anthony Kendall, and Kani Walker on the practice squad. They also have safety Geno Stone available, but Crouch is the most likely. He was active last week in place of Jordan Hancock who has landed on the Injured Reserve list. Brady also said that Ray Davis will be questionable for Sunday’s game. While it’s possible that we could see Frank Gore, Jr again, that would make his third – and final – elevation. It’s more likely that the Bills just go with two running backs and use Jackson Hawes in the backfield if needed. TJ Sanders also received a designation Friday afternoon (doubtful). The second-year defensive lineman has an emergency appendectomy on September 22. He has been practicing this week, but it seems like at least one more week of work would be reasonable. As for the Patriots, head coach Mike Vrabel said that neither cronerback Christian Gonzalez nor defenisive tackle Christian Barmore will play in Buffalo.

title: Does scoring before the end of the half correlate to winning games?
summary: Earlier this week, I published the results of a study I did regarding the massive NFL-wide philosophical shift in end-of-half aggressiveness, and now I have a follow-up to a question I got in the comments of that article. Thanks for bearing with me presenting all that data in article-form. It was a lot. I appreciate […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs through left guard for a 1-yard touchdown against the Los Angeles Chargers during the second quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier this week, I published the results of a study I did regarding the massive NFL-wide philosophical shift in end-of-half aggressiveness , and now I have a follow-up to a question I got in the comments of that article. Thanks for bearing with me presenting all that data in article-form. It was a lot. I appreciate it. If you haven’t read that piece — in short, teams have gotten drastically more aggressive at the end of the first half over the past 25 years. The shift has been staggering really,. Astute Rumbler PaulieB had this thought after reading: Fantastic questions. In this piece, I will answer the first one. Even when writing the results to that original piece, I thought to myself it wasn’t necessarily groundbreaking work… it was more so clear quantifiable evidence that validated what we’ve all probably felt while watching the NFL over the past quarter century. But the answer I can provide to the initial question from PaulieB actually means something. Here are the results, based on 2001 – 2025 regular-season data: Points scored in final 2:00 of 1st half Win % 0 42.1% 3 54.6% 4-6 61.2% 7 65.6% 8+ 75.8% Teams that outscored their opponent in the final two minutes went on to win 64.5% of the time, which is nearly identical to the close to 66% win rate for simply scoring a touchdown in the final two minutes of the first half. So while it doesn’t necessarily guarantee a victory, the data suggests teams scoring in those critical final two minutes does indeed correlate with a team having stronger likelihood to win. Maybe that’s part of the reason why we’ve seen teams get so much more aggressive in those scenarios. From a Bills perspective, starting in 2020 through Week 3 of the 2026 campaign, the Bills are 39-6 when they outscore their opponent in the final two minutes of the first half. That’s a win percentage of 86.7%. Now, even when they were outscored in the final two minutes of the second quarter, Buffalo has gone on to win 62.5% of the time, but that mostly speaks to the team having the most overall wins in the regular season starting in 2020 than anything else. When they scored the same amount of points right before the half, the Bills win percentage is 64.5%. The standout statistic from that research is the 17.5 percentage-point difference in win % when the Bills put more points on the board than their opponent in the final two minutes before halftime. Hope all this answered your question, PaulieB!

title: 5 New England Patriots to watch at the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Buffalo Bills host a New England Patriots team desperate to avoid a 1-3 start this week, as a loss would give the Bills a three-game lead in the AFC East standings plus a head-to-head tiebreaker. If that situation sounds relatively familiar, it’s because the Bills hosted a Los Angeles Chargers team last week that […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills host a New England Patriots team desperate to avoid a 1-3 start this week, as a loss would give the Bills a three-game lead in the AFC East standings plus a head-to-head tiebreaker. If that situation sounds relatively familiar, it’s because the Bills hosted a Los Angeles Chargers team last week that was desperate to avoid an 0-3 start. Sometimes, there’s nothing more dangerous than playing a desperate opponent. While the Bills were able to pull a rabbit out of their hat last week, overcoming five turnovers on their way to a 24-16 win, they certainly don’t want to rely on that kind of magic again. For Buffalo, Sunday’s game is all about playing to their standard and taking care of the business at hand. The Bills have a chance to put an early-season stamp on the AFC East. Here are five Patriots players we’re watching closely this week in hopes of the Bills shutting them down on their way to victory. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Drake Maye What is going on with New England’s quarterback? After finishing last season as a leading contender for MVP, Maye turned in a middling postseason run. At the risk of being too blunt, so far this season, Maye has been absolutely terrible. He’s completed just 58% of his passes with one touchdown against a league-leading six interceptions. For context, he threw just eight regular-season interceptions on 492 passing attempts last season. Maye has taken nine sacks this season and fumbled twice, as well. He doesn’t look confident, he’s forcing bad throws into coverage, and he’s a large part of why the Patriots offense has scored just 36 points so far this season. He has plenty of talent, so he’s going to turn it around eventually, but the Bills hope that he waits at least one more week before he manages to do that. Maye’s decline from MVP-level to pedestrian began against Buffalo late last season , and he has yet to make an adjustment. Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has the blueprint on how to limit the Patriots’ passing game; now, he has to hope the players can execute the plan. If Maye has another game with multiple interceptions, the Bills will likely have a big day, and it could be a rough morning on Boston-area talk radio. RB TreVeyon Henderson With apologies to Rhamondre Stevenson, who is a solid running back, it’s Henderson who offers the most upside. If he can find space against Buffalo’s run fronts, then it will take pressure off of Maye. Success in the run game leads to manageable downs-and-distances, and it also opens up the play-action pass. For a struggling quarterback, a play-action game is a godsend, allowing for simple, “this-or-that” reads against defenders who are just a step behind. If Buffalo can limit Henderson, who has the speed to score from anywhere on the field and the strength to pick up whatever tough yards are necessary, then Maye has to win the game with his arm. That’s something he hasn’t been able to do this season. The run game can also be limited via game script if Buffalo’s offense can come out and play to its potential, but regardless of how it’s done, they’ll need to make sure that Henderson is contained. The Offensive Line Who the heck is going to start up front for New England? They’re down two guards, at least, in Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten, and they might be without starting right tackle Morgan Moses, as well. Going up against a Buffalo defensive front that has been formidable so far this year, that is not an ideal scenario for an already-struggling offense. Part of limiting Maye and Henderson might come from merely taking advantage of the fact that New England is well below full strength along the offensive line. If Greg Rousseau, Deone Walker, Bradley Chubb, and Ed Oliver—as well as resurgent youngsters like DeWayne Carter and Landon Jackson—can do what they’ve done so far this season, the Bills will have a clear advantage in the trenches. They need to make that advantage felt for 60 minutes. LB Gabe Jacas The rookie edge rusher was a bit of a draft crush of mine, as I thought the former Fightin’ Illini product would be a great fit in Buffalo’s new defensive scheme. However, the Bills went with Clemson’s T.J. Parker in Round Two of the 2026 NFL Draft, while the Patriots took Jacas (pronounced ACK-iss, much to the dismay of my 12-year old son). He’s off to a very good start to his NFL career, totaling 1.5 sacks, 11 tackles, two tackles for loss, four QB hits, and an interception already. He plays on most of New England’s defensive snaps, covering 64% of the defensive snaps thus far. He’s looking like a solid complement to veteran edge rusher Christian Ellis, who has one sack through three games. Second-year man Elijah Ponder has 1.5 sacks, as well. There are a few players to look out for on the edges, but for me, it’s the rookie who I think would have been a good fit with the Bills who I’ll be watching this week. CB Charles Woods If Christian Gonzalez, who is one of the NFL’s best corners, isn’t available on Sunday, it looks like it will be Woods as the next man up. If that’s the case, New England isn’t in terrible shape. Woods has allowed 6-of-9 passes thrown his way to be caught, but he has yet to allow a touchdown and has held those receivers to just 46 yards so far. New England could certainly do worse, and while Woods’ sample size is small, he hasn’t been a complete disaster. It’s a huge blow for New England if Gonzalez is out, however, and the Bills will have to test the backup to see if he can maintain solid play over a longer stretch. Look for the Bills to attack No. 22 if No. 0 is out for the day.

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. the New England Patriots
summary: The Buffalo Bills can take control over the AFC East Division this week with a win over the New England Patriots. If they earn a victory on Sunday, they’ll improve their record to 4-0, while the Patriots will drop to 1-3. Even if the Miami Dolphins manage to beat the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, that […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills can take control over the AFC East Division this week with a win over the New England Patriots. If they earn a victory on Sunday, they’ll improve their record to 4-0, while the Patriots will drop to 1-3. Even if the Miami Dolphins manage to beat the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, that means the best a second-place team can be at the end of Week 4 is 2-2, and that’s only possible if the New York Jets go on the road to beat the Chicago Bears. In short, the AFC East is a mess in the early going, as every team but the Bills is dealing with myriad issues. Buffalo looked like a machine on offense in its first two games, but they took a step back last week while struggling against the Los Angeles Chargers. While they ultimately came out with a win, the Bills are hopeful that they can play a much cleaner game this week. Buffalo has a big opportunity in front of them this week. Here are five players we’re watching who can help them open up a big divisional lead. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Josh Allen After two absolutely dominant performances to open the 2026 NFL season, Allen and Buffalo’s offense were not sharp last Sunday. How does he bounce back from a stinker? That’s what I’ll be watching this week, and I expect that he’ll be just fine. Even in what was theoretically a “down year” for Allen statistically last season, he completed 69% of his passes for 446 yards and five touchdowns against just one interception in both games against the Patriots. He had 20 rushes for 101 yards across the two games, as well. With New England’s top corner, Christian Gonzalez, dealing with a shoulder injury and listed as OUT for Sunday, it could give Allen even more favorable matchups. Top Patriots defensive lineman Christian Barmore hasn’t practiced this week, either, so Buffalo is likely facing a banged-up Patriots defense either way this week. Allen was clearly disappointed in himself after last week’s three-turnover performance, and I think it’s important for him to start hot on Sunday to wash that bad taste out of his mouth. He’s been too good for too long for me to worry about it lingering, but it would be fun to see him go five-for-five for 60 yards and a score on a game-opening drive in what is a big-time divisional matchup. An RB Other Than James Cook III Cook has been electric this season, leading the NFL in yards per carry with an absurd six yards per tote so far. He’s also playing on 71% of Buffalo’s offensive snaps, and he’s totaled 62 touches through three games. That’s a heavy workload for Buffalo’s RB1. While it would of course be nice for him to keep producing at the rate he has, I’d like to see someone step in and provide a capable change-of-pace so that Cook doesn’t burn out early on in the season. Ray Davis has essentially become a kickoff return specialist only, as he has just 20 offensive snaps this season. Ty Johnson logged nearly that many snaps (15) in his Week 3 season debut. Cook is phenomenal, and I’d like the Bills to continue allowing him to, well, cook. However, with his position being one where heavy workloads often lead to injury, it would be nice to see another option emerge. DL Ed Oliver Greg Rousseau has been a menace, totaling six sacks, eight tackles for loss, 12 QB hits, and three forced fumbles through three games. Deone Walker has been incredible, as well, notching 10 tackles and a sack to go with two tackles for loss and four QB hits. Now, if Oliver can start terrorizing opposing offenses the way he’s capable, as well? Look out. Oliver had just one tackle last week, but he notched three quarterback hits on Justin Herbert. That tied Rousseau for the team lead for the week. Oliver has six tackles, one tackle for loss, and four QB hits on the season. Facing off against a banged-up Patriots offensive line, Oliver could do damage on Sunday. If he hits his stride, it’s going to make a formidable Buffalo pass rush that much stronger. Sunday could be a good day for Oliver to lasso a quarterback for the first time this season. LB Dorian Williams Let’s give a little love to the middle level of the defense, too. Dorian Williams leads the Bills in tackles with 24, and he’s been mostly excellent against the run this season. There are still some hiccups in the passing game, but last week as a step in the right direction as it relates to communication in coverage. Granted, the Chargers’ passing offense is well below league average, but New England’s passing attack is ranked just No. 19 this season. The Pats haven’t been nearly as effective in the early going of this season as they were last season, and as a result, I expect that their game plan on Sunday will be to establish the run, control the clock, and try to limit Josh Allen’s time with the football. Another solid day of thumping his run fits from No. 42 can help to torch that game plan quickly. CB Davison Igbinosun With Christian Benford (toe) unlikely to play this week, it’s going to fall on the rookie second-round pick to step up this weekend. After Benford went out of the game last week against the Los Angeles Chargers, Igbinosun did just that, logging six tackles and a pass breakup across 30 snaps on defense. He didn’t look like a rookie at all, and he was impactful in both the passing game and the running game. New England’s offense might be struggling, but they have an excellent offensive game-planner in Josh McDaniels, and a quarterback in Drake Maye who is capable of turning surefire losses into big gains. Igbinosun is going to be tested against either Romeo Doubs or Mack Hollins, but he has the physicality and the mindset to win in all three of those matchups. If he plays like he did in last week’s victory, it will be a big boost for Buffalo.

title: Buffalo Bills are about to have an abundance of defensive line depth
summary: The strength of the Buffalo Bills defense through two games has been its play in the trenches and on the edge, and the team’s frontline is on the verge of becoming incredibly deep. Let’s not take anything away from the inside linebacker group — Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard have played quality football. But Greg […]
full_text: The strength of the Buffalo Bills defense through two games has been its play in the trenches and on the edge, and the team’s frontline is on the verge of becoming incredibly deep. Let’s not take anything away from the inside linebacker group — Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard have played quality football. But Greg Rousseau just won AFC Defensive Player of the Month , Deone Walker has been unblockable in the middle, and DeWayne Carter is emerging as one of the better run-stopping rotational defensive tackles in the NFL, out of nowhere. August acquisition Greg Gaines has filled-in admirably too with 55 snaps through three contests. He only has one pressure yet has made four tackles with two stops and done the dirty work on stunts and when asked to eat double teams against the run. Ed Oliver missed Week 2 against the Lions but has five pressures on 64 pass-rush snaps and made plenty of impact disrupting the Texans backfield in Week 1 that couldn’t be found on the stat sheet. Landon Jackson has been the least-effective of Buffalo’s defensive linemen to date, yet he has seven tackles without a miss on 83 snaps through three games in a mostly non-sexy, two-gapping role. Entering Week 4’s clash with the Patriots, the Bills those five defensive linemen have played between 25% and 67% of Buffalo’s defensive snaps. And now likely adding to that group — 2025 second-round pick T.J. Sanders. Sure, his rookie season was underwhelming, and he dealt with a knee injury. He’s yet to appear in 2026 thanks to another knee ailment and an appendectomy. He went from DNP on Wednesday to limited on Thursday, so he’s trending in the right direction for Sunday. I know there’s essentially zero buzz for Sanders right now. I absolutely still believe in him. He’s super talented. In August, I called him the biggest X-factor on Buffalo’s defense . For a team that, on paper, wants to deploy two or three defensive linemen on any given play, Sanders’ return — along with veteran Phidarian Mathis on the practice squad — makes for significant depth. The edge group isn’t as deep, but Jim Leonhard suddenly has plenty of horses on the interior of his defense that offer a variety of differing skill sets to opposing offensive lines.

title: Bills Week 4 rooting interests: Who Buffalo fans should root for
summary: Three weeks down, and so far our rooting interests have been pretty easy to figure out.  The Buffalo Bills should win. The rest of the AFC East should lose. Teams Buffalo has beaten should win, because strength of victory is our friend. Teams still waiting on the Bills’ schedule can win, too, because strength of schedule may eventually matter.  And, when […]
full_text: Football: Buffalo Bills fans display a sign that reads Lets Go Buffalo vs Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium. Orchard Park, NY 11/2/2025 CREDIT: Erick W. Rasco (Photo by Erick W. Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X164794 TK1) Three weeks down, and so far our rooting interests have been pretty easy to figure out. The Buffalo Bills should win. The rest of the AFC East should lose. Teams Buffalo has beaten should win, because strength of victory is our friend. Teams still waiting on the Bills’ schedule can win, too, because strength of schedule may eventually matter. And, when none of that applies, we can always fall back on one of my favorite rules: Bad AFC teams should win enough games to stay away from the really good draft picks, while bad NFC teams are welcome to lose as often as they would like and collect them instead. But we’re getting close to the point where things change. After this weekend, four games will be in the books. That’s still early, but it’s also roughly a quarter of the regular season. Beginning next week, we’re going to have to start paying a little more attention to the top of the AFC standings. Strength of schedule is nice. Making the road to the No. 1 seed a little less crowded is nicer. For one more week, though, we’ll mostly stick with the rules that got us here. _____________________________________________________________________________- AFC East New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills Root for: Buffalo Bills This one needs no explanation. But the win will mean more than a much more pleasant Monday for Bills Mafia. It’s Buffalo’s first AFC East game of the season. New England is 1-2. Not going to lie – watching the Patriots return to reality has been fun. Let’s remind them who the real “Beast of the East” is. Go Bills! New York Jets at Chicago Bears Root for: Chicago Bears This one checks two boxes. The Jets are the Jets, which means we want them to lose. The Bears are also on Buffalo’s schedule later this season, which means a Chicago win helps the strength-of-schedule side of things. No overthinking required. Miami Dolphins at Minnesota Vikings Root for: Minnesota Vikings Miami loses? Good. A future Buffalo opponent wins? Also good. The Vikings are 3-0, but they’re safely tucked away in the NFC, so their undefeated record isn’t standing between Buffalo and anything we want. Let Minnesota keep winning while Miami keeps doing the opposite. _____________________________________________________________________________ Rest of the AFC Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns Root for: Cleveland Browns This is a weird place to start because the entire AFC North is 2-1. There isn’t a bottom-feeder available for us to adopt, and there isn’t a clear division leader for us to knock down. So, we’ll take Cleveland. If the Browns eventually turn into a legitimate AFC threat, we’ll adjust. For now, putting another loss on Pittsburgh works just fine, and we don’t have a strength-of-schedule reason to prefer either one. Indianapolis Colts at Washington Commanders Root for: Washington Commanders Here’s an easy one. Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule, and Indianapolis is in the AFC. Give the AFC team another loss and let Washington take the win. It doesn’t do much for Buffalo, but not every game has to. Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans Root for: Houston Texans Houston is 0-3, which isn’t exactly helping Buffalo’s strength of victory after the Bills beat the Texans in Week 1. A Texans win gives Buffalo’s strength of victory a boost and gets Houston away from the bottom of the standings and, eventually, the very top of the draft. That’s two reasons to temporarily become Texans fans. So, come on, Houston. Do something useful. Tennessee Titans at Baltimore Ravens Root for: Baltimore Ravens Enjoy this one, because I suspect this answer might be different pretty soon.Baltimore is on Buffalo’s schedule and Tennessee isn’t, so under our early-season rules, we’re rooting for the Ravens and the strength-of-schedule bump. But Baltimore is already 2-1 and very much part of the AFC conversation. Once we get through this week, teams hanging around the top of the conference aren’t going to keep getting our support just because Buffalo plays them eventually. Jacksonville Jaguars at Cincinnati Bengals Root for: Cincinnati Bengals There isn’t much direct Buffalo benefit available here. Both teams are 2-1, neither is on Buffalo’s schedule, and they’re both in the AFC. So, this is mostly a pick-your-poison game. Jacksonville currently leads the AFC South, while Cincinnati is stuck in that ridiculous four-way 2-1 tie in the AFC North. We’ll take Cincinnati and put a loss on a division leader. We’re getting close enough to the point where that starts mattering. Kansas City Chiefs at Las Vegas Raiders Root for: Las Vegas Raiders And here is where our rules collide headfirst. Kansas City is 3-0. Las Vegas is 3-0. Both are sitting right beside Buffalo at the top of the AFC, and the Raiders are also on Buffalo’s schedule in Week 6 – a full six weeks before the Bills can handle their own business with the Chiefs. So we’re taking Las Vegas and handing Kansas City its first loss. Los Angeles Chargers at Seattle Seahawks Root for: Los Angeles Chargers Please win a football game, Chargers. Buffalo just beat Los Angeles, but that put the Chargers at 0-3. That’s not particularly helpful for the strength-of-victory column. A Chargers win gives that number a boost and, as a bonus, moves an AFC team away from the premium draft picks. Seattle can take the loss and move a little closer to them instead. This is exactly what our weird little rule system was built for. Denver Broncos at San Francisco 49ers Root for: Denver Broncos This one is mostly about strength of schedule. Denver is a future Buffalo opponent, so every Broncos win makes the Bills’ schedule a little stronger. They’re 2-1, which is worth keeping an eye on in the AFC, but we’re not quite ready to start rooting against every AFC team with a winning record. Plus, a Denver win coupled with our hopeful Kansas City loss keeps the AFC West crowded at the top. Let them spend all their time and energy fighting with each other. Maybe by the time they remember Buffalo is over here, they won’t have much fight left for us. _____________________________________________________________________________ NFC Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants Root for: Arizona Cardinals Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule, so we’re heading to the draft-pick portion of the program. The Giants are 2-1. Arizona is 1-2. Let the Cardinals get back toward the middle while the Giants take the loss. We’re not trying to hand premium draft capital to NFC teams that don’t need our help getting better. Los Angeles Rams at Philadelphia Eagles Root for: Los Angeles Rams Meet next week’s opponent. Buffalo heads to Los Angeles in Week 5, so we’d like the Rams to look a little better before the Bills get there. A Rams win improves Buffalo’s strength of schedule now and could become a strength-of-victory boost later if Buffalo handles its own business. Besides, at 1-2, Los Angeles could use the help. Green Bay Packers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers Root for: Green Bay Packers The Packers are on Buffalo’s schedule. The Buccaneers aren’t. That’s enough for now. Green Bay doesn’t show up until December but wins count the same whether we collect them for the strength-of-schedule pile before or after we meet. Detroit Lions at Carolina Panthers Root for: Detroit Lions Buffalo already beat Detroit, so we know the drill. Every Lions win from here makes that Week 2 victory look a little better. Carolina doesn’t appear on Buffalo’s schedule and can happily absorb the loss. Strength of victory wins this one. Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints Root for: Whoever you want We’ve found it. The game where I can’t come up with a particularly convincing reason to care. Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule. Both are in the NFC. Both are 1-2. If we’re…

title: 5 Questions with Pride of Detroit
summary: Week 4 of the young 2026 NFL season already has the Carolina Panthers and Detroit Lions trending in different directions. The Lions are playoff contenders and quiet Super Bowl hopefuls. Your 2025 NFC South champions, on the other hand, are just hoping that there are fewer injuries in the 13 weeks after their Week 5 […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - SEPTEMBER 27: Carolina Panthers wide receiver John Metchie III (13) celebrates with Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (4) and Carolina Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble (82) after scoring on a 8-yard touchdown pass during the fourth quarter of the National Football League game between the Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns on September 27, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Week 4 of the young 2026 NFL season already has the Carolina Panthers and Detroit Lions trending in different directions. The Lions are playoff contenders and quiet Super Bowl hopefuls. Your 2025 NFC South champions, on the other hand, are just hoping that there are fewer injuries in the 13 weeks after their Week 5 bye than there were in the four weeks prior to it. That doesn’t mean that Lions fans are taking this week for granted or that the Lions themselves haven’t struggled with their more fair share of inuries. Ryan Matthews from Pride of Detroit answered five of my questions about the Lions to try to give us their side of this story. These answers were the sober, attentive reflections of a fan whose team has only very recently known success, at least relative to their history. In short, they did not fill me with confidence and optimism in the Panthers chances of catching Detroit in the midst of a cat nap. The Carolina Panthers are quite literally half the team they expected to be when they started training camp. How are the Lions faring with the injury bug this deep into the 2026 season? The Lions’ 2026 roster has bites going back to 2025 that have really put them in a bind on the backend of their defense. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch, once considered to be the top safety duo in the NFL, suffered season-ending injuries last season, and they’re still on the PUP heading into this Week 4 matchup. Detroit’s secondary has been lit up three straight weeks in a row, and while the cornerbacks haven’t been playing their best ball, missing both Joseph and Branch in their respective safety positions has made for some tough viewing when the Lions defense takes the field. Avonte Maddox, a veteran defensive back, was re-signed to compete for a spot in Detroit’s secondary. He earned it in the summer. Maddox played some free safety, box safety, and in the slot as a nickelback to start the season, but he suffered an injury in Week 2 that put him on injured reserve for the foreseeable future. Thomas Harper is another player who played his way into a spot in the secondary, but he, too, suffered an ankle injury in Week 2’s game against Buffalo that put him on IR as well. That leaves Chuck Clark, a veteran on his fourth stop in as many seasons, to hold down the single-high safety looks for the most part, and safeties coach Jim O’Neil trusts him in that role. Alongside him is Christian Izien, a player who looked like he was shot out of a cannon in his season debut last week against the Jets. Izien had a groin injury crop up at the end of training camp, but he’s a guy who many expected to play the Branch role: box safety, in the slot, up near the line of scrimmage. Izien led the Lions in tackles (11) and finished second in defensive stops (4) against the Jets in Week 3. Unfortunately—or fortunately depending on how you’re looking at it—Panthers fans won’t get to see the return of Cade Mays this weekend in Carolina after he had a freak wrist injury near the beginning of camp. Otherwise, the Lions have been pretty fortunate with injuries! The Lions are already on their second offensive coordinator since Ben Johnson left for the Chicago Bears. What are your hopes and worries three games into the Drew Petzing era? For all the “Dan Campbell is a Ben Johnson merchant” and “Detroit sure misses Ben Johnson” talk, Drew Petzing’s offense has hung 31 points in three consecutive weeks. After a bit of a slow start in terms of opening drives and third-down efficiency, the early returns on Petzing are pretty promising. Jared Goff looks comfortable in the offense, getting into favorable checks and commanding the group. The offensive line dealt with some injuries in the first couple of weeks to their starting left guard—Christian Mahogany—and starting right tackle—rookie Blake Miller—but they looked like a really solid and steady unit when they returned in Week 3. Some mild concerns for me, and they’re admittedly a bit nitpicky, are play calls near the goal line. Last week, nearing the end of the half and the Jets with just one timeout remaining, Detroit called a designed rollout for Goff on first down that he effectively threw away and a fade route to Amon-Ra St. Brown that did result in a touchdown. It left the Jets with 1:36 on the clock and a timeout still at their disposal, but would’ve liked to see the Lions get to their bread and butter by running the football, forcing the Jets to burn their timeout, and playing with their aggressive, four-down approach on offense. Which seems to run counterintuitive to my second nitpick about the offense: the number of run plays on second-and-10. Petzing’s explanation referred back to Detroit’s four-down approach on offense, but against the Bills, it felt like Buffalo knew it was coming, but Detroit still stuck with it, leaving them in plenty of third-and-long situations. Again, early results are trending in a positive way, those concerns are mild at most, but the Lions feel like they’re in a much better spot on offense than they were a season ago. What’s with barely beating the Saints and the Jets? I thought y’all were supposed to be a good team. Is the suggestion here that the Saints and Jets aren’t good football teams? Because New Orleans went into Baltimore and took home a victory, and then they nearly pulled out last week’s game against a 3-0 Las Vegas Raiders team. The Jets are some clock mismanagement away from being a 2-1 football team themselves, so I think Detroit has actually played some pretty tough teams that will challenge for the playoffs in their respective conferences. A rain game where one team is looking to establish a struggling rushing attack against another team that surrendered almost 300 yards in their last home game doesn’t sound like a good time. Any chance Jahmyr Gibbs is on vacation or enough of a Wizard of Oz style witch where he isn’t allowed to get wet? Jahmyr Gibbs figures to be available come rain, sleet, snow, or such poor field conditions that the NFLPA has to file a grievance . You’re going to predict a Lions win, there’s no doubt or shame in that. The interesting question is how big of a win do you think the Lions will have and does that differ from the expectations of the broader Lions fanbase? There’s no way Dan Campbell will have this Lions team overlooking this Panthers team, and I’m not going to either. Their passing attack is explosive, their run defense against running backs has actually been pretty solid the past two weeks, and they’re likely getting Devin Lloyd back for this one. While this one could very well become a shootout—weather permitting—it should be a more tightly contested game. It wouldn’t surprise me if the Lions win by less than one score, and it wouldn’t shock me if the Panthers pull off the upset as home underdogs coming off a disappointing loss in Week 3.

title: Panthers Reacts: Such early despair for a Week 4 fan poll
summary: Fans of the Carolina Panthers were riding high after embarrassing the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3. It rarely takes long in this league to be humbled, however. Week 4 against the Browns turned into a preseason game by the fourth quarter for Carolina, while Cleveland rode their relative health and more conservative coaching to an […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 27: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers attempts a pass against the Cleveland Browns during the second quarter at Huntington Bank Field on September 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fans of the Carolina Panthers were riding high after embarrassing the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3. It rarely takes long in this league to be humbled, however. Week 4 against the Browns turned into a preseason game by the fourth quarter for Carolina, while Cleveland rode their relative health and more conservative coaching to an uneasy victory. Should Panthers fans be optimistic that they nearly beat an NFL team while missing so much talent? Maybe. Are they? Assuredly not. Bryce Young looked like vintage 2024 at times (though he ultimately played better than that lowly standard). The offensive line looked like a group of rookies playing together for the first time. The defense seemed like they got more injured with each passing drive. Asking them to cover or contain a mobile quarterback seemed like secondary goals to getting off the field under their own power The fact of the matter is that fan confidence rides wins and losses like a wave. The trough is bigger the better the won or worse the loss. Sunday’s loss, while understandable from one point of view, just felt bad. A loss to the Detroit Lions is expected. I wouldn’t expect another 30+% dip unless Bryce Young throws an interception so horrendous that he, Terairoa McMillan, and Derrick Brown all somehow land on IR just from that one attempt. Conversely, an upset win vould buoy spirits like little else. We’ll have to wait and see what happens. Checkout FanDuel , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation.

title: Panthers Injury Report & Transactions – Week 4
summary: The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries While the injuries to cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, both of whom have been moved to injured reserve, don’t appear on this week’s formal injury report, there are […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 24: Saahdiq Charles #77 of the Washington Commanders takes the field prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at FedExField on September 24, 2023 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries While the injuries to cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, both of whom have been moved to injured reserve, don’t appear on this week’s formal injury report, there are a lot of banged-up Panthers this week. While the Friday injury report hasn’t been released today with game statuses for each player, here are the key players to monitor: Jalen Coker, WR – Did not practice Wednesday and was limited on Thursday with a quad issue. Xavier Legette, WR – Missed practice on both Wednesday and Thursday due to his knee. Damien Lewis, OG – Sat out practice on Wednesday and Thursday with an elbow injury. Monroe Freeling, OT – Missed Wednesday’s practice with a concussion, but was a limited participant on Thursday. Lee Hunter, DT – The Panthers second round rookie popped up as a limited participant in Thursday’s practice. Transactions With all of the injuries, the Panthers were busy this week with signings, releases, and a host of changes to the practice squad. Here’s what you need to know about the most noteworthy transactions from the last week: Placed CBs Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson on injured reserve. This is about as big of a blow as the Panthers could endure. Hopefully both of them get healthy and can return later this year, but Carolina’s secondary is going to be stretched extremely thin in the interim. Waived LB Claudin Cherelus with an injury settlement. The Panthers waived Cherelus during his fourth season with the team after suffering a shoulder injury earlier in the season. He appeared in 35 games for the Panthers with 61 tackles between playing both defense and special teams. Signed G Torricelli Simpkins to the active roster from the practice squad. Simpkins played the 2024 college season for South Carolina before signing last year as a free agent with the New Orleans Saints. He appeared in 15 games with two starts for the Saints last year, playing 179 offensive snaps. He was released after the 2025 season, signed with the Panthers practice squad in September, and is now on the active roster. Signed G Saahdiq Charles to the practice squad. Charles was a fourth round pick back in 2020 by Washington where he appeared in 35 games and played nearly 1,200 offensive snaps. After briefly retiring in 2024, he signed with Carolina last year and in two games played 10 special teams snaps. Carolina signed him to a reserve/future contract in January 2026, waived him with an injury settlement in August, and have now re-signed him to the practice squad. Signed CB Robert Rochell to the practice squad. To help deal with the injuries to cornerbacks, the Panthers added veteran Robert Rochell to the practice squad. The 2021 fourth round pick has appeared in 54 career games with 30 tackles, playing primarily special teams. He appeared in four games for the Panthers in 2025, playing 33 special teams snaps. Signed OLB Cam Gill to the practice squad. Gill entered the league in 2020 and has appeared in 50 games with 51 tackles and 2.5 sacks. He played for the Panthers in 2024, recording 22 tackles over 10 games. Signed OL Isaia Glass to the practice squad. The undrafted rookie from Arizona State, Oklahoma State, and Vanderbilt spent the preseason with the Panthers, got waived at roster cuts, and has bounced around Carolina’s practice squad all year. He has yet to appear in a game. Additional transactions: Waived LB Maema Njongmeta Released G Chandler Zavala from the practice squad
