title: Brian Answers: Injuries, play call balance, practice squad rules, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re coming off a rough Sunday, but its a new week, the Panthers are playing in prime time, and they have a ton of injuries to figure out. Let’s dive in to all your questions! Brazilian Panther: Okay Brian, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - AUGUST 28: Corey Thornton #31 of the Carolina Panthers reacts during the first half of a preseason game against the Houston Texans at Bank of America Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re coming off a rough Sunday, but its a new week, the Panthers are playing in prime time, and they have a ton of injuries to figure out. Let’s dive in to all your questions! Brazilian Panther: Okay Brian, with almost a month of football so far, tell us two players on the Panthers that disappointed you the most so far and two others that surprised you on the positive side of things. I find it hard to get into early grades on players only 3 games in, but I will give it a try. I’ve been most surprised by Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller at the tight end position. This position was considered to be a need all throughout the off-season, but these two have been showing out so far as reliable pass catching targets which I really did not expect going into the season. Obviously Waller has shown more touchdown production, but they both have carved out reliable roles in the passing game in a tight end room that I think many considered one of the worst in the NFL on paper. As far as disappointments, I think its hard not to point to Derrick Brown as one of them. I think he’ll find his way once again, but he’s definitely played below expectation in these first 3 games. I’d also say Robert Hunt at right guard, for the money they are paying him he hasn’t been a top tier guard so far. Brice Guild: We have had to call on a lot of depth players already this season. Give me your take on the the performance and quality of play we have seen from them. Lee Hunter is certainly playing well enough to justify having a 4th round pick play significant snaps at corner. I would also give Zakee Wheatley props as he’s been graded pretty highly at safety. I mentioned the tight ends already so I won’t rehash that, but on offense Brycen Tremayne is still continuing to show he can play as a wide receiver when called upon. Coach_K: which cornerback are you looking forward to step up or perhaps sign? I don’t know if Carolina will sign a cornerback in the next couple of days, I think they just end up sticking with what they have. This is a great opportunity for Corey Thornton to step up from the practice squad after playing some really meaningful snaps as a UDFA last season before being knocked out due to injury. I think he makes a lot of sense to take some snaps when they need to pull Will Lee off the field or rotate at the nickel position. Thornton showed he can play wherever they need him to, and Sunday would really allow him to build on his rookie season. DBelt: What have you noticed about the difference in the offense with Brad Idzik calling plays, for better or worse? The aggression on offense is definitely up a notch from last season. I like them taking more deep shots down the field, but it really shot them in the foot going for it on 4th down against the Browns and trying to get intermediate completions instead of just getting the sticks. We’ll see if they can level it out, but I do enjoy the idea behind the aggression. CasualFanAlso: What impact, if any, has the performance of the OL had on the timeline for the return of Moton and Ekwonu? I know the team will want to be “cautious”. I don’t expect them to move the timelines up at all, as sad as that may be to read. Taylor Moton’s blood clots aren’t something you can rush and Ikem Ekwonu is still going to be lucky if he plays at all this season. Both will return when it makes sense. schrodingersblackcat: You’re Brad Idzik. How do you address the offense’s struggling ground game? How do you distribute the workload between Chuba and Dillon and whoever else we have in the backfield? What is an acceptable YPC? How do you improve the O Line’s ability to establish a credible run threat early in the game? I don’t really know to be honest. They might be missing their starting left guard and right tackle this week, so that’s already going to be a handicap. My best guess is one cut rushes that don’t take long to develop, and have the back just hit the hole fast. Maybe mix in some presnap motion to get the linebackers moving prior to the snap. More RPOs could also work as an extension of the run game since Bryce Young is so comfortable with those. carolinajerry: Brain, Panthers Nation is panicking. Fans are spiraling. Please instill some good ol’ Panthers optimistic delusion into us and save our sanity. Will we be ok? The optimist in me says that the Panthers probably should have won that football game on Sunday, they just missed some easy turnovers and made mental mistakes, combined with some questionable 4th down decisions in a game where defense was ruling. These are all correctable mistakes, and they aren’t facing a mobile quartertback this week which ultimately cost them a lot of points on defense in weeks 1 and 3. There’s actually a strong chance they can rebound against the Lions if they clean up their own mistakes and force Detroit into a few of their own. And being 2-2 going into a much needed bye week wouldn’t be a bad position to be in at all. Dcangio09: What happened to Derrick Browns strength, anchor and power. I haven’t seen him get repeatedly blown off the line this consistently since his 1st couple years. This is one of those few questions where I don’t really know what to say. Its been quite concerning how much of a drop off we’ve seen, both on the field and as far as dumb penalties and mental mistakes. I’m sure the offenses have schemed around him because he’s one of the best in the game, maybe they will play Cam Jackson more to try and take some of those double teams off of him. DannyLimes: How surprised will you be on a scale of 1 to 43.25 (where 1 is not surprised and 43.25 is a surprised as you could possibly be about something) when we beat the Detroit Lions? What is the main reason for this surprise or lack there of? I actually wouldn’t be all that surprised if the Panthers pulled out a win, so maybe a 28? The Panthers actually match up fairly well against the Lions offensively, if they can control the pass rush a bit. Defensively, the biggest killer for them has been quarterbacks escaping the pocket and extending plays and I don’t see that happening with Jared Goff. This could be a game where Ejiro Evero breaks out some new looks to throw off the offensive gameplan with new personnel due to injury. And its at home. Being unpredictable could really work to their benefit. celticgreen86: With Damien Lewis not out a few weeks, what changes do you anticipate to the OL which will now lose its best player to date? The Panthers clearly liked Corey Bullock quite a bit when they claimed him on waivers during roster cutdowns. So I think he’s just going to step right in and play, which will be interesting to watch. What they do at tackle should Monroe Freeling be unable to play might be more interesting. sgtx: What questions should we be asking that we haven’t ? I miss the food questions. Aggressively_avg2: Based off games played, and the fact we literally could have had Pat Surtain, Jaycee Horn has to go down as a bust, right? Nope. Jaycee Horn has been one of the best at his position, and these same injuries could have befallen Surtain if he were put in the same position. Horn didn’t enter the league with injury concerns. Players getting hurt just happens. Chef: Hey, Brian! Lots and lots of doom and gloom after the Browns debacle. Give me something that no one is talking about that should age well as the season progresses. Position groups, individual players, coaches, ect are all on the table. I need some silver linings, thanks. The Panthers special teams unit is one of the best in the league, and that’s building on what the unit did last season.…

title: Panthers vs Lions: Matchups to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers are very, very banged up. Fortunately, they have an early bye, and this is one of the few times where they’ll probably be happy to see it. But before they get there, they have to host the Detroit Lions in front of a national audience on Sunday Night Football. These kinds of […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - DECEMBER 24: Shaq Thompson #7 of the Carolina Panthers tackles Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions during the fourth quarter of the game at Bank of America Stadium on December 24, 2022 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are very, very banged up. Fortunately, they have an early bye, and this is one of the few times where they’ll probably be happy to see it. But before they get there, they have to host the Detroit Lions in front of a national audience on Sunday Night Football. These kinds of games are always scary given some of the eggs we’ve seen laid by Panthers in this spot, and it’s even scarier given the team’s health. Let’s dive into the key matchups that the Panthers need to win or at least be competitive to give themselves a chance to improve to 2-2. Will Lee and Akayleb Evans vs. Amon-Ra St. Brown Everyone who keeps up with the Panthers knows we have to start here. Amon-Ra St. Brown is one of the best wide receivers in the NFL, and the Panthers aren’t going to have their star cornerback duo to try to stop him. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are both out for the next several weeks at least, leaving rookie Will Lee and Akayleb Evans to handle him outsid. Chau Smith-Wade will have to give it his best shot in the slot, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Lions put St. Brown out wide more to test the Panthers’ corner depth. Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke can muddy up some throwing lanes in the middle to help when St. Brown works in that area, but I don’t know if the outside corners are going to stand a chance if left out on an island. Monroe Freeling or Stone Forsythe vs. Aidan Hutchinson Rookie tackle Monroe Freeling is currently in the concussion protocol, so his status for Sunday’s game is very much up in the air. If he can’t go, Stone Forsythe is poised to fill in. In either case, the Panthers will be at a severe disadvantage against superstar edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson. The offensive line struggled against the Browns, and Hutchinson is arguably better than anyone on that Browns front. He already has 3.5 sacks this season and is liable to wreck the Panthers’ offensive game plan. They badly need whoever suits up at right tackle to at least put up a fight against Hutchinson. Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke vs. Jahmyr Gibbs Jahmyr Gibbs is one of the best players in the NFL regardless of position, so the Lions have elected to build most of their offense out of Gibbs. He’s averaging over 27 touches per game so far this season and converting those into 154.3 yards from scrimmage per game and six total touchdowns. He’s explosive if he gets out into space, and over a third of his carries and over half of his catches go for first downs. The Panthers linebacker duo is going to have their hands full getting Gibbs to the ground and keeping him from generating explosive plays, especially if the weather limits the Lions’ downfield passing game. Football players vs. the rain Current forecasts say it’s going to be cool and very wet on Sunday night. This game is widely expected to be a shootout, but the rain might put a significant damper on that. We’ll see what happens when two good offenses and two depleted defenses go against one another in a game where the weather is playing most of the defense.
author: Jonathan DeLong

title: Panthers vs Lions: Round table predictions, odds, and what’s left of Carolina’s two-deep.
summary: Let’s take a look at where I started this prediction piece last week: Things seem to be looking up for the Carolina Panthers and quarterback Bryce Young. One dominant defensive performance and two excellent offensives ones have given us more good football to start a season than we have seen in years. Welp. Nothing feels […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Devin Lloyd #55 and Jean Phillips #5 of the Carolina Panthers react to a sack during an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s take a look at where I started this prediction piece last week : Things seem to be looking up for the Carolina Panthers and quarterback Bryce Young. One dominant defensive performance and two excellent offensives ones have given us more good football to start a season than we have seen in years. Welp. Nothing feels like it is trending upward after how thoroughly the Panthers fell apart against the Cleveland Browns. Yeah, Bryce Young didn’t play amazing football and had more than a few plays that failed the eye test he was otherwise acing this season. Yeah, Ejiro Evero’s defense couldn’t get a stop at the end of the game. Those are both valid complaints. The early aggressiveness on fourth down and the inability to establish a consistent running game are what cost us that game more so than anything else that was under the Panthers control. The real story, however, continues to be the injuries that the Panthers have suffered. I’m still wary of Young’s future, but I can’t really judge anything when the team can barely field half of the starters they entered the offseason with. This week’s injury news started rough and has only gotten moreso with the release of the injury reports. To put it all in perspective, Pride of Detroit asked us five questions this week and four were related to the Panthers injuries. title: Chicago Bears Week 4 Flashbacks: Bengals Blowout, Hester sets a record, and more!
summary: It’s week 4, a week that has seen many a classic Bears games! Luckily we have some hallmark games from the past to uncover today. Climb aboard Gridiron Time Machine for a trip down memory lane! 1.) 1986, Bears @ Bengals: Chicago overwhelms Cincinnati in a 44-7 rout Coming off one of the most dominant […]
full_text: Chicago Bears wide receiver Devin Hester (23) runs back a kick-off return in the second quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois, Sunday, October 2, 2011. The Bears defeated the Panthers 34-29. (Jose M. Osorio/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) It’s week 4, a week that has seen many a classic Bears games! Luckily we have some hallmark games from the past to uncover today. Climb aboard Gridiron Time Machine for a trip down memory lane! 1.) 1986, Bears @ Bengals: Chicago overwhelms Cincinnati in a 44-7 rout Coming off one of the most dominant seasons in NFL history, the 1986 Bears entered Week 4 looking every bit like a team capable of doing it all over again. The unfortunate team standing in their way was the Cincinnati Bengals. Chicago jumped out to a 21-0 first-quarter lead behind a banged up Jim McMahon rushing touchdown and touchdown passes to Walter Payton and Willie Gault. McMahon would add another touchdown pass to Emery Moorehead in the second half, finishing with 211 yards and three scores through the air. Gault was the star through the air, hauling in 174 receiving yards, while the Bears piled up 476 yards of total offense and 222 yards on the ground. The defense was not exactly taking the afternoon off either. Chicago intercepted Boomer Esiason four times and forced five turnovers overall, holding Cincinnati to seven points in a 44-7 blowout. The win moved the defending champions to 4-0, continuing a start in which it looked like the rest of the NFL might once again be playing for second place. That eventually changed, but on this afternoon the Bears looked every bit as terrifying as the team that had just steamrolled its way through 1985. 2.) 2011, Bears vs. Panthers: Forte runs wild and Hester makes history The Bears entered Week 4 at 1-2 and badly needed a win after dropping back-to-back games to the Saints and Packers. Matt Forte and Devin Hester made sure they got one. Forte gashed Carolina from the start, including a 46-yard run on Chicago’s opening possession and a 17-yard touchdown in the second quarter. He would finish with a career-high 205 rushing yards while adding another 23 through the air, accounting for 228 of Chicago’s 317 total yards. Then there was Hester. With Chicago leading 17-10, Hester fielded a punt and raced 69 yards for a touchdown, giving the Bears a 24-10 advantage. It was the 11th punt return touchdown of his career, setting a new NFL record. The defense chipped in as well, with D.J. Moore returning a Cam Newton interception 20 yards for a touchdown in the first quarter (no not THAT D.J. Moore, but it is pretty interesting that Cam Newton has thrown touchdown passes to multiple people named “D.J. Moore). Carolina still piled up a franchise-record 543 yards of offense, but the Bears found enough big plays on defense and special teams to stay in front. Forte helped put the game away with a 40-yard run late in the fourth quarter, and Chicago escaped Soldier Field with a 34-29 victory. It was about as Bears of a victory as you could draw up. Run the football, steal a score on defense, then let Devin Hester do Devin Hester things. 3.) 2018, Bears vs. Buccaneers: Trubisky trounces the Bucs for 6 touchdowns There might not be another game that better sums up the highs of the Mitchell Trubisky era. Through the first three games of the 2018 season, Trubisky had thrown just two touchdowns, and questions were already starting to build about whether Matt Nagy’s new offense was actually going to unlock the second-year quarterback. Then Tampa Bay came to Soldier Field. Trubisky absolutely torched the Buccaneers. He threw five touchdown passes in the first half alone, becoming the first quarterback in Bears history to accomplish that feat. By the time his afternoon was over, Trubisky had completed 19-of-26 passes for 354 yards, six touchdowns and a 154.6 passer rating. Those six touchdowns went to five different receivers, with Tarik Cohen adding 121 receiving yards as the Bears built an absurd 38-3 halftime lead. Never forget when Mitchell Trubisky threw for 6 Touchdowns 🔥 https://t.co/94cvRmzhjG pic.twitter.com/LztG0LzjLg — Bears on Real (@BearsOnReal) May 17, 2025 The defense joined in on the fun against a Tampa Bay offense that entered the week leading the NFL in both total and passing yards. Khalil Mack recorded his fourth straight game with a strip-sack, while Chicago forced three turnovers and sacked Buccaneers quarterbacks four times. Chicago cruised to a 48-10 win, with Trubisky’s six touchdown passes finishing just one shy of Sid Luckman’s franchise record of seven set in 1943. The win moved the Bears to 3-1 heading into their bye week and gave us the first real glimpse of what Nagy’s offense could look like when everything clicked. Unfortunately, six-touchdown games never became the norm. But for one afternoon at Soldier Field, Mitchell Trubisky looked completely unstoppable. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

summary: Well, I think we can officially call it a slump. Despite the Bears scoring 27 points last week, the props improved from the 0-3 collapse in week 2, but 1-2 isn’t exactly something to get excited about. That puts our yearly record at 3-6. As we close in on this week’s game, there are still […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Cole Kmet #85 of the Chicago Bears reacts during the third quarter of the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, I think we can officially call it a slump. Despite the Bears scoring 27 points last week, the props improved from the 0-3 collapse in week 2, but 1-2 isn’t exactly something to get excited about. That puts our yearly record at 3-6. As we close in on this week’s game, there are still questions abounding, like who is playing quarterback for the Bears? Despite questions, we march forward with what we hope are answers. Is it time to fade me? Up to you, but here are three props I like for this week’s Jets-Bears matchup at Soldier Field. As always, odds courtesy of FanDuel. Cole Kmet OVER 9.5 Receiving Yards, -114 I am expecting Tyson Bagent to start this game for the Chicago Bears. If that’s accurate, there’s one thing I remember from when Bagent started back in 2023: he looked for Cole Kmet. Kmet had some of his best games as a Bear when Bagent started. I’m not saying I think Bagent is necessarily going to spam Kmet for 10 targets, but when you haven’t played much of any QB with this group of players, looking for an old reliable makes a lot of sense. I think Bagent looks for and connects with Kmet for a handful of catches, and we see this one go over at some point in the first half. Also, at the time of this article, there were no D’Andre Swift props due to his injury; he will almost certainly play, and the props should arise this weekend. I think Swift over receiving yards is another good play. Bagent frequently looks for RBs as well. Braelon Allen OVER 56.5 Rushing Yards, -114 Picking some props this week is a little tough. We have no Swift props. No Bears QB props, so we are doing the best we can! I think we can admit that the Bears’ run defense isn’t great. They gave up 175 yards to the Chubba Hubbard, Jonathan Brooks, AJ Dillon trio. They gave up over 100 rushing yards to Aaron Jones, and they gave up 80 first-half yards to Saquon Barkley before the defense clamped down in the second half. If you think the Bears have figured out stopping the run based on the second half of Monday Night Football, look elsewhere, but I think they are still vulnerable in the running game. Breece Hall is out, and that means Allen should receive the lion’s share of the load here. I think he sees at least 15 touches and lands over 70 yards rushing. Luther Burden OVER 46.5 Receiving Yards, -114 As I try to think of how Ben Johnson is going to attack this defense with Bagent, you have to figure it’ll be similar to Keenum in that Bagent doesn’t exactly have a cannon, so short passes will be the way to go. That means targets for Kmet and Swift, but I also think it’ll mean targets for Burden to catch short passes in situations where Johnson sets him up to go for some serious YAC. I think Burden will see the most targets on the Bears this week, and I think he will break a couple of decent chunk gains and get his yardage total comfortably over 50.

full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: Chicago Bears offensive tackle Braxton Jones (70) walks off the field at halftime during the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chicago Bears and New York Jets meet on Sunday in the Windy City, and both teams will be without key contributors. No surprise that Caleb Williams will miss his second consecutive game with his hamstring injury, but head coach Ben Johnson did not name a starting quarterback. “I don’t necessarily know there is a right answer or a wrong answer,” Johnson said about starting either Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum. He said the coaching staff has been split on the decision. Johnson added about his two backup quarterbacks, “I know both of them are well prepared to play and win a game for us” Starting left tackle Braxton Jones is out with the knee injury he suffered Monday night, and Johnson said Theo Benedet would get the start. Ozzy Trapilo had another full week of practice, but Johnson said he’s not quite game-ready for extended action, though he is close. Also technically ruled out for the Bears are three players in their 21-day practice window from the PUP list: defensive tackle Shemar Turner (knee), linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles), and nickel Kyler Gordon (calf). None are eligible to be activated until Week 5, but all three practiced in full today. The only other player on Chicago’s injury report is defensive back Cam Lewis, who is doubtful with a hip injury. He was limited earlier in the week, but did not practice today. The Jets are a bit more banged up, with starters Breece Hall (RB), Adonai Mitchell (WR), Dylan Parham (LG), and Mason Taylor (TE) ruled out, along with backup linebacker Kiko Mauigoa. New York lists EDGE Kingsley Enagbare (knee) and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq (back) as questionable, and both were limited at today’s practice. The Jets will have veteran Pro Bowl safety Minkah Fitzpatrick return after missing the last two games.

title: Jets at Bears Q&A: A battle of former Lions Coordinators
summary: The Chicago Bears look to improve their record to 3-1 this week as they welcome the New York Jets to Soldier Field. The Jets are sitting at 1-2 but have been close in every game and appear like they might be close to turning the corner. Ben Johnson and Aaron Glenn roamed the Detroit Lions’ […]
full_text: Detroit Lions coordinators Aaron Glenn, left, and Ben Johnson, right, landed NFL head coaching jobs in the 2025 offseason. Glenn coaches the New York Jets and Johnson coaches the Chicago Bears. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Chicago Bears look to improve their record to 3-1 this week as they welcome the New York Jets to Soldier Field. The Jets are sitting at 1-2 but have been close in every game and appear like they might be close to turning the corner. Ben Johnson and Aaron Glenn roamed the Detroit Lions’ sidelines together for four years. They know each other well. How will that impact the game? We spoke with MacGregor Wells from Gang Green Nation (SB Nation’s NY Jets site) to get a better idea of where the Jets are three games into the season. Here’s that Q&A. 1. The Jets may be sitting at 1-2, but they seem like a far more difficult out than they’ve been the last couple of years. What’s been driving the positive change? I’m not sure the current Jets are a lot better than the 2024 Jets, but they are clearly better than the 2025 Jets. Mostly the difference is talent. The Jets roster was severely lacking in NFL talent last year, particularly after the team traded away former All-Pro players Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams at the trade deadline. Once those trades were completed, the Jets had a brighter future with a bunch of first-round draft picks going forward, but the 2025 team was stripped bare in the process. The Jets WR1 Garrett Wilson was also injured for most of the 2025 season, leaving the team with no credible weapons in the passing game. Wilson is healthy so far in 2026, and he has been joined by first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq at tight end. That’s a big increase in talent in the passing game. Geno Smith may not be a top quarterback, but he is a pretty big upgrade over the motley collection of Justin Fields, Tyrod Taylor, and Brady Cook at QB in 2025. On defense, the Jets brought in a slew of new talent via trades, free agency, and the draft. The Jets now have 2nd overall pick David Bailey starting on the edge and free-agent pickup Kingsley Enagbare starting on the other side at edge. They brought in several new additions on the defensive line, including David Onyemata and T’Vondre Sweat. They also brought in Demario Davis at linebacker to stabilize the whole defense, and they brought in starting safeties Minkah Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton to shore up the back end. Basically, the Jets completely overhauled the defense, and it is simply a much deeper, more talented unit than it was last year. 2. Aaron Glenn was one of the most criticized coaches in the league last year; this year, he’s already had a couple of questionable in-game decisions that probably cost them a win against the Green Bay Packers (and disappointed many Bears fans). Is Glenn getting better at this or are these decisions eventually going to force the Jets to make a change? It’s not clear Glenn is getting better at this particular aspect of the game. He still makes questionable decisions. He doesn’t seem to have a handle on clock management. His new offensive coordinator, Frank Reich, and the Jets offense look particularly clueless in two-minute drill-type situations at the end of halves. Of course, much of the offensive chaos is the direct responsibility of Reich, not Glenn. However, in the end, the OC was the direct hire of Glenn. If the OC isn’t getting the job done, that ultimately is Glenn’s fault. Will it cost Glenn his job? I’m not sure. If the Jets improve their record to say 7 or more wins this year, I doubt Glenn’s job will be in peril, at least for another year. If the Jets win 5 or fewer games, Glenn will probably be fired, in my opinion. These things probably hold true regardless of these particular coaching issues with Glenn. However, if these issues continue to cost the Jets games, eventually they will probably cost Glenn his job, if not this year, then some time in the future. 3. Geno Smith looked fully cooked last year but has bounced back and looked pretty darn good to start. What is Geno doing well so far this year that has him playing like the Geno from a few years ago? Geno has always had a strong and accurate arm. If he is protected by the offensive line and given good weapons on offense, he will usually produce good play at quarterback. If he is constantly under pressure and has few good weapons to throw to, his play will suffer. These things are true for many NFL quarterbacks. Last year the situation in Las Vegas was pretty bad for Smith. His offensive line was one of the worst in the NFL, as were his weapons on offense once Brock Bowers was hobbled for much of the year. Now he is playing behind a Jets offensive line that may not be at the top of the league, but it is a big step up from his Raiders offensive line last year. In addition, his weapons of Garrett Wilson, Kenyon Sadiq, and Adonai Mitchell may not be at the top of the NFL, but they are a big step up from the Raiders’ weapons last year once Bowers was hobbled. Predictably, the better surrounding talent has resulted in better play by Smith. He isn’t a great quarterback, but if he has time to throw and weapons to throw to, he is perfectly competent. 4. It certainly looks like Breece Hall is going to miss this one. He’s an excellent back but hasn’t had the best numbers this year. How well can Braelon Allen fill that void, and how will the offense change without Hall? Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis may actually be an upgrade over the version of Breece Hall we have seen so far this season. The Breece of years past was, of course, better than those two. However, Hall has looked like a shell of his former self this season. Perhaps he is suffering from an undisclosed injury; I don’t know. What I do know is he has been largely ineffective. Allen and Davis are pretty good backs. They won’t provide the big-play potential of Breece Hall in prior years, but they are solid and can move the chains. They are also both effective as receivers. The Jets probably won’t change a whole lot on offense with Hall absent, though they may run fewer outside runs due to neither Allen nor Davis having the speed to turn the corner that Hall has. 5. The Bears currently sit as a 3.5-point favorite on FanDuel. How do you think this one plays out on Sunday? What’s your final score prediction? If Tyson Bagent starts at quarterback for the Bears, I like the Jets’ chances. If Case Keenum starts, I think the Bears will win. As for the score, this always seems like a random function. Even if I get who wins correct, the score is usually wildly off. Nonetheless, I’ll give this a go. If Bagent starts, Jets 20, Bears 17. If Keenum starts, Bears 24, Jets 20.
author: Bill Zimmerman

title: One stat that shows the Bears’ defense actually has been better so far in 2026
summary: Don’t look now, y’all: the Chicago Bears’ defense just might be back. Ok, give me a break. I had to try. However, after a Week 1 in which they allowed more than 30 points to the Carolina Panthers, the Bears have allowed fewer than 10 points in each of their last two contests. That has […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jaylon Johnson #1 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a defensive stop during the third quarter of the NFL game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t look now, y’all: the Chicago Bears’ defense just might be back. Ok, give me a break. I had to try. However, after a Week 1 in which they allowed more than 30 points to the Carolina Panthers, the Bears have allowed fewer than 10 points in each of their last two contests. That has to count for a little something, right? Even if it was against a backup Minnesota Vikings quarterback (Carson Wentz) and a mercurial Philadelphia Eagles offense still searching for its footing. One advanced stat suggests this isn’t entirely fool’s gold, albeit in a three-game sample. Through the first three weeks of the season, Dennis Allen’s defense ranks ninth overall (!!) in EPA/play allowed at -0.052, according to rbsdm.com . In particular, the Bears have been very stingy against the pass, allowing the fourth-lowest dropback success rate (41.3%) and tied for the fifth-lowest dropback EPA. Stopping the run has been a bit more of an adventure (19th in dropback SR, 25th in rush EPA/play allowed). But in a quarterback-driven league, you might take some light punishment in giving up some plays on the ground rather than in the air. And again, it’s not as if their miscues in run defense have hurt them much. Hopefully it stays that way. Here’s why that stat matters at least a little. Last year at this time, the Bears were among the league’s worst defensive units through three games, sitting 26th (0.089) in EPA/play allowed, putting up appalling numbers against both the pass and run. Naturally, one of those losses came from that absolute dumpster fire against the Detroit Lions. Then again, though, it’s not like Chicago wasn’t giving it in Week 1 this year against Bryce Young, too. So what gives? Maybe it’s just the Bears being in Year 2 of Allen’s system and better understanding what he wants, or perhaps it’s gathering personnel that better fit Allen’s vision for defense, especially up front. Maybe it’s both. Whatever it is, the defense has been stepping up to do its part, as the offense tries to stay afloat with Caleb Williams (hamstring) likely to miss at least half the month of October. Right now, Allen’s unit is showcasing what it means to be greater than the sum of your parts. Though we spent much of the offseason BEGGING for the Bears to make a move up front in the draft or free agency, they stuck to their plan. Now, they have two young defenders—Dillon Thieneman and Malik Muhammad—playing well in their early snaps as rookies, ready to contribute when the moment calls for it. The Bears aren’t an elite defensive team, and a three-game sample size generally isn’t enough to make it one. But for now, they’re not nearly as bad as we all feared, and that’s excellent news.
author: Khari Thompson

title: Bears vs. Jets: Keys to a Chicago victory
summary: The Chicago Bears could be starting a third-straight different quarterback against the New York Jets on Sunday. And for perhaps the first time in Bears history, that isn’t the largest concern. Such is the Ben Johnson experience. That isn’t to say it’s not a problem. It just isn’t the biggest problem. Johnson has proved he […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 27: Head Coach Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets looks on during warm ups prior to the game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on September 27, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears could be starting a third-straight different quarterback against the New York Jets on Sunday. And for perhaps the first time in Bears history, that isn’t the largest concern. Such is the Ben Johnson experience. That isn’t to say it’s not a problem. It just isn’t the biggest problem. Johnson has proved he can design a game plan that will be effective for about any defense and fit whatever players are available to him at the time. So let’s get to the keys to the game for the Chicago Bears to beat the New York Jets on Sunday. Sam: Rely on the ground game, get behind that offensive line and just grind out a win. The Jets’ pass defense will cause problems, but Chicago has the advantage on the ground. On defense, find a way to get after Geno Smith and don’t let Garrett Wilson beat you. Lester: The Jets’ defense has been much improved this season, but that shouldn’t prevent the Bears from imposing their will in the running game. Regardless of which backup QB is playing, trying to replicate Monday’s quick pass game plan wouldn’t make sense. On defense, show blitz to confuse the pass protection, but drop off and cover because Geno Smith is completing 84.6% of his passes against the blitz this season. Josh: I think Ben needs to keep doing Ben things, hunting explosives with relentless attention to the run game and shoving bodies around. Dennis Allen just made doubters look silly, and now he needs to show that it wasn’t a fluke. Take advantage of the loss of Hall and contest every catch. Donald: So I’m going with the theory it is Tyson on Sunday. With that, the key for Tyson is to model himself after Case against the Eagles – quick and efficient passing. Don’t turn the ball over. Lean on the run game. With Swift on the report, I think the Bears will feature Monangai, and I think he can handle the load against the Jets. As for the defense, we know Geno puts the ball in harm’s way. I see Muhammed and Thineman getting on the board with picks. And we will see another good DL line stack with Booker, Sweat, and motivated Dayo getting pressure. If the Bears win the turnover battle and BJ again dissects the opposing defense, the Bears will have another victory in their grasp. Mongo Peanut: The Jets are better than they have been recently, and the Bears need to come in prepared. Still, the Bears are the more talented and complete team, even with Caleb sidelined. The key to the game is for the Bears to simply limit the mistakes. They have committed a lot of penalties and have executed poorly in the red zone thus far, having only scored TDs on 50% of trips, which is good for 21st in the league. If the Bears clean those things up and play an efficient operation, they ought to win this one. What are your keys to the game? Share them in the comments.

title: NFL Predictions: Will the Bears backup QB magic continue vs. the Jets?

The Jets may be 1-2, but they played the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions tough. It took overtime for the Packers to sneak by them in Week 2, and the Lions scored the go-ahead touchdown with 2: 25 left on the clock. Thirty-six-year-old Geno Smith has been slinging it for New York, throwing for 783 yards through three games, 4 touchdowns, and no picks, with a league-leading 75.5 completion percentage. Even if the Bears were at full strength, this one wouldn’t be the gimme many thought, but that said, I like the Bears to win; regardless of who is playing quarterback. Head coach Ben Johnson isn’t going to tip his hand, as he wants to keep the Jets guessing. On the Amazon Prime Video Thursday Night postgame show, James Palmer said that Caleb Williams has been living in the trainer’s room to try to get his hamstring right but is still likely out. He also said the Bears seem to be leaning towards Bagent to start on Sunday. ESPN’s Adam Schefter speculated it’ll be Bagent, and while he made it clear it wasn’t a report (just his opinion), he went on to list several reasons he believes it’ll be Bagent. I’ve been on the Tyson train since Ben Johnson spoke after the Monday night game. It just makes sense given that he’s the backup, Ben has said he believes Bagent is good enough to be a starter in the league, and he’s one of the best-paid number twos in the NFL. And besides, that Keenum moment was magic, so why tempt fate? Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have the Bears as a 3.5-point favorite, and I think they’ll win by at least a touchdown. title: Is front-office pride endangering yet another Bengals season?
summary: Pride comes before the fall. And if the Cincinnati Bengals keep refusing to make the changes they desperately need, that is exactly what is going to happen. The Bengals need a linebacker who can cover tight ends and running backs. Their pride is keeping them from getting one. Sunday’s 30-27 loss to Pittsburgh put that […]
full_text: Pride comes before the fall. And if the Cincinnati Bengals keep refusing to make the changes they desperately need, that is exactly what is going to happen. The Bengals need a linebacker who can cover tight ends and running backs. Their pride is keeping them from getting one. Sunday’s 30-27 loss to Pittsburgh put that weakness on display again. Aaron Rodgers’ first pass went to running back Jaylen Warren on a short crossing route and became a 30-yard gain. Where was the linebacker? By the end of the afternoon, Warren had three catches for 49 yards. Tight ends Darnell Washington, Pat Freiermuth and Robert Tonyan combined for six receptions and another 99 yards. That is nine catches for 148 yards from running backs and tight ends, which was more than half of Rodgers’ passing yardage. The Bengals cannot keep watching opponents exploit the same weakness and insist the answer is already in the building. Washington delivered the most expensive reminder. With the game tied in the fourth quarter, he turned a reception into a 47-yard gain on the possession that produced Pittsburgh’s winning field goal. Cincinnati needed to get someone on the ground. Instead, a tight end helped move the Steelers into scoring position. Some of that was tackling. Some of it was defending receivers in space. Both require attention, and neither gets corrected by pretending the current personnel simply need more time. A week earlier, Dalton Schultz caught 12 passes for 140 yards against the Bengals. Cincinnati won in Houston, but the result concealed a problem that Pittsburgh brought back into focus. A win does not turn a defensive weakness into a strength. The Bengals have enough evidence. What they need now is the willingness to admit their linebacker room needs help. That admission should not be difficult. Teams make personnel decisions, evaluate the results, and adjust. Bringing in a veteran does not require abandoning young players. It requires acknowledging that development and winning this season have to happen together. Instead, Cincinnati is letting pride protect its decisions while opposing offenses collect the benefits. There are options worth pursuing, starting with Shaq Thompson. Buffalo currently lists him on its practice squad, and PFF’s player page gives him a 69.2 coverage grade for 2025, 14th among 88 qualified linebackers. That is enough of a reason to make a call. Jerome Baker deserves consideration as well. He remains on the latest available free-agent list, and his 69.1 coverage grade last season makes him worth examining, even with the limitation of a smaller workload. Bring him in and find out whether he can help. These players are candidates, and the Bengals have work to do before deciding whether either belongs on their roster. They need to assess health, movement, and the ability to handle the assignments that are causing trouble: carrying a tight end through a route and staying with a running back coming out of the backfield. That work should already be underway. The standard cannot be whether a signing validates the Bengals’ offseason plan. The standard has to be whether it improves their defense. Cincinnati does not need to hand a veteran a starting job or promise him every snap. It needs to create competition for the passing-down assignments its current players are failing to handle consistently. If an available linebacker can do that job better, he should be on the field. Joe Burrow’s prime is too valuable to spend protecting the front office’s pride. The Bengals have a weakness, their opponents know it, and help is worth investigating. Admit the need. Make the calls. Give this team a better chance to win.
author: John Acree

title: Amarius Mims draws strong praise from offensive line guru
summary: If there was a true bright spot that has been consistent throughout the season so far for the Cincinnati Bengals, it would be right tackle Amarius Mims playing practically perfect. Mims has shut down every pass rusher he has gone against so far. That list includes the likes of Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter […]
full_text: If there was a true bright spot that has been consistent throughout the season so far for the Cincinnati Bengals, it would be right tackle Amarius Mims playing practically perfect. Mims has shut down every pass rusher he has gone against so far. That list includes the likes of Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter from the Houston Texans. It also includes T.J. Watt from the game on Sunday with the Pittsburgh Steelers. That performance caught the eye of Brandon Thorn — one of the best offensive linemen evaluators — who has high praise after Mims incredible start, calling him a top 5-to-6 right tackle in the NFL. Counted 12 true drop-back, 1v1 reps from Mims vs. Watt, who was shut down working high-side, down the middle and inside. This is a top 5-6 RT in just his 3rd season 📈📈📈 pic.twitter.com/AVGY5fApQ6 — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) September 28, 2026 “This is a top 5-6 RT in just his 3rd season,” said Thorn. The knock on Mims during the draft process was that he couldn’t stay healthy. That always seemed unfounded considering he never even had a major knee injury. Just some moderate to minor injuries that popped up near the end of his time in college and during the draft process itself. It also created a lack-of-experience concern, but he never had an issue in the SEC. That’s why the Bengals may have gotten the steal of the draft at No. 18 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft. He has hit what many called his high ceiling of potential. Those kinds of picks haven’t always worked out, but it is clear they nailed this one if Mims can stay healthy. The only question that comes now is if he eventually gets moved to left tackle. Orlando Brown Jr. has struggled a bit with some of the quicker rushers in the NFL, and it has showed up quite a few times over the years, but he is far from being an unacceptable starter. It may come down to whether they feel the move can be made, and how much exactly they end up having to pay him when that contract needs to be redone. Because he surely should push for elite tackle money, but left tackle will always get more in that area. That is a long-term discussion, though. We get to enjoy him as an absolute dominant offensive tackle right now.

title: Bengals vs. Jaguars: Odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 4 matchup
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals and Jacksonville Jaguars are putting all the chips on the table in this battle of the cats. The Bengals are coming off a disappointing road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that showed some holes in their new-look defense. That could be a problem as the Jaguars offense has been humming mostly through […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals and Jacksonville Jaguars are putting all the chips on the table in this battle of the cats. The Bengals are coming off a disappointing road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that showed some holes in their new-look defense. That could be a problem as the Jaguars offense has been humming mostly through three weeks. How do the oddsmakers and experts see this one playing out? Odds Cincinnati is currently a 2.5-point favorite at home, according to FanDuel Sportsbook. The usual spread based on even teams meeting is the home team getting 3.5 points of favorability, so clearly Jacksonville is eating into the home-field advantage there. The over/under is set at 51.5 points. Cincinnati has gone over that mark twice in their season so far, but the Jaguars have never reached that height. However, they have scored 35 and 34 points so far. That is more than the Bengals’ 33 points against the Tampa Bay Bucs, their highest output of the season. Expert picks ESPN has seven of their 11 experts still going with Cincinnati Four of CBS Sports’ seven experts are taking Cincinnati Three of NFL.com’s five experts are going with the Jaguars NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from experts around the web — has the Bengals being picked 52 percent of the time. Cincy Jungle Prediction Clearly, this is expected to be a close game between two very good AFC teams with good quarterbacks leading them. Joe Burrow and Trevor Lawrence also met in the 2019 National Championship when Burrow and the LSU Tigers defeated Trevor Lawrence and the Clemson Tigers (another game between big cats). Jacksonville boasts the top-scoring defense, only allowing 12 points per game, but when you have played the Cleveland Browns, Denver Broncos, and New England Patriots, it really doesn’t compare to an offense like Cincinnati’s. However, you can say the same about Cincinnati’s defense, as none of the offenses they have faced have exactly lit the world on fire either. This game likely comes down to turnovers and the little things like penalties. That second one has plagued this team so far. However, returning home after a humbling loss could do this team good. The Bengals defense gets to Lawrence just enough to edge out a win over the Jaguars Final Score : Bengals 38, Jaguars 34 Now, send us your game predictions in the comments section! Who Dey! title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Jaguars
summary: As the Cincinnati Bengals get set to host the Jacksonville Jaguars, here are four key matchups to watch for on Sunday at Paycor Stadium. Parker Washington vs. Dax Hill Parker Washington has been the top receiver for the Jaguars through the first few weeks of the season. He comes into this game with 221 receiving […]
full_text: Sep 14, 2025; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) runs with the ball against Jacksonville Jaguars defensive back Travis Hunter (12) in the second half at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As the Cincinnati Bengals get set to host the Jacksonville Jaguars, here are four key matchups to watch for on Sunday at Paycor Stadium. Parker Washington vs. Dax Hill Parker Washington has been the top receiver for the Jaguars through the first few weeks of the season. He comes into this game with 221 receiving yards and 2 touchdowns. Bengals starting nickel corner Jalen Davis was placed on IR Tuesday afternoon. The Bengals have officially moved Dax Hill into the slot corner role on their depth chart. That doesn’t necessarily mean he will play there all the time, but until Ja’Sir Taylor comes off of short-term IR sometime in the next few weeks, we are likely to see him playing there a lot. Hill will be tasked with slowing down Washington this Sunday as the Bengals host the Jacksonville Jaguars. Emmanuel Pregnon and Robert Hainsey vs. Dexter Lawrence Emmanuel Pregnon is the Jaguars rookie left guard. He has had some inconsistent performances to start the season, as should be expected from any rookie offensive lineman. In week 2 against Denver, Pregnon allowed four pressures during the game. However, during week 3 he didn’t allow a single pressure against a very talented Patriots defensive line. Center Robert Hainsey, on the other hand, did allow a couple of pressures and a couple of quarterback hits against New England. Hainsey finished that game with a 36.2 pass block grade. Meanwhile, Dexter Lawrence was able to record 2 more sacks against the Steelers this past week. Lawrence has been an absolute force in the middle of the Cincinnati defense. It wouldn’t be surprising to see a lot of Trevor Lawrence (no relation to Dexter) scrambling all game long on Sunday. Dexter Lawrence vs. Pittsburgh Steelers pic.twitter.com/gOiD8ycO6r — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Orlando Brown Jr. vs. Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker Brown is likely to face off against Hines-Allen more often, but should see both of the Jaguars’ talented pass rushers at times on Sunday. Brown had a rough performance against the Texans during Week 2, giving up three sacks on the day. He was able to bounce back against the Pittsburgh Steelers for the most part. He allowed just two pressures all game, and he did not surrender a sack. Hines-Allen has six pressures, 1.5 sacks, and a forced fumble during the season so far. He has 62.5 career sacks. Opposite of him is typically Travon Walker. The former No. 1 overall pick has 13 pressures so far this season. He has 29 career sacks of his own coming into this one. Amarius Mims has yet to surrender a pressure through three games, so the Jaguars defense will be looking to attack Orlando Brown Jr. If he can hold up as he did against the Steelers, the Bengals should be able to put up a lot of points again in this one. Ja’Marr Chase vs. Travis Hunter The Jacksonville Jaguars traded up to select Travis Hunter with the second overall selection during the 2025 draft. The second-year player is now focused more on being a full-time corner, which was always the most logical spot to play him. While he will occasionally get in for some offensive plays, he has been allowed to really focus on the defensive side of the ball this season. He recorded his first interception of the year in Week 3 against the New England Patriots. He will likely face off a lot against Ja’Marr Chase. After the first week when Chase recorded just two catches for 12 yards, he has been seeing a lot more targets come his way over the last two weeks. Chase has 173 receiving yards with three receiving touchdowns over the past two weeks. He and fellow receiver Tee Higgins are playing at a high level right now. I would expect that to continue on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Ja'Marr Chase puts 6️⃣ on the board @CINvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yeZQQAjlTQ — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026

title: Browns: Would they trade this veteran WR? Should they?
summary: The Cleveland Browns appear to be on the right track at wide receiver. After far too many years of bad draft picks (Jamari Thrash, Michael Woods II, Anthony Schwartz, Antonio Callaway, and Brian Robiskie, to name a few) and ill-conceived trades (Odell Beckham Jr.), general manager Andrew Berry appears to have hit on rookies KC […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns appear to be on the right track at wide receiver. After far too many years of bad draft picks (Jamari Thrash, Michael Woods II, Anthony Schwartz, Antonio Callaway, and Brian Robiskie, to name a few) and ill-conceived trades (Odell Beckham Jr.), general manager Andrew Berry appears to have hit on rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Following Thursday night’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, Concepcion is tied for the team lead with 17 receptions, while Boston leads with 284 receiving yards. Together, the rookie duo has combined for 37 percent of the team’s receptions and 50 percent of the team’s receiving yards. Mix in tight end Harold Fannin Jr. (17 receptions and a team-high three receiving touchdowns), and the contributions from running backs Qunshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders (a combined 25 receptions for 169 yards), and that provides quarterback Deshaun Watson with a nice set of tools in the toolbox to work with. What’s that? There is one prominent name missing from the list? Oh right, Jerry Jeudy. The veteran of the group, the 2026 season has been an odd one for Jeudy, who was not targeted at all in the win over Carolina and only once in the victory over Tampa Bay. Jeudy picks up 17 The Browns are looking for the win. @PITvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qnLA8fM4ZE — NFL (@NFL) October 2, 2026 It was turning into another quiet night for Jeudy against the Steelers before he pulled in two passes on Cleveland’s game-winning drive in the fourth quarter. Those receptions brought Jeudy’s season total to five catches for 62 yards. There are a few ways to look at the situation: After posting career highs in receptions (90) and receiving yards (1,229) in 2024, Jeudy dipped to 50 receptions and 602 receiving yards in 2025. His slow start could be a sign that he is in decline. Watson is more focused on distributing the ball to whoever is open, rather than trying to force a pass to one particular player, which means Jeudy’s time will come, as it did in the fourth quarter on Thursday. Boston and Concepcion are simply better options, and the Browns consider Jeudy a role player. Head coach Todd Monken acknowledged that last point in his comments while crediting Jeudy for being there when the team needed him after the game on Thursday: “I’m so happy for Jerry. And it probably wasn’t enough for a game ball, but for a guy that really isn’t starting now, he’s a rotational player, that’s so cool for him. And it’s not easy for a veteran player to have young players kind of beat him out, but we needed it in a big time, and that was a big time catch.” That leads to the question of how much the Browns need Jeudy and whether or not they could look to trade him before the NFL trade deadline on November 10. ESPN’s Dan Graziano highlighted Jeudy as a trade candidate in his latest column on players who could be on the move in the next few weeks: Jeudy is still only 27 years old, and he’s signed through 2027. But the Browns’ wide receiver corps has been taken over by rookies, and Jeudy might no longer fit squarely into the plans. He’s owed about $23 million in salary and bonus for 2027, but it’s not guaranteed, so an acquiring team wouldn’t likely be deterred by that. It is always tricky when people start talking about trades. If Jeudy’s numbers are truly an indication that he is slipping, then why would another team want him? And how much value would the Browns receive for him? But if the numbers are simply based on Watson having better options and Jeudy is still putting in the work and not complaining, then the Browns are likely better off with him on the roster. Especially since they are only four games into the season and injuries are always a concern. Plus, as he showed against the Steelers, Jeudy can still make a play when the team needs him. So Berry may be hesitant to shake things up when the team is winning. What do you think, Browns fans? Would you look for a trade partner for Jeudy, or is he a nice insurance policy to have? Let everyone know in the comments!

full_text: The Cleveland Browns are currently sitting atop the AFC North with a 3-1 record. It is an unexpected start for many Browns fans, especially after the struggles against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week One. It was a very dramatic Thursday Night Football game in which Cleveland drove the ball down the field in the final minutes to put itself in a good position to kick a field goal for the win. This win makes it the first time the Browns have led in the AFC North since 2021. The Cleveland defense has continued to prove they are a strong unit. This group recorded two interceptions and five sacks in the matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. They made crucial stops and continued to pressure the opposing offense. The Browns offense has been the biggest surprise of the season thus far. While not perfect, the group has multiple young players who are starting to stand out and show their value. In the matchup against the Steelers in particular, they put 21 points on the board in the second quarter alone, along with putting together the game-winning drive. Rookie Denzel Boston had 89 receiving yards and really stood out. Let me know what you think in the comments – The Browns Are Making Their Presence Felt in the AFC North

title: The Browns in the playoffs? Not so fast
summary: The Cleveland Browns find themselves at 3-1-0 in this young 2026 season. Three comeback wins have been featured so far and show that Cleveland has no quit. The win over division rival Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football placed the Browns in first place all alone atop the AFC North Division. RELATED: BROWNS WINNING GAMES […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns find themselves at 3-1-0 in this young 2026 season. Three comeback wins have been featured so far and show that Cleveland has no quit. The win over division rival Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football placed the Browns in first place all alone atop the AFC North Division. RELATED: BROWNS WINNING GAMES BECAUSE OF THE “AND” And that is all well and good. Everyone wants to win games and become fans of something they feel is relevant. It is easier to root for a team that is winning games than to be devoted to a club that continually rests in the basement on an annual basis. With the win, certainly Cleveland will obviously climb in the league power rankings. The league has five undefeated teams going into Week 4, and nine teams that are currently at 2-1-0 that could improve their standing once the smoke from the weekend subsides. Teams that begin their season 3-1-0 have made the playoffs 75% of the time since the NFL expanded its postseason format in 2020. Remember, the consensus for the Browns before the year began was a five-win season, six at most? It is a distinct possibility that Cleveland could be ranked in the Top 10. No, really. There are a few media outlets that are predicting a playoff spot for the Browns. So are numerous Facebook fan pages. Really? Let’s slow this down a bit and be more realistic. Jacob Robinson of The Athletic said this about Cleveland’s sudden ascension: “What about surprise 3-1 teams like these Browns? Projected before the season to win five games, Cleveland had Super Bowl odds of +15000, ranking 28th at the time. This start is very different from most.” For one, it’s just one win. A key division matchup, to be certain, but simply one game on the schedule. There are 13 remaining. Cleveland has beaten the 1-2-0 Carolina Panthers, the 0-3-0 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the now 2-2-0 Steelers. Nothing in this grouping screams potential Super Bowl champion. The only good team they faced was the Jacksonville Jaguars, who took Cleveland to the wood shed to the tune of a 34-10 beatdown. There is a saying: “It’s not what you are, but who you’ve played.” Now, don’t get this all wrong; the Browns have the opportunity to gain double-digit wins this year. No, really. Because they were at the bottom of the division last year, they are set up with what is called “the fourth-place schedule” this year. That means they are pitted against the majority of clubs that also finished dead last in their division in 2025. Playing last year’s crappy teams is a wonderful thing. On the schedule are the New York Jets, New Orleans Saints, Tennessee Titans, Las Vegas Raiders, Indianapolis Colts, New York Football Giants, and Atlanta Falcons. Seven wins from this group? Six? Even five victories place Cleveland at eight wins for the year. With seven playoff seeds in the AFC, getting into the postseason will require a minimum of 10 wins. 11 gets you in. But hold the phone. The Houston Texans were expected to be in the AFC Championship Game this year, and yet currently are 0-3-0. The Browns play Houston in Week 10. If Cleveland can split with every team in the division, that is another three wins. The victory over Pittsburgh is a direct indication that this could happen. The Browns are the only team in the division that has never won an AFC North Division crown. Back in the day, they captured the AFC Central many times, but so far, since the realignment, they have never won the division title now called the AFC North. This could happen. This year. And the playoffs could happen as well. Then again, the bottom could fall out. Lord knows the team collects penalties and allows a team like the Steelers to crawl back into the game after building a big lead. Robinson added: “Should we trust Cleveland? Naturally, fans are concerned. These Browns are also different in another way, as they’re 3-1 despite having a negative points margin (minus-14) on the season. But there’s good news there, too. The recent history of 3-1 teams with negative differentials is a reminder that a winning record is all you need.” Last year, the Arizona Cardinals began their season 2-0-0, and everyone started talking playoffs. The Cardinals are a 127-year franchise, and they ended their season 3-14-0. It was the greatest number of losses in a single season in team history. Yet, they began on top of the world. Let’s just enjoy the moment. When the Browns begin beating the really good NFL teams, like the Baltimore Ravens, then let’s start discussing the postseason. title: Update on Mason Graham’s knee injury for Browns
summary: Cleveland Browns DT Mason Graham was off to a tremendous start to his second season, notching four sacks in his first three games. Then came yesterday’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. Even though it was a feel-good ending to the game with the Browns pulling off the 27-24 victory, Graham suffered […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns DT Mason Graham was off to a tremendous start to his second season, notching four sacks in his first three games. Then came yesterday’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. Even though it was a feel-good ending to the game with the Browns pulling off the 27-24 victory , Graham suffered an injury early in the game that forced him to go to the locker room. Friday afternoon, Ian Rapoport of ESPN provided an update on Graham, which is a combination of good and bad news for the young defensive tackle: #Browns DL Mason Graham, a standout who leads the team in sacks, is expected to miss a few weeks with an MCL sprain and ankle sprain, sources say based on the preliminary evaluation. The MRI revealed some good news, with hopes that it’s not a long-term injury. pic.twitter.com/rDwZFWGS3Q — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 2, 2026 The bad news is that Graham will miss some time, but the good news is that it does not appear to be a long-term injury. Rapoport says that Graham suffered an MCL sprain and an ankle sprain when his leg bent backwards, injuries which should keep him out for a few weeks. Let’s say he misses the rest of October, which would be three games — those would come against the New York Jets, Baltimore Ravens, and Tennessee Titans. Then, on November 1, Cleveland takes on the Steelers again. We’ll see how things go with Graham week-by-week, but if the Browns keep playing the way they are, they could have a solid record by the time he gets back. It’s possible that the Browns place Graham on the short-term IR list too, which would open up a roster spot in exchange for him missing four games. The Browns will rely on Maliek Collins , Mike Hall Jr , and Adin Huntington at defensive tackle. I would expect them to also call up Sam Kamara from the practice squad soon.

title: Browns winning games because of the “And” needed in football
summary: After the Cleveland Browns beat the Carolina Panthers in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season, we asked our readers to share why they believed the team was winning games. The answers were a little all over the place, which is not only to be expected but maybe the point for a young team with […]
full_text: After the Cleveland Browns beat the Carolina Panthers in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season, we asked our readers to share why they believed the team was winning games . The answers were a little all over the place, which is not only to be expected but maybe the point for a young team with a lot of moving parts. After the Browns’ victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football to kick off Week 4, the answer might just be the word “And.” Simple but confusing, right? A few years ago, there was a trend involving the ampersand (&) sign. It ended up on T-shirts, social media posts, and found its way into conversations about a variety of things. In sports, it was used to highlight a group of players from your favorite team. For this year’s Cleveland team, the problem is that the list of reasons they are being successful would be too big for a T-shirt (and we will probably miss one). Yet, the reason the Browns are 3-1 and will enter Week 5 with at least a share of the AFC North lead is the “and” of it all. Each game has heroes, not a hero. Each game has had big plays, not just a big play. Each win saw multiple coaching decisions and scheme adjustments, not just one key one. Players, not player. & Coaches, not coach. & Efforts, not effort. & Decisions, not decision. & Sacrifices, not sacrifice The list goes on and on and on. The difference between this positive start to Cleveland’s season and the few others that they have had seems to be in the collective. The Browns are not winning games just because their opponents make mistakes. Cleveland isn’t winning games because of some heroic effort by an individual or two. The Browns didn’t pull off an upset because of terrible weather, a trick play, or some fluke injury. It is “the we and the us and the we-n-us” like the fictional character Zava from “Ted Lasso” said: That is also why these three straight wins have come down to the wire, left us breathless and shaking at times, and left us wondering how easily things could have gone sideways. And thankful that they did not. The Cleveland Browns are 3-1 AND leading the AFC North AND have a chance to build on the wins AND have extra draft picks AND have the greatest fanbase supporting them AND, at least for one day, are the talk of the NFL. Bask in it Browns fans; enjoy the team-oriented wins. Welcome to Victory Friday, Victory Saturday, Victory Sunday, and Victory Monday. They are so, so sweet.

title: Browns vs Steelers: Winners, losers as Cleveland uses defense, key plays to secure win
summary: The young NFL season has the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers at 2-1-0 and tied for the AFC North Division lead. Well, actually, all four teams in the division have the same record. New head coach Todd Monken has transformed every offensive team that he has been hired to coach. Cleveland is simply his next […]
full_text: The young NFL season has the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers at 2-1-0 and tied for the AFC North Division lead. Well, actually, all four teams in the division have the same record. New head coach Todd Monken has transformed every offensive team that he has been hired to coach. Cleveland is simply his next stop. RELATED: NFL POWER RANKINGS The Browns have had good luck against Pittsburgh in the past five years, going 4-1-0 at home. Could they continue that success on Thursday Night Football and find themselves still on top of the division? Nobody believes that this year’s Browns roster will do anything. QB Deshaun Watson is playing better, kicker Andre Szmyt still hasn’t missed a field goal attempt, and the defense is keeping the production of Jim Schwartz while putting Mike Rutenberg’s spin to things. In the end, Cleveland saw their big lead disappear in the fourth quarter with several turnovers and a ton of untimely penalties. It took a Szmyt 56-yard field goal to win it 27-24 . So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? BROWNIES – Week 4 Winners CB Denzel Ward – What a wonderful pick early in the second quarter as the Steelers were driving. Ward had totally covered up WR Michael Pittman. This set the tone for the game’s defensive effort. Finished with four total tackles, one QB hit, an interception, and one batted pass. Jaleel movin' and groovin' for the score! #PITvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/b2xqYWjjGJ — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 2, 2026 RB Jaleel McLaughlin – If you had to reach for the Browns depth chart to see who #38 was after he scored Cleveland’s first points in the second quarter, so did we. McLaughlin completely juked out two Steeler defenders and got an excellent downfield block from TE Harold Fannin and WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who remained engaged on his man. Stunning run. Defense – DC Mike Rutenberg wanted to make sure that WR D.K. Metcalf was not going to beat his defense, so he devised some double coverage that eliminated him from the Steelers’ offense and forced QB Aaron Rodgers to look elsewhere. That worked well until late in the fourth quarter when Metcalf came alive with several big gains. Twice in the first half, the Steelers drove inside the Red Zone and yet only scored three points. Several third downs became sacks as the defensive backfield had great coverage. After the Deshaun Watson fumble, each pass play was well-covered as Pittsburgh was maneuvering for the field goal until DT Mike Hall returned to the game and got the sack. The Steelers got back into the game with the ball back with just over six minutes to play, yet it was a three-and-out. 60 YARDS DOWN THE FIELD FOR DB! #PITvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/9rrJl5NINH — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 2, 2026 WR Denzel Boston – How did Boston get so open in the second quarter, he made a slight wiggle to affect CB Daylen Everette, then took off deep with his speed. QB Deshaun Watson laid a perfect throw and the Browns were in business inside the 20. With 1:39 left in the first half, Boston recognized that Watson was in trouble and moved towards his QB with a great grab, but the offense accepted a holding call instead. How reliable was Boston when Cleveland was on the one-yard line late in the fourth quarter with a first-down pass when the Browns wanted to work the clock? Led all receivers with 89 yards. QB Deshaun Watson – Terrific flip pass to RB Quinshon Judkins after the Boston huge gain. Watson looked off the safety, who drifted away from the center, and found Q out of the backfield. Down on the one-yard line with the second touchdown on the next play. Getting the safety to move out of the center made this play. Nice toss to Boston for the first down at midfield with 3:22 left before the half. Then two plays later, Steelers DT Yahya Black had gotten past RG Austin Barber and was bearing down when Watson threw a strike to Concepcion that gained 25 yards. How did Watson not get sacked by two defenders with 1:29 left in the first half, and instead find Judkins, who took it to the one-yard line? I LOVE HAROLD FANNIN #PITvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/UH4gsEGues — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 2, 2026 Great recognition for the TD toss to Fannin right before the half, with great coverage by LB Patrick Queen. The Clemson rendition of Watson would have taken off numerous times, but this version left the pocket several times, only to toss some short passes. The lost fumble in the third quarter, the interception in Quarter 4, and the other fumble that he was able to recover with 6:38 remaining in the game are concerning. Each one killed great drives and gave the Steelers hope for a comeback. With 8:34 left in the game, facing a third-and-four and the pocket collapsing, Watson was able to run for 21 yards and a needed first down. View this post on Instagram Missed a wide-open Fannin on the third-down play with just over four minutes to go, which also stopped the clock, and then had the untimely sack on the final drive, already in good field goal range. Finished going 24 for 33 for 268 yards, one touchdown, one pick, sacked twice, with a QB rating of 94.0. LB Carson Schwesinger – How about that tackle on 6’-7”, 265-pound TE Darnell Washington early in the second quarter? Went low, hung on until help arrived, and the result was a one-yard gain instead of running over a bunch of guys. Had the delayed blitz that became the McGuire sack with 6:06 left before the half. Nailed RB Jaylen Warren early in the third quarter for no gain. Led all Cleveland defenders with nine total tackles. Play calling – The first half was on full display as Cleveland’s offense went down and finished drives with touchdowns instead of field goals. Head coach Todd Monken got the message that the Browns could not get the run game going, so he began calling short-to-intermediate passing plays that worked over and over in the first half. Monken then began to call run plays in the third quarter to milk the clock and control the time of possession. The third-and-seven for the short pass to WR Jerry Jeudy for the first down showed Monken’s ability to alter the game plan. Monken also kept up with whether DE T.J. Watt was on the field or not, and ran when he went to the sidelines and passed when he was on the field. Special teams – P Corey Bojorquez boomed his first kick 68 yards; the pooched a punt that got an advantageous bounce, to which WR Malachi Corley was able to down the punt at the one-foot line. Great field awareness for Corley. A whopping punt late in the game was recorded as an 81-yard kick. Is this right? A 62.75-yard final average? The punt and kickoff coverage team had suffocating coverage and gang tackling from Donovan McMillan, Winston Reid, Toriano Pride Jr., and Sam Williams. K Andre Szmyt nailed his first field goal attempt from 44 yards and every PAT, then kicked the 56-yard game-winner with 10 seconds left like it was nothing. FROWNIES – Week 4 losers Penalties – Ahhhh!!! In the first quarter alone, the Browns had five penalties accepted, including on the opening kickoff. Another two were declined: holding – Mekhi Blackmon; illegal contact – Denzel Ward; offsides – Mike Hall; roughing the passer – Maliek Collins; and then Jared Verse’s encroachment gaffe on the one-foot line that gave the Steelers offense some breathing room. The Adin Huntington sack right before the half was wiped out by the hands-to-the-face call on Sam Williams. Nine penalties in the first half. A third-and-eight during the first drive of the second half becomes a third-and-13. The pass interference call against the rookie S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was a fourth-down play that eventually became a touchdown. The nice strike to Jeudy with 1:11 left in the game was negated on a false start by LG Zion Johnson. 14 total penalties in this game. T.J. Joey Porter Jr. without designation, could debut for Cowboys – Todd Archer, ESPN Joey Porter Jr. has been able to get a couple of practices in since being traded to the Cowboys, and all signs point to him playing against the Texans. Newly acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will be available to make his Dallas Cowboys debut Sunday against the Houston Texans . Porter, who prior to joining Dallas had been ruled out of Thursday’s game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns after saying his back was tight, practiced the past two days with the Cowboys and carries no injury designation into Sunday.
