Luckily, safety Malik Hooker and cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. are off the injury report. Two additional players were ruled out on Friday, as cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown will each need at least another game to recover from respective hamstring strains. However, safety Malik Hooker (forearm) and cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. (knee/ankle) returned to practice in a full capacity on Friday and are off the injury report for Sunday’s game. Hooker returns for the first time since suffering the injury in Week 1, while Revel exited the team’s game in Brazil last Sunday in the fourth quarter and did not return. title: Cowboys at Texans: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 4
summary: Our prediction for the Dallas Cowboys offensive and defensive impact player last week didn’t quite pan out as we hoped. George Pickens had a solid game, however, not all that impactful. The same can be said for Quinnen Williams on the defensive side of the ball. We’re hoping our predictions for this week’s impactful players […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Our prediction for the Dallas Cowboys offensive and defensive impact player last week didn’t quite pan out as we hoped. George Pickens had a solid game, however, not all that impactful. The same can be said for Quinnen Williams on the defensive side of the ball. We’re hoping our predictions for this week’s impactful players will come to fruition. This may not be a must-win game for the Cowboys, but if they lose, next week’s will definitely be a must-win. In order to avoid that they need their star players to step up and help sway the game in their favor. Below are the players who we believe will make an impact this week on the offensive and defensive side of the ball. Offense – LT Tyler Guyton Tyler Guyton’s strong play through the first three games of the 2026 NFL season has been one of the biggest surprises for the Dallas Cowboys this year. He’s already faced some the best pass rushers in the entire league and has more than held his own against each one of them. We fully expect him to do the same against Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter in this Week 4 matchup with Houston Texans. The Cowboys best chance of winning this game is probably airing it out to take advantage of the Texans 26 th ranked pass defense, which means protecting QB Dak Prescott is paramount. The Cowboys will have to give some help to right tackle Terence Steele who has struggled in pass protection. So when Anderson or Hunter is rushing from Prescott’s blindside, he will have to depend on just Guyton neutralizing arguably the best pass rushing duo in the entire league. We believe No. 60 will do just that, which is why he’s our offensive impact player this week. Defense – CB Joey Porter Jr. Unless he’s not healthy, there’s no reason why Joey Porter Jr. shouldn’t play some this week against Houston Texans. He may not completely understand what his role is in Christian Parker scheme, but in the little amount of time he’s been here after arriving via trade this week he should know enough to play, especially in man-to-man. After all, it’s not as if the Cowboys have a lot of choice after all the injuries they’ve sustained that has decimated their secondary. Not only do we believe No. 25 will play with just a few days to get up to speed against the Texas this week, but we also predict he’s going to be the Cowboys defensive impact player in this interstate matchup. The best way for Parker to potentially use his new defensive weapon is to have him shadow the Texans best playmaker, Nico Collins. Porter pretty much shut him down in their last meeting and could do so once again this week. In Joey Porter Jr’s final game with the Steelers, he covered Texans Pro Bowl WR Nico Collins in the Wild Card game. – 5 targets – 2 receptions, 17 yards allowed – 2 PBUs – 49.5 passer rating allowed If able to go Sunday, he will face Collins again in his first game as a Cowboy. pic.twitter.com/cmZAFCWM7D — Mike Kennedy (@MikeKennedyNFL) October 1, 2026

title: Digging into the numbers to predict Cowboys at Texans
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. We’ll look at historical data points as well as more recent numbers. At the end, we’ll add it all up to see what Dallas needs to do to secure a win and which team may have the edge. The history The very […]
full_text: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. We’ll look at historical data points as well as more recent numbers. At the end, we’ll add it all up to see what Dallas needs to do to secure a win and which team may have the edge. The history The very first time the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans met was the very first time the Texans ever played, September 8, 2002. They beat Dallas 19-10 at home in Reliant Stadium. Tony Romo’s career began in a blowout win versus the Texans. The future franchise quarterback stepped in late and threw the first touchdown of his career to Terrell Owens. He would be named the starter just two weeks later. The last time the two teams met was November 18, 2024. The Texans poured it on Dallas in a blowout victory, winning 34-10 . Will the pass rush finally get home? The Cowboys are trapped in a world of quarterback pressures without any sacks. With just two sacks in three games, this pass rush needs to figure out a way to get home. However, when we look across the field at what the Texans are working with, this could finally be the week the seal breaks. Houston has allowed C.J. Stroud to live under constant duress so far this season. They’ve allowed the fourth most pressures among quarterbacks with 100 drop backs, and Stroud is tied for second in sacks because of it. Surprisingly, Houston is blitzed at the lowest rate in the NFL meaning they’ve been losing to plenty of four-man rushes. In addition, the Texans have little-to-no run game to speak of. They rank 25th in yards per carry and 30th in rushing yards. According to SumerSports, their rush success rate ranks them 25th in the NFL. Zooming in on last week versus the Ravens, nearly 40% of the rushing yards allowed came from the mobile quarterback and on an end around to Zay Flowers. The Texans don’t have those elements on their offense. If Dallas is able to strangle the Texans’ lackluster run game, this only helps the pass rushers get home on third-and-long. For the first time this season, they’ll be facing a team with a mostly stationary quarterback and a poor offensive line. If there were ever a time for it to click, it’d be this week. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 27 6 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions against the Ravens. He finished with a 91.2 quarterback rating. The run game finally got going in Rio. Javonte Williams finished with 98 yards on 19 carries. The team would tally 148 yards on the ground on 30 carries, totaling a fantastic 4.9 yards per carry. CeeDee Lamb continued his dominant campaign, finishing with seven catches for 112 yards. George Pickens is also starting to come alive. He totaled 82 receiving yards on seven receptions. The defense only allowed three first downs on nine third down attempts on the day. They did not allow the Ravens to convert either of their two fourth down attempts. This defensive unit improved on third down, but first and second down were still losers overall. Texans key stats from last week The Texans fell to the Colts last week, losing 19-17 . Last week was a strange one for Houston. The Texans forced three turnovers while committing none of their own, yet still gave up the game. You won’t see many losses with a turnover differential like that on the board. Superstar edge Will Anderson Jr. finished the game with seven tackles and 2.5 sacks. He added two forced fumbles, one of which set up a go-ahead score near midfield. What do the numbers mean? If there was ever a time that the Cowboys pass rush should be able to establish themselves, this would be it. Every available metric points to the pass rush getting home on Sunday. Unfortunately for us analytical types, football is played on the field and not on pieces of scratch paper. The numbers may indicate one thing, but at the end of the day the players need to play. With that in mind, it will be interesting to see exactly which personnel Parker rolls with off the edge this week. Against the Ravens, Malachi Lawrence saw only 17 snaps. But he’s been one of the most successful pass rushers when we look at win rate. There were concerns around his ability to contain Lamar Jackson and so he sat for nearly 75% of the snaps. This week, however, there is a much smaller threat in terms of quarterback mobility. I would expect to see a ton of Lawrence and Donovan Ezeiruaku pairings on the field – especially on third down. The secondary is banged up. This is a massive cause for concern. Dallas began to address this issue by making a trade once again with the Pittsburgh Steelers for cornerback Joey Porter Jr . If the new corner is active this week, expect a limited snap count while he acclimates. When he is on the field, his best immediate usage is to man up in press coverage. Parker’s defense relies on communication and it’s unrealistic to expect him to be on the same page as the other defensive backs right out of the gate. Give him a think-free assignment for now and allow him to play fast. On the offensive side, Dallas is facing a stiff test this week. The Texans are currently ranked fifth in the NFL versus the run. However with linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair currently listed as doubtful for the game, that linebacker corps is looking extremely thin. Dallas may even be facing an old friend in Kenneth Murray as a practice squad elevation should things get dire enough for the Texans. Look for Brian Schottenheimer to establish the run, effectively limiting the extremely talented Will Anderson Jr. and his pass rush off the edge. With how injured the Texans are at linebacker, this could be another week where we see the offensive line ( and Brevyn Spann-Ford ) plowing the way for Javonte Williams on the ground once again. On the flip side, it’s also logical to assume Dallas would attack the Texans through the air. That defense ranks 26th versus the pass but does have one of the league’s premier game-wreckers on the edge with Will Anderson Jr. Tyler Guyton has held up so far this season but Terence Steele has struggled on the right side. Could this be a week where the Texans identify that matchup and force Dallas to commit extra help to Steele’s side? It’s certainly a matchup to keep an eye on. If given time, however, Dak and his elite receiving corps should be able to pass the ball around the field. The Houston Texans are desperate. They’ve yet to win a game, but have lost two of three by a single possession. They’re close. And they’re most likely getting the dangerous Nico Collins back this week. It’s possible Collins goes off against a devastated Cowboys secondary. It’s also possible Dallas limits the Texans offense by cutting off their ground game and finally converting pressures into sacks versus the most stationary quarterback they’ve faced this season. Regardless of how dangerous the caged animal may be, I’ll take Dallas getting back on track this week with a win over the Texans.

title: Cowboys at Texans: Matchups to watch in Week 4
summary: Many of us had this Week 4 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans circled on our calendar. This was supposed to be an interstate rivalry between two teams with Super Bowl aspirations this year, but so far both the Cowboys and Texans have fallen way below expectations by getting off to disappointing starts. […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images Many of us had this Week 4 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans circled on our calendar. This was supposed to be an interstate rivalry between two teams with Super Bowl aspirations this year, but so far both the Cowboys and Texans have fallen way below expectations by getting off to disappointing starts. Despite that, and maybe even because of it, this game may be even more exciting with both teams seasons hanging in the balance. While there is still a lot of football to play this season, both the Cowboys and Texans desperately need to start stringing some wins together with their seasons already potentially circling the drain. Putting a “W” in the win column this week could help jumpstart things and the best way to walk away with the victory is exploit certain matchups. Below are the ones we’ll be watching for the Cowboys. WR CeeDee Lamb vs. CB Derek Stingley Jr. Stingley will likely see his fair share of George Pickens as well, but so far this season it’s been CeeDee Lamb that Dak Prescott has shown the most trust by targeting him early and often to move the Cowboys offense up the field. This is one of those best against best matchups we all like to see, and one that could help sway the game one way or another. If No. 88 continues to produce like he has in the past few weeks, Dallas’ chance of victory increases, but if not the scales could tip in favor of the Texans. CB DaRon Bland (and maybe Joey Porter Jr.) vs. WR Nico Collins Collins has missed the last few weeks with a hamstring injury, but has returned to practice this week and has a good chance of playing. This could be problematic for the Cowboys secondary who has been decimated by injuries, leaving DaRon Bland as their best option to neutralize the Texans most consistent and best offensive weapon. This shapes up as a match that favors Houston, but that could change if Joey Porter Jr. somehow suits up this week after being acquired via trade. Then the advantage could shift Dallas’ way. In Joey Porter Jr’s final game with the Steelers, he covered Texans Pro Bowl WR Nico Collins in the Wild Card game. – 5 targets – 2 receptions, 17 yards allowed – 2 PBUs – 49.5 passer rating allowed If able to go Sunday, he will face Collins again in his first game as a Cowboy. pic.twitter.com/cmZAFCWM7D — Mike Kennedy (@MikeKennedyNFL) October 1, 2026 Offensive tackles vs. DE Will Anderson Jr. Tyler Guyton’s play so for through the first three games of the 2026 NFL season has been one of the Cowboys biggest surprises this year. Terence Steele’s play has not surprised as he has once again struggled in pass protection. Will Anderson Jr. is a different animal than many pass rushers in this league and is arguably better than what Steele and Guyton have seen this year. You can expect the Texans to try and isolate Anderson on the tackles, especially against a struggling Steele. If Dak Prescott doesn’t have the time needed to find his weapons in the passing game the “W” could be out of reach.
author: Brian Martin

title: Cowboys control own response vs. Texans, need to apply pressure
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have faced a gauntlet of defensive-minded head coaches to start the 2026 season, and twice in the span of the next week, this trend will continue. For a Cowboys team with a deeply talented and experienced offense, the way they’ve struggled at times to protect a defense that needs time to learn […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have faced a gauntlet of defensive-minded head coaches to start the 2026 season, and twice in the span of the next week, this trend will continue. For a Cowboys team with a deeply talented and experienced offense, the way they’ve struggled at times to protect a defense that needs time to learn under Christian Parker has been concerning. At the same time, the way the defense couldn’t keep the Baltimore Ravens out of field goal range in just seven seconds at the end of last week’s game in Brazil was perhaps even more concerning. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer has caught the most heat this week for both aspects of this in his role as offensive play-caller and head coach overseeing. His next assignment to scheme against is DeMeco Ryans and the Houston Texans. Solely on paper, this game is there for the taking for the Cowboys as the Texans are 0-3. Football is never played on paper, and this all-Texas matchup sees the home team in the same spot they were a year ago – and one they dug out of very well. It’s time for our weekly look at how the Cowboys can win this game, and why they might not. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Houston Texans if… their EDGE rushers make a splash. Last week against the Ravens, we put this spotlight on the defensive tackles against Derrick Henry and that physical Baltimore offense. Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, and the rest of this group actually passed the test with a solid grade, and in turn the Cowboys should have won the game to go with this lift they got from their highly-paid defensive interior. Now against the Texans, it is time for the pass rush off the edge to get in on the mix a lot more. As much as Cowboys fans are unhappy with the coaching on offense at the moment, Texans fans have jumped right back into being unhappy with second-year offensive coordinator Nick Caley. Their offense has continued to look static in the pre-snap phase, they can’t push the ball downfield well, new addition David Montgomery has faced loaded boxes out of the backfield, and as a result of all this the protection hasn’t been there for C.J. Stroud. If the Cowboys defensive front picks up where it left off against the Ravens, they can drop bodies into coverage to clog the passing lanes for Stroud. This will be a necessity anyway, as the Cowboys’ coverage unit won’t include P.J. Locke, Cobie Durant, or Jalen Thompson for the foreseeable future. The next piece to this is pressuring Stroud in the pocket, and getting to the quarterback that’s been sacked more than any other besides Baker Mayfield this season. The time is right now though for the Cowboys to get more off the edge in this defense. Rashan Gary did not play well against the Ravens, Donovan Ezeiruaku was around the QB a bit but still couldn’t finish, and Von Miller was a non-factor. Malachi Lawrence only played 17 snaps. For the entire outlook of the season, the Cowboys need more production here, but if it starts with this matchup against the Texans, that outlook will be improved at 2-2. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Houston Texans if… they don’t finish in the red zone again. The red area of the field will be critical for both teams in this game, and the Cowboys need to keep the pressure on with touchdowns in these situations. So far in three games, the Texans held the Bills to 1-3 converting touchdowns in the red zone, the Colts to 1-3 last week, and didn’t even allow the Bengals to reach the red zone (despite losing 20-6) in week two. Houston being a woeful 0-4 in this game was a big factor here. The Cowboys will have their options to attack the Texans defense in the scoring area, but as has been discussed this week, perhaps that’s not the best case scenario for Schotty’s offense. Getting too cute with spreading the ball around in ways it didn’t need to be cost the Cowboys points against the Ravens. The Texans have struggled to cover from the linebacker position this season, and if opportunities are there for Jake Ferguson to stretch the field Dallas should take them, but this would also be an opportune spot to continue the CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens show – all the way down the field. The Texans defense is going to swarm and look to stay true to their identity with their backs firmly against the wall, but the Cowboys have the players to stay composed. Not getting cute in big spots to hand the Texans momentum and answering the bell by leaning on Javonte Williams and the big two at receiver is the key here. The Houston offense is likely to have Nico Collins on the field for the first time since the opener, their own answer to who can score six points for them in the red zone, giving even more reason for the Cowboys to need a highly-efficient game of their own here. I’d like to thank one of the first-ever people I met while living in the state of Texas, a die-hard Texans fan named Ricardo, who gave me some insights on his favorite team this week. Enjoy the Texas showdown in H-Town.
author: Sean Martin

title: Dallas Cowboys: Reading Between the Line vs. Houston Texans
summary: Every week, we’re digging into the trenches, because that’s where the real action happens. We shine the spotlight on the Dallas Cowboys offensive line, who’s holding it down, who’s opening holes for the running backs, and who’s keeping Dak Prescott clean. Let’s get to it. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for […]
full_text: Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we’re digging into the trenches, because that’s where the real action happens. We shine the spotlight on the Dallas Cowboys offensive line, who’s holding it down, who’s opening holes for the running backs, and who’s keeping Dak Prescott clean. Let’s get to it. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 50% 16th Run Block Win Rate – 67% 31st Pressure rate allowed – 28% 10th Sacks allowed – 3 (2nd) Last three week trend: Pass pro good, run blocking improving The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Terence Steele has a Will Anderson Jr. problem There is no need to overcomplicate the biggest concern for Dallas this week. Will Anderson Jr. is playing outstanding football. Against Indianapolis last week, Anderson produced nine pressures from only 32 pass-rush snaps. PFF credited him with three sacks and gave him a 93.3 pass-rush grade for the game. Official NFL statistics credit Anderson with 2.5 sacks in the game and four through three weeks. Anderson was on the left side of its defensive front, meaning many of his snaps naturally bring him toward Dallas’ right tackle. Steele has already been the more concerning tackle in pass protection this season, while Tyler Guyton has taken a noticeable step forward on the opposite side. Anderson can win in several ways. He is quick enough to race around the outside, but he also has the strength to drive a tackle backwards toward the quarterback. PRESSURE POINT: Houston can squeeze the pocket from both directions Stopping Anderson does not end the problem. Danielle Hunter is on the opposite edge. His start statistically has been quieter with four pressures and one sack, but this is a player who generated 92 pressures across the 2025 season. Houston also has Sheldon Rankins attacking through the middle. Rankins has six pressures and a 72.3 PFF pass-rush grade through three games. If Anderson pushes Steele backwards from one side while Hunter does the same from the other, Prescott normally has room to step forward. If Rankins is also winning through the middle, that escape route disappears. That is how Houston can create sacks without having to blitz heavily. The good news is Dallas has allowed only three sacks through three games, so the protection has generally held up well despite Smith’s absence. Keeping that number low against this front would be one of the offensive line’s best performances of the season. Where to attack Every defensive line has a weakness, here’s the Texans soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Run toward Danielle Hunter, not Will Anderson Houston does not have an obvious weakness against the run. The Texans have allowed only 260 rushing yards through three games at 3.5 yards per carry, with opponents yet to reach 90 rushing yards in a game. But Dallas still has to run the football, the key is choosing where. Anderson currently owns a 91.0 PFF run-defense grade. Running repeatedly toward him would be asking for trouble, Hunter is a different story. His current 50.6 run-defense grade ranks 88th among qualifying edge defenders. That gives Dallas a target. When Hunter is lined up opposite Tyler Guyton, Dallas should test that side with Javonte Williams. Let Guyton use the strength he has shown as a run blocker and make Hunter repeatedly defend rather than rush Prescott. Guyton’s development is particularly encouraging here. He currently carries a 79.6 PFF run-blocking grade, sixth among offensive tackles. That is strength against weakness. Dallas finally established a running game against Baltimore. It should not abandon it just because Houston has impressive season-long rushing numbers. GREEN LIGHT: Attack Sheldon Rankins in the running game There is another possible opening inside. Rankins has provided useful pass rush production, but his run defense has been significantly weaker. His current 41.5 PFF run-defense grade ranks 100th among qualifying interior defensive linemen. This is where Tyler Booker and Cooper Beebe should become important. Booker has been one of Dallas’ best run blockers this season. Through the available PFF data, his 78.6 run-blocking grade ranked ninth among guards. Dallas can put Booker and Beebe together on combination blocks against Houston’s interior defenders. That is exactly the type of physical football Dallas showed more of against Baltimore. Houston is good against the run overall, so these yards will not necessarily come easily. But Dallas does not need five yards every time. Four yards on first down is useful because it keeps Anderson and Hunter guessing. The Chaos Report Here’s the Houston Texans defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 11 (3rd) Pass Rush Win Rate – 42% 30th Run Stop Win Rate – 31% 10th QB Pressure Rate – 23% (26th) Last three week trend: Pass rush trending up Matchup of the week Terence Steele vs. Will Anderson Jr. This may be the most important individual offensive-line matchup Dallas has faced this season. Anderson is not simply playing well. He is currently one of the most disruptive defenders in football. Steele struggled at times against Baltimore and was also responsible for a costly holding penalty that removed an important Dallas first down. If Steele handles Anderson himself, Dallas can leave tight ends in the passing game and allow running backs to release into routes. If Steele needs constant help, Houston begins dictating what Dallas can do offensively. That is why this matchup affects much more than two players. Best route to success: Stay out of third-and-long and make Houston’s edge rushers defend the entire playbook rather than simply hunt Prescott. Injury Updates: Nothing to add to the Cowboys, but Tyler Smith can officially return from injured reserve after this week. For Houston, Jadeveon Clowney and Mario Edwards Jr. are both questionable. Kayden McDonald went to IR with an ankle injury two weeks ago.
author: Mike Poland

title: Making sense of the Cowboys non-existent pass rush
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are struggling to get to the quarterback. Three games into the season, the team as a whole has two sacks. One of those came from Caleb Downs strip/tackle of Jaxson Dart in the opener, but even he didn’t get the pleasure of bringing him down because the ball popped into the hands […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are struggling to get to the quarterback. Three games into the season, the team as a whole has two sacks. One of those came from Caleb Downs strip/tackle of Jaxson Dart in the opener, but even he didn’t get the pleasure of bringing him down because the ball popped into the hands of an offensive lineman who took off running. The only other sack the team had came in the same game, but it was shared between Donovan Ezeiruaku and Jonathan Bullard, who collectively collapsed on Dart. That’s it. Two lousy sacks. And it’s hard to get sacks when they’re not pressuring the quarterback very much. The Cowboys have a pressure rate of14.4%, which ranks 23rd in the league. They are just not creating much of a disruption in the backfield. But why? There is no obvious answer to this question. Many question the quality of talent on the edge, as it features a combination of young draft picks and newly acquired veterans. The guys doing most of the heavy lifting on the edge include: Donovan Ezeiruaku (69%), Rashan Gary (66%), Malachi Lawrence (34%), and Von Miller (24%). Are these guys just not cutting it? Or does this have more to do with the defensive scheme of new defensive coordinator Christian Parker? The answer consists of a little bit of both, and looking over the game film of the first three games we can compile a laundry list of explanations for their ineffective pass rush. Here they are in no particular order. They don’t seem to have a plan. The rushers aren’t utilizing any creative pass-rush strategy. No stunts, twists, or disguised looks to create pressure. It’s just predictable, straight-up rushes. They’re not winning . This defensive scheme relies on the edge players winning their one-on-one matchups on the outside, but it’s not happening. They are being outmuscled, they don’t offer much of a hand battle, and aren’t showcasing any pass-rushing moves to maneuver around their blocker. They are often wild and undisciplined. When they attack, they fly all over the place. They don’t seem to be in sync with any type of collective plan or responsibility. They act as independent soldiers who will sometimes become victimized by their own aggression, allowing quarterbacks an easy escape route. They can never finish. There will be times when the energy is there, and it sure looks like they’re about to get someone, but at the last second, the quarterback gets loose. Too often, they just get caught out of position, where they are left reaching and lunging, only to come up empty. Off-balance tackling attempts won’t cut it. Things get a little chippy. Sometimes the Cowboys’ edge rushers had to navigate through multiple blockers to get to the quarterback. The Ravens approached this very wisely and employed a tight end or running back to chip the rusher at the line of scrimmage. These were very effective, as they disrupted the timing and forced the edge rusher to take a more scenic route to the quarterback, where they never arrived at their destination. They were protecting against the run. One thing about this edge-rushing group is that most of them are antsy to dart inside and snatch that running back for a huge tackle for a loss. This split-second delay in assessing the play impedes their get-off, putting them in a tough spot right out of the gate. They hang back in coverage. These guys are not pin-their-ears-back pass rushers. At. All. They’re multiple, remember? Whether it’s defending the run or sliding back into coverage, they have a variety of responsibilities. Even if they were effective in their pass-rushing reps, this element of their game would always suppress their number of pressures. The Cowboys need to be better at generating a pass rush. Failure to do so is really a strain on their secondary, especially considering how banged up that unit is. They need to find ways to get these guys to be more effective. Another part of this is that they’re never going to be great at this. The way the defense is set up, these players have a lot of responsibilities and none of them are elite pass rushers. They’re versatile players who the team is hoping can provide a good balance of pass rush and run support. Is it going to get better? Probably. The young players are still developing, and they should be more effective as they improve elements of their game. It’s a little more discouraging for the veterans. There’s still a chance that things start to fall into place a little better and they become a solid group that can more effectively carry out their plan, but don’t be surprised if there are more bumps along the way. What do you see as the biggest issue with the pass rush?

title: Cowboys news: Team ‘hopeful’ Joey Porter Jr. makes season debut Sunday
summary: The big news for the Dallas Cowboys has to be the Joey Porter Jr. trade. The Cowboys were desperate for help in an injured secondary, and they got a true upgrade. The question is can he play Sunday, and for how many snaps. We jump into the Cowboys news. Dallas Cowboys reveal their Week 4 […]
full_text: Photo by Mark Alberti/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The big news for the Dallas Cowboys has to be the Joey Porter Jr. trade. The Cowboys were desperate for help in an injured secondary, and they got a true upgrade. The question is can he play Sunday, and for how many snaps. We jump into the Cowboys news. Dallas Cowboys reveal their Week 4 plan for Joey Porter Jr. following blockbuster trade – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports After being ruled out for the Pittsburgh Steelers Thursday night game against the Cleveland Browns, the Cowboys are now optimistic that Porter Jr. could make his debut on Sunday against the Texas if all goes well in practice. The Cowboys are extremely banged up in the secondary and could use his help versus a struggling Houston Texans offense. The Dallas Cowboys may not have to wait long to see their newest cornerback in action. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer spoke to reporters for the first time since Dallas acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers. He shared a positive update ahead of Sunday’s Week 4 matchup against the Houston Texans. Schottenheimer said the Cowboys are hopeful Porter Jr. can play against the Texans. He also liked what he saw from the cornerback in his first practice with the team, according to The Athletic’s Jon Machota : “He moved around good today. It was a good start today.” Joey Porter happy for fresh start with Cowboys, eyes Sunday debut – Todd Archer, ESPN.com The Cowboys have been in the hunt for a cornerback all year, and they finally land a great one in Joey Porter Jr. Porter speaks with the media for the first time as a member of the Dallas Cowboys and says all the right things. When the week began, Joey Porter Jr . thought he would be playing Thursday night for the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Cleveland Browns . Now, he hopes to make his Dallas Cowboys debut Sunday against the Houston Texans . “We’re just trying to take things day by day,” Porter said after his first practice in Dallas, “and if everything looks good, then we should be out there.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Cowboys team has a great chance to get back on track in Houston – BTB There is a lot of optimism surrounding the Cowboys right, which is a bit surprising given how their week three game ended. After falling to 1-2 last week in Rio, the Cowboys have a prime opportunity to even things up at 2-2 and carry good vibes into their week five game against Tampa Bay where Joey Porter Jr. will be a for sure full-go. Through three games Prescott has completed 73 of 105 passes for 730 yards, seven touchdowns and only one interception with a passer rating of 107.2. Thanks to Dak and his leadership, Dallas is averaging over 29 points per game, seventh-best in the NFL. Houston is averaging only 18 points, ranking 24th. That is an important difference. Dallas has shown that it can score enough points to survive difficult games, Houston hasn’t. The Texans are 0-3 and have scored only 54 points across those games, Dallas has scored 88. ‘Boundary eraser’: Cowboys DC Christian Parker reacts to Joey Porter Jr. trade – Clark Dalton, Yardbarker.com Cowboys’ DC Christian Parker spoke for the first time since the Cowboys loss in Brazil. While he briefly touched on the unfortunate ending to the game, the Joey Porter Jr. addition dominated the conversation. To a surprise to no one, Parker is very excited. Parker called Porter a “boundary eraser” in pass coverage (h/t Ed Werder of WFAA-TV in Dallas). “He certainly fits what we do and how we want to play,” Parker continued. “When you have opportunities, and I get asked about guys like that, it’s usually a yes. “I’m always trying to add more good players.” Boundary corners play the shorter side of the field and are typically excellent in pass coverage, like Porter. In 2025, Pro Football Focus credited him with the third-lowest passer rating allowed among corners (55.9).

title: Broncos vs. 49ers: 3 Players to Watch in Week 4
summary: The Denver Broncos battle the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Riding the highs of back-to-back comebacks, the Broncos are in pursuit of a third straight win. However, the 49ers present a big challenge for Denver given how good they are on both sides of the ball. In order to achieve a key road victory, […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs throws a pass against Jonah Elliss #52 of the Denver Broncos during the third quarter in the game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos battle the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Riding the highs of back-to-back comebacks, the Broncos are in pursuit of a third straight win. However, the 49ers present a big challenge for Denver given how good they are on both sides of the ball. In order to achieve a key road victory, these three players will need to perform at a high level. Bo Nix — Quarterback Bo Nix boasts a good start to his career. With 26 wins, a dozen game winning drives, and ten fourth quarter comebacks, Nix has certainly outperformed his 2024 NFL Draft peers at the position. He’s arguably the comeback king of the NFL, but fans across Broncos Country are still waiting for more consistency and better starts to games. I have no doubt a much more consistent rushing attack would benefit the third-year signal caller. However, he simply has to play better. This year, there has been significant regression with Nix’s first and third down passing. Last season, Nix did very well on first downs, but this year’s output is less than optimal. Third-and-short to third-and-medium range passing situations continue to be an issue as well. Under the guidance of Raheem Morris, the 49ers sport a sound zone-heavy defense that has done a good job of limiting the impact of opposing offenses thus far. They are winning on early downs. They have playmakers that can cover a lot of ground and do well erasing opportunities in down the field and over the middle. I’ll be watching how Nix performs closely on Sunday—he has to have a good start and be a lot more consistent. Jonah Elliss — Edge Rusher With Jonathon Cooper sidelined to begin the season on the NFL Commissioner’s Exempt list, the Broncos have been banking on the progression and development of edge rusher Jonah Elliss . The former third-round pick has a significant increase in snaps at nearly 65-percent of the defense’s total—up from 38-percent his first two seasons in Denver. Unfortunately, through three games Elliss has struggled a fair bit. He doesn’t have a sack and has registered just two hurries and five pressures. We are seeing a significant drop off in hurry and pressure rate. Additionally, containment and setting the edge has been an issue for the former Utah standout. Though I’ll admit that issue hasn’t just been singular to him. Nobody has been able to sack Brock Purdy thus far. Moreover, the 49ers have one of the best rushing attacks in the league. Will this be the week Elliss steps up and makes some big plays on defense? Denver will need him to play at a high level to keep Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, and Kaelon Black in check. Alex Singleton — Inside Linebacker One player I have major concerns about this game is inside linebacker Alex Singleton. I felt Singleton had a rebound performance in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. However, I was less than impressed with his outing against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football . The eighth-year pro has 32 tackles on the season. Though none of them are for loss and he is already credited with 8 missed tackles. Moreover, #49’s numbers in coverage don’t look particular good either. That may be a problem going up against a 49ers team that runs the ball well and is extremely efficient through the air. 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan is a master at finding matchups against opposing defenses that play to his advantage. I have a feeling Shanahan has drawn up a handful of plays that feature players like Christian McCaffrey or George Kittle attempting to expose Singleton’s deficiencies. Alongside the aforementioned Elliss, he is another defender I’ll be keeping close tabs on Sunday.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 5 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Week 5 of the NCAA football season is here. That means another installment of Future Broncos. Here are three players Broncos Country should keep their eyes on in today’s action-packed slate of games. LJ Martin — Running Back — BYU One position I haven’t discussed any prospects at thus far is running back. Over the […]
full_text: COLLEGE STATION, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 12: Reed Harris #3 of the Arizona State Sun Devils signals first down after play during the first half of a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Kyle Field on September 12, 2026 in College Station, Texas. (Photo by Joe Buvid/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Week 5 of the NCAA football season is here. That means another installment of Future Broncos . Here are three players Broncos Country should keep their eyes on in today’s action-packed slate of games. LJ Martin — Running Back — BYU One position I haven’t discussed any prospects at thus far is running back. Over the past two drafts, the Broncos have made investments in RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman. They also re-upped J.K. Dobbins to a two-year deal, but he hasn’t looked as explosive as he did in the first part of their 2025 gridiron campaign. I think any fan would admit Denver has issues running the ball to start the season. For me, it’s still a relatively mild concern, but definitely not a top-tier need that has to be addressed. I’m not arguing for an early investment at running back. However, a certain prospect I feel would provide an immediate boost to Denver’s rushing woes is BYU senior LJ Martin. I discussed him last year , but he opted to return for his fourth and final season with the Cougars. Martin is coming off an impressive junior campaign where he had 236 rushes for 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns. He also was a viable receiver out of the backfield hauling in 36 catches for 255 yards. At 6’2” and 220 pounds, Martin is one of the most physical runners in this year’s class at the position group. A throwback runner that wins in between the tackles and gets downhill quickly, Martin has routinely been amongst the best in the nation gaining yards after contact and forcing missed tackles. He doesn’t have elite athleticism or breakaway speed, but his strengths are extremely enticing. There is a long way to go in the season, but I think he could be a Top 100 pick next April. Whether or not Denver has interest remains to be seen, but if their stable of backs continues to struggle, I’m guessing they will be intrigued by the BYU standout. You can catch Martin and the tenth ranked Cougars this evening going up against TCU on the road. Reed Harris — Wide Receiver — Arizona State A few weeks ago, I discussed Rutgers wideout K.J. Duff. The reason for doing so was to find a prospect at the X position for Denver given Courtland Sutton’s age and salary cap situation. As the collegiate season continues, I’ll keep my eyes peeled on prospects that line up with that. Arizona State’s Reed Harris fits the bill. Harris started his career at Boston College back in 2023. He didn’t play much as a freshman but became a full-time starter for the Eagles in 2024 and hauled in 17 receptions for 481 yards and four touchdowns. Yes, you read that right. That’s a 28.6 yard per catch average. In 2025, he notched 39 catches for 673 yards and five touchdowns. For his senior season, he transferred to Arizona State to play for the Sun Devils. Through three games, the wideout has 19 catches for 374 yards and 5 touchdowns and is on pace to break all his collegiate high totals. He is big at 6’5” and 220 pounds and has sneaky agility for a guy his size and the ability to dominate with contested catches. Overall, Harris is just an explosive playmaker with great hands and quality traits. That’s worth monitoring as the season progresses. Everyone knows Head Coach Sean Payton loves big wide receivers. I’m sure once he gets to the prospect evaluation process, he will be a big fan of #3. You can catch Harris in action late this evening when the Sun Devils host Baylor. Quincy Rhodes Jr. — Defensive End — Arkansas The Broncos have invested multiple Day 2 selections the past two drafts to select Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim to add to their defensive front seven. It’s still early in their careers, but we honestly haven’t seen anything at all from them to date. That’s a little bit worrisome even with Denver’s depth at the position group. A player I was high on last year, but also opted to return to college for his senior season was Arkansas defensive end Quincy Rhodes Jr . At 6’6″ and 275 pounds, Rhodes boasts tantalizing size and an elite wingspan that helps him with his pass rush and getting after opposing quarterbacks. Last season, he led the Razorbacks with 8 sacks and 15.5 tackles for loss—proving he is a disruptive force against the run and the pass. His alignment versatility is one of the reasons I like him as a fit for Denver in Vance Joseph’s defense. He has played all over Arkansas’ defensive front and been extremely disruptive. Rhodes still isn’t the sum of all his parts, but he has elite physical traits that are worth betting on. So far, he already has two sacks on the season. If he continues to develop, he seems like an easy bet to hear his name called in the Top 64 picks next April. I can imagine a lot of NFL defensive line coaches pounding the table for a prospect who has a lot of untapped potential. You can catch Rhodes in action this evening when the Razorbacks head on the road to face Texas A&M in an SEC matchup.

title: Sean Payton gives high praise for 49ers coaching staff ahead of Week 4 matchup
summary: After decades of coaching in the National Football League, Denver Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton has seen a lot of coaches come and go. During his time with the New Orleans Saints in the NFC South—Payton became quite familiar with Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris—who will be leading the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Those […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 9: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers with Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos after the game at Levi's Stadium on August 9, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. The Broncos defeated the 49ers 30-9. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images After decades of coaching in the National Football League, Denver Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton has seen a lot of coaches come and go. During his time with the New Orleans Saints in the NFC South—Payton became quite familiar with Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris—who will be leading the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Those two men, as well as a quality roster of players, stand in the way of the Broncos’ pursuit of third straight victory. Under their guidance, the 49ers are undefeated to start their 2026 season. San Francisco sports both a Top 5 offense and defense and appear to be a championship caliber squad. Yesterday after practice, Payton had a lot of praise for Shanahan, who is in his tenth season leading the 49ers. “There are so many things he does well. He—like his father—it started with an elite run-game plan. That hasn’t changed. Some of the play-actions that come off of that run game, I can recall snaps in Atlanta where Matt Ryan is extending the ball, and then all of the sudden pulls it up, and you look down the field and there’s somebody wide open,” recalled Payton with respect to memories of Shanahan over the years. “That’s just one element of what makes him special. I think that balance relative to run and pass. We had a number of years together in the division, and then over the years as he’s become a head coach and you’re at Owners Meetings and Combines. I’m close with his father. We have a great relationship.” Shanahan has done well calling plays and leading the 49ers’ offense. They are near the top of the league in points scored and have been incredible on third down and in the red zone. When it matters most, Shanahan’s players have been executing at a high level. As Payton mentioned, the running game is front and center of Shanahan’s offensive game plans. This year, they have one of the best ground games in the NFL with Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-round pick Kaelon Black. If Denver hopes to win on the road, they can’t let McCaffrey and Black run wild over their defense. On top of that, their passing offense has been incredibly efficient too. Bringing back Deebo Samuel was a good choice by their front office. Moreover, adding Mike Evans at wide receiver has really opened things up for fifth-year quarterback Brock Purdy in the passing game. Purdy leads the NFL with 9 touchdowns and only one interception and has yet to be sacked through three games. What Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph has in store to contain the 49ers’ high-powered offense is anyone’s best guess. Without question, it will certainly be quite the chess-match for Joseph, who has had his fair share of battles against Shanahan over the years. On offense, the Broncos are still trying to find their way. They’ve looked much better in the second half in their back-to-back comeback victories. Unfortunately, their overall efficiency and productivity have been hampered by slow starts. Denver hasn’t been able to run the ball well consistently, are struggling converting third downs, and have had too many penalties and turnovers early on in games. It’s not a recipe for success and something the Broncos will have to figure out in short order to be top-tier competitors the rest of the season. This Sunday, Payton and Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb hope to establish an operable game plan that can combat one of the league’s best defenses coached by Morris. The 49ers allowed just 20 points in their first two contests but had issues stopping the run and getting pressure in their Week 3 win against the Cardinals. “He’s done a real good job defensively. They’re playing real good red-zone defense. They present a lot of problems,” remarked Payton. “There’s so much more film that we’re all looking at. We all see it. The defense was different. This goes all the way back to when he was at Tampa. I’ve known Raheem for ages. Joint practice here with the Rams. He was in Atlanta. He’s a tremendous coach with great juice,” added Payton. Sunday’s matchup will be a huge test for the Broncos. The 49ers a well-coached team with a roster stacked with quality players all across the board. In order to achieve a victory, Payton and his staff are going to be at their best. Which coaching staff will come up with the better game plan? You’ll just have to tune in and find out.

title: Broncos will have extreme heat to contend with vs. 49ers
summary: The Denver Broncos had a rough time at it on the road in Kansas City when the area was experiencing a hot and humid weather event. Now in Week 4 they’ll be on the road again to play the San Francisco 49ers and it may end up being the hottest temperature in that stadium’s history […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton looks on in the fourth quarter during a game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos had a rough time at it on the road in Kansas City when the area was experiencing a hot and humid weather event. Now in Week 4 they’ll be on the road again to play the San Francisco 49ers and it may end up being the hottest temperature in that stadium’s history with kickoff looking to be in the mid to low 90s. “92 [degrees], yes,” Head coach Sean Payton said today when asked about the heat. “The old stadium was by the water, and it could get real cool. This one’s 45-50 minutes away. We’ll have all the plans in the place.” I wouldn’t normally worry about it, but its actually rare for Denver to be playing in heat like this. I had to go back to 2024 to a game in Tampa for a temperature at 85 degrees. They won that game. However, the only two games where kickoff was above 90 since 2024 appears to be the Week 1 loss to the Chiefs and this upcoming game. One area the Broncos have struggled has been with time of possession. If that continues in this game, I do not believe the defense will be able to stay fresh enough in the heat to keep this game close. That is where the problem lies, in my opinion. Bo Nix and the offense has to keep their drives sustained to have a chance here. Broncos daily recap No Bull Perspective: Early season woes The Broncos early game woes have more to do with the offensive line and running backs than Davis Webb or Bo Nix. Scouting the Enemy: San Francisco 49ers The Denver Broncos head on the road to battle the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Here is a deeper look at their Week 4 opponent. Broncos know they need to start faster before slow starts catch up to them The Broncos have overcome slow starts dating back to last season, but they know they can’t keep up this trend. Potent quotables Sean Payton On appearing on ESPN’s ManningCast during Monday Night Football and the 20th anniversary of the reopening of New Orleans’ Superdome after Hurricane Katrina “It doesn’t feel like 20 years, so I’ve probably already done three visits on it. There were so many things… I don’t know that any player or coach on that team when everyone kind of got there could expect what all of it was going to mean. I do remember this though, training camp was away because of facilities. It was a long training camp— it was seven weeks in Jackson, Mississippi. The preseason games, four at the time, our home games were Shreveport (Louisiana) and in Jackson. So it felt like you were gone forever. Then when we got back and started the regular season, it was at Cleveland, close win, at Green Bay, came back and won a big game. So a lot went into that. Atlanta was 2-0, we were 2-0 and that was really our first time just playing in that facility. So we went over there Friday night to get a practice in to get used to the lights and everything. But even with all that being said, as much as you try as a coach to prepare for what the environment’s going to be like, it’s hard to do that. So that was unique. We were going to rush one of the punts, and it just so happened on the first series, we get the three-and-out. We almost recover a fumble on third down, and it goes out of bounds. [Former Saints Special Teams Coordinator] John Bonamego said, ‘You want to rush the first one?’ I said, ‘Go ahead.’ [Former Saints S Steve] Gleason, his timing, those things [have] got to be hit just right. [It was] probably the loudest, it would be the loudest I’ve ever heard for a period of five minutes, and there was so much more to it than just football. So I think the feeling from a team standpoint is it’ll only be special if we win it though. So that was an important division game at that time with those two teams, both 2-0. So yes, all good.” On the atmosphere during the Saints’ first home game after Hurricane Katrina “It was a much bigger… There were so many other people that maybe normally wouldn’t be at a Saints game. Then there was a lot of symbolism, obviously, as the first event back there at a place that was literally broken. Yes, there’s nothing, like I said, none of us could have envisioned what was going to become of that season.” On if he ever watches the ManningCast “I don’t. We’re game planning, so I’m on for a brief period of time. I was fired up when [Pro Football Hall of Fame QB] Peyton [Manning] said that they were paying half a million dollars to each guest. (Laughs) I’m kidding. Yes, all good. Both Peyton, [former NFL QB] Eli [Manning], Cooper [Manning] all grew up and went to high school there. I got real close to their family when I got hired. [Former NFL QB] Archie [Manning] and Olivia [Manning] are still there, and of course Cooper and his wife. But usually on Mondays, and this will be just a step away and then go back into meetings. I know it’ll be a meaningful game for the city.” On the growth he has seen from G Quinn Meinerz “It starts with—a lot of things with him, his athleticism is rare. So then you put that with the work ethic, the toughness. It wasn’t long ago, I remember looking at the draft stuff, and then every once in a while you’ll get some video and he was running through the woods with a tree on his back. You separate yourself when one of those videos comes out. I’ve seen a guy jump out of a swimming pool, land on the concrete with two feet. So I’d always remember, You’re the guy that jumped out of the swimming pool.’ But besides that, holy cow. I think a lot of it’s just his passion. He loves football, loves his teammates. It’s contagious, but you have to be a real good athlete at that size to do the stuff he’s doing.” On whether the team highlights film of the offensive line in team meetings “Yes, we’ll pull them up every once in a while. Obviously it’s the most important position in your building because it can permeate the building if you’ve got the right group. He’s certainly a huge part of that.” On if G Quinn Meinerz’s block on Rams DE Aaron Donald was shown this week “No, I think there’s enough social media clips of it. Look, there’s a lot of respect for him, but we’ve all seen those clips of great defensive linemen or great offensive linemen. If they get leverage the right way, you’ve seen [Pro Football Hall of Fame DT] Reggie White lift a tackle in the air. When you play this game long enough, you’re probably going to be on both ends of that, and that’s why they’re the elite Pro Bowl All-Pro players at their level and you don’t get surprised when you see it.” On what stood out about T Mike McGlinchey when evaluating him ahead of his first free agency in Denver “[He’s] smart, tough. We had a clear vision for right tackle. We had seen it. Both he and [G] Ben [Powers] were key targets for us because we wanted that position room to really take on a completely new group, if you will, some of the guys that are here or that were there starting. So we each had a vision for what they did really well. [T] Mike [McGlinchey] has great pedigree. He’s a healthy player, it’s important to him, he’s played in big games, he’s won. That trait when you’re coaching, and game planning, and you know exactly what you’re going to get from a player is a real good trait. It’s much more difficult if you don’t know week-to-week what you’re going to get. So with Mike, you do know what you’re going to get and it’s a good thing.” On facing 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw “He’s such a passionate player. [I’m] a huge fan and it’s why we signed him. He got nicked up, and the injury bug was something that he was fighting, but just that process of getting to know him and him being here, I feel like we’re better for it. He’s exactly what you’re looking for in a football player, not any position specific, but it’s all football.” On what they…

title: No Bull Perspective: Early season woes
summary: In the comments section of my most recent No Bull Review, we were talking about the offensive line play and how it has been a little subpar compared to what we saw from them last season. I think that point is worth dissecting a bit, as the media and community have been harping quite a […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Denver Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb looks on during the second quarter of the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the comments section of my most recent No Bull Review , we were talking about the offensive line play and how it has been a little subpar compared to what we saw from them last season. I think that point is worth dissecting a bit, as the media and community have been harping quite a bit on Davis Webb and Bo Nix without noticing the problem in the trenches so far this season. It is early in the season – keep that in mind As a fan, I think it is worth a reminder that every season there is a reset button that is hit. Teams have fewer preseason games to play, more restrictions on how much practice time the players can be involved in, and don’t really tackle that much until the season gets going. Tackling is a great example. Our defense looked like a bunch of noobs in Week 1 against the Chiefs. But since then, we’ve not seen anything like the level of ineptitude from the defense. They are using much smarter angles and are making sure to wrap up. I do think some fair criticism can be laid at the feet of the coaching staff on this point, but it isn’t like Sean Payton hasn’t been mentioning these things consistently in the past few years. He and his staff are aware of these issues and know they can do a better job. So what is the issue? It is easy enough to look at the last game we played and say, “Wow, this Denver offense sucks in the first half.” Then talk about the big media stories of the new playcaller or how Bo Nix isn’t good, blah blah blah. I’m sorry, but NFL football is far more nuanced than that. That offense has 11 players needing to execute in order to make plays work. 3rd downs are key, and they really have had trouble producing on those downs. If you want to really get to the root of the offense’s woes, you will need to dig a little deeper. Is it because Webb sucks at calling plays? He’s a new playcaller for sure. He absolutely has made mistakes in each game this season. I haven’t liked some of his play calls for sure as well (not that that matters…what Dragonslayer69 thinks in his Mom’s basement eating Cheetos and drinking Mountain Dew means about as much as Chris Collinsworth’s takes on pass interference calls). Do you know who else consistently made mistakes calling plays? Sean Payton in every game I’ve watched since he joined the Broncos. Sean calls way too many screens. He also gets away from the run way too quickly and forgets to go back to it. He is also one of the best play callers this league has ever seen, with stones the size of boulders. Always keep in mind our human brains are designed to hold onto negative things and ignore things that are going well. So yeah, you might kinda think Davis Webb sucks because of a number of play calls you can recall that were bad. But let’s dig a little deeper and be better analysts out here in Broncos Country. Remember the good stuff Webb has called. He’s had far more good calls than bad and is likely to only get better with experience. The offensive line has work to do Many of the problems we’re seeing from this team early in games have to do with how the offensive line is executing. We’ve seen right tackle Mike McGlinchey get owned quite a few times early, costing the offense undue pressure. We’ve seen the line also be fairly poor at run blocking. At the end of last season, I was harping on how often I saw huge holes for our backs who either didn’t see them or couldn’t get past an arm tackle to use them to any great effect. I’m not seeing those same huge holes so far this season. I also recall that I didn’t see much of them early last season either. It takes good blocking from the line and good running from the backs for the run game to really have an impact. The running backs don’t look good We’ve honestly had some poor luck with injuries early this season in the running back room. Jonah Coleman has a high ankle sprain, JK Dobbins had a hip and hamstring issue, and RJ Harvey also had a hamstring issue. Thankfully, none of these are major. That being said, Dobbins looked like a shell of his normal self running last week. I do not think he was anywhere close to 100%. We already know RJ Harvey isn’t the back you treat like a bell cow and run between the tackles on repeat. That’s not his forte. I’m really excited about Coleman, but that ankle is keeping him from being the guy to step in and help get the offense on track. Without a good run game, the pass game gets extra pressure Until this team sorts out how to effectively run the ball, they are going to have trouble passing well when they need to early in games. In each game, your team usually scripts a bunch of plays. All of these help inform the offense about how the opponent is going to play them. So early in football games, there are a lot more questions for your playcaller and quarterback. They don’t have as many reads on what to expect, so the play call, pre-snap reads, and post-snap read time needed all get tougher. But a run game peeling off 4-6 yards a pop solves all some of those problems. It forces defenses to get out of their 2-high shells and bring down help to stop the run. For some opponents, this will also mean more man looks in the passing game. That makes reads easier. That makes completing passes easier if we get mismatches (which we do quite often and consistently…thank you, Payton and Webb). The No Bull Solutions The first thing the team needs to do is address the run-blocking woes the same way they addressed the poor tackling earlier this season: drill it. Spend time during your week doing the boring work of blocking up your run plays and coaching up techniques. Don’t force it, but get your backs healthy. This is a no-brainer step and one you can’t really do much to speed up. Our training staff is one of the best in the league, so I know they are all over getting our guys right. Finally, shake up the early game plan a bit. Too often, the early calls are passes 5 yards deep at most. We’re running on first down in predictable personnel groups. Let’s design some intermediate quick throws as our early plays to help set up the run. Quick outs and slants come to mind here. Play action on some of those early downs that teams are keying in on as runs. What does Broncos Country think? Hit up the comments and let us know what you think the issues are. Does Bo Nix kinda just suck early? Do we have the right backs? Should we just all go out of the gate not giving any hoots, like Smokin Jay Cutler?

title: Scouting the Enemy: San Francisco 49ers
summary: The Denver Broncos trek to the West Coast to take on the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. At 3-0, the 49ers are one of the only undefeated teams in the NFL. They boast a high-scoring offense and well-rounded defense and present a tough matchup for the Broncos. Here is a deeper look at Denver’s Week […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers' head coach Kyle Shanahan talks with Brock Purdy in 1st quarter during Niners' 30-13 win over New England Patriots during NFL game at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., on Sunday, September 29, 2024. (Photo by Scott Strazzante/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) The Denver Broncos trek to the West Coast to take on the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. At 3-0, the 49ers are one of the only undefeated teams in the NFL. They boast a high-scoring offense and well-rounded defense and present a tough matchup for the Broncos. Here is a deeper look at Denver’s Week 4 opponent. 2025 San Francisco 49ers Season Review The 49ers finished their 2025 regular season with a 12-5 record earning second place in the NFC West. They lost to the Seattle Seahawks in a blowout during the NFC Divisional Playoff Round. 2026 San Francisco 49ers Offseason Additions and Departures The 49ers made a few big moves in free agency to bolster their offense and defense. They brought in longtime veteran wide receiver Mike Evans to be a high-volume target for quarterback Brock Purdy. Another move at the position was bringing back Deebo Samuel who spent the ‘25 season with the Washington Commanders. On defense, another reunion took place. Inside linebacker Dre Greenlaw to pair with Fred Warner after his one-year stint with the Broncos last season. They also made a trade to bolster their defensive trenches sending a third-round pick to the Dallas Cowboys for versatile defensive lineman Osa Odighizuwa. In the 2026 NFL Draft , the 49ers were aggressive moving up for Ole Miss wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling at the top of the second round. Unfortunately, he suffered an ankle injury in the first week of the season and is expected to be out until late in the year. A pair of defenders, Texas Tech’s Romello Height and Oklahoma’s Gracen Halton are starting on their defensive front seven. Though it appears Height will be out this week against Denver. Third-round running back Kaelon Black is performing well in his split opportunities at running back, with 107 yards on 25 carries thus far. Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Brock Purdy Brock Purdy is off to a great start with the 49ers. Purdy has been one of the most efficient and accurate quarterbacks in the league to start the season. He touts a 72-percent completion percentage and 9 touchdowns to just 1 interception thus far. The 49ers red zone and third down offense have also been incredible. Without question, the fifth-year quarterback isone of the NFL’s most underrated signal callers. In addition to being extremely accurate in the pocket, Purdy does a masterful job on play action and making throws on the move. When you couple that with his underrated ability to use his legs, he needs to be considered as a dual threat at quarterback. He can scoot when the opportunity presents itself. Limiting his impact will be mission critical if the Broncos want to escape San Francisco with a victory. The 49ers offensive line has done an incredible job protecting him. He hasn’t been sacked at all through three games. Without edge rusher Jonathon Cooper and John Franklin-Myers, the Broncos haven’t been getting as much pressure on opposing quarterbacks. Vance Joseph’s defense needs to dial up the heat and figure out a way to get to the quarterback on a more consistent basis. Defensive X-Factor: Linebacker Fred Warner One of the best inside linebackers in the NFL, Fred Warner is looking to rebound this season after playing in only six games last year. So far, so good for Warner. He is off to a ferocious start, posting 33 tackles, a half sack, and two forced fumbles over the course of San Francisco’s first three games. The four-time All-Pro and Pro-Bowl linebacker is my key player for them on defense. In his ninth season in the league, he is still performing at an elite level. His coverage remains sound and that’s an area he has excelled at with ten career interceptions. Additionally, he remains one of the best run defenders at the position. He’s a star player the Broncos will certainly be aware of. Denver needs their running game to work well in order to achieve a victory. Warner has a penchant for making plays in the backfield and gets downfield in a hurry shooting the gaps. Denver’s offensive line will need to be at their best to give J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey good running lanes to get through. They can’t let Warner ruin their running game endeavors. If that happens, that will put even more pressure on Bo Nix to try and win the game through the air. How the Broncos can secure a victory over the 49ers This road game is another big challenge for the Broncos who have one of the toughest first half of the season schedules in the NFL. My keys to the game on defense are stopping their running attack, limiting Purdy’s impact, but also finding a way to create turnovers. Denver’s defense has done a great job thus far in that regard—posting four turnovers in three games. On offense, the Broncos have to start off hot. The three-and-outs, constant penalties, and poor third down rate are absolutely crushing their offensive potential. This is a week Bo Nix needs to stand out and perform at a high level throughout the game. Their defense is pretty staunch, and he has struggled facing zone coverage. It will be interesting to see how they plan to attack the 49ers. If they can accomplish most of those things, they’ll have a great shot at winning. A lot of folks are picking the 49ers, but I think Denver’s back-to-back comeback victories have given them a lot of confidence and swagger. I expect this to be a close game with Denver prevailing. Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 24, 49ers 20.
