title: 5 Questions with Hogs Haven: The Tea on Colts vs. Commanders in London
summary: In Week 4 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will travel to London to take on the Washington Commanders. Knowing the party was crossing the Atlantic I sat down with Andrew York (eboracum) of Hogs Haven, SB Nation’s Washington Commanders blog. We swapped questions and answers about both the Commanders and Colts and what follows is […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Sonny Styles #52 of the Washington Commanders celebrates his play against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 4 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will travel to London to take on the Washington Commanders. Knowing the party was crossing the Atlantic I sat down with Andrew York (eboracum) of Hogs Haven , SB Nation’s Washington Commanders blog. We swapped questions and answers about both the Commanders and Colts and what follows is what I’ve learned about this week’s enemy. You can find my answers to his questions here. Chris Shepherd: Based on the first three weeks of the season, if you were an offensive coordinator tasked with creating a game plan to attack the Commanders defense, what does your plan look like? What areas of the field are you attacking, what weaknesses are you targeting? How do you beat this Commanders defense? Andrew York: Well, I’ll start by saying the defense is run by Daronte Jones (not Dan Quinn) and borrows primarily from the Brian Flores defense of the Vikings. It features lots of blitzing, lots of simulated pressures, misdirection, and a complex zone coverage that allows players from any part of the field to either blitz or drop back into coverage. You might normally expect such a defense to be best against the pass, but it is actually strongest at stopping the run, as the last-minute movements and misdirection play havoc with run-blocking keys. As a result, the Commanders are allowing the 3rd-fewest rushing yards (just ahead of the 4th-ranked Vikings) and no rushing TDs so far this season. Where the defense has been weak is against explosive passing plays. I think this is for a few reasons:. 1) the DBs are probably the team’s weakest position group, 2) the complex and shifting zone responsibilities lead to coverage busts by players new to the system, and 3) the scheme just prioritizes sending more people at the QB, which leaves less help on the backend. Due to all of this, my gameplan to attack this defense would be to air out the ball as much as possible. Play 3- or even 4-WR sets (forcing Washington’s worst personnel on the field) and layer their routes to hit all areas of the field, expecting a coverage bust somewhere. I’d particularly target Mike Sainristil in coverage, who has had a rough season and has been relegated to primarily slot CB responsibility. The trick here is to protect your QB well enough to enable him to have time to throw. Dallas and Seattle had good enough pass protection that they could air out the ball to the tune of 279 passing yards and 379 passing yards against us respectively. As a primarily zone defense, the Commanders can also struggle against running QBs, as Jalen Hurts demonstrated in week 1. I know Daniel Jones can make plays with his legs, so using some read option might make sense too. Chris Shepherd: Last week Washington turned in the most surprising upset of the season so far, beating the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks, 33 to 31. Just looking at the stats of that game, the average person might assume Sam Darnold’s 379 yards passing and four touchdowns would have propelled Seattle over Marcus Mariota’s 183 yard, three touchdown performance but the final score tells a different story. How did the Commanders pull off the upset and do you think those results will be repeatable with Mariota at quarterback? Andrew York: Well the biggest reason is that Washington didn’t give up any turnovers while securing three turnovers that got converted to TDs (including a pick six). It’s a lot easier to score TDs on a short field set up by your defense and that accounted for 20 of Washington’s 33 points (there was a missed extra point). To add a bit more depth to the answer, despite several key injuries, players were executing at a higher level than in previous weeks, which I mostly attribute to good coaching and players on both sides of the ball being more comfortable in new systems. It is also worth noting that both of Washington’s playcallers (OC David Blough and DC Daronte Jones) are new to playcalling in the NFL and I think they’ve had a bit of a learning curve. Although the team lost Jayden Daniels to injury the previous week, Marcus Mariota is one of the better backup QBs in the NFL and has a similar playstyle to Jayden (mobile QB who can read the field well), so the playbook didn’t have to change much to accommodate him. The turnover differential may have been a bit flukey, but I do have confidence in Mariota to continue to play well and lead the team to victory if the defense can continue to keep games within reach. Chris Shepherd: Given that Jayden Daniels might miss week four’s game, I was curious about Washington’s ground game without him. In total the Commanders have rushed for a very solid 396 yards (8th most) on 96 attempts, good for 4.1 yards per carry (ranked 16th in the league) in the first three weeks of the season. If you remove Daniels’ 100 yards on 12 carries, the Commanders drop to 296 rushing yards on 84 carries and a rough 3.5 YPC. Last week’s win over the Seahawks saw the Commanders rush 32 times for 82 yards (a 2.6 YPC average). Is this a concern for Washington’s offense moving forward or did the Seahawks just do a good job bottling up an otherwise decent rushing attack? Andrew York: It’s a bit of a concern and I think there are a few things going on here. First, the OL is decimated by injury right now. LT Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps in Training Camp, forcing the team to move LG Brandon Coleman to LT and weakening both positions. Also, RG Sam Cosmi has been out with a concussion sustained in week 2 (he will not fly to London either). To account for Cosmi’s injury, C Nick Allegretti has moved to RG and Lucas Patrick (signed to the team 2 weeks ago) is starting at Center. So not only has the OL lost its two best players to injury, but 4 players are having to shuffle around to accommodate it. They have still played as a well-coached unit, but that much change has to hurt the run blocking. In addition, it’s not like Washington has sunk a lot of resources into the RB room. The two RBs likely to play significant snaps are Jacory Croskey-Merritt (goes by Bill Merritt) and Rachaad White. Bill is an explosive between-the-tackles runner, but weak in pass protection and as a pass catcher and was a 7th-round pick in 2025, so understood to be a bit of a developmental player. White is a much better pass-catching and pass-protecting back, but used a lot less between the tackles and not great at running through contact and a bit of a journeyman RB. So neither are complete backs or difference makers by themselves and can be a bit easy to gameplan against. Worth noting the team just signed RB Austin Ekeler. It’s unlikely he’ll play this week, but he’d add an explosive element while also being a good pass catcher and pass protector if he is ready to suit up. Chris Shepherd: Can you give me one player on offense and one on defense that Colts fans might not be familiar with who you expect to have an impact on Sunday night? Andrew York: On offense, I’ll go with RT Josh Conerly Jr. He was the 29th pick of the 2025 NFL draft and although he had a bit of an up-and-down rookie season, he got better as the season went on. He’s continued to build on that momentum and has looked like the best player on the OL right now (with Tunsil and Cosmi sidelined). He didn’t allow a single pressure against a great Seahawks pass rush and looks like the best healthy run blocker on the OL. On defense, I’ll go with CB Amik Robertson. He’s a 5’9″ stick of dynamite who flies all over the field making plays and had 6 total tackles, 4 passes defended, and a critical forced fumble against the Seahawks last week. He gave up 3 catches for 46 yards and a TD against Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but didn’t allow a single catch against any other Seahawks…
author: Chris Shepherd

title: A look back at the Colts’ international game history
summary: The Colts are heading overseas again. Indianapolis will face the Washington Commanders in London in Week 4, marking the franchise’s fourth regular-season international game and its third trip overseas in the last four seasons. What once felt like a rare event has quietly become a fairly regular part of the Colts’ schedule. The franchise has […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 02: Members of the armed forces hold the national flags of the United Kingdom and the United States before the start of the during the NFL game between Indianapolis Colts and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 2, 2016 in London, England. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Colts are heading overseas again. Indianapolis will face the Washington Commanders in London in Week 4, marking the franchise’s fourth regular-season international game and its third trip overseas in the last four seasons. What once felt like a rare event has quietly become a fairly regular part of the Colts’ schedule. The franchise has played internationally before in the preseason, including a 2005 American Bowl matchup against the Falcons in Tokyo, but the more interesting history begins with the regular-season games. The Colts have already played in London, Frankfurt and Berlin, and they enter this weekend with a 2-1 record outside the United States. Here is a look back at how those regular season games played out before Indianapolis returns to London. 2016: Jaguars 30, Colts 27 — London The Colts’ first regular-season international game came in 2016 against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium. Indianapolis fell behind 23-6 before making a late push, scoring three touchdowns in the fourth quarter and getting within three points. Andrew Luck threw for 234 yards and two touchdowns, but the comeback fell short as Jacksonville held on for a 30-27 win. It was also an AFC South game, which made the stakes a little different from the usual international matchup. The Colts were technically the road team and left London at 1-3 after a frustrating start to the season. The NFL’s international operation was still much smaller at the time. London games were becoming more common, but Germany had yet to enter the rotation and the league had not expanded its overseas schedule anywhere close to what it looks like today. For the Colts, it was their first taste of regular-season football abroad, and it ended with a loss. 2023: Colts 10, Patriots 6 — Frankfurt Seven years later, the Colts finally returned overseas, this time to Germany. The result was much better, even if the football itself was not particularly memorable. Indianapolis beat New England 10-6 in Frankfurt in one of the stranger games of the 2023 season. Gardner Minshew threw for only 194 yards, the Colts scored one touchdown and the two teams combined for just 16 points. Jonathan Taylor scored Indianapolis’ only touchdown, while the defense did most of the work. The Colts intercepted Mac Jones late in the fourth quarter before New England eventually turned to Bailey Zappe for its final possession. It was not pretty, but nobody asks how an international win looks afterward. The victory gave the Colts their first regular-season win outside the United States and evened their international record at 1-1. 2025: Colts 31, Falcons 25 (OT) — Berlin The Colts did not have to wait another seven years for their next trip. Indianapolis faced Atlanta in Berlin last season, playing in the first NFL regular-season game ever held in the German capital. Unlike the previous two international games, the Colts were the designated home team. This one was easily the most entertaining of the three. The game went to overtime tied at 25 before Indianapolis finished it with a touchdown to earn a 31-25 victory. The win improved the Colts to 2-1 internationally and gave them consecutive victories in Germany after the 2023 win in Frankfurt. It was also part of what has become a much larger NFL push into Europe. Germany has quickly become one of the league’s biggest international markets, and the Colts have now been involved in games in two different German cities. For a franchise that went seven years between its first and second regular-season international appearances, the trips have suddenly started piling up. 2026: Back to London If the previous three trips are any indication, expecting another close game would make sense. Every Colts regular-season international game has been decided by six points or fewer. They lost 30-27 to Jacksonville in 2016, beat New England 10-6 in Frankfurt and needed overtime to beat Atlanta 31-25 in Berlin last season. The settings have changed, the opponents have changed and the quality of football has certainly varied, but the Colts have never had an easy afternoon overseas. Even the 2023 Patriots game, which was not exactly an offensive showcase, stayed undecided until the final minutes. There is also an element of unpredictability that comes with these games. The travel schedule is different, the routine during the week changes and both teams are playing in an environment they do not normally experience during the season. That does not automatically make every international game close, but the Colts’ history suggests they have rarely been comfortable either way. Indianapolis comes into this one trying to build off its win over Houston after an 0-2 start, so another one-score game would hardly be surprising. The Colts have already played two tight games in the last two weeks, and their international history has followed the same pattern. Ten years after their first London trip, the Colts are back in England with a 2-1 regular-season international record and a chance to make it three straight wins overseas. Based on how their previous trips have gone, they may have to sweat through another one to get there.

title: Colts Week 3 Film Review: Tough Win vs. the Texans
summary: As I’ve had time to sit with Sunday’s result, I feel pretty much the same way as I did when the clock hit zero. Yes, the Colts finally won a game, but they won a game in a way that they haven’t in a long time. Ugly vs. a good team. The Anthony Richardson era […]
full_text: As I’ve had time to sit with Sunday’s result, I feel pretty much the same way as I did when the clock hit zero. Yes, the Colts finally won a game, but they won a game in a way that they haven’t in a long time. Ugly vs. a good team. The Anthony Richardson era featured some ugly wins, the Chicago and Miami games come to mind in 2024. But never have they won an ugly game vs. a good team. They’ve gotten out to hot starts before, but they’ve never made enough plays when it matters. Sunday, they finally did. Despite being 0-3, I think there’s a lot to be scared of when it comes to Houston… well their defense at least. Their defense absolutely came to play. It felt like the Colts had to earn every single yard. They were better up front, they wrecked havoc in the backfield, and really forced the Colts to play a certain way without Alec Pierce. Daniel Jones INT Colts go FIB and motion Downs to the Field to get the matchup they want on Bullock. Great defense. Poor decision to throw that while drifting backwards in the pocket. pic.twitter.com/aHTiDZhNoU — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 28, 2026 Daniel Jones had a plethora of turnovers vs. the Texans. The biggest issue that I’ve noticed is that he has been drifting backwards in the pocket and getting himself into trouble before he even throws the ball. Quarterbacks like Patrick Mahomes have elite arm strength to make some of the throws without hitching work, but even then it’s gotten him in trouble. Because your tackles don’t know where the launch point of the QB is, they think they’re riding the DE “around the hump” but actually just leading him right to the QB. My favorite play-call in all of football is Dagger. Used to call it constantly on Madden as a kid and have always loved seeing it run on Sundays. Colts went to Dagger on the late throw to Laquon Treadwell to set up the game-winning kick pic.twitter.com/XBhyETuSSk — Zach Hicks (@ZachHicks2) September 28, 2026 The Texans play a lot of vision zone or spot drop defense. They aren’t matching any routes or passing things off, they are just dropping to their landmarks in relation to where the QB’s eyes are. Jones was fantastic in this game in moving the hook defenders off their spot to create throwing windows— especially late in the game when it mattered most. I know the Texans are going through it, but they are so well coached and talented on defense. Reed Blankenship "Melting" in C3 when Daniel Jones starts by looking outside, and then holding his landmark when Jones work his eyes back inside. Eliminates the Downs crosser. pic.twitter.com/Sj0m2PWDO9 — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 30, 2026 Here’s a great example of what elite vision zone defense can do to a QB. Reed Blankenship is reading the eyes of Jones in Cover 3. Vision droppers are taught to drift their landmarks based on where the QB is looking. So when Jones works his eyes closer to the sideline, Blankenship “melts” outside. But if the QB looks right at you, you’re taught to hold your landmark. It’s very similar to the combine drill we see every February. 2nd Level RPO Stingley is carefully tracking Downs outside hip, since he knows Downs likes to work the other way after the catch to punish tacklers for overcommitting. But it doesn't even matter 😂 pic.twitter.com/tYsGzPtlEU — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 29, 2026 I thought Josh Downs was fantastic in this game. He is schematically limited as a player, only due to his size, but he owns his role as well as anyone in football. Downs is fantastic after the catch. Here the Colts are running a 2nd level RPO and running a glance route to put the WILL LB in conflict. Another Josh Downs completion on a three level vertical stretch concept. The impressive part is Downs natural feel after the catch. He has eyes in the back of his head at times pic.twitter.com/XVVSmSOv90 — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 29, 2026 Downs works back the other way after the catch on a lot of these in-breaking routes. I wonder how teams will start to defend that going forward. It definitely will affect how future players take angles in order to tackle him. Sometimes it doesn’t matter because Downs just has a natural feel for space, but he’s put this move on tape, so I think teams are going to be thinking about it all week. Some moments where the light just seems to go out for Daniel Gets to 5-0 protection which is great, but you don't have time vs. this front to be indecisive on whether you want to hit the snag on a concept you've read a million times in this offense. pic.twitter.com/cK0Xn0I2Gx — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 30, 2026 Some very weird reps in this game. The Colts are running Snag + Basic (a concept that the Colts have ran a million times with Jones, Minshew, Richardson, Flacco, you name it). The goal is to put a horizontal stretch on the curl-flat player. Is he going to take the RB fast to the flat or hang with the snag route. This is a clear read to get the ball to the RB in the flat. But Jones hangs on the snag route and then gets stripped sacked in a key point in the game. The defense had a bounce back game, but it’s important to take it with a grain of salt. A Nico Collinsless Texans offense is not explosive, and other than CJ Stroud being very accurate, they do nothing particularly well. They also essentially choked the game away when it mattered most in the 4th Quarter. Now granted, they deserve credit for hanging in there while losing the turnover battle… but Stroud did what Stroud has done in almost every matchup he’s had vs. the Colts. Made plays when they mattered most. Perfectly executed stunt. Adetomiwa Adebawore and DeForest Buckner look lightning fast on 3rd downs. Can't tell because of the stupid shadows, but looks like this could be an unreal throw from CJ Stroud. pic.twitter.com/ZXBA0JlFzj — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) October 1, 2026 I think the Colts can build on their third down sub package with Tomi and DeForest Buckner. Both of them are lightning quick off the ball. This is a perfectly executed stunt. Anytime you can get a free runner in an interior gap your chances of winning that down skyrocket When Justin Walley can line up with proper leverage pre-snap, he can be very sticky in man coverage. pic.twitter.com/enAhaFbRmt — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) October 1, 2026 I think Justin Walley is really building some confidence as a nickel corner. He’s gotten better every single week that he’s been out there. Look how sticky the Colts play man coverage on this rep. Granted, it hasn’t looked like that through the month of September, and part of that is lack of talent in the Texans WR room, but that’s how the Colts want to play defense. WHAT AM I LOOKING AT HEADING INTO WEEK 4? Heading into Week 4 I think the Colts have to find their identity on offense again. In order for the Colts to survive without Alec Pierce, they need to find someone, literally anyone, that can catch the ball down the field. Right now, it’s really hard to chase explosives when you don’t have any speed on the field. Safeties don’t have to play as deep, the coverage is compressed, and you can be way more aggressive in coverage. If they can lighten up some of these boxes, I believe Jonathan Taylor can be the guy who was almost guaranteed to rush for over 120 yards a weekend. Burks is a guy that I’m looking at. He’s been their jet motion/sweep player. He has speed but doesn’t have the route or target equity for defenses to truly respect it. I think that will have to change very soon. Defensively, I think the Colts need to preform well this weekend in order to feel confident about them moving forward. You’re playing a backup QB without any receivers that should challenge a corner that you gave up 2 first round picks for. I’m looking at the pass rush in this matchup. The interior pass rush has held up their end of the bargain, but I think it’s time for Laiatu Latu to start effecting the game. I don’t care what…

Final practice report for #INDvsWAS . pic.twitter.com/tzC0QsSzFO — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 2, 2026 Wide receiver Ashton Dulin (ankle) had been listed as QUESTIONABLE for Sundays game against the Commanders. title: Hopefully, the Colts remembered to pack their newfound defense
summary: Toiletries? Check. Clothes? Check. Identification? Check. There are a few travel essentials any time one leaves home for a trip. Going overseas can heighten the stress to ensure everything is in the suitcase before walking out the door because although you can probably pick up toothpaste at your final destination, doing so is a pain. […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 27: Justin Walley #27 of the Indianapolis Colts tackles Foster Moreau #87 of the Houston Texans during the first half of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Toiletries? Check. Clothes? Check. Identification? Check. There are a few travel essentials any time one leaves home for a trip. Going overseas can heighten the stress to ensure everything is in the suitcase before walking out the door because although you can probably pick up toothpaste at your final destination, doing so is a pain. The Indianapolis Colts won’t have the luxury of “picking up” a defense in London, so they better make sure the one we saw on Sunday came with them. Yes. That specific one. You can pack clothes for your trip, but are they the right type for the location and season? The Colts could bring any old defense. They could bring the one we saw Week 1 against the Ravens. That defense was gashed as much as a defense could be gashed. Poor tackling, a lack of containment, and huge plays created a painfully long afternoon. Bringing that defense would be like packing shorts for Antarctica. Sure, you can wear them, but good luck. The Colts need to ensure the defense we saw against the Texans is tucked between the underwear and socks. That defense featured DeForest Buckner creating havoc. That defense saw Justin Walley round into form after a dreadful start to the season. That defense had sacks and created pressure at the line of scrimmage. That defense can compete. That defense will be able to beat the Commanders on Sunday in London, regardless of who lines up at quarterback across from them. That is the only defense that gives the Colts a chance. Check it or stow it away in a carry-on, it doesn’t matter. Just don’t leave it behind. The Colts need the defensive mentality and intensity we saw last week. It was clean, aggressive, and in your face. That is the defense that is going to right the ship. Pull it out and iron it to get any last-minute wrinkles out. The defense needs to be sharp and ready to roll come Sunday morning.

His NFL journey has had 4 different stops since he lost the starting job to Ryan Tannehill mid-2019 season: The Las Vegas Raiders backup QB (2020-2021) 13 Game Starter with the Atlanta Falcons (2022) Backup QB for the Philadelphia Eagles (2023) Backup QB with the Washington Commanders, 8 starts in 2025 with Daniels injured (2024-present) Marcus Mariota helped lead the @commanders to a 100% chance of winning their first game of the season 📈 pic.twitter.com/zZ3qnShLwQ — NFL (@NFL) September 28, 2026 Since leaving the Titans, Mariota has appeared in 43 games (22 starts) and recorded some solid stats as a journeyman: 420/671 Passing = 62.6% Completion % 4,966 Passing Yards 7.4 Yards Per Attempts 35 Passing TDs 18 INTs 52 Sacks 91.3 Passer Rating 189 Carries 1,068 Rushing Yards 5.7 Yards Per Carry 8 Rushing TDs 16 Fumbles As both teams journey to London, England to face off at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Colts have an opportunity to beat an old foe once again and Mariota has a shot at redemption against one of his biggest obstacles from early in his career.

title: Chris Jones thinks the arrow is pointing up for Sack Nation
summary: Star defensive lineman and CEO of Sack Nation, a defensive subsidiary of their parent company, the Kansas City Chiefs, which specializes in security infiltration, spoke to media members Thursday afternoon. Jones admitted the early returns haven’t been what the company hoped for this fiscal year; so far this season, the Chiefs have accumulated only four […]
full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Star defensive lineman and CEO of Sack Nation, a defensive subsidiary of their parent company, the Kansas City Chiefs , which specializes in security infiltration, spoke to media members Thursday afternoon. Jones admitted the early returns haven’t been what the company hoped for this fiscal year; so far this season, the Chiefs have accumulated only four sacks. Jones acknowledged that Sack Nation has faced a unique set of circumstances while trying to achieve its ultimate goal: tackling the quarterback behind the line of scrimmage while he still has the ball in his hand. “We’re close, statistically-wise,” Jones told reporters. “You look at the numbers, the quarterback has been getting rid of the ball [in] 2.3 seconds. I don’t care how good of a pass rusher you are, when they’re throwing the ball that quick, it’s tough for anyone,” Jones explained. To make matters worse, he added that when the opposition holds onto the ball to take a shot downfield, they keep extra men back to bolster their line and prevent any incursion. “You got seven, eight men in there protecting,” Jones said. “So, it’s like, the opportunity is going to come. I think don’t waver from what we’ve been doing. We’ve done a lot of good. We put a lot of good on film. I think we stay committed to that and just find ways to get sacks out of it so y’all can stop writing about us in the media.” Chiefs DT Chris Jones on the D-Line's pressure and sack stats so far this season: "It gives y'all another week to write the Chiefs defensive lineman suck." #ChiefsKingdom pic.twitter.com/XNEPZCmg8y — Rob Collins (@RobCollinsTV) October 1, 2026 The job doesn’t get any easier this week, when Jones and his team take on the Las Vegas Raiders . The Raiders have only allowed five sacks through three games this season and are tied for the NFL lead in passing touchdowns with nine. Part of the Raiders’ success is also due to their quarterback, Kirk Cousins, getting the ball out of his hands quickly this season. Through Week 3, Cousins has the seventh-fastest time to throw in the NFL in 2026 at 2.58 seconds. The Chiefs will need to get home and pressure Cousins to disrupt his rhythm in the passing game. Not just because it will help Sack Nation improve its bottom line, but also because the alternative is another week of media stories about Sack Nation underperforming. “It’ll just give you another week to write about the Chiefs defensive linemen suck and why did you all pay me and George (Karlaftis).”

title: Chiefs News: Patrick Mahomes’ deep ball is back
summary: One reason the Kansas City Chiefs’ offense has failed to click on all cylinders in recent seasons is the lack of deep completions, throws of 20 or more yards in the air. It was hard to diagnose the main issue, but it seems quarterback Patrick Mahomes has found his groove in 2026 regardless. He is […]
full_text: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images One reason the Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense has failed to click on all cylinders in recent seasons is the lack of deep completions, throws of 20 or more yards in the air. It was hard to diagnose the main issue, but it seems quarterback Patrick Mahomes has found his groove in 2026 regardless. He is tied for the third-most “big-time throws” on deep passes this year despite ranking 20th in deep attempts, per Pro Football Focus . Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs have rediscovered the deep pass | ESPN Mahomes struggled much of last season to connect with his pass catchers on deep passes. He completed only 42 of his 101 attempts in which the ball traveled at least 15 yards. His 41.6% completion percentage ranked 19th in the league. Mahomes also threw more interceptions (five) than he had touchdowns (two) on such throws. The Chiefs’ deep-passing attack should be tested in Sunday’s game against the Raiders, who have created a league-high nine takeaways, including four interceptions. Jerry Jeudy has disappeared from Browns offense: Five teams that could trade for WR | CBS Sports Kansas City Chiefs While the Chiefs did not invest in any wide receiver help in the offseason, they have the look of an offense that could benefit from another weapon out wide or in the slot. Jeudy and Rashee Rice can both move around in the formation while Xavier Worthy remains a deep threat and YAC accumulator out wide. The depth in this group is minimal, and the top two have been just as active as pass-catchers as running back Kenneth Walker III and tight end Travis Kelce, so the wait for one of them to emerge as a go-to target continues (and may never end). With this team squarely back in the Super Bowl conversation, it needs to both maximize its wide receiver output and add insurance behind the starters in order to prevent late-season regression. Kansas City Chiefs DC Steve Spagnuolo dropped a grenade ahead of Week 4 vs. the Las Vegas Raiders, and fans have reason to worry | A to Z Sports “Well, we were on a course to kind of keep Chamarri (Conner) in one spot,” Spagnuolo said. “I don’t know if we’re still there now or not. Listen, both Jaden (Hicks) and Alohi (Gilman) have done an admirable job. They would have liked to have some plays back in the Miami game. Obviously, on those deep throws, and the one that we could have caught. But Chamarri, listen, I think I’ve said this before, but it seems like every year he’s been here and we’ve done cut-ups at the end of the season, and we’re looking through the film, 27 keeps showing up, making plays. So, hopefully we can get him back there doing that.” What Raiders players and coaches are saying about the Chiefs ahead of Sunday’s game | The Kansas City Star Defensive end Maxx Crosby on the Chiefs “They’re doing a really good job running the ball,” Crosby said. “They run a lot more than they have in the past, and Pat is playing really well, playing at a high level. Kelce’s been in the groove as well. They do a lot of things and they have a lot of speed on the field. You know, Xavier Worthy and those guys. So they offer a lot of different challenges. And when you have a guy like Andy Reid calling the plays and putting them in good positions, it offers a lot of challenges. Three Different Ways Chiefs Can Work to Ensure a Win vs. Raiders on Sunday | Sports Illustrated Opportunistic, aggressive and feisty would be three accurate terms to help describe this Las Vegas defense. Following Thursday Night Football , the Raiders still have at least a share of the league lead in forced turnovers (nine), made up of five fumble recoveries and four interceptions. According to TruMedia , Vegas is seventh in total turnover EPA with 10.73. The Chiefs have done a very respectable job protecting the rock thus far. Their plus-three turnover differential is tied for the fourth-best figure in the sport, and they’re in the upper half of the league with just a pair of giveaways (both interceptions by quarterback Patrick Mahomes). In hostile territory, not coughing up the rock would force Las Vegas’ offense to capitalize on a higher clip of its possessions. Around the NFL Tony Romo, CBS Sports part ways after July OWI arrest | The Athletic Romo, who said in a statement Friday that he is “proud” of what he accomplished at CBS Sports, worked alongside Jim Nantz since 2017. The pair called three Super Bowls together, most recently in 2024, and Nantz had said he hoped the two would become the “modern-day version” of Pat Summerall and John Madden. “I’m going to use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity,” Romo, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback, said in a statement released shortly after CBS’ announcement Friday. “I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans.” QB Tyson Bagent likely to start for Bears on Sunday vs. Jets | NFL Network “My understanding is that Tyson Bagent took the majority of the first-team reps at practice this week. While Ben Johnson has not yet named a starter, the expectation is that the backup quarterback, Tyson Bagent, is the starter on Sunday,” Rapoport said on Friday’s episode of The Insiders on NFL Network. “[Johnson] has not yet made it official. Certainly, Case Keenum would still be in the mix, especially after the heroics of last week, but it certainly seems like the direction they are going is going to be Tyson Bagent.” NFL trade rumors: Browns would ‘welcome deal at right price’ for Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, per report | CBS Sports According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the Browns “would probably welcome a deal at the right price” for one of their backup quarterbacks, given Watson’s early-season play. “I could see if they get the right offer for whoever it is, I think Taylen Green they’d like to keep as a developmental, so it would probably have to be Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel,” Fowler said Thursday. “I am not saying they’re definitely trading, I am saying they have the flexibility. This is very much a value-based team. The Browns are that more than any other.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Will the Chiefs’ pass rush return to form this week against the Raiders? This was already a relatively advantageous matchup for the Chiefs’ defensive line, and it looks like it’s getting better. Brandon Thorn of Establish The Run ranked the Chiefs’ defensive line vs. the Raiders’ offensive line as the fifth-biggest mismatch in the league this week. He has the Raiders rated as the 21st “best” offensive line in the league. The Chiefs rate as the fifth-best defensive line. full_text: Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Las Vegas Raiders in the late window of Week 4 games. We welcome Matt Holder of Silver and Black Pride — our sister SBNation site covering the Raiders— for Five Questions with the Enemy . In case you missed it, Matt took time to answer your questions in the Feed on Thursday morning. Check out his post for more enemy perspective. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Silver and Black community through Sunday’s game to get perspectives from both sides of the Week 4 matchup! 1. The Raiders have already matched their win total from last season and are 3-0 for the first time since 2021. How much has this start changed the expectations surrounding the team in Las Vegas A lot has changed in Vegas over the last three weeks. Heading into the season, I think even the most optimistic Raiders fan had the team topping out at eight or nine wins and sniffing the playoffs but falling just short. However, with an undefeated start and an opportunity to finish the first quarter of the season in first place for the AFC West, the postseason feels like it’s a more realistic possibility than it was at the end of August. To be fair, the Raiders were favored against the lowly Dolphins, and the 0-3 Chargers are a dysfunctional mess right now. On top of that, the Raiders are about to hit a gantlet in their schedule with the Chiefs, Patriots (on the road), Bills and Rams over the next four weeks. So, the upcoming stretch will tell us a lot about how much of a contender the Silver and Black really are. However, make no mistake about it: the franchise is taking a step in the right direction by separating itself from the bottom of the league, and the rebuild feels like it’s ahead of schedule. 2. Kirk Cousins leads the NFL with nine touchdown passes, and Brock Bowers returned against New Orleans with 10 catches for 116 yards and a touchdown. How does having Bowers back change what Klint Kubiak can do with this offense? Bowers’ return gives Cousins a go-to target and someone who can win in the intermediate range. The tight end was expected to be and is the centerpiece of Klint Kubiak’s offense, making it surprising that the Raiders were able to put up 53 combined points in the two games without him. But it’s no surprise that the offense had its best performance to date in his season debut last week. While they play slightly different positions, Kubiak is using Bowers similarly to how he deployed 2025 Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba with the Seahawks last year. Smith-Njigba would line up all over the place for Seattle, making it difficult for the defense to account for him since they didn’t know where he’d be, allowing Kubiak to scheme up favorable matchups. Bowers’ unique skill set, where he’s closer to being an X-receiver than a true tight end, allows that to happen. He actually took more snaps out wide or in the slot than he did in-line last week. As for Cousins, Vegas has a good deep threat in wide receiver Tre Tucker, who hauled in some shots down the field against the Chargers (five catches, 119 yards and a 40-yard touchdown). And running back Ashton Jeanty has been a decent check-down option — though he did have three drops in L.A. — and so can No. 2 tight end Michael Mayer. Meanwhile, Tucker is decent on intermediate routes, but his bread and butter is in the vertical passing game. That’s the void Bowers can fill with his route running and ability to beat man coverage, giving Cousins a weapon in all three areas of the passing game. 3. Ashton Jeanty has rushed for 206 yards on 63 carries—an average of 3.3 yards per attempt—and has yet to score a rushing touchdown. What has been the primary reason for his slow start on the ground? Jeanty is still 10th in rushing yards , and he had a 100-yard performance on the ground in Week 1. So, I wouldn’t 100% agree that he’s had a “slow start”, but the production over the last two games has certainly been underwhelming. In Los Angeles, the second-year back likely had flashbacks to his rookie season. The Raiders’ offensive line — more specifically, the interior three — had a tough time handling the Chargers’ defensive tackles and got punched in the mouth. For example, Pro Football Focus charted Jeanty with 54 yards after contact while he only rushed for 48 yards total. Last week was more on him, though, with 35 yards after contact and 56 total rushing yards. Jeanty suffered a sprained ankle at the end of training camp and might have reaggravated it against the Saints. The CBS broadcast team reported that he was getting his ankles taped (or retaped) mid-game, and he didn’t have the same explosion or lateral movement skills that we’ve seen from him in the past. So, I wouldn’t be surprised if rookie fourth-round pick Mike Washington Jr. gets more carries this week. Washington is a home-run hitter who has 15 carries for 102 yards (6.8 ypc) and scored his first NFL touchdown on a 36-yard scamper last week. The problem is that two runs have accounted for over half of the Arkansas product’s production, where he’s averaging just 3.7 ypc when removing those from the equation. So it remains to be seen if he can still be efficient with a bigger workload and more attention on him. 4. The Raiders’ defense has generated nine takeaways and 10 sacks through three games while creating pressure without relying heavily on the blitz. Can that defensive approach remain effective against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense? The Raiders finally have their version of Steve Spagnuolo with Rob Leonard getting promoted to defensive coordinator in the offseason. Like Spags, Leonard has been creating a lot of confusion for quarterbacks by constantly rotating coverage post-snap and dialing up simulated pressures or creeper blitzes. Las Vegas has also been running a lot of pattern-matching concepts to avoid getting put into bad matchups in the secondary, similar to what Spagnuolo does on the backend of the Chiefs’ defense. That gives me hope that the Silver and Black can continue to put pressure on Mahomes and force him into a mistake or two. However, the 10-year pro is the most experienced and best quarterback they’ve faced so far. Tyler Shough (12 career starts) and Malik Willis (six) have about a full season’s worth of starts between them. Meanwhile, Justin Herbert (98) played better against Las Vegas than his stat line suggests; the Chargers just had several drops and one play where a tight end had a PBU on a pass intended for his teammate (yes, you read that correctly). So, I’m optimistic that Leonard can force Mahomes to hold onto the ball and heat Mahomes up given how good Leonard’s scheme has been over the last three weeks. But, simultaneously, I’m realistic that he hasn’t put together a game plan and called plays against a quarterback of this caliber yet. We’ll have to see how it plays out on the grass! 5. With both teams entering Sunday’s game 3-0 and the early AFC West lead at stake, what is your prediction for how this matchup plays out? I’ll be honest with you: the Chiefs should win this game. Experience is on their side since they’ve been in games like this plenty of times over the last few years, and Kansas City certainly has the more talented roster from top to bottom. Hence why the Chiefs are favored on the road and have much higher expectations than the Raiders do this season. But screw all of that! Kubiak’s crew hasn’t given me a reason not to believe in them, so I’m going to be a homer and not bet against the Raiders until they prove me otherwise. Give me the Silver and Black, 35 to 31!
author: Maurice Elston

title: Madden Simulation Week 4: Chiefs visit Arrowhead West to play Raiders
summary: On Sunday, the (3-0) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road at Arrowhead West, taking on the (3-0) Las Vegas Raiders. Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 27. Note: The Chiefs Madden Simulation has predicted three correct Chiefs victories. First quarter The Las Vegas Raiders were able to pick up one […]
full_text: On Sunday, the (3-0) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road at Arrowhead West, taking on the (3-0) Las Vegas Raiders . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. Note: The Chiefs Madden Simulation has predicted three correct Chiefs victories. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here. First quarter The Las Vegas Raiders were able to pick up one first down on the ground with Ashton Jeanty, but back-to-back tackles for loss and a delay-of-game penalty forced the Raiders to punt. The Kansas City Chiefs’ first play was a pass to Tyquan Thornton for 44 yards to instantly flip the field. Thornton then proceeded to catch another pass over the middle for 24 yards. On fourth-and-three from the Raiders’ five-yard line, Patrick Mahomes dropped back and found Travis Kelce on a short comeback route in the end zone for a touchdown. The Raiders immediately went back to Jeanty, who broke off a 21-yard run before catching a 15-yard pass on a Texas route, juking Nick Bolton along the way. End of first quarter: Chiefs 7, Raiders 0 Second quarter Kicker Matt Gay drilled a field goal to open the quarter. The Chiefs started to gain first downs in chunks with a 15-yard run by Kenneth Walker, a 15-yard catch-and-run by Xavier Worthy, and a 13-yard catch by Travis Kelce. On third-and-eight, Tonka Hemingway got to Mahomes for a sack, ending the drive, and Harrison Butker connected on a field goal. The Raiders went three-and-out and punted back to the Chiefs. On third down, Mahomes hit Kenneth Walker on a corner route for 26 yards and a first down. The very next play, Mahomes connected with Worthy on a slant, and Worthy burned the man-coverage defender for a 42-yard touchdown. The Raiders picked up one first down, but the drive stalled on a sack by Nick Bolton, forcing the Raiders to punt back to the Chiefs with under a minute remaining. End of second quarter: Chiefs 17, Raiders 3 Third quarter Maxx Crosby sacked Mahomes on third down to force a Chiefs punt. Chris Jones ran through the middle untouched and sacked Kirk Cousins on third down, meaning A.J. Cole trotted out to punt. The Raiders had just 84 total yards with five minutes remaining in the third quarter. Worthy caught his second touchdown pass of the afternoon on a seven-yard slant route. The Chiefs were now up by three possessions. End of third quarter: Chiefs 24, Raiders 3 Fourth quarter Brock Bowers finally showed up with a 24-yard catch to get the Raiders to the Chiefs’ 44-yard line. A Khyiris Tonga sack pushed the Raiders out of field-goal range, and to add insult to injury, Chris Jones sacked Cousins on the next play. The Raiders turned the ball over on downs. The Chiefs punted back to the Raiders. On fourth down, Cousins tucked the ball and ran for 26 yards to convert a first down. A screen pass to Jeanty got the Raiders to the Chiefs’ 20-yard line. Chris Jones strip-sacked Cousins, and George Karlaftis scooped up the fumble. A 37-yard wheel-route connection from Mahomes to Walker put the Chiefs in the red zone. Emmett Johnson finished the drive with a six-yard touchdown run. End of the fourth quarter: Chiefs 31, Raiders 3 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 24 for 31 passing, 328 yards, 3 touchdowns Kenneth Walker: 5 rushing attempts, 25 yards, 4 receptions, 71 yards. Emmett Johnson: 4 rushing attempts, 17 yards, 1 touchdown. Xavier Worthy: 5 receptions, 74 yards, 2 touchdowns. Travis Kelce: 5 receptions, 42 yards, 1 touchdown. Tyquan Thornton: 4 receptions, 91 yards. Rashee Rice: 3 receptions, 33 yards. Nick Bolton: 8 tackles, 1 sack, 1 tackle for loss Chris Jones: 3 sacks Khyiris Tonga: 7 tackles, 4 tackles for loss, 1 sack Harrison Butker: 1 for 1, longest field goal 43 yards. Kirk Cousins: 12 for 21 passing, 114 yards, 26 yards rushing, Ashton Jeanty: 16 rushing attempts, 76 yards Brock Bowers: 3 receptions, 22 yards. Tonka Hemingway: 2 sacks Maxx Crosby: 1 sack Matt Gay: 1 for 1, longest field goal 41 yards. Next week the Chiefs are on a bye.

title: Chiefs-Raiders Week 4 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Las Vegas Raiders, our writers predicted the final score and result. For the second consecutive week, the Chiefs will play at a venue where quarterback Patrick Mahomes has delivered a Super Bowl […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Las Vegas Raiders , our writers predicted the final score and result. For the second consecutive week, the Chiefs will play at a venue where quarterback Patrick Mahomes has delivered a Super Bowl win. This time, the action unfolds at Allegiant Stadium — the site of Super Bowl LVIII. Kansas City currently sits as 4.5-point road favorites according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Few expected this Week 4 matchup to be a showdown between two of the NFL’s five remaining undefeated teams. The Chiefs dominated the Raiders in a Week 7 home matchup last season. They closed 2025 battered and broken and dropped the season finale to the Raiders at Allegiant. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) This will easily be the most hyped matchup in the Chiefs vs. Raiders rivalry in my years covering the team. The job Klint Kubiak has done through his first month on the job should be lauded. I expect the Raiders to play hard and give this moment their best shot. I also think both teams have the tools to exploit the opposing defense. The Raiders can frustrate Steve Spagnuolo’s crew with multiple tight ends that can be dangerous from the slot and a running back that can keep them out of obvious pass rush situations. The middle of the Las Vegas defense can be spotty, however, and I expect Kenneth Walker to have a big day knowing the Week 5 bye is ahead of him. I expect a high-scoring game where the Chiefs’ experience in winning close contests will show. Chiefs 34, Raiders 31 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) This game will end up holding quite a bit of weight at the end of the season if things continue going the way they have for each team. The Raiders are not perfect, but they are playing good football under a new coaching staff and, most importantly, finding ways to win games. They rely heavily on turnovers defensively, and offensively they rely heavily on Klint Kubiak’s offensive scheme, which is centered around a quick passing attack and solid ground game. The Chiefs are the more talented team, but the Raiders will come out on fire in front of their home crowd in this game. Offensively, the Chiefs will likely continue to lean on Kenneth Walker as well as the play-action passing attack to move the ball, which in turn should keep Patrick Mahomes firing at a high clip. Ball security will be at a premium for both teams. Chiefs 35, Raiders 21 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I think the Raiders are legit, but this is where the Chiefs remind everybody who still runs the AFC West. Kansas City has the No. 2 offense in football right now, Ken Walker is leading the league in rushing, and Mahomes has been dealing. The Raiders can get after the quarterback, but I trust Andy Reid and Mahomes to have an answer for Maxx Crosby, and I trust the Chiefs’ defense way more than I trust Kirk Cousins in a game this big. Give me KC to go into Vegas, hand the Raiders their first loss, and move to 4-0. Chiefs 31, Raiders 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) It has been a while since a Chiefs-Raiders matchup carried this much weight this early in the season. Both teams enter Week 4 at 3-0, and Las Vegas has been one of the league’s biggest surprises. I expect a tough battle, with Maxx Crosby presenting another major test for rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson. Denver already challenged him, but keeping Crosby from disrupting Patrick Mahomes will be critical. On the other side, Brock Bowers returned last week with 10 catches for 116 yards and a touchdown. Steve Spagnuolo will need a coverage plan that keeps him from exploiting mismatches against Kansas City’s linebackers and safeties. Ultimately, I don’t think the Raiders have enough depth to beat the Chiefs. If Kansas City keeps building around the running game and play-action, it can keep Las Vegas’ defense guessing and give Mahomes opportunities to attack. I expect big games from both Mahomes and Travis Kelce, with Kelce reminding everyone that he still belongs among the league’s best tight ends in his 14th season. Containing Bowers will be the biggest defensive key. Both teams will put points on the board, but I trust Kansas City to make more plays when it matters. Chiefs 35, Raiders 24 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) This one could be fun. It’s been a long time since we could call the Raiders an actual ‘rival’. They simply haven’t been on the same level. But perhaps the tide is turning with the trio of Kirk Cousins, Ashton Jeanty, and Brock Bowers. Clint Kubiak has these guys playing some decent ball. Meanwhile, the Chiefs have reinvented themselves and look tough to beat– and haven’t peaked yet. Kenneth Walker has been a game changer– if he keeps this up, it’s an OPOY-type season. I would say MVP, but that award may be spoken for. Patrick Mahomes is absolutely thriving on play action and getting the ball deep down the field. The young defense has had more ups than downs, and they’re getting healthier. There’s no way I’m picking against KC this week. Chiefs 31, Raiders 24 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) It’s Raiiiiiiiiders week. And finally one to be excited about. This rivalry is just better when both teams have something to play for. The Raiders are one of the major surprises of the NFL season. Unfortunately, many of their team strengths play great against the weaknesses of the Chiefs. Brock Bowers will likely have a fantastic day against the Chiefs’ linebackers and secondary, but the Chiefs will be able to contain Ashton Jeanty and their receivers. I see this one being competitive throughout. Ultimately, the Chiefs’ big game experience serves them well, and they come out on top. But this Raiders team is ascending, and this could be the beginning of the rivalry renewed. Chiefs 27, Raiders 21 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) I’d rather eat Creed Humphrey’s jockstrap than pick against the Chiefs on Raider week. Luckily, I think the Chiefs are still the better team. Our offensive tackles will have their work cut out for them as they always do when facing off against Maxx Crosby. On the offensive side of the ball, the Raiders have Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers, but the Chiefs have a good counterpunch with Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce. What the Raiders don’t have is the cornerbacks the Chiefs have, and most important of all, number 15, the greatest quarterback of all time, and who is playing the best football of his life coming into this game. I think this is the week the Raiders turn into a pumpkin and come out looking worse than Mark Davis’ hair. Chiefs 31, Raiders 13 Nate Christensen This is an exciting game. There hasn’t been a Chiefs-Raiders game with these stakes since probably 2016, when the Chiefs pulled away from the Raiders to win the AFC West. The Raiders’ 3-0 record is probably misleading, but they are definitely a competent team. Kirk Cousins is running Klint Kubiak’s offense well, and now that Brock Bowers is back, they have a legit weapon in the passing game. Ashton Jeanty can maul over any defender. The Raiders defense has also played02 better than expected after a phenomenal start of the year from Maxx Crosby and good free agent additions at linebacker with Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean. I expect the Raiders to keep this game competitive, but I think the Chiefs still have more talent top-to-bottom and will win a close game. Chiefs 27, Raiders 20 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) It feels good to be excited about a matchup with the team that feels like the definition of a “rival” for the Chiefs when history and fandom is all accounted for. Beyond that, the matchups on the field are very intriguing. It feels like a less-mobile quarterback like Kirk Cousins could be the recipe for success the Chiefs’ defense needs, but he also could be finding tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer…
author: Jared Sapp

title: Chiefs-Raiders: 5 things to watch in Week 4 matchup
summary: This week, the Kansas City Chiefs will take on the Las Vegas Raiders in a Week 3 showdown in Las Vegas. The game is set to kick off at 3:25 p.m. Arrowhead Time and will be broadcast locally on CBS (KCTV-5). Both teams are undefeated, and the winner will take sole possession of first place in the AFC West. The 3-0 […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, the Kansas City Chiefs will take on the Las Vegas Raiders in a Week 3 showdown in Las Vegas. The game is set to kick off at 3:25 p.m. Arrowhead Time and will be broadcast locally on CBS ( KCTV-5 ). Both teams are undefeated, and the winner will take sole possession of first place in the AFC West. The 3-0 Chiefs defeated the Miami Dolphins 24-10 a week ago, and although it was not the team’s cleanest appearance, they still pulled out the win by two possessions. Running back Kenneth Walker has electrified the league, winning AFC player of the month for September. Walker’s presence has fueled an offensive resurgence in Kansas City, helping the Chiefs jump to second in the league in yards per game at 416. The run game has also opened up the passing game once more, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes looks as if he is back to MVP form less than a year after coming off of an ACL injury. With a brand new regime, the Raiders are off to their best start since 2021 under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak and new quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Raiders have used solid defense and a revamped offense to get off to a hot start, and this will be a statement game for them. Here are five things to watch in another AFC battle. 1. The Raiders’ pass rush One of the Raiders’ strengths this season has been their pass rush, and all eyes will be on star defensive end Maxx Crosby against the Chiefs’ offensive tackles. The Raiders have been one of the best teams in the NFL at getting home against quarterbacks, and they have done so with one of the lowest blitz percentages. The Raiders are tied for fourth in the NFL with 10 sacks through three games. They have done this by blitzing on only 21% of defensive snaps, the 3rd-lowest in the NFL. — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 30, 2026 The Raiders’ defensive line has done a great job rushing the passer, and it started up front with Crosby. While Crosby draws the attention, auxiliary rushers like Malcom Koonce and Kwity Paye have helped clean up, and seven total Raiders have recorded sacks so far this season. The Chiefs’ offensive line has done an adequate job protecting Mahomes despite issues late last week. Rookie Kahlil Benson has been aided by the fierce run game and play action, and has played well enough to win AFC Rookie of the Month. The rookie has played well so far, but this will be the biggest test of his career. Look for the play-action attack to continue, but the one-on-one situations between Benson and Crosby will be telling. 2. Walker and Kubiak reunion In February, Kubiak and Walker both played pivotal roles in helping the Seattle Seahawks hoist the Lombardi Trophy, and less than a year later they find themselves as adversaries in the same division. Kubiak served as Walker’s offensive coordinator for only one season, but during that season, Walker had the second-highest rushing total of his career, along with a dominant postseason run that helped him win Super Bowl MVP. #Raiders HC Klint Kubiak on the Chiefs "This is a very talented team that we have to get on the ground" He said Kenneth Walker is a guy with big play opportunity and can hit a home run on any play — Jesse Merrick – Silver & Black Sports Network (@JesseSBSN) September 30, 2026 Despite the monster postseason, Walker spent the season in a time share with fellow Seahawks back Zach Charbonnet, up until Charbonnet went down with an ACL injury in January. Kubiak left to become a head coach, and Walker signed with a team that needed a lead back. It will be interesting if either is able to use any inside knowledge to help their current team prepare. 3. Turnover takeaway difference Turning the ball over is never a conductor for success, but this season both teams lead the league in turnover takeaway differential. The Raiders lead the league at +5, while the Chiefs are tied for 5th at +3. A huge four-takeaway game in Week 3 boosted this number for the Raiders, but in overall turnover numbers they still lead the league with five fumble recoveries and four interceptions. Their numbers could be higher, but three Kirk Cousins interceptions and another fumble lower the margin. With a +5 TO/TA differential, the Raiders have been very opportunistic this season. Herbert leaves a pass a bit short with no pressure in the pocket, Njoku bobbles, and it ends up a pick. pic.twitter.com/c6YdWkYTVN — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) October 1, 2026 The Chiefs have turned the ball over only twice — two interceptions by Mahomes — but forced two fumbles and intercepted three passes. Last season both teams finished in the negative for the margin, with the Chiefs at -1 for the season and the Raiders nearly last at -7. Ball security could play a huge role on Sunday. 4. Chiefs YAC dominance The Chiefs are the best team in the NFL in yards after catch this season with 519, largely due to tight end Travis Kelce, who leads the league with 155 at age 37. Wideout Rashee Rice is also in the top 10 with 119 after the catch. The Chiefs have used an impressive play-action passing attack to get their best players open, and Mahomes has not hesitated to take the easy completions. There is so much to process for the defense here. Rodriguez respects Walker's legs, then Kelce crosses him, only for Mahomes to loft a pass to a wide-open Rashee Rice. pic.twitter.com/PkTahLQrUX — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 29, 2026 The Chiefs have used the threat of Walker’s legs to pull defenders into the box, and that is where the offense’s brilliance has shown up this season. Giving Kelce and Rice free lanes to run has led to explosive plays, and given the defense very little margin for error. 5. Rivalry renewed It has been many years since the Chiefs and Raiders have played a truly meaningful game, but this one could signify yet another shift during the Mahomes era for the Chiefs’ primary Rival in the AFC West. The Los Angeles Chargers are off to a disastrous start after being the Chiefs’ primary threat during the Mahomes era, while the Broncos seem to be regressing after their 2025 campaign. The Raiders have new faces all over, and most importantly, they have the talent and coaching to use it. Their biggest asset will likely not even play this week, but the Chiefs should still be ready for the Raiders’ best shot, especially with the division standings on the line early in the season. Patrick Mahomes on the Raiders 👀 “I wouldn’t be surprised if it’s a very hostile environment, take it back to those Oakland Raiders days—they’re playing great football, you can see it on tape, that 3-0 record is real.” pic.twitter.com/udee0lmCCJ — SleeperChiefs (@SleeperChiefsKC) September 30, 2026
author: Caleb James

title: Will the Chiefs’ pass rush return to form this week against the Raiders?
summary: Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. It’s a quote made famous by Mike Tyson, and it applies in all aspects of life. Especially football. Imagine you’re standing in your backyard playing catch with your 7-year-old son. It’s easy to throw a pass 10 yards away. No pressure, right? But what […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. It’s a quote made famous by Mike Tyson, and it applies in all aspects of life. Especially football. Imagine you’re standing in your backyard playing catch with your 7-year-old son. It’s easy to throw a pass 10 yards away. No pressure, right? But what if there’s someone in front of your child? Suddenly the throw becomes more difficult. Now imagine a 290-pound grown man sprinting toward you at full speed as you’re attempting to make the throw. Yeah, good luck. That’s the life of an NFL quarterback. Every. Single. Week. It sounds miserable. It’s no wonder fewer than 20 people in the world can do this job at a high level at any given time. Applying that pressure on opposing quarterbacks is the goal of every defensive coordinator in the league. Don’t let the opposing quarterback get comfortable. Get him off his spot. Throw him off of his rhythm. We hear this every single week. It’s easier said than done. But when you do it, it’s special. It’s what made the Seattle Seahawks ’ defense stand out a year ago. It felt like a new player was getting after the quarterback on every single play. That defensive line came at opposing offenses in waves. It was constant, relentless pressure. It’s the kind of thing every team in the league hopes to replicate. The Kansas City Chiefs are no different. After the first week of the season, it felt like Kansas City might be on its way to a better year in that regard. The defensive line made Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix look uncomfortable from the very first snap. Steve Spagnuolo was in his bag. The results were hard to argue. Chiefs defenders had three sacks and five quarterback hits in that season-opener against Nix and the Broncos. This same defense has zero sacks and five quarterback hits over the past two weeks… combined. Wait, what? Why? How? Didn’t this team just spend millions on a new nose tackle and multiple top-50 selections on defensive linemen? And aren’t they spending $50 million against the cap on two other defensive linemen? Yupp. They are. The results should be better. But they aren’t. Not yet, at least. What’s gone wrong? Let’s dive into the numbers, shall we? Team: Time to Throw: Average Depth of Target Pressure Rate Sacks Blitz Rate Broncos: 2.48 sec 4.1 yards 21% 3 45% Colts: 2.65 sec 5.7 yards 24% 0 24% Dolphins: 2.9 sec 9.2 yards 26% 0 31% *Stats courtesy of Dynatize & Pro Football Reference So, yeah, it’s a bit all over the place. The Chiefs blitzed the Broncos, and Denver responded by getting the ball out of Nix’s hands as quickly as possible. It resulted in a ton of dump-offs and a lower pressure rate, but the Chiefs’ blitzes paid off with a few sacks. The blitz rate dropped over the past couple of weeks. The pressure rate did increase ever so slightly, but the Chiefs’ ability to finish plays in the backfield all but disappeared. It’s strange. It’s hard to explain. It needs to change. This is a good week to get things back on track. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins is the first true pocket passer the Chiefs have faced all season. He’s been sacked five times and hit 10 times over the past two weeks against the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Chargers , and he could be without starting right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson this week. Powers-Johnson has missed practice each of the past two days with a groin issue. His replacement would seem to be Caleb Rogers, a player with six career starts. That sound you hear is defensive tackles Chris Jones and Peter Woods licking their chops. This was already a relatively advantageous matchup for the Chiefs’ defensive line, and it looks like it’s getting better. Brandon Thorn of Establish The Run ranked the Chiefs’ defensive line vs. the Raiders’ offensive line as the fifth-biggest mismatch in the league this week. He has the Raiders rated as the 21st “best” offensive line in the league. The Chiefs rate as the fifth-best defensive line. That’s a lot of faith in a group that hasn’t produced. There are reasons why smart individuals like Thron still have so much belief in a group that’s failed to produce a sack over the past two weeks. It’s entirely possible the Chiefs’ defensive game plan focused on stopping the run against the Indianapolis Colts . At times, it looked like they played more of a contain rush against quarterback Malik Willis to force him to win from the pocket. It’s also possible safety Chamarri Conner’s absence has forced Steve Spagnuolo to run a more vanilla game plan on the back end of the defense in recent weeks. Throw in a nagging calf injury for Jones, and you’ve got a formula for limited pass-rush production. That’s all fine and dandy. But eventually this unit has to start putting pressure on the opposing quarterback again. This would be a good week for it to start.
author: Brandon Kiley

title: Steve Spagnuolo sees accountability among Chiefs’ defense
summary: Although the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 3-0 start, fans have found the last two defensive performances stressful. After a dominant Week 1 showing against the Denver Broncos, the Indianapolis Colts took the unit to overtime and nearly won after advancing to the Kansas City 17-yard line in the extra period. In Week […]
full_text: (Photo by Alie Skowronski/Getty Images) | Getty Images Although the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 3-0 start, fans have found the last two defensive performances stressful. After a dominant Week 1 showing against the Denver Broncos , the Indianapolis Colts took the unit to overtime and nearly won after advancing to the Kansas City 17-yard line in the extra period. In Week 3, the lowly Miami Dolphins posted their highest yardage total (and their lowest-scoring performance) of the season against Kansas City’s defense. Per Next Gen Stats , the Chiefs are actually fourth in expected points added (EPA) per defensive play at -0.16. Still, the unit is not passing the eye test for many observers, including their leader. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo explained before Thursday’s practice that everyone is well aware of the recent deficiencies. “By the time Tuesday rolls around when I first see them, they’re chewed out,” remarked the coach. “I’ve already chewed myself out for a whole day. So, we like to have constructive criticism. The good thing about this group is they’re all pretty accountable. Even if I’m standing in there and pointing something out, I see a lot of heads shaking, ‘Yeah, you’re right,’ so that part I don’t even worry about.” Spagnuolo shares frustrations that opponents seem to get out of trouble in third-down situations that should favor the defense. He is happy with how his squad has come through multiple times in key fourth-down moments. “You look at third down percentage, and it looks crappy,” he acknowledged, “but I kind of dissect the whole thing. That’s a run play I think [Miami] had — there was one third and 10 there that they had a really good design route concept that beat what we had out there. So, I’m going to give them that, but all of a sudden, if you take three [plays] out of there, it’s a whole different ballgame. What was good was when we were able to stop them and get it to fourth down. We had the three fourth-down stops that were key. Now, we don’t want to always be banking on that because those are pretty difficult. But would I like to be better in third down? Yeah, and we’ll dissect it and hopefully come up with something a little bit better this week.” The team’s pass rush has underwhelmed, going two weeks without a sack and giving teams extra time to get out of difficult situations. While the team’s pass rushers have knocked down some key passes, they aren’t getting to the quarterback quickly enough. “I think we’d all like to see it better on first and second down,” said Spagnuolo. “That’s where some of those plays got long. We’ve got to do better on the back end with those explosive passes, but when the down gets extended, guys have a tendency to kind of get open at some point. So, first and second down is one thing that we’ve looked at. I was happy that we got our hands up and knocked some balls down. That play [defensive tackle Chris Jones] made with [defensive end George Karlaftis] was really important. “I thought we could have had five turnovers. I thought we had three missed opportunities. We’ve got to get those…Third down was something we’d like to get better at. Pass rush on first and second down. We’ve talked about all those things.” Sunday’s road matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders will show whether those discussions are proving fruitful. Spagnuolo does not expect an easy day against veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Raiders are currently second in the league with 0.56 EPA per third-down pass play. “Big challenge,” Spagnuolo said of Cousins. “I’ve been down this road before. Kirk’s one of these quarterbacks that I’ve got a tremendous amount of respect for. He’s been doing it for a long time. I think he’s a quality guy. Every time I see him, I tell him how much I respect his character. That part is great, but on the football field, he gets the ball out so quick that he makes it really difficult. I think the knocking down of passes will be really important. The sticky coverage and making him throw it into tight windows will be really big. When we do that, we need a couple of knockdowns by a corner or a safety to get him in a longer down the distance or get us off the field. We’ll have to mix it up, but I think you’ve got to be a little bit careful with a guy that’s as smart as Kirk is.”

title: NFL predictions: Chargers vs. Seahawks face intriguing Week 4 matchup
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are facing off against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4 at Lumen Field hoping to grab their first win of the season. The Chargers have dropped their first three games and have been one of the more disappointing teams in the league. Nothing more would get them back on track with […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers throws a pass during the second quarter of the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are facing off against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4 at Lumen Field hoping to grab their first win of the season. The Chargers have dropped their first three games and have been one of the more disappointing teams in the league. Nothing more would get them back on track with a statement win in Week 4 against the defending Super Bowl champions. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , the Chargers are an underdog by a touchdown. Let’s take a look at some predictions for the game. Over/Under: 43.5 The Chargers and Seahawks have both been inconsistent this season when it comes to their offense. At times, the Chargers have looked flat, while the Seahawks have looked better. After scoring just 13 points in their debut against the New England Patriots, the Seahawks have posted back-to-back 30-point performances, one each from Drew Lock and Sam Darnold. This number suggests there will be at least six touchdowns in the game, assuming all the extra points are made as well. This game could turn into a track meet if the Chargers score early, but if the Seahawks grab a lead, they will do anything they can to protect it. I believe the Seahawks will strike first, making this a low-scoring game. Prediction: Under Chargers +7 FanDuel is giving the Chargers a touchdown to start the game. Given that the game is taking place in Seattle, that would usually give the home team a field goal advantage. The line is a bit surprising, given how the Chargers have not played well. Los Angeles has lost by more than seven points in each of their first three games this season, making this a line that I’m not willing to trek into. Seattle is playing in front of the 12s for the first time since the season opener and they will be hungry to cheer on their team, making it extremely difficult for Los Angeles. Prediction: Seahawks -7 Final Score The Chargers are facing an uphill battle in this game. A win would be exactly what they need to kickstart their year, nothing about the first three weeks of the season has suggested that they will go out and win this game. It’s an incredibly difficult schedule they are facing over the next couple of weeks, and this one might be one of the toughest games in that stretch as the Seahawks look to bounce back from a loss of their own. The Chargers have the talent to make this game interesting, but I think the Seahawks will score early, and their defense will carry throughout the game.
