title: Chargers-Seahawks Game Preview: 5 Questions with the enemy
summary: This week were joined by Mookie Alexander from our Seahawks sister site, Field Gulls, to help us preview Chargers-Seahawks! Mookie is one of the best in the business so we greatly appreciate his help and expertise! Without further ado, let’s get into it! 1.) The Seahawks lost starting quarterback Sam Darnold in Week One but […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - SEPTEMBER 27: Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (11) celebrates after his second touchdown catch of the game during the Seattle Seahawks versus Washington Commanders National Football League game at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, MD. (Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This week were joined by Mookie Alexander from our Seahawks sister site, Field Gulls , to help us preview Chargers-Seahawks! Mookie is one of the best in the business so we greatly appreciate his help and expertise! Without further ado, let’s get into it! 1.) The Seahawks lost starting quarterback Sam Darnold in Week One but still managed to beat the Patriots and then stay afloat with a win in Week Two while Drew Lock took over. In Week Three, Darnold returned but the Seahawks lost a close one to the Commanders. What have you learned about this team through the first three weeks and has that changed your preseason expectations at all? My preseason expectations of another Super Bowl run (except they don’t repeat) are unchanged. Darnold looks like he’s in for another strong season and other than the awful pick-six he threw, he played very well given the lack of a running game against the Commanders. The passing game will likely be the strength of the offense over the inconsistent rushing attack, just as it was for much of last year. Defensively there’s almost an incomplete grade because they shut down the Patriots and Cardinals, but those are not particularly impressive offenses. The Commanders scored 33 points but a lot of that came off short fields and a pick-six. With that said, the defense wasn’t at their best against the Commanders and part of that was being down starting safeties Ty Okada and Julian Love. I don’t expect Okada back this week but Love definitely will be back and he’s a pivotal part of Seattle’s defense. The interior of the defensive line is as strong as ever with Byron Murphy II, Leonard Williams, and Jarran Reed, and that’s where the Seahawks have the biggest advantage in this game and really against most of the rest of the league. The biggest regression we’ve seen is the Seahawks special teams, which has not covered kickoffs well and is struggling to do anything with punt returns. Seattle is still a top team until proven otherwise, and I think the Commanders game is a blip on the radar. Mike Macdonald has proven to be such a top-flight coach so quickly that I think he’ll “make it right” given his obsession with attention to detail. 2.) Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on a whole other level compared to the rest of the NFL. How has he become arguably the best in the league so early in his career? How does he manage to produce week-in and week-out at an elite level? He’s an elite route-runner with supreme footwork and terrific hands. As a rookie, he was mostly a screen pass guy and couldn’t really generate consistent separation. Something clicked when they lost to the Los Angeles Rams in 2024. JSN dropped a pass that led to an interception, and then finished the game with 7 catches for 180 yards and 2 touchdowns, showing off his YAC threat and his ability to separate deeper down the field. After that game, he essentially became the top target over DK Metcalf and Tyler Lockett, and his Offensive Player of the Year performance in 2025 proved the Seahawks were right to build the passing offense around him. And yes, Chargers fans, it’s not lost on me that Seattle got JSN one pick before Quentin Johnston. I have evidence of my desire to avoid drafting QJ , and unfortunately the Chargers didn’t heed my warning. While JSN is not known as a super speedy player, he’s faster than advertised and has mastered the art of not telegraphing his route tree. There’s a Hard Knocks clip compiling his route breaks and you can see why he’s such a successful receiver. The Seahawks have had a deep history of very good receivers, and their gold standard is Steve Largent. I think when all is said and done, JSN will be the best receiver in Seahawks history and join Steve in Canton. 3.) If you were Chargers defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary, how would you attempt to put a cap on JSN and the rest of the Seahawks offense? Who are some other offensive players you would also have to watch out for? Well, stopping JSN has really only been done by Brian Flores’ incessant blitzing and selling out his coverages exclusively to him. The Patriots did a good job in the Super Bowl but Darnold also missed a few plays he normally makes, plus JSN left the game briefly due to injury. You can run bracket coverages and do whatever you can to clog up passing lanes in zone defense. This probably means some sim pressure looks and more disguises. O’Leary should also consider not loading the box so heavily to stop the run; when Seattle struggled at times last season, it’s because defenses didn’t commit so many numbers to the run game and instead paid more attention to Seattle’s passing attack. Of course, the Seahawks are more than JSN, and a name to watch is tight end A.J. Barner, who just caught 5 passes for 69 yards and was quietly Seattle’s second-leading receiver in 2025. He’s a quality blocker (which is what he was known for out of the draft) but offensive coordinator Brian Fleury is finally getting him more involved as a receiver again, and he’s been a security blanket for Darnold. When Seattle runs play-action boots, look for Barner underneath for easy-access throws. I’d also keep an eye on Tory Horton, who missed half of last season with an injury and barely played the first two weeks, but he had 3 catches for 48 yards against the Commanders. With Rashid Shaheed struggling for targets and effectiveness, Horton may build off of last week and showcase some more of what made him a fifth-round steal of a receiver. Horton can also return kicks and housed a 95-yard punt for a touchdown last season. 4.) Same question as above but flip sides of the ball. If you were offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, how would you go about trying to attack this Seahawks defense? Which players would you attempt to avoid? Which players would you try to exploit? The Seahawks are terrific at defending long passes but they have been vulnerable to passes under 10 air yards, ranking 27th in success rate. McDaniel should utilize the short passing game as much as possible, particularly with his running backs and tight ends (which, I admit, is a problem on the TE front given Gadsden’s dropsies). Screen passes have caught the Seahawks out in their rare blitzes. Seattle’s pass rush from the edges is fine but not elite, but the interior rush still means Herbert will likely be pressed for time, so McDaniel has to scheme up quicker throws. Herbert’s arm is fantastic but waiting for something to open up downfield is probably going to end disastrously. Ladd McConkey, if healthy enough to play, will likely present challenges for Seattle’s corners (particularly Josh Jobe, who’s good but penalty prone). There’s really not much else to say regarding the Chargers receivers. Running the ball with Omarion Hampton is likely a waste of time and downs against Seattle’s front, so going into the teeth of the defense is like an invitation to punt. 5.) Let’s top this off with a final score prediction. How do you see this game shaking out? Will it be lopsided or closer than you think? I think the Chargers defense can make it close but the lack of offense is going to be the downfall. Let’s go with 24-14 Seahawks in which maybe a tie score at halftime turns into a 24-7 lead before the Chargers tack on a garbage time score to lose by a little less. Seattle has been turnover prone throughout Mike Macdonald’s tenure (except for the literal playoff run to the Super Bowl, amazingly) and the Chargers did just get five turnovers last week, so that’s essentially the path to victory.

full_text: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) readies to snap the ball against the Philadelphia Eagles (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Looking to even the ledger after a 1-2 start to the season, the Los Angeles Rams travel across country to the east coast to do battle with the 2-1 Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday October 5. Kickoff is set for 10 a.m. PDT at Lincoln Financial Field in South Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The fall weather will be much more temperate than a winter date. Although full clouds are expected and a 60 percent chance of rain is forecast, temperatures are expected to be in the mid-60’s with mild wind conditions, 7 to 14 miles per hour. It was 1937, when the Rams were based in Cleveland that the series with Philly had its origins. The pair have squared off 47 times over that span with the Eagles holding a 26-20-1 advantage and have out-scored L.A. 983 to 961. Since Sean McVay took the Rams reins in 2017, Philadelphia has been the bane of his coaching existence, winning six of the seven matchup’s and the last four in a row. Both teams have been bitten by the injury bug early and several starters have been ruled out of Sunday’s tilt. For the Eagles, tight end Dallas Goedert and receiver’s Devonta Smith and Hollywood Brown will be absent from an offense that is in the NFL’s Bottom 10 in scoring and total yards. Defensive starters designated as out are linebacker Zach Baun and safety Marcus Epps. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle), cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), and defensive tackle Aaron Donald (back) won’t play for the Rams, while tight end Colby Parkinson and edge Josaiah Stewart are questionable. Ferguson will join edge Myles Garrett and offensive linemen Justin Dedich and Keagan Trost on the Injured Reserve List, all were expected to be prominent pieces in the 2026 season. The Rams will have to find a way to overcome with or without Donald, and they still won’t have Myles Garrett. It’s another example of this team not playing […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are expected to have Puka Nacua back in the fold, but just as they perhaps get Nacua back, Aaron Donald is out. The Rams will have to find a way to overcome with or without Donald, and they still won’t have Myles Garrett. It’s another example of this team not playing the way so many envisioned before the start of the season. The idea was a team of star players all playing at together. That hasn’t happened yet. There’s still time, but in the NFL there’s never enough time. The Rams need to get healthy fast, and they need to win faster if they want to make the postseason. Talk of the “superteam” is no more. Rams’ Aaron Donald to miss Week 4 game vs. Eagles, Puka Nacua’s status updated (cbssports) “Donald unretired this offseason, returning to play for his former team after initially retiring in 2023. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year’s return has not been as smooth as he or the team had hoped. He sat out the opener when the Rams fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, and Sunday will mark his second missed game of the season. Head coach Sean McVay said Donald felt soreness in his back after the team’s Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos . “He’s working as hard as he can to get himself feeling as good as possible. And we’re hopeful and optimistic that good days are ahead,” McVay said. When Donald is healthy, he is an offense’s worst nightmare. The 35-year-old’s resume includes a Super Bowl win, eight first-team All-Pro nods and 10 Pro Bowl selections. I think that he’ll do the necessary things to be able to sustain at that position for us.” Sean McVay is 0-4 against Nick Sirianni (nbcsports) “Rams coach Sean McVay has had tremendous success since becoming a head coach in 2017. Against one specific coach, McVay has struggled. Via NBC Sports research, McVay has an 0-4 record against Eagles coach Nick Sirianni. McVay gets his next chance to get his first win over Sirianni on Sunday in Philadelphia. The 1-2 Rams desperately need to avoid falling to 1-3. The next year, the Eagles won again in L.A., 37-20.“ Los Angeles Rams Among 3 NFL Teams In Desperate Need Of Week 4 Win (sports.yahoo) “No one expected the Los Angeles Chargers to start off 0-3, and yet, that’s where Jim Harbaugh’s squad finds itself heading into Week 4. If the Chargers are going to save their season, they’ll need Justin Herbert to put on his Superman cape this weekend.“ Are the 0-3 Houston Texans already cooked? Plus, the emergence of Greg Rousseau and Dallas Turner (nfl.com) “The Houston Texans have climbed out of the grave multiple times during DeMeco Ryans’ tenure to ultimately claim a playoff berth. title: Rams place Terrance Ferguson on IR

full_text: The Los Angeles Rams entered the season with a plethora of offensive weapons for Matthew Stafford, but now another one of those options is injured: The Rams placed tight end Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve on Friday. Ferguson left Week 3’s loss to the Denver Broncos with an ankle injury. He is third on the team with 12 targets, catching seven passes for 63 yards and a touchdown. The 2025 second-round pick had 11 catches for 231 yards as a rookie, but is in danger of prolonging the wait for patient Rams fans hoping to see the potential that made him a top-50 pick for Les Snead. Rams placed TE Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve due to his ankle injury. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 2, 2026 The Rams entered the season with seven receivers, five tight ends, and three running backs. Among the laundry list of issues already: Puka Nacua missed the last 2 games Ferguson is on IR Ronnie Rivers is on IR Xavier Smith was waived on Friday Colby Parkinson has not practiced this week and is Questionable C.J. Daniels has been a healthy scratch every week Tutu Atwell has been active for one game Max Klare has been a healthy scratch every week Nacua is set to return to the field for the Rams on Sunday against the Eagles. Alex Bachman, yet another receiver who did not make the original 53-man roster, is set to become the team’s punt returner after waiving Smith. Klare is probably going to make his NFL debut in wake of the injuries at tight end. The Rams are not beating the “shades of 2022” allegations. But if they can just beat the Eagles, who ruled out receiver DeVonta Smith this week, that would help.

title: This should be a big week for the Rams defense
summary: There are polarizing ways to look at the Los Angeles Rams defense so far this season. On one hand, in a 1-2 start they’ve given up 27 and 30 points to the San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos, which aren’t especially encouraging totals. On the flip side, advanced metrics have been higher on L.A. so […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Defensive Coordinator Chris Shula of the Los Angeles Rams calls a play during the first half of a game against the New York Giantsat SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are polarizing ways to look at the Los Angeles Rams defense so far this season. On one hand, in a 1-2 start they’ve given up 27 and 30 points to the San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos, which aren’t especially encouraging totals. On the flip side, advanced metrics have been higher on L.A. so far, with the Rams finding themselves well into the top half of the league in several notable statistics. This week’s game with the Philadelphia Eagles should be a chance for defensive coordinator Chris Shula’s group to make a positive statement. There’s a hint of desperation for both squads going into this game. The Rams are off to a disappointing start considering their lofty aspirations this year, while the Eagles are 2-1 but have two less-than-decisive wins over supposedly inferior teams and were just blasted by the Chicago Bears on Monday night. It’s early, but this feels like an important tilt for both sides. The Eagles, however, are in an especially tight spot offensively. Philadelphia is trying to ride out the early season growing pains that come with a new offensive coordinator and scheme (at least to some degree the scheme is new, anyway), while its pass-catching group is in flux heading into the weekend. Devonta Smith isn’t expected to play , taking away the Eagles’ best receiver and one of the more underrated receivers in the sport. Tight end Dallas Goedert has also missed time this week, as has receiver Hollywood Brown, and first-round pick Makai Lemon hasn’t been productive through his first handful of NFL games. “I heard at the beginning of this week that DeVonta Smith is likely to miss this game and maybe another one. Could be a two or three week hamstring injury.” via @Bo_Wulf https://t.co/2NWTJspywI — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) October 2, 2026 Jalen Hurts, to his credit, has played well enough to start the year. But that’s a lot of question marks, at best, in terms of his offensive weapons. Depending on where you look, the Rams are on the fringes of the top 10 around the league in defensive EPA/play so far (RBSDM.com’s calculation has them 10th, while SumerSports has them 11th). The passing defense has been especially solid according to some advanced metrics. Per RBSDM, the Rams defense is 5th in dropback EPA and 11th in dropback success rate. They are making things challenging for opposing passing attacks, especially when it comes to generating chunk plays. Run defense, however, has been a different story for Los Angeles. While its rushing success rate currently sits 13th in the league, it ranks 26th in rush EPA/play. That tells you that L.A. is allowing too many big gains while being decent on a down-to-down basis. Thankfully for the Rams, this matchup should, in theory, allow them to dedicate more resources to stopping the run while still limiting the passing game. With such a banged up corps of pass catchers, it is likely going to be even more challenging to move the ball through the air for a team that is already struggling to do that (the Eagles are 25th in dropback EPA/play through three weeks). Now, the Eagles have been decent at generating explosive pass plays , but the Rams have trusted their cornerbacks on islands this year, playing man coverage on 29.5% of snaps, the ninth-highest rate in the NFL per Next Gen Stats. Even without Jaylen Watson this week, Los Angeles can probably afford to keep trusting those cornerbacks. It’s important to mention trench play here as well, which is admittedly more concerning with Aaron Donald now out for the matchup . He would have been especially valuable against the Eagles’ offensive line, which has been solid in pass protection this year overall but exceptionally poor at the guard spots in particular (see the embedded post below). Pass block grades in true pass sets only You'll never guess who comes in last here pic.twitter.com/6ChM4tRjpl — Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) September 30, 2026 If your guards are grading out worse in pass protection than the ones in Green Bay, something is going heinously wrong. Donald would likely feast in that matchup, but it’s a golden opportunity for Braden Fiske to bounce back after having one of the least productive games of his career in Week 3. Against Denver, Fiske posted just the second game of his career without a single pressure. Shula will likely try to create as many favorable interior matchups as possible, so even without Donald there’s an optimistic case for the Rams to win plenty up front. As mentioned above, the pressure point in this game for the Rams defense will likely be its ability to stop the run. They’ve struggled in that department this year, but the Eagles haven’t been unstoppable, either. At 10th in the league in EPA per rush, the Eagles are solidly good on the ground, but not elite so far this season. If the pass defense indeed controls the game through the air, it could allow Los Angeles to put heavier personnel on the field more often to help buoy the run defense. The Rams are playing dime 36.3% of the time this season per Next Gen Stats, the highest rate for any team in the last three years. That’s understandable, given the quality of talent in the secondary and the comparative lack in the linebacker corps. But if they add another front seven/six player just a little more often it could pay major dividends. There are plenty of “shoulds” and “coulds” above, because yes, we won’t know any of this for sure until the teams actually take the field. But in terms of forecasting this matchup, in a world of zero guarantees, there’s reason to believe the Rams are in position to have a strong defensive showing on Sunday.

title: Aaron Donald ruled out for Week 4 against Eagles
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have ruled out defensive tackle Aaron Donald for Week 4’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles with a back injury, but they do believe that Puka Nacua will return. Unfortunately, the super duo of Myles Garrett and Donald has yet to actually play together this season and now they won’t have either […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have ruled out defensive tackle Aaron Donald for Week 4’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles with a back injury, but they do believe that Puka Nacua will return . Unfortunately, the super duo of Myles Garrett and Donald has yet to actually play together this season and now they won’t have either of those defensive linemen against the Eagles on Sunday. Donald was inactive for Week 1 and Garrett has been on IR since Week 2. The Rams do not have a timeline for when Garrett will return from a knee injury that required surgery, but the latest update put the absence around six weeks . Aaron Donald is out for Sunday’s game vs. the Eagles due to his back injury. Puka Nacua is expected to play. pic.twitter.com/A3ML2iB7G7 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 2, 2026 Donald has not had the type of impact on the field that many were hoping he would have , optimism that was surely shared by the Rams after they paid him at least $20 million to come out of retirement and to play with Garrett. By pressure rate, Donald is among the bottom-10 defensive tackles in the league so far. The bigger issue at hand for Sunday though is that in spite of those returns, Donald may still bet he Rams’ best defensive lineman. Players like Braden Fiske and Byron Young have been underwhelming, if not bad, while Kobie Turner isn’t having as good of a season as the type of performances he was having over his first three years in the NFL. How long Donald could miss is unclear, as the possibility of him being out didn’t crop up until the middle of the week . At 35 though, there’s no predicting what kind of a season Donald will actually have.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Case Keenum beat the Eagles, why not Matthew Stafford?
summary: Bears third-stringer Case Keenum had a standout game against the Eagles on Monday, so there’s reason to believe LA Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford can do the same in Week 4. Keenum, who was on the verge of retirement entering this season, started his first game in three years in a 27-7 win on Monday Night […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams jogs off the field before a game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bears third-stringer Case Keenum had a standout game against the Eagles on Monday, so there’s reason to believe LA Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford can do the same in Week 4. Keenum, who was on the verge of retirement entering this season, started his first game in three years in a 27-7 win on Monday Night Football. The veteran completed just over 70% of his passes and had three total touchdowns. It was one of the best performances of his career, and it was certainly jaw-dropping to watch unfold in real time. Case Keenum’s first 3-TD game since the 2019 season opener against the #Eagles while with Washington. Tonight, at age 38, he matches it to lead the #Bears to a huge win without Caleb Williams. pic.twitter.com/hJ41b6YtQ7 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) September 29, 2026 So I’m going to ask again: Why not Stafford? The 38-year-old Rams QB and reigning MVP has the experience and ability to exploit the same weaknesses the 38-year-old Keenum did in front of a national audience. Part of Keenum’s success against the Eagles came from getting the ball out of his hands quickly. His average time to throw, 2.41 seconds, was the quickest of all quarterbacks this season with at least 30 passing attempts. It certainly helped that Ben Johnson didn’t scheme up long developing plays or rollouts for him. Instead, Johnson cooked up a variety of quick passes that Keenum and the offense feasted on all game. Case Keenum passing chart vs. Eagles pic.twitter.com/9tzBtnI9rx — Dave (@davebftv) September 29, 2026 Per Next Gen Stats, Keenum’s passes were largely in the 10- to 15-yard range throughout the game. Those short passing plays were effective, as the Eagles struggled to defend them. This should at least give Sean McVay a blueprint for how to take on Philly’s defense. McVay and Stafford don’t need to completely copy Chicago’s gameplan, but adding more quick-play concepts to the playbook can help keep Philadelphia’s pass rush off-balance. Plus, Stafford’s average time to throw this season isn’t too far off from Keenum’s. According to Pro Football Focus , the Rams QB averages 2.67 seconds to throw, which ranks 28th in the NFL among 36 qualified passers. While that may seem concerning, PFF noted that Stafford has gradually taken longer in the pocket to get the throw out throughout his time in LA. The increase in his average time to throw is thanks to improvements along the Rams’ offensive line in that span. Stafford has used that extra time to target receivers downfield, as shown by his willingness to throw beyond the sticks and by increasing his average depth of target, highlighted by a mark of 10.1 during his 2025 MVP campaign. That’s where Stafford differs from Keenum. A short passing game has proven to do the trick against the Eagles, but Stafford and the Rams have been able to successfully move the ball on Vic Fangio’s defense with their downfield attack in the past. In three meetings since 2024, Stafford has a 6-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio against Fangio’s defense, averaging two touchdown passes per game: Week 12, 2024: 24-of-36 for 243 yards and two touchdowns; 104.5 passer rating Divisional Round, 2024 season: 26-of-44 for 324 yards and two touchdowns; 97.2 passer rating Week 3, 2025: 19-of-33 for 196 yards, two touchdowns and one interception; 82.4 passer rating While Stafford’s stats are solid on paper, he was sacked 11 times in those three games, including a combined 10 times during both 2024 meetings. That can be the crutch of relying so much on a downfield passing scheme. Stafford’s been productive against Fangio’s unit, but in return, LA has allowed the pass rush to make a sizable impact. The Rams don’t have to entirely switch up their gameplan or completely abandon the downfield passing attack that has served them well in the McVay era. McVay and LA’s offense would benefit from adding more quick-play passes to get Stafford into a rhythm and, most importantly, take the Eagles’ pass rush out of the game. Finding a mix between the Rams’ usual offensive scheme and the Bears’ gameplan Monday night could serve Los Angeles better this weekend. Stafford has had success against this team and defense before. Only this time, a healthy diet of passing plays should keep the Eagles on their toes and force them to defend the entire field.
author: Evan Craig

title: Rams reacts: Fans adjust win-loss expectations
summary: Despite the Los Angeles Rams losing two of their first three games, almost half of the fan base still expects the Rams to win at least 10 games. In this week’s SB Nation Rams reacts poll question asking “How many wins do you expect the Rams to get over the last 14 games”, 53% of […]
full_text: Despite the Los Angeles Rams losing two of their first three games, almost half of the fan base still expects the Rams to win at least 10 games. In this week’s SB Nation Rams reacts poll question asking “How many wins do you expect the Rams to get over the last 14 games”, 53% of fans predicted “10 or 11” and another 6% voted “12 or more”. The Rams are 1-2, so that would leave the team somewhere between 11-6 and 15-2 by the end of the season. The low end of that projection would come in under what many expected would happen before L.A. started 1-2, when the Rams were still favored to win the NFC West with at least 13 wins. The Rams are 3.5-point favorites against the Philadelphia Eagles this weekend, according to FanDuel . Before the season, FanDuel had the Rams at 12-5 . So, a win this week would help get the Rams closer to that 12-5 record, at least. And reinforcements are on the way. If Myles Garrett returns sooner than later, if Puka Nacua stays healthy, then it’s possible the Rams wind up stronger in the second half of their season than the first, as is often the case. What is telling is that fans still believe this team can have a strong 2026 season. The hope is there; will the Rams deliver? Good question. Are you confident in the direction of the Rams? Fans may still expect a strong 2026, however in terms of the direction of the franchise, there’s a fair amount of concern. As mentioned above Garrett has been hurt, Nacua hasn’t suited up and the Rams have not been the powerhouse in 2026 that many expected, and the fans level of concern reflects that. Of course, if the Rams rattle off a few wins, then perhaps the confidence meter will shift, but as it stands, fans are worried and that’s fair given that this team went from Super Bowl favorite to questioning whether or not they can win their own division. Through 3 weeks, the San Francisco 49ers look like perhaps the best team in the NFC, not the Rams. Do the Rams even have a backup quarterback they could trade? When it comes to the backup quarterback position for the Rams, they potentially have their QB of the future with Ty Simpson, however could Stetson Bennett be moved? Not likely, but you never know and as quarterback injuries pile up, a team may be desperate enough to send a late pick for Simpson. A majority of fans surveyed seem to think that a backup quarterback is worth a Day 3 pick, and if Bennett were to be moved, it’s hard to see him going for anything more than a seventh rounder. Odds are Bennett isn’t moved given the amount of other backup signal callers potentially available. Still, teams and their backup positions, especially at quarterback, are something to monitor. Which rocky start through three weeks is the most troubling? If the Los Angeles Chargers weren’t such a massive disappointment, then the Rams would be getting more ire. Then again when you see teams like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Houston Texans starting 0-3, then perhaps the Rams aren’t in as much trouble as it seems. That being said, the Rams don’t need to worry about other franchise’s records, for now, but they do need to worry about getting back in the win column ASAP. For teams like the Chargers, Bucs and Texans, they are looking to get into the win column at all. In the world of the NFL, things don’t always get better, but they can always get worse. The Rams will try to avoid some of the negative storylines that other struggling teams are getting. Thank you for giving us your feedback! Please keep checking out The Feed for information, surveys and more and you never know! Your next post on the Feed could be the next big talking point right here at Turf Show Times.

full_text: The Los Angeles Rams waived receiver and punt returner Xavier Smith on Friday, eight months after his muffed punt in the NFC Championship game may have cost the team a trip to the Super Bowl. Smith was retained after the playoffs and kept on the 53-man roster, but Sean McVay has seemingly seen enough and is ready to see another option on special teams. The first name that comes to mind is Dean Connors, the running back who was signed to the 53-man roster this week after an impressive preseason. LA Rams Roster Moves: • Waived, No Recall WR Xavier Smith pic.twitter.com/GnSNy8rRP9 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 2, 2026 Smith had 303 receiving yards last season, but zero catches on one target in 2026. The former undrafted free agent had seven punt returns in the league this year, the most in the NFL, and has also been L.A.’s main kickoff returner. The Rams felt they needed the spot for someone else and they’re moving in a different direction. Some fans are wondering what took so long.

title: Aaron Donald not practicing for Rams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are gearing up for Week 4 against the Philadelphia Eagles, and they may have Puka Nacua back, but they may be without Aaron Donald and others. The start to the season has been shaky for Los Angeles with flat performances, injuries and some unlucky calls. At times, the Rams have looked […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are gearing up for Week 4 against the Philadelphia Eagles, and they may have Puka Nacua back , but they may be without Aaron Donald and others. The start to the season has been shaky for Los Angeles with flat performances, injuries and some unlucky calls . At times, the Rams have looked good too, so there’s that. The question for this Rams team is how good will they be? They have the talent; they are still competing the last two weeks despite some real injuries (Myles Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1). The Rams will see if Donald can suit up for them on Sunday and or they’ll see if they can withstand some more bad luck. Rams’ Aaron Donald Update Teases A Possible Break For Eagles (sports.yahoo) “When the head coach Sean McVay met with reporters, he revealed that Donald is dealing with a sore back. Currently, the superstar’s game status is up in the air. “I wouldn’t want to say anything of that nature yet,” McVay said regarding Donald’s status for Sunday’s action, according to Rams reporter Zach Edwards . “But (his) back’s a little bit sore, and he’s as tough as it gets, we’ll continue to have updates as the week goes.” Rams OC expects Nacua (groin) to practice in full (nbcsports) “Scheelhaase also said that Nacua “twisted” to catch a pass thrown behind him yesterday, which the offensive coordinator took as a good sign. Nacua is on track to face the Eagles in Week 4. As long as he gets through the practice week without suffering a setback, Nacua is an elite WR1 this week.“ Sean McVay addresses speculation that Puka Nacua’s absence was contract-related (ramswire) “During Nacua’s absence, some speculated that he wasn’t injured at all and that it was all contract-related. Nacua, of course, has not yet signed an extension with the Rams despite being in the final year of his contract, causing some to spread the rumor that he was quietly holding out. During an interview on ESPN Los Angeles Wednesday, McVay addressed that speculation and denied its plausibility. “Yeah, it’s not true,” McVay said. “He just did a great job with our walkthrough. He’s been working, chomping at the bit to get back out there with his teammates and this week, we expect him to be out there.” What Is Jalen Hurts’ Career Record Against Los Angeles Rams? (athlonsports) “Heading into Week 4, Hurts has played against the Rams four times as a starter for Philadelphia and he boasts a 4-0 record in those games. Hurts won his first start against the Rams in October of 2023 in a 23-13 Eagles victory. He threw for 303 yards, 1 TD and 1 interception in that game, while also adding 72 rushing yards and another TD with his legs.“ Rams special teams coach backs Xavier Smith but admits he must improve (ramswire) “Ventrone’s group brought in a new long snapper, Joe Cardona, and added linebacker Grant Stuard to assist with their punt and kick coverage. The Rams chose to stick with Xavier Smith at returner, despite his muffed punts in the NFC Championship Game. In 2026, results have varied, and on Thursday, Ventrone spoke about Smith’s work. Calling it for what it was, Ventrone said Smith has been inconsistent and needs to do a better job of tracking and fielding punts. However, Ventrone also made it clear that Smith is still the guy moving forward.“ Sportsbook Insiders: Examining the Latest Super Bowl Odds Movement; Why Rams Remain Highly Rated (si.com) “After all, they’ve lost to two contenders in San Francisco and Denver and have fallen to third in the odds to win their own division. Going to the Super Bowl – never mind winning it – out of a wild card spot won’t be easy, but that’s the path the Rams may have to take in 2026. Sports Illustrated recently spoke to several oddsmakers about the Rams’ outlook – and their latest Super Bowl odds – to see if they’re still viewed as the best team in the NFL. “The Rams are currently still our highest power rated team, but the gap has narrowed significantly since preseason,” a FanDuel Trader told Sports Illustrated. “Once they get Puka and Myles Garrett back, they should regain a healthy lead as our highest rated team.” Rams’ Week 4 clash vs. Eagles could have pivotal playoff implications later (ramblinfan) “While still early, LA’s division odds are shrinking fast. 3-0 San Francisco and 2-1 Seattle lead the NFC West. Both have easier schedules. Further complicating the climb, the Horns have dealt with constant injuries in the first three games, including many to key starters. Judging where things stand now, they will most likely need to navigate the Wild Card route through the playoffs. Knowing this, games against NFC opponents grow in importance. A Week 2 victory over the Giants was a step in the right direction. Beating the Eagles would be even better.“ Evan Silva’s Matchups: Rams at Eagles (establishthefun) “The Rams’ unprecedented early-season travel schedule rolls on, following up a Sunday night road game in Denver with a cross-country trip to Philadelphia. Matthew Stafford more than made things work sans top WR Puka Nacua (hip) in each of the last two games, notching Weeks 2-3 fantasy finishes of QB5 (vs. NYG) and QB6 (@ DEN). Nacua’s expected return heightens Stafford’s ceiling, while Bears third-stringer Case Keenum ’s picking apart of Philly last Monday night further inspires confidence in the NFL’s reigning MVP. … Blake Corum isn’t going away as a change-of-pace back, but Kyren Williams distanced himself in a high-efficiency Week 3 performance at Denver, out-snapping Corum 61 to 25 and out-touching him 21 to 8. Sean McVay is understandably more willing to lean on Williams in hostile environments, which Philadelphia obviously presents. Williams’ every-week RB1 value is set in stone. Corum remains a mere bench stash, albeit a still-exciting one.“ Los Angeles Rams vs. Philadelphia Eagles NFL Pro Week 4 Preview (nfl.com) “Brett Kollmann and Trevor Sikkema deep dive into the Rams vs. Eagles matchup with key Next Gen Stats insights from NFL Pro.” Rams’ Puka Nacua listed as limited at practice, but his update is better than that (sports.yahoo) “”Rams-Eagles injury report for Thursday. Puka Nacua said he was a full participant today, but he’s officially listed as ‘limited,'” Grosbard posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter. Los Angeles has looked efficient on offense under coach Sean McVay . Davante Adams expectedly handled the air attack slack in Nacua’s absence. But fans know this system is at its most explosive best with Nacua inside the huddle. Yet this offense became turnover prone against the Broncos. Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga stepped in front of two errant Matthew Stafford passes: One that handed Denver a 23-19 lead on a pick six, then the second to seal the win at Empower Field.“ Comment of the Day: “Honest conversations about AD and Garrett would probably suggest that we won’t get a lot from either. Garrett could still pay off down the line, but this is looking like a very sad return for the Ram legend. Things can change, but it doesn’t look good. That said, if the O can stay healthy and peak, we can at least get back to last year with a leaky defense and a high powered offense. No reason that can’t happen. Adams seems MUCH MORE locked in w/ Stafford, and if Puka is getting right, that’s dynamic. TEs when healthy are a solid committee, and our backfield is productive.” -Dr.Ram Feedpost of the Day:

title: Las Vegas Raiders-Kansas City Chiefs FEED topic: Can Raiders’ rushing attack get back on track?
summary: In Week 1, it looked like the Las Vegas Raiders were going to have a much improved running game this season. Second-year running back Ashton Jeanty had just his third career 100-yard game, toting the rock 23 times for 102 yards (4.4 ypc). Additionally, rookie Mike Washington Jr. had seven carries for 41 yards (5.9 […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 1, it looked like the Las Vegas Raiders were going to have a much improved running game this season. Second-year running back Ashton Jeanty had just his third career 100-yard game, toting the rock 23 times for 102 yards (4.4 ypc). Additionally, rookie Mike Washington Jr. had seven carries for 41 yards (5.9 ypc). However, after the last two weeks, that’s looking more like a fluke and says more about the Miami Dolphins than how much the Raiders have improved. Both Jeanty and Washington struggled to find breathing room against the Los Angeles Chargers, combining for 24 rushes and 54 yards (2.3 ypc), as Las Vegas’ offensive line struggled to handle Los Angeles’ front. However, Week 3 was a slightly different story. The line still had room for improvement but did a much better job of creating space in New Orleans, though Jeanty had just 56 rushing yards on 19 carries (2.9 ypc). Meanwhile, it was a much smaller sample size, but Washington found success with five carries for 54 yards and a touchdown (10.8 ypc). That’s led to some debate about who should be getting the lion’s share of touches in the Raiders’ backfield moving forward. However, to be fair, opponents are more concerned about stopping the run when the 2025 first-round pick is in the game. He’s faced “stacked box” (eight or more defenders on the first or second level of the defense) at a higher rate than the rookie has every week, according to Next Gen Stats . Food for thought on the Ashton Jeanty. vs Mike Washington Jr. debate %age of stacked boxes faced week by week, per @NextGenStats Jeanty: 34.8% (MIA), 47.6% (LAC), 31.6% (NO) Washington: 14.3% (MIA), 33.3% (LAC), 20.0% (NO) #Raiders — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 1, 2026 Additionally, Jeanty appears to have reaggravated the ankle injury he suffered at the end of training camp in New Orleans. He wasn’t listed on the Week 3 injury report , then CBS’ broadcast team mentioned he got his ankle retaped mid-game, and he popped up on Wednesday’s Week 4 injury report with an ankle injury. Albeit, the running back was at least a full participant in practice. Regardless, the Raiders are about to play their biggest game of the season yet, with first place on the line against hated rival, the Kansas City Chiefs. Facing an undefeated opponent and an organization that has played in five Super Bowls since 2020, Las Vegas needs to be firing on just about all cylinders to pull off an upset as 4.5-point underdogs. Adding more importance to the Silver and Black’s rushing attack this weekend, the Chiefs’ defense ranks third in the NFL in EPA per pass (-0.20) and is 0.01 points behind the first-place Jacksonville Jaguars, according to Sumer Sports . However, Kansas City is slightly below league average in EPA per rush, coming in at -0.07 and 17th overall. So, whether it’s the offensive line — which could be down a starter after Jackson Powers-Johnson suffered an injury last week — or the two running backs, Klint Kubiak’s crew has to turn back the clock and establish the run this Sunday. That’s why we’ll be focusing on the ground game in this week’s game day discussion on The FEED . The game kicks off at 1:25 p.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!

title: Scouting Patrick Mahomes : Las Vegas Raiders Chiefs Week
summary: Patrick Mahomes has been the gold standard for NFL quarterbacks since coming into the league and sitting behind a pro bowl veteran as a rookie. Drafted 10th overall and getting a year to watch Alex Smith win the division and make the pro bowl showed him what it took to win. What he needed to […]
full_text: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Patrick Mahomes has been the gold standard for NFL quarterbacks since coming into the league and sitting behind a pro bowl veteran as a rookie. Drafted 10th overall and getting a year to watch Alex Smith win the division and make the pro bowl showed him what it took to win. What he needed to do to take the Chiefs to the next level. Which is what the Raiders are attempting to recreate with Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza. Mahomes has been good coming off his season-ending knee injury and is still getting back into the swing of things. The Chiefs offense has been incredibly successful on the ground and he hasn’t had to do much through the air. However, he has shown some things we haven’t been used to seeing. Like all invincible quarterbacks who get injured, the pass rush now seems to affect him a lot more than it used to. Against the Broncos Pressure up the middle appears to be what makes him the most uncomfortable as with all quarterbacks, the game plan against the Broncos called for getting the ball out quickly. The route combinations were floods against zones and crossers against man. Never-ending motions and check-motions in attempts to get the defense to top their hands. Lots of run-pass options and play actions. However, when pressure came from the outside, he was able to negotiate it and find preferable outcomes by escaping up the middle, which he did numerous times and scored on one of them. Replacing the blitzing defender with the football for a completion, or evaded them as a whole. He did throw an interception to the safety deep across the middle on a bad ball. Vs the Colts Mahomes threw the ball a staggering 47 times completing 32 of them for 382 yards and three touchdowns in the overtime contest against the Indianapolis Colts. All three touchdowns were short passes to the right side of the field (13,1,1). Starting with the quick screen RPO game, he completed 11/13 passes behind the line of scrimmage, inside 10 yards he was 16/20, 3/6 in intermediate areas and ⅔ to the deep right. Vs the Dolphins Mahomes was much more efficient against the Miami Dolphins completing 20/24 passes for 246 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception. Three weeks in and throwing nearly 30% of his passes behind the line of scrimmage (7/7, 1 touchdown), 33% (seven of eight) in the short range. In the intermediate range (10-20 yards) Mahomes was three of five all to the right side with a touchdown, and two of three to the deep left with an interception. How best to attack Mahomes in 2026 When blitzing Mahomes from the outside it’s best to do it while pressing his receivers. Forcing him to hold the ball and not hit the first/hot read allows the defense the time to get home. Pressures up the middle lead to errant throws. Do not under any circumstances leave the middle of the field uncovered. Linebackers are going to need phenomenal eye discipline. The window dressing is designed to get them to vacate the middle of the field and Travis Kelce is making a home in between the hashes. Twists and stunts can be effective when used in proper combination, it isn’t recommended to blitz from the side of the field Kelce is on. A big game from Folorunso Fatukasi, Adam Butler and Tonka Hemingway would be ideal. The Raiders are #1 in pressure percentage and doing it with little blitzing is the way to go.

title: What has Kenneth Walker III brought to Kansas City Chiefs’ offense leading up to Week 4 matchup vs. Las Vegas Raiders?
summary: While the Las Vegas Raiders and Kansas City Chiefs have a historic rivalry, the two teams haven’t met with first place in the AFC West on the line in about a decade (Dec. 8, 2016). Technically, Las Vegas has never been involved in this type of matchup with Kansas City since the Raiders were still […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Las Vegas Raiders and Kansas City Chiefs have a historic rivalry, the two teams haven’t met with first place in the AFC West on the line in about a decade (Dec. 8, 2016). Technically, Las Vegas has never been involved in this type of matchup with Kansas City since the Raiders were still in Oakland back then. It’s still early in the season, but the Week 4 contest between the Raiders and Chiefs is one of the biggest regular-season games the Silver and Black have played in a long time. To preview the huge matchup, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our frienemies at Arrowhead Pride, and Maurice Elston was kind enough to answer a few questions about Kansas City for Raider Nation. Q: Kenneth Walker III was the Chiefs’ big offseason addition and hasn’t disappointed, with 442 yards from scrimmage and four total touchdowns in the first three games. How has he revitalized Kansas City’s offense? A: The easiest way to explain Walker’s impact is that Patrick Mahomes has never had a 1,000-yard rusher during his career as the Chiefs’ starting quarterback. Kareem Hunt rushed for 824 yards in 11 games during Mahomes’ first season as the starter before being released, but every Chiefs backfield since then has consisted primarily of serviceable players rather than a dynamic, home-run threat like Walker. Walker has helped Kansas City operate from under center and lean more heavily on play action. Against Miami, Mahomes completed 11 of 12 play-action passes for 183 yards. That is a dimension we have not consistently seen from this offense in recent years, when it relied more heavily on shotgun formations and RPOs. Walker’s success also changes how defenses must prepare for Kansas City. In previous seasons, opponents could concentrate on limiting Mahomes and preventing explosive passing plays. Now, if a defense sits back in coverage with light boxes, Kansas City can hand the ball to Walker. His presence has restored balance and forced opponents to defend every part of the offense. Q: What’s going on with expected starting left tackle Josh Simmons? Is there any timeline for his return? What can you tell us about Fernando Mendoza’s college teammate, Kahlil Benson, who has been filling in for Simmons? A: The Chiefs have been extremely vague about Josh Simmons’ back injury. Andy Reid has described him as week-to-week but has not provided a firm timetable, recently telling reporters that he would let them know when Simmons was ready to return. I do not believe anyone outside the organization can confidently offer more than assumptions right now. One of my high school coaches always said that you cannot worry about who is not on the field—you have to focus on who is. Right now, that player is Kahlil Benson, an undrafted rookie who played with Fernando Mendoza at Indiana. Benson has experienced some expected challenges while transitioning from primarily playing on the right side to starting at left tackle in the NFL. However, nobody should be disappointed with his overall performance. Through three games, he has allowed six pressures and two quarterback hits but no sacks. He has been particularly effective as a run blocker, earning a 74.7 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus . His pass protection has been serviceable, and sometimes that is exactly what an offense needs from a rookie thrown into this situation. He certainly has not hurt the offense. Sunday’s matchup with Maxx Crosby will easily be one of the most difficult tests he has faced. Q: It’s only been three games, but Travis Kelce has his highest yards per game ( 77.0 ) since 2022 and looks much more like his old self so far this season. Besides marrying one of the biggest celebrities in the world over the summer, what’s been different for Kelce compared to the last three or four years? A: The improved running and play-action games have helped Kelce as much as anyone. He remains an excellent route runner who understands how to find the soft spots in a defense. Now, linebackers and safeties must respect Walker and the running game before dropping into coverage. Kansas City has used play action on 36% of its passing plays, the highest rate in the league. That has helped create open space for Kelce, who has 14 catches for 231 yards and is averaging 16.5 yards per reception through three games. Kelce also deserves personal credit. He appears to be in some of the best shape we have seen him in over the past few seasons, and he is playing with a fire that seemed to be missing at times during the last couple of years. I believe he will return to the 1,000-yard mark this season and remind everyone why he is still one of the NFL’s best tight ends—and, in my opinion, the greatest tight end of all time. Q: Kansas City made some significant changes in the secondary this offseason, most notably trading away All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie and drafting Mansoor Delane as McDuffie’s replacement. How have the rookie and the rest of the defensive backfield looked so far? A: Delane could not have scripted a much better beginning to his career. He intercepted the first NFL pass thrown in his direction against Denver, although he injured his shoulder on the play. He missed the remainder of that game and dressed against Indianapolis only as an emergency option. His first complete game came against Miami, and he showed why the Chiefs selected him sixth overall. Delane recorded 10 tackles, including a tackle for loss, and broke up a fourth-down pass. He was targeted seven times and allowed five completions, but those catches produced only 24 yards. His tackling, physicality and ability to limit yards after the catch were impressive. Opposite Delane, Nohl Williams has been excellent. I believe the Chiefs’ belief in Williams—and what they saw from him as a rookie—helped give them the confidence to trade McDuffie. Delane and Williams already look capable of becoming a strong young outside-cornerback combination. The rest of the secondary has been more inconsistent. L’Jarius Sneed has allowed an 80% completion rate when targeted, although he continues to contribute in other ways. Against Miami, he generated five pressures as a blitzer and forced a turnover. The safeties had a difficult game against the Dolphins, with Alohi Gilman taking some poor angles and Jaden Hicks not playing the ball as well as we are accustomed to seeing. Chamarri Conner’s eventual return from his knee injury should help. It will also give us our first real opportunity to see him consistently play his natural safety position rather than primarily working in the slot. This is a young secondary, but I expect it to improve as the season progresses. Q: When it comes to the Chiefs’ defensive line, Raider Nation knows Chris Jones and George Karlaftis pretty well at this point. But is there a d-lineman or two who is new or flying under the radar and could make a major impact on Sunday? A: R Mason Thomas is the first player who comes to mind. The rookie has natural pass-rushing ability, gets off the ball quickly and already has his first NFL sack. His role is also expanding. He played 41 defensive snaps against Miami, which was 10 more than starter Felix Anudike-Uzomah. Peter Woods is another rookie whose role continues to grow. He played 35 snaps against Miami, five more than starting defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga. Woods has not produced many traditional pass-rushing statistics yet, but he is becoming a bigger part of the defensive-line rotation every week. The player I would watch most closely Sunday, however, is Anudike-Uzomah. He is in a contract year after the Chiefs declined his fifth-year option, and he has quietly played solid football. The Chiefs’ overall pass rush has not been as productive as expected, but some of that can be attributed to Chris Jones playing through a calf injury. Once Jones returns to full strength and starts dominating the interior again, it should create more one-on-one…

title: Raiders injury news: Jackson Powers-Johnson out against Chiefs
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders will be without a starting offensive lineman in their pivotal battle of 3-0 teams when they host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday as coach Klint Kubiak ruled out right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson on Friday. Powers-Johnson missed the entire week of practice after he suffered a groin injury that cost his […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders will be without a starting offensive lineman in their pivotal battle of 3-0 teams when they host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday as coach Klint Kubiak ruled out right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson on Friday. Powers-Johnson missed the entire week of practice after he suffered a groin injury that cost his the five final plays at New Orleans on Sunday. Earlier in the week, Kubiak said the team was hopeful Powers-Johnson can practice at some point this week to give him a chance to play against Kansas City. 2025 third-round pick Caleb Rogers spelled Powers-Johnson on Sunday and is in line to start Sunday. He started six games as a rookie last season. Powers-Johnson beat out Rogers, a Texas Tech product, in training camp this year. Kubiak has said the team feels that both players are starting-caliber types. This will be Powers-Johnson 12th missed game due to injury out of a possible 38 NFL games. The 2024 second-round pick out of Oregon missed the final eight games of last season with an ankle injury. Meanwhile, No. 3 quarterback Aidan O’Connell is still away from the team. He has been gone for 15 days dealing with the death of his father. Kubiak said this week that the team would hopeful O’Connell would return for this game and Friday Kubiak maintained that hope. He is listed as questionable to play Sunday. Both tight end Brock Bowers (knee) and wide receiver Cody White (ankle) were limited in practice Friday after working fully Wedensday and Thursday. However, they are ready to play Sunday. Every other player on the 53-man roster is healthy enough to play Sunday, so most of the inactive players will be healthy scratches. Meanwhile, Kubiak said wide receiver Dont’e Thornton is working hard to return from the injured reserve. The team can activate him after Sunday’s game. Kubiak did say she is not sure of Thornton’s timeline.

title: Jeremy Chinn is Las Vegas Raiders’ best chance at stopping Travis Kelce in Week 4 key matchups vs. Kansas City Chiefs
summary: The stakes couldn’t be higher for an early-season game than they are in the Week 4 contest between the Las Vegas Raiders and Kansas City Chiefs. First place in the AFC West is on the line, with both teams entering the battle undefeated at 3-0. That adds some importance to the three key matchups below. […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The stakes couldn’t be higher for an early-season game than they are in the Week 4 contest between the Las Vegas Raiders and Kansas City Chiefs . First place in the AFC West is on the line, with both teams entering the battle undefeated at 3-0 . That adds some importance to the three key matchups below. Chinn vs. Kelce Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is a future Hall of Famer who famously had seven consecutive 1,000-yard seasons from 2016 to 2022. However, Kelce failed to reach that mark during the next three years. The statistical regression and his age made it seem like retirement was on the table, where the Ohio native would just enjoy life with a celebrity wife and wait to get his gold jacket in Canton. But that hasn’t been the case. The soon-to-be 37-year-old returned to Kansas City’s sideline for another year and has seemingly found the Fountain of Youth through the first three games of the 2026 campaign. He’s hauled in 14 catches for 231 yards and two touchdowns while averaging 77.0 yards per game , just 1.7 yards fewer than his 2022 rate that resulted in over 1,300 yards and a first-team All-Pro bid. On top of that, Kelce is moving much more like his old self. According to Next Gen Stats , his average route speed is the highest it has been in four years (h/t Yahoo! Sports’ Nate Tice on X/Twitter ). Meanwhile, the Raiders’ defense is coming off a game where they allowed 12 catches, 86 yards and four touchdowns to New Orleans Saints tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant. Part of the reason for that is rookie free safety Treydan Stukes missed last week with a concussion, and Stukes’ replacement, Isaiah Pola-Mao, was the unit’s primary issue in coverage. Head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed that the rookie will be back this Sunday , which should keep Pola-Mao sidelined and allow strong safety Jeremy Chinn to play in the box more, where he projects to draw plenty of matchups with Kelce. Chinn is known for what he brings as a run defender, but the 6-foot-3, 220-pound safety who posted a perfect Relative Athletic Score (10 out of 10) as a draft prospect is physically the best option the Raiders have to match up against Kelce. While Chinn has below-average ball skills and production, allowing five catches on five targets so far in 2026, he can be effective at limiting the damage. According to Pro Football Focus , he’s only allowed 53 yards over three games, is giving up a reception once every 22.6 coverage snaps, and has 10 tackles with two ‘ defensive stops ’ in coverage. Also, PFF has Chinn giving up just two grabs for 19 yards and one first down against tight ends specifically so far this season. Granted, he hasn’t faced a player of Kelce’s caliber yet, and he had a tough time against Kansas City’s passing attack last year, giving up five catches for 45 yards and a touchdown in the only game he played against the Chiefs. To be fair, Noah Gray did more damage against Chinn than Kelce did. But expect Andy Reid to test the safety with his best pass-catcher early and often this time around. Raiders’ LBs vs. Walker Week 4 will be Kenneth Walker III’s introduction to the Raiders-Chiefs rivalry after signing with Kansas City during free agency this past spring. Seeing as he’s currently the NFL’s leading rusher with 360 yards on the ground, you’d be hard-pressed to find a more impactful offseason addition in the early stages of the campaign. A big reason why Walker has gotten off to a hot start with the Chiefs is that he also has the most yards after contact (303) in the league, and leads running backs with at least 15 carries in yards after contact per attempt (4.66), according to PFF . Additionally, the former Seattle Seahawk has forced the most missed tackles at the position with 34, 12 more than anyone else. To make matters even more complicated for the Silver and Black, Walker has been a productive receiver out of the backfield, collecting 11 catches for 82 yards and two touchdowns through three games. Those figures rank tied for sixth, eighth and tied for first , respectively, at his position. But the Raiders have a decent counter when it comes to this matchup and impactful free-agent signings, as linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker have been strong to begin the year. Those two enter the contest with Top-20 PFF run defense grades , with Walker ranking tied for ninth at 76.0 and Dean coming in at 17th with a 71.4 mark. Additionally, the latter is tied for 10th with seven defensive stops against the run at a fairly high rate (10.1%), which is 18th-best. Dean has also made several impactful plays by forcing a fumble in every game so far. However, he has had some tackling issues with six misses (tied for the second-most at his position) and a 17.6% miss rate (11th-highest), per PFF . That needs to get cleaned up moving forward, but five out of six have come in coverage, and this is where Walker can step in. The other former Georgia Bulldog’s contributions have gotten somewhat overshadowed by his running mates’. But make no mistake about it, his presence has been felt on Vegas’ defense. Walker is second on the team with 24 tackles , only three behind Dean, and he’s only been charged with one miss so far. Also, he’s yielded just 43 yards in coverage and has yet to give up 20 yards in a single game. Given every player in the equation’s skill sets, this could be a situation where Dean’s primary focus is to stop the Chiefs’ running back in the ground game while Walker draws him in coverage. In other words, both backers have to be on their games and fill their roles. Also, it wouldn’t be surprising to see defensive coordinator Rob Leonard try to take advantage of Walker’s unique size and athleticism (6-foot-4, 241 pounds and a 9.63 RAS ) to help slow down Kelce. Raiders’ IOL vs. Jones/Bolton Technically, a couple of matchups are getting lumped into one here. The reason for that is one has to do with Las Vegas’ passing game and the other is centered on the rushing attack, while both involve the interior offensive line. Like Kelce, Raider Nation knows all too well about Chris Jones, as the defensive tackle has tormented the Silver and Black for about a decade. Jones has 13.5sacks in 10 career games against the Raiders and has consistently been a pest for the club over the years. Granted, the 32-year-old has shown signs of slowing down in recent seasons and has had a slow start so far this fall. He’s yet to get to the quarterback and only has eight pressures on 81 pass-rush snaps, while ranking just 22nd among defensive tackles with a 12.2 win percentage, per PFF . To be fair, the pressures and win rate aren’t bad numbers by any means, but it’s certainly not the standard we’ve become accustomed to from Jones. Also, he’s been battling a calf injury, and it wouldn’t be surprising to see him get up for a game of this magnitude. On the other side of the trenches, free-agent signing and center Tyler Linderbaum has brought some stability to Vegas’ offensive line, especially in pass protection. He’s been credited with getting the entire unit on the same page, one of the position’s biggest and most important tasks, and has given up just two pressures on 101 opportunities so far. The guard spots are still dicey for the Raiders, though. Left guard Spencer Burford has yielded 12 pressures , which is tied for the most among guards with Houston Texans rookie Keylan Rutledge, who has had 33 more opportunities to give up a pressure than Burford has. Right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson has been a little better with seven pressures allowed. However, he left last week’s game with a groin injury and is questionable for Sunday at the time of writing. Second-year pro Caleb Rogers is the next man up and has pass-blocked exactly one time this season. It was a good rep, though, as he didn’t get beaten! In the running game, linebacker Nick Bolton has built a reputation as one of the better two-down defenders in the league. This…

full_text: (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders improved to 3-0 with a 35-27 Week 3 win at the New Orleans Saints . Let’s look at their wide-receiver production in the game Jalen Nailor The free-agent addition played 40 snaps (57 percent), which was tied for the team high by wide receivers. He had 1 catch for 16 yards on three targets. He has five catches for 62 yards on 11 targets in two games. The Raiders signed him to a three-year, $35 million contract this offseason. Tre Tucker Tucker also played 40 snaps. He had four catches for 43 yards, as he caught all four of his targets. In Week 2, Tucker five catches for 119 yards and a score. He had two catches of 40-plus yards. Of course, star tight end Brock Bowers stole the show in Week 3 with 10 catches for 116 yards and he lined up as a receiver often. Cody White: The player, elevated from the practice squad, played 15 offensive snaps. He had 1 catch for four yards and yes, it was another touchdown. He has three catches for three touchdown. Wild. Dareke Young: He played 12 offensive snaps for the second straight game. He was not targeted Jack Bech The 2025 second-round pick played 1 snaps in Week 3 before breaking his forearm. He will be out for an extended period. Bech wasn’t target before his injury. He has five catches for 48 yards on six targets this season. Malik Benson The rookie sixth-round pick played played four offensive snaps in Week 3 and was targeted once without a catch. He has played 19 offensive snaps in three games. He has one catch on four targets. Conclusion: The Raiders’ wide receivers had six catches for 63 yards and a touchdown against the Saints on 11 targets. Yes, Bowers was essentially a receiver, but the others in this group need to produce more.

(Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings will be without top wide receiver Justin Jefferson for their Week 4 game against the Miami Dolphins, head coach Kevin O’Connell told the media on Friday. Jefferson is dealing with an ankle injury that he sustained during the team’s Week 3 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Vikings will rely on wide receivers Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings in Jefferson’s absences. The four-time Pro Bowl receiver has 13 receptions for 179 yards and two touchdowns this season. O’Connell had indicated earlier in the week that he was optimistic that Jefferson would be able to play, but the receiver will now have to sit out at least Sunday’s game. The loss of Jefferson is not a good situation for quarterback Kyler Murray and the Vikings’ offense, which is statistically the worst offense in the NFL through three weeks, averaging just 238.3 yards per game. In comparison, the Dolphins rank 27th in total offense this year, averaging 290.7 yards per game. The full injury report will be released Friday afternoon.

title: Miami Dolphins vs. Minnesota Vikings: Three reasons the Dolphins can win, lose in Week 4
summary: The Miami Dolphins show signs of life.  They hung with the Kansas City Chiefs for most of the game and could have been in contention for a win without penalties, mistakes, and other issues young teams need to clean up.  This week, the Dolphins face the 3-0 Vikings, making Miami the 2nd team in NFL […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass against the Kansas City Chiefs during the first quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Alie Skowronski/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins show signs of life. They hung with the Kansas City Chiefs for most of the game and could have been in contention for a win without penalties, mistakes, and other issues young teams need to clean up. This week, the Dolphins face the 3-0 Vikings, making Miami the 2nd team in NFL history and the 1st since 1986 to have their first 4 opponents go undefeated (hat tip to Urthling). Talk about a brutal schedule. Maybe we could have foreseen the Chiefs and Niners, but the Raiders and Vikings are a surprising 3-0. Anyway, this game is not without its own glimmers of hope. Reasons for hope Miami’s offense is showing some potential The Chiefs’ defense generally doesn’t get much media attention because all the focus is on quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the offense. But their defense is top 5 or top 10 in total yards allowed (4th), passing yards allowed (6th), rushing yards allowed (10th), and in scoring defense (3rd). Miami was expected to struggle offensively, despite being at home. It was supposed to be even worse when they lost Achane to injury. However, the Dolphins managed 329 yards of offense, including some explosive plays, and for the first time this season, they didn’t have a single 3-and-out… unless you wanna count the 3-play drive to end the game when it didn’t matter. They moved the ball without Douglas and Achane for all or most of the game. Now, it wasn’t all sunshine and rainbows. The Dolphins had 2 drives that ended in a turnover on downs. They also fumbled in scoring territory where at least a field goal was likely. The offense committed several penalties that set them back, and this team isn’t capable of consistently overcoming that. But they made progress and should keep developing as the season moves forward. Minnesota’s offense is bad Despite everything I just wrote, the Dolphins’ offense is still bad. At least in terms of scoring. They are averaging 12 PPG and haven’t gotten over 13 points in any game. But in terms of yardage, they aren’t the worst. Their opponent this week IS the worst offense in this regard. The Vikings are dead last in total yards at 715, passing yards at 411, and are just above the Dolphins in rushing yards at 304 (tied for 16th; Miami is 20th at 295). The Vikings score more than the Dolphins, averaging 23.7 PPG. But they have faced the Bears (7th in scoring defense), Bucs (23rd in scoring defense), and the Packers (30th in scoring defense). The Dolphins have faced the Chiefs (3rd), 49ers (5th), and Raiders (8th). The Dolphins have faced the 6th, 10th, and 14th best passing defenses. The Vikings have faced the 11th-, 12th-, and 13th-best passing defenses. The Dolphins have faced the 10th, 15th, and 20th best run defenses. The Vikings have faced the 2nd, 21st, and 28th best run defenses. I could make other comparisons, like opponents’ pressure percentages and so on, but I think you can smell what The Earl is cooking here. As bad as the Dolphins offense has been, the Vikings have been similarly bad. If there was ever a game for a struggling secondary to have a chance… Miami’s defense is also showing some potential So far, the Dolphins have faced some tough offenses. They got their feet wet against the Raiders and Ashton Jeanty. They faced the juggernaut 49ers and their arsenal of weapons, then came home to face off against Mahomes and the league’s leading rusher. The Dolphins have faced the 2nd- and 3rd-ranked teams in scoring offenses this season. The Niners are averaging 32.7 PPG while the two AFCW teams are tied at 29.3. That is a LOT of scoring. Yet in Week 3, they held the Chiefs to 17 points until a late drive pushed them to 24. The Chiefs and Niners are tied for 6th in passing yards. I discussed the issues with the total number of incompletions Miami allowed, but they have faced tough opponents. In the last two games, the Dolphins have allowed less than 100 yards rushing, including just 88 total yards to the Chiefs, who have the league’s top rusher. They limited him to 70 yards on 18 carries – 3.9 YPC – including a 22-yard run. Meaning they held him to 48 yards on the other 17 carries – 2.8 YPC. That’s solid work against a guy who went over 100 yards in the previous 2 games. The Chiefs said they wanted to lighten his workload, but the other RB went 6 for 17. The passing defense still needs work, but instead of Purdy or Mahomes, they get the Murray/Wentz combo that is averaging 137 passing yards per game. Something will have to give here. The rookies are also stepping up. Miami also saw rookie CB Chris Johnson go untargeted by Mahomes all game. Rookie LB Jacob Rodriguez is tied for 7th in the league in combined tackles at 28 and has 3 TFLs, which is tied for 17th with several players. That is solid considering he doesn’t get sacks added to that total. He also generated a turnover this week with the INT and is now the leading favorite to win defensive rookie of the year. The Dolphins still haven’t recorded a sack but did manage to generate 8 pressures in this game (per PFR). Miami’s 3 previous opponents have lower-end pressure percentages, but now face Murray, who is pressured about as much as we have seen Willis get pressured. Could this be the game for the defense to get things right, build some confidence, and start to turn this ship around? Reasons for Concern Vikings still have weapons As fun as it is to discuss the Vikings’ potential offensive ineptitude, they still have a dynamic WR duo in Justin Jefferson (who may not play) and Jordan Addison, plus a good receiving TE in TJ Hockenson. They have Aaron Jones at RB, who is currently 12th in the league with 203 yards. Despite the emerging potential from the pass defense, they have still not forced more than 6 incompletions in the last 2 games. Part of that is a lack of pressure, and part of that is softer coverage. If either or both of those issues show up, the Vikings have more than enough talent on offense to make the Dolphins pay. The Vikings have also faced circumstances that could explain a lack of offensive production. They scored 39 points at home in week 1 but lost their starting QB in the 1st quarter. That generally puts a damper on the offense, even if the backup is good. That backup then had to travel to face a good Chicago team in week 2, the one top-ten scoring defense they have faced. Then they had to travel to Tampa Bay to face the 6th-ranked defense in yards allowed. One home game with injury issues and 2 road games. Now the Vikings have their starter back and will be playing at home against a defense that allows 80.3% of opponents’ passes to be completed and allows 28.7 PPG. Maybe the Vikings offense is the one that can help the Dolphins defense turn their ship around. Or maybe the Dolphins defense is the one for the Vikings offense to turn their ship around. On the road again The Dolphins are singing like Willie because they travel to face an opponent for the 3rd time in 4 games. Road games in the NFL are tough for anyone and even more so for a struggling team. The Vikings are more than a TD favorite, and ESPN’s matchup predictor gives Minnesota an 83.1% chance to win . For an offense that has struggled with pre-snap issues, they now have to go play in a raucous environment where noise will be a factor. Miami committed 8 penalties in week 1 and 7 penalties in week 2. In each game, 6 of those penalties were offensive. This issue can rear its ugly head again this week, and this offense cannot afford to get behind the sticks and in unfavorable down-and-distance situations because… Vikings defense and the Brian Flores factor I saved the worst for last because this has the potential to unravel any of the hope I mentioned. We’ll start with Flores. Everyone is…
