title: NY Giants news: Malik Nabers, J.J. McCarthy, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about as the Giants look to stay atop the NFC East with a win this Sunday. NFL Week 4 preview | ESPN.com The Giants seem to know they’re not facing the Titans’ offense again this week. It was mentioned several times […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about as the Giants look to stay atop the NFC East with a win this Sunday. NFL Week 4 preview | ESPN.com The Giants seem to know they’re not facing the Titans’ offense again this week. It was mentioned several times that the Cardinals are “very similar” offensively to the Rams — who dismantled the Giants two weeks ago — which DC Dennard Wilson noted because of Arizona coach Mike LaFleur’s ties to Sean McVay. New York knows it’s going to be a difficult challenge, particularly stopping rookie RB Jeremiyah Love, who it had ranked as a top-three player in the 2026 draft. Can Jameis Winston hold off JJ McCarthy? Where’s the pass rush? What to watch for in Giants-Cardinals | The Athletic A weak Arizona Cardinals pass defense should provide the streaky Winston an opportunity to find his groove. But if Winston struggles again and the Giants lose, the focus immediately will shift to his job security. A key variable will be how quickly McCarthy learns the offense. He only has 10 career starts and the Giants’ offense puts a lot on the quarterback’s plate. Rushing McCarthy into action before he’s ready would be a huge mistake. But there’s an understanding that McCarthy won’t be able to fully get up to speed on the offense midstream. With an upcoming stretch against the 1-2 Cardinals, the 1-2 Commanders, the 1-2 Saints and the 0-3 Texans, the Giants’ best bet to building momentum is Winston turning things around. If the 2-1 Giants can’t string some wins together now, it will be asking a lot for McCarthy to save the season when the schedule stiffens after their Week 8 bye. New Giants QB candid about if he can thrive amid fresh start: ‘Nobody knows’ | NJ.com McCarthy said he’s attacking the new offense day-by-day, but said he feels he’s picking it up pretty quickly. When asked how close he is to being ready to go into a game, McCarthy said, “At the end of the day, I’m just focused on watching this practice, learning from it and making sure I get this game plan down. I’m really just focused on being in the present moment and going from there.” McCarthy wasn’t interested in dwelling on what went wrong in Minnesota. “There’s a multitude of things you can think of, but at the end of the day, it’s all in the past,” he said. “All I care about is what’s important now — that next rep, that next meeting, that next game. That’s really all I’m focused on.” Giants rookie Colton Hood ‘baptized by fire’ by intense NFL initiation | New York Post Initiations into the NFL don’t get any more difficult than defending Matthew Stafford throwing to Davante Adams in your first career start. But Hood also allowed Wan’Dale Robinson’s touchdown last game. Hood has allowed 11 catches on 15 targets for 106 yards and two touchdowns over three games, according to NextGenStats. Opposing quarterbacks have a 132.2 rating when throwing at him. “I’m encouraged by, just watching the film, none of it is, ‘This guy is just better than me and beat me,’ ” Hood told The Post. “It’s more just seeing things for the first time and processing things post-snap. It’s just that I’m at a different level and learning how to combat those things. The routes in the league are different, you have to adjust to the depth. And the coverages, you have to understand not just your job but the people around you’s job so you can play tighter.” Rush to judgment as Giants defense promises to crank things up on QBs | The Record The New York Giants have looked in the mirror. They’ve studied the tape and scoured the stat sheet, only to be left incredibly disappointed with what they have seen. DC Dennard Wilson thinks Jihad Ward can be ‘good factor’ in Giants defense | SNY.tv Ward appeared in all 17 of Tennessee’s games (starting 12 of them) and he recorded career-highs in defensive snaps (708), quarterback hits (22), and sacks (5.0). “Haddy is a guy that played extremely well for me,” Wilson said. “He brings versatility to play on the edge, he brings versatility to play in the middle of the defense if we need, and he can be an interior rusher if we need, too. Haddy’s going to be ready when his number is called. We’ll see how it plays out from today going forward to Sunday and the weeks after that — but he’s an ultimate professional, and he’s going to be prepared. He’s been in camp with the Vikings, he’s in shape, so we’ll see how the chips fall here — I feel that Haddy could be a good factor in our defense moving forward.” Scouts: Giants Unlikely To Find Buried Treasure In McCarthy | FOX Sports “There’s no doubt McCarthy has talent,” one scout told me. “He’s probably a good fit for what they want to do, too. But honestly, if the Vikings were willing to dump their one-time franchise quarterback for a fifth-round pick, you really got to wonder what they know. Teams don’t usually dump young quarterbacks like that, especially ones they took 10th overall.” “Think about that,” one NFL assistant told me. “He couldn’t beat out Murray or Wentz. That doesn’t happen to a high first-round pick. That’s what happens with late-round and practice squad-type guys. So that tells you everything about what Minnesota thinks of him. Maybe a change of scenery will help. But O’Connell is pretty good with quarterbacks. If he couldn’t get anything out of the kid, I don’t know if anyone on the Giants can.” From Big Blue View Despite McCarthy-mania, Matt Nagy reminds that Jameis Winston is the Giants’ QB No Giants’ players with injury designations heading into game vs. Cardinals Malik Nabers still learning to trust his knee after surgery Giants vs. Cardinals: Arizona offense poses challenges for New York Giants vs. Cardinals: Arizona defense presents an opportunity It’s an underdog weekend for the NFC East Giants vs. Cardinals, NFL Week 4: News, injuries, analysis, more This week’s opponent Cardinals Defense Prepares For Jameis Winston Experience | AZCardinals.com Cardinals Deep Dive: 3 Problems Standing Between Them and 2-2 | SI.com Will the Arizona Cardinals take advantage of an ailing New York Giants? | Revenge of the Birds Rip The Band-Aid Off: Why Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr. Needs A Career Reset | FOX Sports BBV mailbag Have a Giants-related question? title: No Giants’ players with injury designations heading into game vs. Cardinals
summary: New York Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) was a limited practice participant on Friday, and coach John Harbaugh said he is trending toward playing Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. Thomas does have a game status on the official injury report, meaning he is expected to play. Thomas did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, likely […]
full_text: New York Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) was a limited practice participant on Friday, and coach John Harbaugh said he is trending toward playing Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. Thomas does have a game status on the official injury report, meaning he is expected to play. Thomas did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, likely as part of the plan to keep him available on game day. Starting center John Michael Schmitz missed practice due to a family matter. Harbaugh expects Schmitz to be ready to play on Sunday. All other Giants were full practice participants. That means cornerback Deonte Banks, who has missed two games, and safety Tyler Nubin, who missed one, should be available. Both have been dealing with calf injuries. Running back Tyrone Tracy, held out of Wednesday’s practice with a knee injury, was also a full participant. For the Cardinals, safety Dadrion Taylor-Demerson is out due to a back injury. Linebacker Josh Sweat is questionable with a groin injury.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants’ WR Malik Nabers still learning to trust his knee
summary: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers has 12 catches in three games as he comes back from last season’s torn ACL. He admitted this week that he is still learning to trust his surgically-repaired knee. “It looks better each and every day. Little things that I see when I’m watching myself play that I’m […]
full_text: Malik Nabers | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers has 12 catches in three games as he comes back from last season’s torn ACL. He admitted this week that he is still learning to trust his surgically-repaired knee. “It looks better each and every day. Little things that I see when I’m watching myself play that I’m like, okay, I’m going to emphasize that in practice the next day. So just overall, just trusting my knee,” Nabers said. “I think that’s the last thing everybody’s been talking to me about is you got to be able to trust your knee and just go out there, do exactly what I feel like I can do and do it like just do it. If you never do it, you never know if you really can do it if you don’t push yourself to do it. So, I think just trusting it and just do it.” Nabers is averaging 4.0 receptions, 8.0 yards per catch, and 32.0 yards per games. Those numbers are well off the 7.3 catches, 11.0 yards per catch, and 80.3 receiving yards per game he averaged as a rookie in 2024. Nabers knows there are plays where he has left yards on the table. “Just like the slant I ran this past week, just overall, just that’s one of those catches that I made before that I’m able to take 25, 30 yards, maybe even more. But I left a lot,” he said. “No, it wasn’t really, just it wasn’t really just thinking on that route. I caught it, seen a hole and then broke out running. But probably could have got way more. I think before I would have got injured, what I would have got maybe more? I probably think for sure.” Skattebo pleads for fan support Cam Skattebo noticed the empty seats last Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Miserable weather conditions had a lot to do with that, but the second-year running back is hoping for a rowdy crowd Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. “Obviously it’s hard, but – because a lot of people come to the games to see certain players. And if that’s why they didn’t come that game and that’s why they weren’t rowdy, then I understand,” Skattebo said. “But there’s still – we have 14 more games to play at minimum. We have to continue to bring our fan base in, have people coming in and giving their efforts and spirit to us. You know, that’s – teams are built off of what’s surrounding them. And if they have a good fan base – I was at Arizona State, for instance, and the fan base when I first got there was not very good. We ended up building an amazing fan base, sold out every game my senior year, and look (at) what team we turned into. “So, when you get that camaraderie from the people around you in your city, the people walking down the street when you’re going to the grocery store, you feel better about yourself when people are talking to you about how good the Giants are. That makes you feel better. And when you come in the building, your football team is better because everyone feels that way. And I think if we continue to have the city of New York, the state of New Jersey, continue to build on what we have, I think we’re going to be just fine.” Yes, we’re talking about the long-snapper Punter Jordan Stout was outstanding last Sunday against the Titans. Rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada went 4 of 4 on field goals, accounting for all of the Giants’ points. Special teams coordinator Chris Horton this week gave rookie long-snapper Ben Mann props for his role in helping those things happen. “Ben had a heck of a day. I mean, just fired up for him, him running down the field, making a tackle, just being in the right place,” Horton said. “And if you know anything about just those three guys, that’s why I said specialists, those three guys, they go hand in hand because everything starts with that snap. That ball is wet. He’s got to put a good ball back there. He’s got to give a great ball to Jordan. And then Jordan’s got to get that ball down in order for us to make kicks. “So, I mean, everything that we talk about with our specialists, when I’m talking specialists, I’m talking all three guys, just playing at a high level. And that’s what we want to see. I thought those guys did a heck of a job.”

title: Giants vs. Cardinals: Arizona offense poses challenges for New York
summary: The New York Giants will host the 1-2 Arizona Cardinals at 1 p.m. Sunday, with Arizona favored by 2.5 points and the Over/Under set at 44.5. The Cardinals opened the season with a surprising 26-14 road victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, though Los Angeles has since shown itself to be a struggling team. Arizona […]
full_text: Jacoby Brissett has been a pleasant surprise | Getty Images The New York Giants will host the 1-2 Arizona Cardinals at 1 p.m. Sunday, with Arizona favored by 2.5 points and the Over/Under set at 44.5. The Cardinals opened the season with a surprising 26-14 road victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, though Los Angeles has since shown itself to be a struggling team. Arizona followed that win with a lopsided 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 2, but bounced back with a strong showing against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 3, falling 36-30 in a more competitive game, especially after trailing 23-6. The Giants are 2-1, coming off an uninspiring 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Jameis Winston has struggled over the past two weeks, and he’ll face an Arizona defense that surrendered 297 passing yards and four touchdowns to Brock Purdy in Week 3, following a Week 2 performance in which Drew Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns. The seat is beginning to warm up for Winston. New York traded a 2027 fifth-round pick for J.J. McCarthy, raising an obvious question: How much longer will the Giants tolerate inconsistent quarterback play? Can New York’s defense continue giving the offense enough opportunities to win close games, as it did in Week 3? Complementary football has long eluded the Giants. The special teams unit has been a bright spot, but the defense faces a major test against Arizona—especially after the injury to Brian Burns. Can New York’s defense hold up without one of its leaders against an Arizona team that’s shown more competency than many anticipated, despite their 1-2 record? Let’s look at the Cardinals’ personnel and statistics to answer that question. The Cardinals’ offense Over three games, the Cardinals rank 18th in points per game, averaging 21 points per game. The Giants are 28th in the NFL, averaging 15.3 points per game. The Cardinals rank 23rd in total yards, averaging 303 yards per game, while the Giants allow 271 yards per game, ranking 29th in the league. Arizona ranks 15th in third-down conversion rate (41%) and 20th in red-zone touchdown rate ( 55% ). The Cardinals average 210 passing yards per game ( 17th in the NFL ) and 93 rushing yards per game ( 25th ). However, running back Jeremiyah Love — who was selected in the top five — saw his role increase significantly against the 49ers. He had a 63% snap share after just 42% in Week 2. Love suffered a high-ankle sprain in preseason Week 1, leading to heavy usage for Tyler Allgeier in the first two weeks of the season. Allgeier will have a role, but Mike LaFleur seems comfortable showcasing the talents of Love, who had 26 total touches in Week 3, which is what had TOTAL in his first two games. Love has 160 yards on 41 carries (3.9 YPC), with one touchdown, 2.76 yards after contact, and five missed tackles forced. Allgeier has 24 carries for 70 yards ( 2.9 YPC ), with 2.38 yards after contact and five missed tackles forced as well. The Cardinals run a lot of DUO up front and want to displace at the point of attack in the run game. Paris Johnson Jr. starts at left tackle and Elijah Wilkinson is the starting right tackle. The latter has struggled as a run blocker, while the former continues to be one of the better young tackles in football. Isaac Seumalo and Isaiah Adams start on the interior — both bigger, more physical interior offensive linemen — and Hjalte Froholdt is their starting center. The Giants have to expect a similar DUO blocking scheme that they faced against the Rams in Week 2 — New York surrendered 163 yards on the ground against Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Expect Love’s role to be similar to Week 3, with Allgeier working in on short-yardage and to spell the talented young rookie. The wide receiver situation in Arizona is interesting, to say the least. 2024 Top-five pick Marvin Harrison Jr. looks completely disinterested and has appeared this way through two coaching staffs. The Internet believes he could be traded. Here’s Mike LaFleur responding to a question about plays being designed for the disgruntled young receiver: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur on if he has plays specifically designed for Marvin Harrison Jr. “The thing about the guys that are actually catching the football is they're in command and not in control.” Via ( @AZCardinals ) pic.twitter.com/MiMXvjnOg3 — Andrew Bernson (@andrewbernson) September 25, 2026 Harrison Jr. has four receptions on nine targets for 73 yards through three games, despite playing more than 70% of the snaps in each game. Tight end Trey McBride has been a target monster, leading the team with 31 targets and catching 26 for 211 yards and two touchdowns. Michael Wilson continues to outshine Harrison Jr. The former Stanford Cardinal has been sensational with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. Wilson averages 10.6 targets and 85.3 yards per game across the last 11 matchups; the Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase averages 10 targets and 79.7 yards per game through that same span. AZ Cardinals WR Michael Wilson cut ups from week 3 There’s just so much to love about Wilson, the elite hands, the physicality, the IQ. He rocks. Only 3 weeks of tape obviously, but I’m comfortable saying he has improved as a route runner in 2027 and looks to be ascending still pic.twitter.com/ItwkJIIqMy — Jason Lewis (@Jasonlewis54) September 28, 2026 Michael Wilson #AZCardinals Good out vs outside leverage. The head and eyes tell the story at the top of the stem and flat break. pic.twitter.com/INqKkIAgkc — Matt Waldman (@MattWaldman) September 28, 2026 Michael Wilson 4th and 2 conversion. Feet-switch and counters defender's hand which prevents any call of a push off. #AZCardinals pic.twitter.com/3pq6eChUjI — Matt Waldman (@MattWaldman) September 28, 2026 Wilson has 18 catches on 27 targets for 163 yards and a touchdown. New York will have its hands full with both Wilson and McBride. Kendrick Bourne is the third receiver, and he’s been efficient, catching 12 of 14 targets for 108 yards. The matchup Brissett is playing good football. He’s keeping the Cardinals’ offense on track with a quick, efficient passing attack that matches up well against the Giants. Brissett is completing 70% of his passes with 652 passing yards, four touchdowns, and just one interception. He has a 1.6% big-time throw rate and a 2.3% turnover-worthy play rate, and his receivers have dropped 4.7% of his passes, with 5.6 yards per attempt. Brissett’s surface-level statistics check out with the more advanced analytics. The Arizona offense ranks 11th in the NFL in EPA (Expected Points Added) per play; they’re especially efficient in short EPA (7th in the NFL), while ranking 27th in deep EPA. The Cardinals, however, are dead last in explosive-play EPA. Arizona is specifically good out of 11 and 13 personnel, recording the ninth-best EPA from the former and the third-best from the latter. Their 13 personnel package consists of McBride, Eliah Higgins, and Hunter Long. Tight end Tip Reiman is injured, which has affected the Cardinals’ ability to run effectively. The Giants may look to dial up more pressure without star pass rusher Burns, but Brissett has done well against pressure. He is sixth in EPA when pressures, but 16th in EPA against the blitz. The Cardinals have used 11 personnel at a 62% rate, 12 personnel at a 12% rate, and 13 personnel at an 18% rate. Expect the Giants to align in nickel against 11 and stay mostly in base versus heavier personnel. The addition of Jihad Ward — who is familiar with Dennard Wilson’s scheme — should lead to a different role for Kayvon Thibodeaux, who will be replacing Burns. There could be lighter fronts in passing situations with Ward, Abdul Carter, Thibodeaux, and Chauncey Golston. New York ran middle-of-the-field closed often against Cam Ward and the Titans. The Giants may align a bit more in middle-of-the-field open against Brissett. New York should be getting Tae Banks back to help the secondary. Brissett has done well against single-high…
author: Nick Falato

title: Despite McCarthy-mania, Matt Nagy reminds that Jameis Winston is the Giants’ QB
summary: During his weekly press conference on Thursday, New York Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy was peppered with questions about newly-acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Nagy answered them, but he did remind that it is important to remember that Jameis Winston, not McCarthy, is the team’s starting quarterback. “I think it’s important to say, I understand the […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | Getty Images During his weekly press conference on Thursday, New York Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy was peppered with questions about newly-acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Nagy answered them, but he did remind that it is important to remember that Jameis Winston, not McCarthy, is the team’s starting quarterback. “I think it’s important to say, I understand the questions on J.J., I get it, but I also don’t want to lose sight of where we’re at with the time that we’re spending on Jameis,” Nagy said. Winston is 25 of 49 (51%) for 229 yards with no touchdowns, one interception, a passer rating of just 55.6, a league worst QBR of 22.9, and an EPA per play of -0.31, 34th of 36 graded quarterbacks. The Giants did win the game Winston started despite having to settle for four field goals in a 12-7 victory. “So, the first game with the Rams, that’s not easy. That’s a difficult situation to walk into. So, that one’s a little tough to fairly criticize, I think, in my opinion,” Nagy said. “Then the second game, there was a little bit of weather, or whether we like it or not, that’s what’s real. So, but at the same point in time, we need to score touchdowns. That’s what, it’s my job as offensive coordinator. It’s our job as players. “And so, I have a ton of trust. And I really feel great about what’s about to happen and what he can do. And I think he’s got a resume that’s shown that. And our players, our coaches, everyone here believes in Jameis, everybody. There’s no doubt. We just got to go out there and we got to do it. And scoring touchdowns will help that confidence. Scoring touchdowns will help that trust and that belief.” Malik Nabers echoed Nagy’s faith in Winston. “I think we got pretty good confidence in Jameis on his ability to throw the ball downfield, do play action, get involved with the run game. So, I feel like Jameis can do a lot in this offense,” Nabers said. “Jameis has been a part of a lot of different offense. So, this offense is probably nothing different than what he’s already seen. So, we got pretty good confidence in his ability to give us the ball and manage the offense.” McCarthy-mania No matter how many times you remind Giants fans, or most of the media, that Winston is the quarterback and will be until he plays his way out of the job, the attention is all on McCarthy and how quickly the Giants can get him ready to play. “There’s a lot involved, it takes some time, I guess is my point, what I’m saying,” Nagy said. “So, what our job is going to be is to balance it, to see what’s fair to him. What can he handle, what’s real? And then you just go from there. And I think that’s where, as long as we all have kind of the same standards and expectations as we go through this, then that’s only fair to everybody.” Nagy was non-committal about whether McCarthy would know enough to be the No. 2 quarterback vs. the Arizona Cardinals, or possibly be used in a sub-package. “What’s most realistic to get him ready to be a backup, right? That’s where you start, and that’s where we’re at, and that process takes some time,” Nagy said. “And there’s a little bit of realization in knowing it’s not going to happen in one or two days. I think that’s only fair, but we just got to see each and every day how much can he handle, and then we continue to throw more and more at him, and then we got to make our own judgment on, now, what is he doing on the field, and where does that take him as a number two or number three?”
author: Ed Valentine

title: Giants vs. Cardinals: Arizona defense presents an opportunity
summary: Can the New York Giants get their offense on track against the Arizona Cardinals? That’s one of the big questions hanging over the team as they enter Week 4. The Giants offense has been, in a word, bad since their surgical, suffocating win over the Dallas Cowboys back in week 1. Since then, they’ve scored […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Can the New York Giants get their offense on track against the Arizona Cardinals? That’s one of the big questions hanging over the team as they enter Week 4. The Giants offense has been, in a word, bad since their surgical, suffocating win over the Dallas Cowboys back in week 1. Since then, they’ve scored 6 points in a loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2 and a whopping 12 points against the Tennessee Titans in Week 3. That isn’t going to cut it going forward, and the Giants need to figure out their offense. Will that start against the Cardinals? The Cardinals’ defense The Cardinals were one of the (many) teams to hire a new head coach this offseason, hiring Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur. LaFleur made the surprising decision to retain Nick Rallis as the Cardinals defensive coordinator rather than start fresh on that side of the ball. Rallis has been the Cardinals’ defensive coordinator since 2023, which means that the decision to keep him gives the Giants much more tape to plan for his scheme and tendencies than they’d have if LeFleur hired a new coordinator. And while Rallis spent two years coaching linebackers for the Philadelphia Eagles (2021 and 2022), he isn’t the same kind of “Fangio Adjacent” defensive mind that the Giants have seen in each of the first three weeks of the season. Instead, he runs an unorthodox defensive scheme that’s built on a “three-deep” coverage shell and the versatility of safety Budda Baker. By using a three-deep coverage shell, the Cardinals look to both take away explosive plays as well as add uncertainty to quarterbacks’ pre-snap reads. They typically play with three defensive linemen, leading to light boxes that invite runs. However, Rallis makes heavy use of disguise in his scheme and led the NFL by disguising his defense on 70% of plays last year. To do that, he relies chiefly on Baker as a flex player who can either play deep or rotate down into the tackle box as a MONEY backer, or safety/linebacker hybrid. That allows the Cardinals to effectively play base 3-4 concepts against heavier personnel sets or nickel concepts against lighter sets, as well as fluidly transition between base and nickel defenses on a moment’s notice. Unfortunately for the Cardinals, they lost starting cornerback Will Johnson to a neck injury, forcing 2025 fifth- round pick Denzel Burke into the starting role. Burke started eight games for the Cardinals last year and played relatively well, though he had eight missed tackles. This year he seems to have taken a step backward and surrendered a 72.7% completion rate, two touchdowns, and 9.1 yards per target through three games (one start) It’s worth noting that none of the Cardinals’ corners are taller than 5-foot-11, which could present an opportunity for Malachi Fields and Isaiah Likely. More importantly, while the Cardinals’ defense is unorthodox and generally well-schemed… It hasn’t been very good this year. They’re bottom three in the NFL with 0.15 EPA per play added to to the opposing offense , bottom three in passing touchdowns allowed (eight), as well as giving up a league-worst 6.5 yards per play. Their run defense has been better than their pass defense, however they’re still in the bottom third of the NFL in yards and yards per carry allowed. Overall, the scheme of the Cardinals’ defense will put the onus on Matt Nagy and Jameis Winston to decipher their rotations. Once they do, however, their propensity to run zone coverages and Cover 3 offers opportunities for Malik Nabers and Darnell Mooney to pick up yards after the catch, while Fields and Likely are proving to be effective zone busters. Likewise, their tendency to play lighter packages and counter the run with scheme may be an opportunity for the run-heavy Giants. That said, the Giants may look to use pulling blockers and attack the edges of the Cardinals’ defense if they play more TITE fronts to clog interior gaps. Jameis Winston at quarterback, again Giants’ head coach John Harbaugh confirmed after the Giants traded for J.J. McCarthy that Winston would remain the starting quarterback through the foreseeable future. However, that doesn’t mean that his job is safe indefinitely. Winston has been shaky — at best — since taking over for Jaxson Dart. He hasn’t appeared sure of his reads, has held the ball at times, and has consistently thrown short of his targets. Winston, and the Giants were able to do enough to beat the Titans, but only because the defense — and elements — shut Tennessee out in the first half. The question is how much of Winston’s performance was due to a short week and the nor’easter. Can Winston settle in and finally develop a rapport with his receivers on a normal week of practice and find them on a sunny fall day? Matt Nagy and the Giants’ brain trust has generally done a decent job of creating easy answers for their quarterback. Winston’s targets were open by an average of 3.3 yards against the Titans and he only attempted a tight window throw on three passes. It seems likely at this point that the Cardinals will almost certainly use their base defense concepts to gap out the Giants’ offensive front. We’ll likely see Baker playing downhill while the Cardinals use a TITE front to try and force the Giants’ slower running backs to run laterally. The Giants want to run the ball. They have the seventh-most rushing attempts in the NFL despite having the sixth-fewest drives in the NFL. It seems likely that the Cardinals will plan to force Winston to prove that he can beat them with his arm. The Giants’ ball control offense looked suffocating in Week 1, but it needs to end in touchdowns to work. Not only do the Giants have the sixth-fewest drives in the NFL, their average drive eats up the most clock in the NFL. That means that points are at a premium, because they simply don’t get many opportunities per game to score with the style of football they want to play. New York may need Winston to prove that he’s still a productive passer in order to open things up for the run game if Arizona decides that the Giants won’t beat them on the ground. The red zone offense The Giants did a pretty good job of moving the ball between the 20’s against the Titans’ defense, particularly in the second half. The were largely able to do what they wanted and pretty easily marched down the field to get into scoring position multiple times. However, their red zone offense was both bad, weird… And utterly ineffective. It’s possible that Nagy didn’t fully trust Winston in the red zone, particularly the low red zone where the defense is the most condensed and the game is the fastest. It’s also possible that the Giants were wary of the tricky conditions brought about by the storm. Whatever the reason, they squandered every opportunity to score touchdowns and build a commanding lead over the Titans. The Giants had nine plays against the Titans in the red zone. Of them, only two were passing plays and of the seven running plays, only one (a toss to Najee Harris from the 16 yard line) got more than 10 yards. Likewise, of the Giants’ nine red zone plays, only two were vertical — a run up the middle by Cam Skattebo and a pass into the end zone from Winston. Everything else was designed to go laterally. That’s a stark contrast from what the Giants did in Week 1 against the Cowboys. They had 12 plays in the Red Zone against the Cowboys, seven of which were vertical, while five were designed to be lateral. The Giants had four red zone plays against the Rams, and only one of them (an off tackle run by Harris) began by advancing the ball toward the end zone. And even the run by Harris still had a downhill component. It’s certainly possible that Winston isn’t reading the defense quickly enough or isn’t fully comfortable with the scheme or receivers. But that shouldn’t excuse play calls and play designs that actively work against the strengths of the…

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Chicago Bears
summary: The New York Jets face their third NFC North opponent in a row on Sunday, as they are in the Windy City to face the 2-1 Chicago Bears. New York beat Chicago 31-10 in the last meeting between these teams back in 2022. Prior to that the Jets had last beaten the Bears all the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 27: Darrynton Evans #21 of the Chicago Bears gets tackled by a pair of New York Jets players in the first half at MetLife Stadium on November 27, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets face their third NFC North opponent in a row on Sunday, as they are in the Windy City to face the 2-1 Chicago Bears. New York beat Chicago 31-10 in the last meeting between these teams back in 2022. Prior to that the Jets had last beaten the Bears all the way back in 2000. Let’s break down the Bears’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks The situation at quarterback is cloudy for the Bears, who may be about to start their third different quarterback in three weeks. After an inconsistent rookie year, Caleb Williams led the Bears to an 11-6 record last season, and was showing signs of this being his breakout into superstardom when the Bears racked up 59 points in their opener. However, he got injured in week two and the Bears were without him last Sunday, and will be this Sunday as well. Tyson Bagent had been considered the number two, but he missed practice during the week leading up to last weekend’s game, so the Bears prepared for Case Keenum to lead them against Philadelphia on Monday Night Football. Surprisingly, he put together a terrific performance to lead them to an easy win with 247 yards and two touchdowns. Ordinarily, you’d expect them to stick with Keenum after a performance like that. However, head coach Ben Johnson has kept his plans under wraps and Chicago beat writers have suggested it may be Bagent who gets the nod this week. Keenum is obviously more experienced than Bagent, who went 2-2 as a rookie starter in 2023 but has only thrown 15 passes since. Neither offers the same run threat as Williams. Offensive Line The Bears had a solid offensive line last season, with no offensive lineman giving up more than three sacks. Three of the five starters are returning, too, as right guard Jonah Jackson, pro bowl left guard Joe Thuney and right tackle Darnell Wright are back after each starting every game last year. They’ve kept the unit strong, as no offensive lineman was credited with giving up any of the six sacks that have been surrendered so far this season. The center position underwent a change due to Drew Dalman’s sudden retirement but veteran Garrett Bradbury has taken over that role, although he has four penalties in three games. At left tackle, Braxton Jones remains the number one choice, but he continues to be injury prone after missing considerable time in 2023 and 2025. He’s been ruled out again on Sunday but both Theo Benedet and Ozzy Trapilo started several games in his place last season and they remain on the roster. Benedet filled in for Jones for part of each of the first three games so he figures to start. The rest of the bench is low on experience as Logan Jones is a rookie second rounder and Luke Newman and Jordan McFadden have started two NFL games between them. Wright led the Bears with 12 offensive penalties last season. Running Backs The Bears currently have the number one running game in the NFL, although Williams being out affects that. D’Andre Swift is seventh in the NFL in rushing yards while Kyle Monangai is averaging 5.9 yards per carry. They each rushed for 100 yards in the first game, with Monangai doing that in just 10 carries as most of his yardage came on a 61-yard touchdown scamper. Roschon Johnson remains with the team as a backup although his workload has been reducing over the past few years. Pass catchers At wide receiver, the Bears were banking on recent draft picks Rome Odunze and Luther Burden to step up with DJ Moore having been traded after the pair had combined to catch 91 passes last year. However, early on, it’s been ex-Jets receiver Kalif Raymond who has elevated his game. Johnson was familiar with Raymond from his time in Detroit and brought him over this offseason. So far, Raymond’s role has been bigger than expected as he’s caught 19 passes on 21 targets for a team-high 214 receiving yards. Burden is also off to a good start as he has 15 receptions already this year. Odunze, on the other hand, only has eight catches, although he is averaging 17.4 yards per catch. In terms of backups, third round rookie Zavion Thomas and Jahdae Walker each have just one catch for one yard, although Walker’s was for a touchdown. The Bears have also had good production from their tight ends in recent years with Colston Loveland leading the team with over 700 receiving yards last season and Cole Kmet having posted similar numbers in the past. Both are off to a slow start this year, though. The third tight end is rookie Sam Roush, who played for Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich at Stanford. Defensive Line The Bears have more or less returned most of the edge rotation from last year, but their interior line rotation is completely different other than the returning former pro bowler Grady Jarrett. The starter alongside Jarrett is Kentavius Street with Neville Gallimore and third round rookie Jordan van den Berg also getting playing time. The main playmaker on the edge is Montez Sweat, who had 10 sacks last year. The other starter across from him is Dayo Odeyingbo, who already has two sacks after having had just one all year in 2025. The main reserve on the edge is Austin Booker, who had 4.5 sacks last year, with James Lynch also in the rotation. Edge Jamree Kromah and defensive tackle Jayden Loving are also on the roster for depth. Linebackers 2025’s leading tacker Tremaine Edmunds is now with the Giants, so the Bears brought in Devin Bush Jr. to start along with TJ Edwards, who had 67 tackles and five passes defensed in just 10 games last season. D’Marco Jackson also sees playing time when three linebackers are on the field, but Noah Sewell, who was in the rotation last year, is on the PUP list. Fifth round rookie Keyshaun Elliott and special teamer Jack Sanborn round out this unit. Defensive Backs The Bears’ secondary was the key to their winning record last year as they racked up an incredible 23 interceptions. Even more incredible, though, was their decision to get rid of literally everyone who had more than one. Pro bowlers Nahshon Wright and Kevin Byard are gone, along with C.J. Gardner-Johnson. To make matters worse, Kyler Gordon is still on the PUP list and safety Coby Bryant is on injured reserve. It’s perhaps not surprising that they gave up 37 points in their first game of the season with all these changes, but they’ve regrouped well to allow just 16 points in the last two games. At the safety position, they addressed the need by drafting the athletic Dillon Thieneman in the first round and he’s responded by leading them in tackles through three games. According to Chicago’s unofficial depth chart, Xavier Woods is listed as the other starting safety. However, Cam Lewis – listed as the starting nickel – has been playing safety instead of him so far this year. Lewis is listed as doubtful for Sunday, so Woods is likely to make his first start of the year with Elijah Hicks as the third safety and Skyler Thomas available as cover. At cornerback, Jaylon Johnson is hoping to get back to the level that saw him voted to the pro bowl in 2023 and 2024 before he missed half of last year due to injury. The other starter is Tyrique Stevenson, who broke up 10 passes last year. Fourth round rookie Malik Muhammad has been the primary slot cornerback so far. Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips III are each available for depth. Special Teams Literally a quarter of the NFL has a former Jet as their placekicker right now, and the Bears are one of those teams as Cairo Santos has made his home there. Santos’ only miss of the year so far was a blocked chip shot field goal in the Vikings game where there was an issue with the snap count. Punter Tory Taylor is off to a good start, posting career-best numbers so far with a gross…

title: Jets vs Bears: Five Questions with Windy City Gridiron
summary: The New York Jets are on the road on Sunday for the 4th game of their 2026 campaign. They will be facing the Chicago Bears. The Bears are 2-1 on the year. They are coming off a dominant 27-7 shellacking of the Philadelphia Eagles last week. Previewing this matchup, Bill Zimmerman, Deputy Manager at Windy […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 27: Ty Johnson #25 of the New York Jets runs for a touchdown in the third quarter of a game against the Chicago Bears at MetLife Stadium on November 27, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are on the road on Sunday for the 4th game of their 2026 campaign. They will be facing the Chicago Bears. The Bears are 2-1 on the year. They are coming off a dominant 27-7 shellacking of the Philadelphia Eagles last week. Previewing this matchup, Bill Zimmerman, Deputy Manager at Windy City Gridiron , was kind enough to answer a few questions regarding the 2026 Chicago Bears. 1. The Bears will likely not have starting quarterback Caleb Williams available against the Jets. Case Keenum led the Bears to a big win over the Philadelphia Eagles last week in Williams’ absence, but Tyson Bagent might be healthy and ahead of Keenum on the depth chart against the Jets. Who do you think should start, who do you think will start, and can the Bears offense continue to have success with backup quarterbacks? The Case Keenum story from Monday Night Football was genuinely awesome. I was totally caught up in the human-interest angle of it. But I think you have to take what Ben Johnson said after the game at face value: “There’s a reason that we broke camp with Tyson as our QB2.” The Keenum story was awesome, but I think after having 60 minutes of tape to analyze, I’m not sure another 60 minutes of Keenum will work unless Ben Johnson wildly changes up the game plan. I think Tyson Bagent should start, and I think Bagent will start. As for continued success with backup QBs, why not? I think Ben Johnson is an offensive genius. I’m in awe watching what he does each and every week. He’s truly playing chess. He sets up explosive plays in the second half with plays he runs in the first half. He’s a Monet. I think he can adjust his scheme and have success with Bagent. If Caleb Williams was out for the year, I think Ben Johnson would run out of magic beans, but I absolutely think he can do it for 2 to 4 weeks. 2. The Bears have held each of their last two opponents under 10 points and under 260 yards of offense. What have been the keys to that kind of dominant defensive play and is it sustainable? The defense has looked much better the last two weeks, but this is still the same defense that gave up 37 to Carolina in week one. Here’s where I am at with the Chicago Bears defense. It’s not very good, but their defensive play caller, Dennis Allen, is elite. The Vikings game is tough to evaluate. Wet doesn’t describe what that game was. It was a steady rain for the entire game and it rained a ton prior to the game as well. The conditions were awful and I think the conditions were too much for the offenses to overcome. Carson Wentz struggled to get the ball down the field, and that allowed the Bears’ defense to excel on third down. But the defense’s performance against the Eagles was truly special. They completely shut down the Eagles offense in the second half, and Allen called a phenomenal game. This defense is tough to see where they are at. In the secondary, Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, and Cam Lewis are allowing roughly a 130.0 passer rating against when they are targeted. However, when teams target rookies Dillon Thieneman or Malik Muhammad, they can barely complete a pass; their targeted passer rating against is around 30.0. The defensive line was supposed to be the weakest unit on the team, but thanks to Grady Jarrett turning the clock back a couple of years and Dayo Odeyingbo creating interior pressure, it’s been decent. Will that hold up? Will they revert to week one? Your guess is as good as mine. For this defense to be successful, Dennis Allen is going to have to continue to call fantastic games, and they are going to have to create turnovers; they were able to create three last week against Philly. 3. Can you give us a synopsis of what the 2026 Bears draft class has looked like so far, and what you expect from them as the year goes on? Overall, you have to be pretty pleased with the draft class, but not everything has been smooth. As I mentioned before, Dillon Thieneman, their first-round pick, is starting at safety and looks the part. He’s going to be a 10-year safety in the league. Malik Muhammad, a fourth-round CB out of Texas, has really boosted the secondary with some solid play while the other CBs struggle. They have been a huge boost to a defense that desperately needed it. As for the other picks, DT Jordan van den Berg, their 6th-round pick, was turning heads in the preseason; even Brian Baldinger did a breakdown on how well he was playing. However, in the regular season, van den Berg has been out there for 54 snaps and has recorded one tackle. Teams have handled him pretty well. Second-round pick C Logan Jones hasn’t played yet, as he’s Garrett Bradbury’s backup. Third-round pick Zavion Thomas has been on the field a little, but we haven’t seen much yet. He’s looked good returning kicks, and he has tremendous speed. It feels like Ben Johnson will find some spots for him during the regular season to get an explosive play or two, but he isn’t quite there yet. Their other pick, TE Sam Roush, has been awful. He was the key guy so they could run 13 personnel, but he’s been bad on multiple levels. He dropped a touchdown pass that would have given them the win against the Vikings; he also missed a block on a FG attempt that resulted in a blocked kick. Last week the Bears had a phenomenal chance to down the ball at the 1 against the Eagles on a punt, and he touched the ball when his foot was in the end zone that resulted in a touchback. He’s been a mess. Hopefully he improves soon. 4. Every team has a player or two who may be somewhat unfamiliar to other teams’ fans but is known to be an unsung hero by fans of his own team. Who are the Bears’ unsung heroes? If possible give us one guy on each side of the ball. I think the Bears offense has several names that most football fans know. But I think the offense’s unsung hero is TE Cole Kmet. Kmet has been a solid TE in the league for many years, but with the drafting of Colston Loveland and Ben Johnson’s offense, Kmet’s role has changed. He’s used as a FB; he does a lot of the dirty work at TE, and he will leak out and get used occasionally in the passing game. He’s a key piece to the offense that doesn’t show up much on the stat sheet anymore. Defensively, I’ve already mentioned quite a few names. But one name I haven’t mentioned is Austin Booker. I don’t know if Booker is an unsung hero, but he is a key piece to the defense. He plays the bulk of the edge snaps opposite Montez Sweat (by far their best DL), so Booker needs to complement Sweat. When he plays well, he elevates the entire defensive front. Last week Booker had a forced fumble; the week before, he had a sack. If Booker can make 1 or 2 big plays a game, it changes the outlook of the defense. 5. If you were an opposing head coach, how would you attack this Bears team on offense and on defense? Defensively, the Bears struggle to stop the run. I would make sure I establish the run, and once that’s done, I would use play action and pick on the CBs, especially Tyrique Stevenson. Dennis Allen is going to get creative and use blitzes and stunts to generate pressure so the QB has to be on the lookout for those blitzes and try to attack the hole in the defense before the pressure gets home. How to stop the Bears offense? Well, rain certainly did the trick in week two. I would make it rain. I’m joking, obviously, but I don’t think there’s just a straight way to beat the Bears offense because Ben Johnson is that good. He’s a lot smarter than me, so anything I tell you, he already knows. But this offense does go with how the offensive line goes. I would make sure the defense keeps the offensive line off balance. When the OL plays great, the offense hums. Get the offensive line…

title: Eagles thoughts: Course corrections
summary: The Eagles are an uninspiring 2-1. The Rams are a disappointing 1-2. Someone is going to walk away on Sunday feeling somewhat less bad about themselves. Football is not a meritocracy  Before the season began I asked if the new Sean Mannion led offense would get complimentary players more involved. We got our first look […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the first quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Tafoya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are an uninspiring 2-1. The Rams are a disappointing 1-2. Someone is going to walk away on Sunday feeling somewhat less bad about themselves. Football is not a meritocracy Before the season began I asked if the new Sean Mannion led offense would get complimentary players more involved . We got our first look at an answer on Monday with a stark result: no, not even a little. Against the Titans, Darius Cooper had a nice catch and run for 23 yards on 1st and 17, and later scored the game winning TD. He’s been outstanding on special teams. The head coach likes him. His reward? 4 snaps on offense against the Bears, fewer than Elijah Moore. Meanwhile Makai Lemon played 35, a season high 70%. Tank Bigsby was the only skill position player to play fewer snaps than Cooper. Will Shipley, EJ Jenkins, and Johnny Mundt all played double digit snaps on both special teams and offense. Cooper did so against the Titans. Now with DeVonta Smith set to miss a few games, Cooper should get the chance on offense he deserves. There is no excuse not to. The red flag of yellow flags In my preview of the Rams, I noted that they had the best penalty differential in 2025 , which was unlikely to repeat itself in 2026. The Eagles, coincidentally, had the worst. Through three games the Rams have most definitely not repeated their success: they have the worst penalty differential, with -13 total penalties and -105 penalty yards. The Eagles are 18th. Half of the Rams penalties were last week against the Broncos, but in each of their first two games they had double the amount of their opponent, so this wasn’t just a one week thing. There’s no guarantee that this trend will continue, if anything they’re due for a game where they have a positive differential, but it is one reason among several why they’re 1-2 to start their supposed dream season. Lies, damn lies, and statistics Nick Sirianni has never lost to Sean McVay, going 4-0 against him. Since Sirianni became a head coach, he’s been more successful than McVay: Wins: Eagles 2nd, Rams 10th Points: Eagles 6th, Rams 9th Yards: Eagles 7th, Rams 9th Super Bowl appearances: Eagles 2, Rams 1 Super Bowl wins: Eagles 1, Rams 1 College Football Watch List 12:00 – Alabama at Mississippi State The 2027 QB draft class is so predictably disappointing that people are already on to the 2028 class, which is was also extremely predictable. Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor is already high on next year’s radar. Bulldogs RB Fluff Bothwell (not his real name) is a dual threat RB making a name for himself. Alabama QB Keelon Russell is also on next year’s radar (neither he nor Taylor are draft eligible this year). For this year safety Bray Hubbard is fun, a big hitter who can make plays, 8 INTs and 4 FFs. 3:30 – Ohio State at Iowa and Florida at Missouri You are not going to believe this but Iowa has some OL, TE, and safety prospects. Shocker, I know. All three are Eagles needs! RG Kade Pieper is one of the top interior lineman prospects, and LT Trevor Lauck one of the top OT prospects. At 6’5” Lauck is smaller than teams, especially the Eagles. traditionally like in OTs. Pieper has experience at center.

title: Eagles-Rams Final Injury Report: DeVonta Smith and Zack Baun among 6 players ruled OUT
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final official injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. The Eagles ruled six players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Zack Baun, Dallas Goedert, Marcus Epps, Hollywoood Brown, and Fred Johnson. Smith is dealing with a hamstring injury that […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 19: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs in pre-snap motion during the first half of the NFC Divisional Playoff game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on January 19, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final official injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. The Eagles ruled six players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Zack Baun, Dallas Goedert, Marcus Epps, Hollywoood Brown, and Fred Johnson. Smith is dealing with a hamstring injury that prevented him from practicing this week. Reports indicate he could miss another game or two after this weekend . Not great for the Eagles to be missing their top receiver at all, let alone against some tough opponents. With Smith and Brown out, the Eagles will be down to the following five receivers: Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore, Darius Cooper, and Britain Covey. Wicks figures to be the Eagles’ No. 1 target in Smith’s absence. Lemon could also see increased opportunities … just hopefully not in the entirely predictable screen reception variety. Moore played more snaps than Cooper last week despite being a healthy scratch in either of the first two games. The Eagles might trust Moore to play more on offense, even though Cooper has shown potential there. Cooper could still get some more chances than usual while also playing on special teams. Covey is the Eagles’ punt returner. Baun is missing a game for non-rest reasons for the first time since joining the Eagles. He wasn’t able to practice this week due to a concussion. His absence means that Jeremiah Trotter Jr. will make his first career start in a game where the Eagles aren’t resting starters. It’ll be interesting to see how Trot Jr. fares. He has some athletic limitations but he’s very savvy and plays with great anticipation. Smael Mondon will be the top backup. The Eagles could look to temporarily elevate newcomer Anfernee Orji for emergency depth and special teams purposes. Chance Campbell was placed on the practice squad injured reserve list earlier this week. Goedert is missing his second straight game due to a knee injury. And so the Eagles will be without both their top wide receiver and top tight end against the Rams. Goedert’s absence means the Birds will roll with Zach Ertz, Johnny Mundt, and E.J. Jenkins as their tight ends on Sunday. Mundt played the most snaps of any player at his position in Week 3 but Ertz had just rejoined the team days prior. We’ll see if Ertz’s workload increases at all. Also will be interesting to see if the team leans more into 12 personnel with DeVonta out. Epps was unexpectedly added to the injury report on Thursday as a limited participant. He then did not practice on Friday. Maybe he has a legitimate injury. But maybe the Eagles are soft benching him? Maybe not, though, because now they only have one full-time safety on the roster: Andrew Mukuba. Michael Carter II figures to start in place of Epps but he’s a converted nickel cornerback. Ditto for Kenny Moore, who is slated to make his Eagles debut this weekend. Of course, Cooper DeJean will play safety when the Eagles utilize their base defense, which could be often against the Rams, who utilize 13 personnel at a very high rate. If the Eagles want more safety depth, they could look to temporarily elevate Cole Wisniewski from the practice squad for this game. Brown apparently got injured in practice last week. He’s set to miss his second game in a row. Brown was previously active for Week 1 but played zero snaps. He took a couple designed touches in Week 2. Johnson apparently got injured in practice last week as well. He’s also set to miss his second game in a row. Rookie blocker Markel Bell will be the swing tackle in his absence. He might already be the swing tackle when Johnson is healthy; that much is unclear. The Eagles ran one play last week with Bell as a sixth offensive lineman. Players notably listed without a game status : Jihaad Campbell, Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Moro Ojomo, Jonathan Greenard, Byron Young, Will Shipley, Tank Bigsby, Darius Cooper, and Jonathan Jones. Campbell was limited on Friday with a “knee/rest” injury designation. He was previously limited on Wednesday before being upgraded to full go on Thursday. And then back down to limited on Friday. That’s a little unusual. But he’s going to play. The Eagles certainly need him to be able to suit up with Baun out. Carter spoke to reporters in the locker room on Friday and revealed that his cast will come off in the near future. I’m no medical expert, clearly, but it seems like he probably shouldn’t be playing right now? Would be good to heal him up with the bigger picture in mind. But that won’t be the case. Eagles DT Jalen Carter says he expects he’ll only have to wear that cast on his right wrist a couple more weeks. Carter admits the injury has limited him but is starting to get more strength back in his wrist. — Dave Zangaro (@DZangaroNBCS) October 2, 2026 Davis and Ojomo were limited on Wednesday and Thursday before being upgraded to full go on Friday. They’re ready to play. Greenard was full go in practice this week. That’s an upgrade from last week, when he was limited for two days and full go for one day. Seems like he might be able to handle a bigger role than he played against the Bears, which was only 25% of the Eagles’ defensive snaps. Shipley was slowly ramped up this week. He was listed under DNP on Wednesday before being upgraded to limited on Thursday. He was full go on Friday. Young, Cooper, and Bigsby were all full go in practice all week. Jones is a new addition to the report with a quad injury. He was a full participant on Friday, however. PHILADELPHIA EAGLES INJURY REPORT (FRIDAY) OUT LB Zack Baun (concussion) WR Hollywood Brown (ankle) S Marcus Epps (groin) TE Dallas Goedert (knee) OT Fred Johnson (knee) WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) … RESERVE/INJURED CB Jakorian Bennett TE Grant Calcaterra OG Landon Dickerson S Andre’ Sam TE Eli Stowers WR Johnny Wilson Bennett, Calcaterra, and Stowers are eligible to return to the active roster after Week 4. Dickerson is eligible to return to the active roster after Week 5. Sam and Wilson are out for the season. RESERVE/NON-FOOTBALL INJURY S Tucker Large LOS ANGELES RAMS INJURY REPORT (FRIDAY) The Rams ruled three players OUT: starting defensive tackle Aaron Donald, starting cornerback Jaylen Watson, and No. 2 tight end Terrance Ferguson. The Eagles dodging both Donald and Myles Garrett is a nice break for their offensive line. But we’ll see if they can actually take advantage. Watson’s absence puts Emmanuel Forbes in line to start against the Eagles. Ferguson ranks second among Rams tight ends in targets, receptions, and yards. The Rams ruled two players QUESTIONABLE: Colby Parkinson and Josaiah Stewart. Parkinson, who leads all Rams tight ends in snaps played, did not practice this week. Players who don’t practice typically don’t play and the Rams already have a lot of tight end depth. But we’ll see. Stewart is a new addition to the report. He missed Friday’s practice due to a groin injury. Stewart has been starting in place of Garrett. Maltepes is one of the nation’s hottest sports betting experts who appears weekly on national radio and has his own website, www.thephillygodfather.com [thephillygodfather.com] . Los Angeles Rams (1-2) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-1), 1:00 p.m. Sunday The Line: Rams minus-3.5/Total: 42.5 What is the line telling you: The Rams’ defense is all banged up heading into Philly, while the Eagles’ offense is limping into this home game. The good news is that the Eagles have owned Sean McVay, winning 6 of the last 7 meetings against him. The Birds are back home after an embarrassing Monday night loss, so the betting public is expecting them to bounce back in a big way. However, I’m not sure the bookmakers do. Even with their 1-2 start, the Rams are still the odds-on favorite to win the Super Bowl. Meanwhile, the Eagles have seven teams ahead of them in the Super Bowl odds. If I recall correctly, the Eagles haven’t been +3.5-point home underdogs since the 2018 NFC Championship Game against the Vikings, so that’s a little bit of a tell here. The bookmakers have clearly downgraded this Eagles team since the season started. Bottom line: The look-ahead line for this game before the season was Rams -1, yet we’re now sitting at Rams -3.5—a 2.5-point move toward Los Angeles despite all the injuries the Rams are dealing with. And here’s another number that jumps out: When’s the last time a sub-.500 team came into Philly, while the Eagles were sitting in first place, and was laying -3.5 points? Maybe never. If you’re looking to invest in Philly this week, you might be walking into a trap. The books are begging Philly fans to take the points with the Birds. I’m not biting. I think the Rams are the right side here. If you want a little insurance, buy it down to Rams -3. Prop bets for the game: Davante Adams anytime TD +115 Dontayvion Wicks anytime TD +280 Jalen Hurts over 170 passing yards -150 (Betting lines are subject to change.)

title: Eagles opposing player to stop, Week 4 edition
summary: The Eagles defensively were a mess on Monday night in their 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears, who were playing without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, replaced by 38-year-old Case “Montana” Keenum. The Eagles struggled to barely get by the No. 19 (Washington) and No. 31 (Tennessee) offenses in the NFL. They will now host the […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams throws a pass during the first quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles defensively were a mess on Monday night in their 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears, who were playing without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, replaced by 38-year-old Case “Montana” Keenum. The Eagles struggled to barely get by the No. 19 (Washington) and No. 31 (Tennessee) offenses in the NFL. They will now host the No. 1 offense in the league, and future Hall of Famer Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams this Sunday at 1 p.m. There were some glaring problems in the Eagles’ first two victories this season, magnified in the Bears’ loss. For one, the Eagles are getting no push up front, with three sacks in three games, tied for 29th overall in the NFL with, ironically, their visitors this Sunday, the Rams. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio does not have his defensive backs covering tight, giving way too much cushion to opposing receivers, and missed assignments abound. On the third-quarter, 41-yard TD dagger against the Bears on Monday night, corners Cooper DeJean or Riq Woolen did not know whether to cover motion man Luther Burden or slot Kalif Raymond. DeJean stayed with Burden as he motioned left to right, and should have picked up the inside receiver Raymond, since DeJean was the inside defender. Instead, DeJean and Woolen both stayed with the motioning outside receiver Burden, leaving Raymond uncovered down the middle of the field. It is a blown coverage elite quarterbacks like Stafford salivate over. “Yeah, they’re really good,” replied Fangio when asked this week about the Rams’ extensive offensive arsenal. “Not counting their San Francisco game in Australia, their last three games going back to the NFC championship game, they’ve gotten 500 yards in all three games against Seattle, the Giants and Denver. Three good defenses. That in and of itself explains to you what the chore is we have. They run it very well. They stay committed to the run and they’ve got a really good play action game off of it that they marry very well to the run game. You’ve got [Rams QB Matthew] Stafford at quarterback, guy’s going to be a first ballot Hall of Famer. Got the weapons and the tight ends that they have and they’re probably having the [Rams WR Puka] Nacua back this week. “So yeah, it’s a tough assignment because they’re balanced and they run and throw it very effectively.” Complicating the Eagles’ problems on Sunday is the strong possibility middle linebacker Zack Baun will be out due to concussion protocol. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. is a more than capable backup, but the Eagles may have a huge problem moving forward—Jihaad Campbell. According to a couple of Bears’ sources who were on the field against Campbell on Monday, they felt Campbell was a great athlete with a great future ahead of him though was also someone right now who “doesn’t know what he’s doing.” It may partially explain why the Bears had so freedom down the middle of the field Monday night. That could be a major issue against the three tight end sets Rams coach Sean McVay likes to run.Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson and Davis Allen have a combined 21 receptions for four touchdowns and 176 yards. “Yeah, their tight ends are versatile,” Fangio said. “They’re pretty good receivers, and obviously the blocking and they create extra gaps in there. They’re committed to it and they’re good at it.” With DeVonta Smith questionable with a hamstring, and Baun possibly out with a concussion, the Eagles’ four-game winning streak against McVay, who has never beaten Nick Sirianni, may be in serious jeopardy this Sunday. McVay is 1-6 against the Eagles. Stafford is 4-4 in eight starts against the Eagles, though has thrown 16 TDs and been intercepted twice. Three games into the season, the Eagles have no takeaways for the first time in franchise history, while turning the ball over five times. Their minus-5 turnover differential is among the worst in the league, only one better than the bottom, where the Atlanta Falcons sit. The Eagles are the only team in the NFL without a takeaway this season. The recipe smells like this could be uglier than the Eagles’ game against the Bears. The Rams are 1-2, a desperate team in great need to make a point, while the Eagles already look exhausted three games into the 2026 season, just getting by teams that they were supposed to pummel, and losing games to Case Keenum.

title: Eagles News: “This season can get turned around if Nick Sirianni has the right messaging and can push the right buttons”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Whereas I felt like the onus was on the Eagles’ defense entering Week 3 against the Chicago Bears (and Vic Fangio’s group certainly failed that test), I feel like Week 4 is on Nick Sirianni. It’s important to see how the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Whereas I felt like the onus was on the Eagles’ defense entering Week 3 against the Chicago Bears (and Vic Fangio’s group certainly failed that test), I feel like Week 4 is on Nick Sirianni. It’s important to see how the Eagles respond to their Monday night loss. On paper, they’re not in a great spot. The Rams are a tough opponent. The Eagles are going to be missing some key players. But this is a situation where the head coach needs to get his team to rally. I’m not even suggesting that the Eagles MUST win this game. But it will be disheartening if they’re not more competitive than they were against the Bears. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Glass Half Full – Iggles Blitz The NFC East isn’t loaded right now. Dallas has a terrific offense, but their defense remains a work in progress. Trading for CB Joey Porte Jr should help, but it won’t solve all their problems. Jameis Winston has struggled since taking over for Jaxson Dart in NY. Injuries are hurting that team. Washington has played better than anyone expected, but they lack talent and you just can’t trust them. This season can get turned around if Nick Sirianni has the right messaging and can push the right buttons. I believe the biggest problems are intangibles and those can usually be fixed. I’m not ignoring the tangible issues (poor safety play for instnace), but all 32 teams have weak spots. The Eagles can turn things around quickly if Sirianni can get this team to play smarter and tougher. The Eagles don’t have to win on Sunday to give me hope. I need to see them play good football. If the Rams happen to make an extra play or two and win, so be it. I just need to see major improvement from the Birds. That would help me to believe in them going forward. Eagles-Rams Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 4 enemy – BGN After two weeks on the road, the Philadelphia Eagles are returning to Lincoln Financial Field to host a familiar enemy: the Los Angeles Rams. In order to preview this Week 4 matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Turf Show Times . The excellent Evan Craig kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 194: Week 4 Preview, Cowboys get Joey Porter Jr. – NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel A new week is upon us in the NFC East and we have four games to rip through to prepare for it! The Philadelphia Eagles are set to take on the Los Angeles Rams and dropping a second straight game would certainly not be ideal. Meanwhile, the New York Giants will play the Arizona Cardinals in JJ McCarthy’s first game with the team. The Washington Commanders are across the pond in London to play the Indianapolis Colts and try to build on last week’s momentum. Stateside the Dallas Cowboys have a Texas State matchup against the Houston Texans and will take them on with a new player on the team as they just traded for Joey Porter Jr. on Wednesday night. RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss it all! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! 5Qs, 5As with Bleeding Green Nation: How is Jalen Hurts faring with yet another new OC? – Turf Show Times The Los Angeles Rams take on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4 for the fourth straight season. Los Angeles is searching not only for its first win over the Eagles since the 2020 campaign, but also for its first win over Philly with Nick Sirianni at the helm. Ahead of an important matchup between NFC contenders who suffered bad losses last week, I spoke with Brandon Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation to get the inside scoop on Jalen Hurts working with yet another new offensive coordinator, Vic Fangio’s defense and more. NFL Expert Picks for Week 4 – SB Nation The one game to really circle: Rams vs. Eagles. Here are two teams assumed to be the top of the NFC, but both have struggled to start the season and find themselves in need of a win. It’s seeming like one of these teams is going to miss expecations this season, and this game could definine that. If Zack Baun misses Week 4? ‘Trot was born ready’ – NBCSP With All-Pro Zack Baun likely sidelined with a concussion for Sunday’s game against the Rams, the Eagles are expected to turn to Jeremiah Trotter Jr. How ready is the young Axe Man? “Trot was born ready,” fellow linebacker Jihaad Campbell said. “Whether he’s got to play or not, at the end of the day, he always practices like a pro, he always takes notes and studies like a pro. He’ll be fine.” Trotter, 23, has technically started two NFL games before but both of those had little actual meaning. He started in Week 18 against the Giants in 2024 and Week 18 against the Commanders in 2025. This situation is a little bit different. The Eagles on Sunday afternoon are facing a desperate Rams team that has put up 480+ yards of offense in back-to-back weeks and are led by Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams, Puka Nacua and more — not to mention an offense that uses a ton of eye candy to constantly put linebackers in conflict. It’s not going to be easy on Sunday. NFL Week 4 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game – NFL.com Why Gennaro picked the Eagles: Last Sunday night, Los Angeles blew a 16-0 halftime lead at Denver to drop back below .500 in a season that began with the Rams as prohibitive Super Bowl favorites. One night later, Philadelphia was blown out of Chicago by a Bears team that was forced to give Case Keenum his first start in 1,009 days. So, after a pair of nationally televised debacles, who’s in better position to bounce back? Well, the expected return of star WR Puka Nacua is certainly a boon to Sean McVay’s squad. But can the Rams coach exorcise his demons against the Eagles? McVay is 1-6 vs. Philadelphia, having dropped all four matchups against Nick Sirianni. Last season’s loss at Lincoln Financial Field was particularly painful: Not only did the Rams blow a 19-point third-quarter lead, but they had two fourth-quarter field goal attempts blocked, including a would-be game-winner from 44 yards out on the last snap of the contest. In addition to swatting that final kick, hulking DT Jordan Davis memorably scooped up the ball and galloped for an exclamation-point touchdown. But the big man’s triumphant rumble was easily the Eagles’ best run of the day, as the Rams held Saquon Barkley to just 55 total yards on 22 touches. That was a huge departure from Barkley’s previous two games against L.A., when he piled up 534(!) scrimmage yards. Philly’s had trouble getting a consistent ground attack going under new OC Sean Mannion, but Barkley did enjoy success against Chicago this past Monday night before the game got out of hand, potentially signaling a schematic breakthrough. In a matchup between two established powers that have yet to play up to their talent level this season, I’m far from bullish on the Eagles. But I anticipate Sirianni will rally the troops once again versus McVay, with the Birds feeling disrespected as home underdogs. title: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy regrets altercation with Aaron Rodgers
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are now 2-2 following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night. But it was a verbal back-and-forth between quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy that got as much attention as the result of the game itself. During the Steelers’ first drive, Rodgers shouted to the sideline at […]
full_text: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are now 2-2 following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night. But it was a verbal back-and-forth between quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy that got as much attention as the result of the game itself. During the Steelers’ first drive, Rodgers shouted to the sideline at McCarthy saying, “What the f—k! Call it!” Rodgers was upset at the play call taking too long. The broadcast caught his words on a hot mic, and then caught McCarthy seemingly giving it right back to Rodgers, using some colorful language of his own. When asked about the verbal exchange after the game, McCarthy said he wished he didn’t use the language he used. “Communication sometimes is not the best choice of words, but everybody’s competing on the field,” McCarthy said via Brooke Pryor of ESPN . “I think what’s said on the field, the way I grew up in this game, usually stays on the field. That’s not the case today. I understand that. But any negative communication on my part, I wish I wouldn’t use those words.” Rodgers and McCarthy were of course fine later on, embracing and laughing after Rodgers’ successful quarterback sneak for a two-point conversion. This also isn’t something that’s unheard of in the NFL, or sports as a whole. It’ll get talked about because it happened in front of a national audience, but these two have worked together for a long time – this is largely a nothing burger. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!
