title: The Steelers is the Steelers, and this is their new normal
summary: Trade Joey Porter Jr. and lose to the Cleveland Browns in a 24-hour span. This is the new normal for the Pittsburgh Steelers. And I say “new normal,” but it’s not exactly new, is it? The Steelers haven’t beaten the Browns in Cleveland since Ben Roethlisberger’s final season in the NFL back in 2021, and […]
full_text: (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Trade Joey Porter Jr. and lose to the Cleveland Browns in a 24-hour span. This is the new normal for the Pittsburgh Steelers. And I say “new normal,” but it’s not exactly new, is it? The Steelers haven’t beaten the Browns in Cleveland since Ben Roethlisberger’s final season in the NFL back in 2021, and they’ve made a habit of trading top players at key positions without any sort of backup plan in place. They did it with Diontae Johnson in 2023 and didn’t find an adequate No. 2 for George Pickens. They then traded Pickens in 2025, didn’t find a good No. 2 to put opposite DK Metcalf, and Pickens went on to be an All-Pro. Now, they’ve dealt Porter and their secondary was immediately exposed by Deshaun Watson and the Browns. This isn’t the team from the 2000s where their defense was the best in the league for a six-year span and the offense was being led by a young star at the position. At some point, they stopped being the big brother that would give the Browns a noogie twice a year. Instead, they are the brother that is past their prime and still clinging to his glory days at a high school reunion. At some point, it’s time to take off the letterman jacket and class ring and leave your hometown. The Steelers haven’t done that, though, and it doesn’t feel like they ever will. Not with this owner, at least. Rather than being a team that consistently competes for Super Bowls like they did 15-20 years ago, now they trade players they don’t want to pay and lose to the Browns every year. Because that’s who they are now. Draft a good player, player showcases high-end talent, trade player away, try trading for another player to replace the player you just traded. The whole “Browns is the Browns” joke is certainly rich coming from any Steelers fan who still says it, because at this point, the Steelers is the Steelers, and this is their identity. But hey, that 2008 season was special, wasn’t it? It’s the morning after game day, and it’s time for the Steelers to change how they do business. Aaron Rodgers miscues Aaron Rodgers had several misses that severely impacted the outcome. In the third quarter, he had DK Metcalf wide open for what would have been the easiest deep touchdown pass of his career. He didn’t see it and instead checked it down to Ben Skowronek. Aaron Rodgers didnt see a wide open DK metcalf pic.twitter.com/Xwm9ktR19K — Tanner Phifer (@TannerPhifer) October 2, 2026 On the final play of the game for the Steelers, Rodgers had Metcalf open again. This time, it would have been an easy completion to put the Steelers at the 35-yard line for what would have been a 52-yard field goal for Chris Boswell to try and send the game into overtime. Instead, he forces a ball to Roman Wilson that gets picked off and seals the game. DK Metcalf was WIDE OPEN Aaron Rodgers blew it pic.twitter.com/AC7mUWR8Qh — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 2, 2026 Pressure on Rodgers puts hard cap on Steelers offense The Browns found a specific defense that worked and just ran it into the ground all night. Per Sumer Sports, Cleveland played one-high safety on 80 percent of looks, which usually coincided with pressure getting to Rodgers. They rushed five on roughly one third of snaps, and the Steelers couldn’t figure out a counter for what the Browns were doing for most of the night. There were sacks where Rodgers held the ball for quite a bit, but that had a lot to do with the Steelers’ receivers complete inability to generate separation against man coverage. The Steelers don’t have consistent man-beaters, and that’s something that defenses can certainly hone in on throughout the year. Atrocious tackling and coverage The lack of ability to take down a ball carrier was abhorrent. Cole Holcomb and Rayshawn Jenkins both riffed on bringing down Jaleel McLaughlin on the Browns’ first touchdown of the night. Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen both had dreadful nights when it came to bringing down ball carriers, and there were whiffs on potential sacks. It was a largely bad game from the defense, especially in the first half when the Browns scored 21 unanswered points. Additionally, coverage was terrible. Daylen Everette was torched multiple times, including a 60-yard bomb to Denzel Boston that set up a Browns touchdown, and a slant while playing outside leverage while Cleveland was deep in its own territory. If only they had a high-quality young cornerback on their roster. Other notes T.J. Watt continues looking like his old self. He finished with a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and a sack. Jalen Ramsey needs moved to safety permanently and Brandin Echols should take the nickel spot. The current safety rotation just isn’t getting it done. The offense needs to run through Jaylen Warren. On money downs, and short yardage situations, he needs to be the guy. I’m officially at Defcon 3 with Chris Boswell. If he makes his first kick of the night, we are having a very different conversation right now. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers stock report after Thursday night loss to Browns
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers lost in a heartbreak on Thursday in Cleveland 27-24. After tying the game with just over a minute to play, the Steelers came up just short once again against the Browns on Thursday Night Football. As always, here is our weekly stock report after the Steelers fell to 2-2 on the season. […]
full_text: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers lost in a heartbreak on Thursday in Cleveland 27-24. After tying the game with just over a minute to play, the Steelers came up just short once again against the Browns on Thursday Night Football. As always, here is our weekly stock report after the Steelers fell to 2-2 on the season. Stock Up WR Roman Wilson Why not Roman Wilson? After catching a 38-yard touchdown pass last weekend against Cincinnati, Wilson was on the bench for most of the second half after letting a pass bounce off his hands that resulted in an interception. The Steelers did not shy away from going to Wilson in this one. He took a touch pass 12 yards to the end zone for the game’s first score. Later in the contest, Rodgers found Wilson streaking up the seam for a huge chunk gain of 49. The inconsistencies continue to haunt Wilson, but tonight was a bright spot as Wilson has now scored in consecutive games for Pittsburgh. TE Darnell Washington Washington continues to be one of the most impactful players on the Steelers offense. His biggest and most notable play of the night came on his 21-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter. Washington became the target of choice for Rodgers on the game-tying drive, as he was the target on three straight plays. The defensive pass interference that the tight end drew in the end zone set the Steelers up to eventually tie the game. Washington is a matchup nightmare that continues to see more work in the Steelers offense. QB Aaron Rodgers Unc still got it. What a gutsy fourth quarter from the veteran quarterback. The Steelers seemed all but dead and buried down 24-10 well into the fourth quarter, but Aaron Rodgers kept them alive. For as much as his age showed up in the pocket in this game, Rodger rolled out and delivered a strike to Washington in the end zone to kick off the fourth quarter. The veteran quarterback then led another drive downfield and tossed a touchdown on a bootleg to Pat Freiermuth. We have to give some credit to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy for the playcall on the 2-point conversion after the penalty from Cleveland. Rodgers did not get much of a push from the offensive line, but he found enough room to sneak in. The Steelers do not come back and tie this game if not for Rodgers, who took a serious beating tonight. Stock Down Offensive Line It was just a messy game from the offensive line as a whole. Rodgers was sacked five times in the game and took a serious beating with 10 quarterback hits. Jaylen Warren ran the ball incredibly well once again as he averaged 5.5 yards per carry, so the line does deserve some credit for that. However, Rodgers was pressured and hit a ton, and that really put them in a hole that proved to be too much. K Chris Boswell Boswell missed his third field goal of the season in Week 4, as the 48-yard attempt went wide left. It’s nowhere near time to panic or sell your stock in Boswell, but this inconsistency is something to monitor. Secondary Joey Porter Jr. was almost certainly watching this game with a smile on his face from his new apartment in Dallas. Deshaun Watson has a 94.0 passer rating to the tune of 268 yards and a touchdown. The Steelers continued to play a lot of zone coverage, which is going to continue to be a hot topic of conversation as opposing quarterbacks carve up the Steelers secondary. Watson did plenty with his legs tonight, but it was obvious that the Steelers’ secondary is in major need of help. Jamel Dean left the game with an ankle injury and did not return, so an already thin secondary could be without their now-top corner. Deshon Elliott is eligible to come off injured reserve as early as needed this week, which should provide a boost, but this secondary needs major help and fast. title: Seahawks name game captains vs. Los Angeles Chargers, including ex-Charger Uchenna Nwosu
summary: The Seattle Seahawks will need veteran leadership to right their ship in Week 4 after a loss to the Washington Commanders, at least according to the team’s captains, which were announced on Friday. Seattle announced that Cooper Kupp, Mike Morris, Nehemiah Pritchett and former Los Angeles Charger Uchenna Nwosu will have the honors of being […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks will need veteran leadership to right their ship in Week 4 after a loss to the Washington Commanders, at least according to the team’s captains, which were announced on Friday. Seattle announced that Cooper Kupp, Mike Morris, Nehemiah Pritchett and former Los Angeles Charger Uchenna Nwosu will have the honors of being captains on Sunday. Between the four of them, they represent 26 years of experience in the NFL, though the majority of that stems from Kupp (10) and Nwosu (9). This is every player’s first selection this season and marks the first time that Pritchett, who is stepping up to replace Riq Woolen at starting cornerback, has been named a captain. Pritchett had an interception in Week 1 and has anchored an injured secondary through three games. Our Week 4 captains. Read more » https://t.co/kiaCZk0LRL pic.twitter.com/LkktVFuCe4 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 2, 2026 Nwosu being named captain is an obvious choice as he was a second-round pick by the Chargers in 2018 before signing with the Seahawks in 2022. In addition to the bit of gamesmanship, Nwosu has become a fan-favorite in Seattle after he propelled a terrible pass-rush in 2022 and became a key part of the “Dark Side” defense. Not to mention his hit on Drake Maye in the Super Bowl, which led to a game clinching interception. Kupp, the lone offensive representative, has the second most receiving yards of any Seahawks player. The Eastern Washington alum has proven that he still has juice left to squeeze this season after a decade in the league, recording an immaculate catch in Week 1 and being a reliable target in clutch moments. Lastly, Morris, who is repping the special teams, returned to the lineup last week against the Commanders. The Seahawks fifth-round pick has been a staple of the team’s defensive line rotation the last two seasons, recording two TFLs and 23 tackles in that time frame. These four will lead the Seahawks onto the field as they face the winless Chargers at Lumen Field on Sunday at 1:25 p.m.

title: Seahawks-Chargers game designations: Jadarian Price ruled out after re-aggravating injury
summary: The Seattle Seahawks will be without their rookie running back against the Los Angeles Chargers. Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Friday that Jadarian Price, who suffered a chest injury in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals and played through the injury in the Week 3 loss against the Washington Commanders, re-aggravated his injury […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks will be without their rookie running back against the Los Angeles Chargers. Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Friday that Jadarian Price, who suffered a chest injury in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals and played through the injury in the Week 3 loss against the Washington Commanders, re-aggravated his injury during practice and has been ruled out for Week 4. Macdonald does not know yet whether or not Price’s injury is a concern beyond this week. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani are the only running backs on the 53-man roster, so the Seahawks will elevate from the practice squad. Velus Jones Jr has one more practice squad elevation left, while Jacardia Wright has yet to be elevated. Macdonald indicated that Wright has some issues of his own, so it looks like it’ll be Velus as the third option. For any positive injury news, Ty Okada is questionable to return with a hamstring injury that has kept him out of the previous three games. Okada being a full practice participant bodes well for his season debut. Fellow starting safety Julian Love is off the injury report completely, so his absence from the Commanders game due to calf tightness was a one-off. Special teams ace Chazz Surratt is questionable, so he’s a late add to the injury report after not appearing in Wednesday or Thursday’s reports. Here is the full, final injury report.

title: Seahawks vs. Chargers, Week 4 preview: Can Seattle get back on track at home?
summary: After opening the season with two wins, the Seattle Seahawks enter Week 4 looking to bounce back from an unexpected 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders. On the other side, the Los Angeles Chargers are still winless in 2026. They lost to the Arizona Cardinals, Las Vegas Raiders, and Buffalo Bills, but the Chargers were […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 10: George Holani #36 of the Seattle Seahawks scores a touchdown against the Los Angeles Chargers in the first half before a preseason game at SoFi Stadium on August 10, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images After opening the season with two wins, the Seattle Seahawks enter Week 4 looking to bounce back from an unexpected 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders. On the other side, the Los Angeles Chargers are still winless in 2026. They lost to the Arizona Cardinals, Las Vegas Raiders, and Buffalo Bills, but the Chargers were in position to win their latest game after taking a 10-0 lead over Buffalo before eventually falling 24-16, despite forcing five turnovers. The matchup will be played at Lumen Field in Seattle on Sunday, October 4, at 1:25 p.m. local time. It will be the first regular-season meeting between these teams since 2022, when the Seahawks defeated the Chargers 37-23 in Los Angeles. For Seattle, this game is also an opportunity to prevent the loss in Washington from becoming the start of a negative stretch. The Seahawks committed three turnovers against the Commanders, and all three resulted in touchdowns, accounting for 20 of Washington’s 33 points. Seattle gained 437 yards compared to just 229 for Washington, but ultimately lost because it could not protect the football in the most important moments. Can the Seahawks’ run game get back on track? Perhaps the biggest question for Seattle entering this game is the running game. The Seahawks managed just 44 rushing yards against Washington after producing much better numbers during the first two weeks. The challenge now comes against a Chargers defense that has produced very different results from week to week. Los Angeles allowed 116 rushing yards to Arizona in Week 1, then held Las Vegas to just 57 yards in Week 2 and Buffalo ran for 176 yards in Week 3, with James Cook accounting for 154 of them. Through three games, the Chargers are allowing about 116 rushing yards per game. That means there is an opportunity for Seattle to try to re-establish its identity on the ground, but the matchup is not necessarily a simple one. Dalvin Tomlinson is an important piece of the interior defensive line, with Teair Tart and Jamaree Caldwell also there. Tomlinson might miss the game due to injury. For Seattle, the goal will be to find a way to consistently gain yards without turning every run into a second- or third-and-long situation. After the struggles against Washington, establishing some offensive balance could also help take pressure off Sam Darnold. The offensive line vs. the Chargers pass rush The other major test for Seattle’s offense will come in pass protection. The Chargers have one of the more interesting pass-rush groups in the league, with Khalil Mack, Tuli Tuipulotu, and first-round rookie Akheem Mesidor giving them three players who can win from the edge. Mesidor gets a hard set where defender is low on him, defeats the hands with double swipe, clears defender with rip pic.twitter.com/d21FxAzVRj — betz (@adaptskill) September 30, 2026 Tuipulotu has already generated 12 pressures and two sacks through three games, while Mesidor has added five pressures and 1.5 sacks despite playing just 66 defensive snaps. Mack has also recorded two sacks this season. The Chargers showed against Buffalo that they can create pressure without constantly sending extra rushers. Tuipulotu, in particular, was a problem for the Bills, finishing the game with 1.5 sacks and two quarterback hits. Abe Lucas struggling in 2026… — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-10-01T00:02:09.155Z That will be a major test for Seattle’s offensive line. Abe Lucas has been almost unrecognizable compared to the level we are accustomed to seeing from him this season, and this would be a good opportunity for him to get back to his usual level. Grey Zabel was listed on the injury report (groin), which could help explain some of his struggles over the past two games. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-30T23:46:22.358Z Grey Zabel will also need to rebound after a down game against Washington. The Seahawks cannot afford to let the Chargers’ edge rushers consistently win early in the down. If Mack, Tuipulotu and Mesidor can create pressure without requiring additional help, Los Angeles can make life difficult for Darnold and limit the time available for Seattle’s deeper passing concepts. Turnovers: the Chargers can take the ball away There is an important similarity between these two teams entering this matchup: turnovers have already played a major role in their seasons. Seattle turned the ball over three times against Washington, and all three turnovers became touchdowns. The Chargers, meanwhile, just experienced almost the exact opposite situation. Against Buffalo, Los Angeles forced five turnovers — two interceptions and three fumble recoveries — but still lost. That makes protecting the football particularly important for Seattle, especially for rookie running back Jadarian Price ( assuming he plays after not practicing on Thursday ). The Chargers have shown that their defense can create opportunities, and another game with multiple takeaways could give Los Angeles a path to victory even if the offense does not have a dominant performance. Justin Herbert has given defenses opportunities Justin Herbert remains the central figure of the Chargers’ offense, but there have been opportunities for opposing defenses to make plays against him this season. Justin Herbert was really fortunate to get out of that Bills game with only one turnover. First clip is the literal first pass he threw. pic.twitter.com/aUrPeUWybE — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) September 30, 2026 Through three games, Herbert has thrown for 627 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions, while taking eight sacks. More importantly for Seattle, his four interceptions do not tell the entire story. PFF has charted Herbert with seven turnover-worthy plays through his first three games. That creates an interesting opportunity for Seattle’s defense. Herbert has already put the ball in harm’s way more often than his interception total suggests, and the Seahawks’ defense could be looking to turn those opportunities into actual takeaways. Against Buffalo, Herbert finished with 226 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception. His interception came in the fourth quarter, when C.J. Gardner-Johnson undercut a throw intended for Marquez Valdes-Scantling near the goal line and returned it 41 yards. Seattle’s pass rush vs. the Chargers offensive line This matchup goes both ways. While the Chargers’ pass rush will test Seattle’s offensive line, the Seahawks’ front has a favorable opportunity against an offensive line that has had its share of problems through three weeks. The Chargers’ interior has been particularly inconsistent. Cole Strange has allowed seven pressures through three games, while his PFF pass-blocking grade sits at just 25.6. The unit has also struggled with penalties. Joe Alt was flagged four times against the Raiders in Week 2, and he was penalized again against Buffalo. That brought his season total to six penalties through three games, the most in the NFL . That said, Alt’s season should not be reduced to those penalties. He had a strong performance against Buffalo and finished Week 3 with an 83.6 PFF grade, according to Chargers-focused reporting. Still, the penalties are something Seattle can try to exploit. The Seahawks have the defensive line talent to make the Chargers play behind the chains, and the interior matchup against Strange could be particularly interesting. Seattle’s pass rush will be particularly important here. Through three games, the Seahawks have generated seven sacks and 21 quarterback hits, with Leonard Williams and DeMarcus Lawrence leading the pressure production against Washington. If Seattle can create pressure while maintaining its coverage…

title: NFL predictions: What’s going to happen in Seahawks vs. Chargers
summary: After a disappointing loss versus the Washington Commanders, the Seattle Seahawks look to get back on track at home versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Per FanDuel Sportsbook, they look to be seven-point favorites at the time of writing this. How will this get accomplished? Let’s take a look. 1. Aerial attack against Chargers secondary The […]
full_text: After a disappointing loss versus the Washington Commanders, the Seattle Seahawks look to get back on track at home versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , they look to be seven-point favorites at the time of writing this. How will this get accomplished? Let’s take a look. 1. Aerial attack against Chargers secondary The Seahawks are averaging 266 passing yards a game so far this season, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, averaging 135 of those yards. The Chargers are allowing opponents to throw for 233 yards per game. The Seahawks have had eight passing touchdowns so far this season, while the Chargers have allowed four. Expect Jaxon to have another 100+ yard receiving game, with one to two more touchdowns to add to his six current touchdowns. He is on a historic pace right now . Prediction: Jaxon Smith-Njigba 125 yards and 2 Touchdowns Elite company. pic.twitter.com/ePvBRiOLja — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 29, 2026 2. The Dark Side to stop the run The Chargers offense has averaged 113 yards rushing per game, but I do not expect that to continue. The Seahawks defense is allowing only 87 yards of rushing per game and 3.3 yards per attempt, and they haven’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in almost two full seasons. Even with getting 113 yards per game, the Chargers are only averaging 4.2 yards per attempt. I expect that to continue as the Seahawks defense is still ranked third per DVOA. Meanwhile, the Chargers have the 26th ranked offense per DVOA. Not a favorable matchup for them. Prediction: Hold the Chargers to 90 rushing yards, no rushing TD’s 3. Expect the Seahawks to cover The Seahawks are the seven-point favorite, and I expect them to cover that. With the bad weather and Sam Darnold’s first game back, I believe the loss to the Commanders was an anomaly. I have full faith that Mike Macdonald with get the team back on track and with the help of the fans cheering the team on at home, win this game. The Seahawks have been outscoring their opponents by 8.3 points and are ranked seventh in point differential across the league. Meanwhile, the Chargers are ranked 30th in point differential and allow opponents to outscore them by an average of 10.6 points. Prediction: Seahawks cover the seven points 4. Under the 43.5 Points FanDuel has the game at 43.5 points. The average Seahawks came is currently around 41.7 points, while for the Chargers their games are averaging 40 points total on the dot. Averaging those totals together comes to 40.85, just under three points from the Fan Duel prediction. The Seahawks are averaging 25 points per game while the Chargers are allowing opponents an average of 25.3. On the other side, the Chargers are averaging 14.7 points per game while the Seahawks are allowing opponents and average of 16.7 points per game. Prediction: 25-15 Seahawks victory , total points 40. Concluding Points The Seahawks generally do not lose back-to-back games. The last time it happened was in 2024 when they lost to both the Packers and Vikings in Weeks 15 and 16 during Macdonald’s first season. After that season, Macdonald was able to make the team more in his image, and has not lost back to back games sense, and just finished a 12 game winning streak (stopping there in respect to the 12’s). I expect the Seahawks to continue to try to run the back with the committee of Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani to set up the passing game. Will this be the game where Price gets his first rushing touchdown? That will depend on the offensive line that has had its struggles with opening up running lanes in the red zone. With John Benton coaching up the offensive line, I foresee the offensive line getting back on track, opening up running lanes for the running back stable, and Price getting his first touchdown of the season. title: Colin Kaepernick suggests the 49ers were tanking with Chip Kelly in 2016
summary: 2016 was a rough time to be a 49ers fan, with the team going 2-14 while dealing with a dysfunctional front office. Former 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick suggests the 49ers didn’t want to win anyway. Kaepernick’s memoir, “The Perilous Fight,” has been out for a couple of weeks and tells his perspective on growing up […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - NOVEMBER 27: San Francisco 49ers head coach Chip Kelly talks with San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick (7) before a play during the NFL football game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Miami Dolphins on November 27, 2016, at the Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL. The Miami Dolphins defeated the San Francisco 49ers by the score of 31-24. (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 2016 was a rough time to be a 49ers fan, with the team going 2-14 while dealing with a dysfunctional front office. Former 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick suggests the 49ers didn’t want to win anyway. Kaepernick’s memoir, “ The Perilous Fight ,” has been out for a couple of weeks and tells his perspective on growing up and playing both college and professional football. 49ers fans looking for stories from his time as the starting quarterback won’t be disappointed. We’ve talked about his relationship with general manager Trent Baalke and head coach Jim Harbaugh, but Kaepernick also shares his perspective playing for the coaches that followed Harbaugh: Jim Tomsula in 2015, whose regime Kaepernick called “a disaster,” and Chip Kelly in 2016. Kelly named Blaine Gabbert the starting quarterback over Kaepernick. On the surface, it may have seemed like Gabbert beat Kaepernick for the starting job. In reality, Kaepernick was still rehabbing and returning from injury. There were also reports of injury guarantees on Kaepernick’s contract that he eventually restructured to remove—something many (including Kaepernick) speculate was the real reason he stayed off the field. That’s all common knowledge; what is interesting is Kaepernick’s take on the 49ers in 2016: I should add that the Niners didn’t seem interested in winning football games. They appeared to be in full “tank” mode. They were calling Chip Kelly’s first season a “rebuilding” year, but in actuality they had no plan to go get the talent Coach Kelly wanted. Kaepernick used the wide receiver situation as an example. Saying the 49ers’ No. 1 wideout that year was “the number five or six receiver on a different team.” No names are given, but Jeremy Kerley led the team in catches and yards receiving in 2016. Many may think of Torrey Smith as the “designated” wide receiver. Either way, Kerley’s team-leading 516 yards in receiving that year should tell you just how bad the 49ers were. “The team didn’t get us another receiver,” Kaepernick wrote. “Despite having the money to do so, something like $40 million in salary cap space.” Publicly, the 49ers were rebuilding. Even then, it was clear Baalke’s seat was nuclear after the press conference following Tomsula’s sacking took place; 49ers owner Jed York said he told Baalke he was not satisfied with the state of this [the 49ers] team. Was the team tanking? It wouldn’t be surprising. The 49ers’ lack of spending in free agency both in 2015 and 2016 didn’t make sense then, and it doesn’t make sense now (though there were rumors that players didn’t want to go to the 49ers with all the issues). The same could have been said for the Chip Kelly hire. We’ve already mentioned the offense, but Kelly’s defense under Jim O’Neil was one of the worst in league (not team) history. While the hire was a head-scratcher to begin with, the 49ers didn’t help Kelly get into a position to succeed. Kelly might have been a bad coach no matter what happened, but he was put in a failing situation regardless. There’s a strange alternate reality of what would have happened if Kelly had stayed with the 49ers for another couple of years and the team only let go of Baalke at the end of the 2016 season. It’s doubtful Kelly’s system would have succeeded no matter what the 49ers would have done, but it’s definitely a weird twilight zone moment.

title: 49ers News: Let Brandin Cook(s)
summary: What will we learn about this team from this match-up? The Broncos are like a scaled-down version of some of the beasts they’d need to slay on their way to the Super Bowl. A legit defensive line (but not quite Seattle), an athletic quarterback (but not quite a peak Mahomes or Josh Allen), and a […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 17: Ja'Quan McMillian #29 of the Denver Broncos fights for the ball with Brandin Cooks #18 of the Buffalo Bills during overtime of an AFC Divisional Playoff game at Empower Field At Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images What will we learn about this team from this match-up? The Broncos are like a scaled-down version of some of the beasts they’d need to slay on their way to the Super Bowl. A legit defensive line (but not quite Seattle), an athletic quarterback (but not quite a peak Mahomes or Josh Allen), and a veteran coach on Kyle’s level (but not quite Andy Reid). This almost feels like the starting gun to the “real” season. Here are the things I will be looking for, beyond the box score, that can tell us a lot about this team… Can the 49ers handle a ferocious pass rush? It’s great that the offensive line hasn’t given up a sack. They haven’t faced a defensive line this good yet. Seattle next week will be even better. Connor Colby and the interior o-line have exceeded my expectations so far, but this isn’t Miami or Arizona. Can the 49ers keep exploiting linebackers in coverage without their best wide receivers? Mike Evans might not play. All due respect to Brandin Cooks, but they need big games out of their non-WR skill players like George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and even a little Kyle Jusczyzk. That’s always been the case but especially so against the “elite DB/vulnerable LB” combination that Denver has going. Can the 49ers establish the run? Kansas City provided the blueprint in Week 1 when they forced the Broncos to miss 26 tackles. Can they keep an athletic quarterback in the pocket…. without Nick Bosa? Bo Nix isn’t as good as Matt Stafford but he is the most athletic QB they’ve faced yet (that’s still a mid-tier or above passer). He’s maddenly inconsistent but can also win games on his own. How’s the secondary holding up? Jaylen Waddle is good to go, and Courtland Sutton is no slouch. I can see a world where the Broncos start slow and then start coming back because of coverage busts on the back end. It just takes one bad bust to breathe life into Bo Nix, who otherwise struggles when forced to step up in the pocket. Wait, is the 49ers O-line actually good? Broncos, Seahawks can help settle the debate (paywall) “Offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said the big red zone sack Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga had against the Los Angeles Rams late in Denver’s win Sunday shows how efficient — and aggressive — defensive coordinator Vance Joseph’s unit can be. Hufanga, a former 49er, lined up to quarterback Matthew Stafford’s blind side at the last second and was unaccounted for as he came off the edge. “He knows when to call his shots,” Kubiak said of Joseph. “He knows when to be aggressive and come after the quarterback. That group’s been playing together for a while. And when they call those blitzes, they usually work.” Part of the 49ers’ winning formula so far this year is that they aren’t hurting themselves.” Five 49ers to watch as Brock Purdy leads charge to stay undefeated vs. Broncos “Defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa clearly is the main guy. The 49ers need another player or two to stand out among their nine-man rotation. Rookie Gracen Halton could be on the verge of a breakout. Halton, a fourth-round 2026 NFL Draft pick, will make his third start in a row. He has a couple of tackles for loss, and appears to be trending toward making more big plays.” 49ers add a rookie to the injury report; Dante Pettis hurt his calf “Evans will be a game-time decision with his rib injury. Shanahan compared his rib injury to Evans, saying, “he’s definitely a lot tougher than me. Hopefully, he’s got a shot.” Brandin Cooks will make his 49ers debut on Sunday.” 49ers vs. Broncos: The Standard’s 5 fast predictions (paywall) “Kawakami: Broncos 27, 49ers 26. This would be a disappointing way for the 49ers to go into next weekend’s clash in Seattle. But they’re probably due for a flat performance perhaps with some natural focus on the flight to the Northwest coming up. Also, any more Eddy Piñeiro extra-point misses could be huge in a close game.” Kyle Shanahan shares final updates ahead of 49ers-Broncos “When you’re talking to your team about an upcoming opponent, do you find yourself have to talk up the opponent more or do you want to build your team’s confidence or appropriate fear? How do you approach it? “All of the above. Depends where we’re at at the time, where the team’s at. It changes every week. You can have it come off a huge win and people question the team you’re playing. That happened to us in Week Two. A big win versus the Rams in Australia. Then people have us as huge favorites and stuff the next week versus Miami. I don’t try to talk people up because I don’t think people believe words. I think people believe what they see and I can’t talk people up unless I believe it. So, I usually try to find it in the tape and show people what people can be and what they need to be worried about. It’s something I usually do earlier in the week. I think that fear to fail or respect of people, however you want to word it, is what gets you to work a certain way. The whole goal is to work hard enough so you don’t feel that way, and to me, the goal is to not feel that way by Saturday night so you go into Sunday confident. And if you feel that way on Monday, I usually think you’re in trouble. You’ve got to earn that. It’s got to be real, and that’s through the work you do and the preparation. You prepare the right way if you respect an opponent and I believe we respect whoever we’re playing every week.”

title: 3 former 49ers will play pivotal roles for the Broncos on Sunday
summary: The San Francisco 49ers host their third straight home game this Sunday as they take on the Denver Broncos. Familiar faces will be on the other side, as the Niners will face some of their homegrown talent: DJ Jones, Mike McGlinchey, and Talanoa Hufanga. DJ Jones Jones has never been the kind of player that […]
full_text: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers host their third straight home game this Sunday as they take on the Denver Broncos. Familiar faces will be on the other side, as the Niners will face some of their homegrown talent: DJ Jones, Mike McGlinchey, and Talanoa Hufanga. DJ Jones Jones has never been the kind of player that you could quantify statistically. Now, 31, Jones is still trucking along in the same role he had with the Niners from 2017 through 2021. Jones plays anywhere between 40 and 58% of snaps for Denver, depending on the game flow. He has a couple of run stops and a few pressures. But we know DJ. The 49ers know DJ. Kyle Shanahan knows DJ. He’s a bowling ball who will cause chaos and do his job, while freeing up the linebackers behind him. Last week, when Jones was on the field, the Rams had 14 carries for only 3.1 yards per carry. That’s who Jones is. Mike McGlinchey There are no secrets with McGlinchey, either, who was always known as a plus run blocker and a shaky pass protector with the 49ers. This season, McGlinchey is allowing a pressure rate of 8.1%. Per Sports Info Solutions, he’s earned 5 total points, with six blown blocks in pass protection and only one against the run. McGlinchey has allowed a run stuff and a sack, and has been penalized once. Sumer Sports has McGlinchey down for two impact plays this season across 166 snaps. Let’s compare that to the player who took over for McGlinchey, Colton McKivitiz, who has played 163 snaps. Colton has six impact plays and a pressure rate of 3.4%, has earned six points, per Sports Info Solutions, with two blown blocks in pass protection compared to one against the run. Percentage-wise, the blown block rate favors McKivitz: 1.9% to 4.3%. We’re not going to pretend each offense asks each tackle to do the same duties, but when you look at average depth of target and time to throw for Bo Nix and Brock Purdy, the 49ers are holding onto the ball longer. Week 4 is a game where you hope to have Keion White, but you wish Nick Bosa would be out there to give McGlinchey fits. Rookie Romello Height’s speed could play a factor. Talanoa Hufanga Hufanga left the 49ers with no choice after he couldn’t stay healthy during the final two seasons of his rookie contract. That’s unfortunate, because he looked like a blossoming star during his first season as a starter. Sure enough, Talanoa stayed healthy for all of 2025 and was named second-team All-Pro. Hufanga picking up where he left off last year. Only three players have more impact plays at safety. Hufanga picked off Matthew Stafford for the second time in his career in Week 3. That was his second interception of the season, and he has three pass breakups. Tack on three tackles for loss plus a sack, and you have yourself an All-Pro player. 49ers tight end George Kittle credited Hufanga’s prep as the reason for his success. “He’s watching every single game. He’s watching tendencies. He’s watching guys break down on their routes. How do you not let him do that? Well, hopefully he gets us wrong a couple a times. Those instincutal players, right? He’s gonna make plays, and we gotta make sure he doesn’t make all the plays.” Kittle hinted at using Hufanga’s aggressiveness against him. It’s easy to envision Huf jumping on Christian McCaffrey’s routes out of the backfield or Kittle down the middle. Kittle caught several underneath passes in Week 3. A double move on Hufanga with Kittle may be in the cards for the 49ers.

title: 49ers owner Jed York suspended six games by NFL
summary: 49ers owner Jed York has been suspended for six games for a violation of the league’s personal conduct policy. York, who was also hit with a $500,000 fine, has stayed away from the team for the first three games of the 2026 season, in addition to league meetings, after pleading no contest to two misdemeanor […]
full_text: (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 49ers owner Jed York has been suspended for six games for a violation of the league’s personal conduct policy. York, who was also hit with a $500,000 fine, has stayed away from the team for the first three games of the 2026 season, in addition to league meetings, after pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges on August 24 after being arrested in Ohio. He was arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution . The league will count those three games toward his six-game ban, meaning he will be able to return on Tuesday, Oct. 20. A statement from York read: “Today, the NFL concluded its review, and I accept its decision in full. “To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake, and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. “While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one’s failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. “Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don’t take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead.” The first 49ers game following the end of his suspension is the Week 7 road game with the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 25. With San Francisco having a bye after that trip to the Southeast, the first home game York can attend will be the meeting with the 49ers’ old Bay Area rivals, the Las Vegas Raiders, on Nov. 8.

title: NFL predictions: Fast starts for the 49ers; Blitzing Broncos’ Bo Nix
summary: Coming off a tight 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals, the San Francisco 49ers have a nice early test at home with the Denver Broncos coming to town. San Francisco’s offense has been the big story so far, as Brock Purdy has led one of the most efficient offensive attacks in the NFL so far. […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off a tight 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals, the San Francisco 49ers have a nice early test at home with the Denver Broncos coming to town. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . San Francisco’s offense has been the big story so far, as Brock Purdy has led one of the most efficient offensive attacks in the NFL so far. The 49ers are fifth in yards per game, second in points per game, and first in EPA/play by a wide margin. They’re also first in success rate, EPA per dropback, and dropback success rate, illustrating the success of the passing game. That has come even with a plethora of injuries at wide receiver, as Brock Purdy has emerged as an early MVP contender, throwing for 789 yards, nine touchdowns, and an interception through three games, while rushing for 93 more and another score. But the 49ers will get a good test this weekend, as they take on the Denver Broncos, who have looked much better the last two weeks after a stinker against the Kansas City Chiefs in the opener. Heading into the game, the 49ers are 2.5-point favorites, while the over/under is quite high at 47.5 points, according to FanDuel. Here are my three predictions for this week’s game between the 49ers and the Broncos. But first, let’s take a look at last week’s results. Last Week 49ers run game finally gets going It will be a heavy blitz day for Raheem Morris 49ers drop 27+ for a third straight week The 49ers have been cruising past opponents, but its run game hadn’t been as dominant as you’d hope through the first two weeks. Still, I thought last week’s spot was a good one for San Francisco to establish itself in the run game, especially with the advantage up front in the trenches. That turned out to be right, as the 49ers ran for 140 yards, while averaging over six yards per carry. Christian McCaffrey saw a healthy workload, taking 15 carries for 75 yards and a touchdown. Kaelon Black added 17 more yards on four carries, while Deebo Samuel had 14 yards on two carries. The pass game still dominated, as Brock Purdy had a quality day, tossing for 297 yards and four touchdowns, but it was good to see the offense be complementary and the run game start to develop. With Jacoby Brissett in the pocket, I thought the 49ers would look to blitz more, especially with their situation at quarterback. Well, Raheem Morris blitzed 14 times on 41 Brissett dropbacks, with the 49ers getting pressure on four dropbacks. Brissett generally was throwing short of the sticks, but he averaged just 4.9 yards per attempt on those 14 dropbacks when blitzed. The 49ers offense also had a big day and hit the 30-point marker again, with the offense getting a late touchdown to seal the deal. Now, let’s move on to this week. 49ers get off to a fast start A big part of San Francisco’s offensive success has been their quality starts. They’ve scored on their opening drive in each of their three games. Two of those drives with long, sustained drives that took up a big chunk of first-quarter clock, and the third was the quick hook-and-ladder touchdown drive last weekend against Arizona. Denver has also gotten off to slow starts repeatedly this season. For whatever reason, they’ve struggled to start hot, and that could come to fruition again in Week 4, especially with the 49ers at home. Denver has struggled against the run as well this season. I’d expect the 49ers to rely a bit on that run game early for a sustained drive and set the tone early in a physical game. There will be turnovers on both sides Brock Purdy has been essentially mistake-free after his poor interception in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams, and the 49ers offense has been humming as a result. But these are two opportunistic defenses, which is why I could very well see a turnover on both sides. Bo Nix has been inconsistent to start the year, as his QBR ranked 24th in the NFL, while he’s completed only 60.2 percent of his passes. He’s also been sacked five times, committed a whopping eight turnover-worthy plays, and has four turnovers (three interceptions, one fumble). Denver has also gotten four takeaways, though, including two major Talanoa Hufanga interceptions last week. I think they’ll look to play more opportunistically defensively and try to spring a turnover out of the 49ers. The 49ers have obviously protected the ball quite well, with the team losing just two turnovers so far this season. Brock Purdy has played a big role in that, but it will be a good challenge for San Francisco here on Sunday, and I could see a game where turnovers play out on both sides. It’s an in-breaking game for the 49ers offense Denver’s linebackers have not looked great to start the year. It’s potentially the team’s biggest weakness so far, and that’s music to Kyle Shanahan’s ears. The 49ers will have to figure out their personnel for the game with their injuries, but I think they’ll look to attack the middle of the field a ton against Denver. Naturally, that could lead to a turnover, as shared above, but this feels like a game that Deebo Samuel can win on the inside, while Mike Evans gets a good challenge on the outside against Patrick Surtain. It also feels like a great opportunity for George Kittle (who might also get some Hufanga matchups) and certainly Christian McCaffrey in the passing game. The Broncos also mightily struggled with tackles in Week 1 before improving on that in recent weeks. We’ll see if the 49ers can exploit that as well after the catch or after contact.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Can the 49ers wear down the Broncos in 90-degree weather?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers begin the first tough stretch of the 2026 season on Sunday, hosting the Denver Broncos. Sean Payton and the Broncos enter Santa Clara after some earning brownie points with the 49ers for their Sunday night win over the Los Angeles Rams. That result, combined with San Francisco’s Week 3 win against […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball during the first quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers begin the first tough stretch of the 2026 season on Sunday, hosting the Denver Broncos. Sean Payton and the Broncos enter Santa Clara after some earning brownie points with the 49ers for their Sunday night win over the Los Angeles Rams. That result, combined with San Francisco’s Week 3 win against the Arizona Cardinals, put San Francisco two games up on the Rams with the tiebreaker currently in hand. But it’s a little too early to watch the standings; for now, collecting wins is the priority, and Denver will offer the 49ers their toughest test with the best defense the San Francisco offense has faced so far. So let’s start there, looking at how the 49ers can take advantage of the Denver defense with this week’s numbers to know: 380.7 Yards. The Broncos defense has allowed 380.7 yards per game this season, the fourth-most allowed in the league. Denver’s defense will be the toughest test of the season (until Seattle next week) for the upstart San Francisco offense. But the Broncos haven’t quite found their stride yet, though they showed signs on Sunday night in the second half in their win over the Rams. The Broncos finished only behind Houston in yards per game allowed (278.2) and Houston and Seattle in points per game allowed (18.3) in 2025. That hasn’t been the case through Denver’s first three games: they’ve allowed the fourth-most yards, but they’ve done much better at keeping opponents out of the end zone, allowing 23.3 points per game, right smack in the middle of the league. It’s a defense that bends but doesn’t break. The 34.6 yards per drive Denver allows is the ninth-most allowed in the league, but once opposing offenses get into the red zone, it’s less than a coin-flip chance a touchdown is scored. The Broncos have allowed only five touchdowns on 11 red-zone entries, a 45.5 percent touchdown rate. As a result, Denver allows only 2.12 points per drive, again finding itself in the middle of the league despite the yards allowed. The 49ers haven’t had issues gaining yards (fifth at 399.3 yards per game) or scoring in the red zone (first at a 90 percent touchdown rate). Sunday could come down to whether the San Francisco offense can figure out Denver’s top-ten red zone defense. 33.1 Percent. Denver’s defense blitzes on 33.1 percent of dropbacks. The 49ers offensive line has been perfect through three games. Zero sacks, only four negative plays allowed- you know all the stats. But they haven’t faced an attack yet like they’ll face against Denver on Sunday. Vance Joseph’s defense will be the first team the 49ers offensive line has faced in the top half of the league in blitz percentage, with the ninth-highest rate in the league at 33.1, according to Pro Football Reference. So far, the 49ers have faced: Los Angeles: 22.9 percent (19th in blitz rate) Miami: 19.8 percent (24th) Arizona: 18.9 percent (27th) But that blitz rate hasn’t equated to pressures for the Broncos. Denver ranks 19th in pressure rate, getting after the quarterback 22.6 percent of the time. Those pressures have resulted in eight sacks, tied for seventh-most in the league, led by Zach Allen with three. Brock Purdy has been kept clean this season, but Denver’s front will be a litmus test for where the 49ers offensive line actually is. Purdy’s elusiveness and mobility, and how frequently he can extend plays with his legs before the Denver pass rush gets to him, will be a factor. 91 Degrees. It will be around 91 degrees in Santa Clara at kickoff. And that’s 91 degrees at kickoff. It’s expected to reach 93 degrees at Levi’s Stadium. It’s going to be miserable. It’s going to be draining. It’s going to suck. Plus, both teams are coming off games where they were on the field for 80+ plays a week ago. There could be some tired legs out there. When the calendar turns from September to October, the second summer starts in California. In recent years, the beginning of fall has signified some of the hottest weather of the year, and this year seems to be no different. The thing is, it’s not something that will benefit either side; it will be just as bad for both teams. A war of attrition would be the best way to describe it. And it’s not a game situation the 49ers are used to. According to Pro Football Reference , the 49ers have played in only one game with temperatures higher than 90 degrees, and that was back in 2019 when the 49ers defense intercepted Jameis Winston three times en route to a Week 1 victory in Tampa Bay. The Broncos, however, have played in high temperatures much more recently than the 49ers, and it might be a good sign for San Francisco. It was 91 degrees on a Monday night in Kansas City a few weeks ago, when the Denver defense allowed a season-high 31 points in the Broncos’ only loss of the season. It’s going to be a hot one in Santa Clara. I, for one, will keep those sitting on that side of Levi’s Stadium in mind while I am sitting in my air-conditioned Sacramento apartment. If you think the weather will play a factor, scroll down and let us know in the comments.

title: Where the 49ers have surprised the most through three weeks
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are off to a hot 3-0 start to the 2026 season, securing wins over the Los Angeles Rams, Miami Dolphins, and Arizona Cardinals. So far, it’s been their offense that’s been the story, as the 49ers have excelled behind Brock Purdy, playing mistake-free football and ranking first in the NFL (by […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Offensive tackle Trent Williams (71) of the San Francisco 49ers in action against the Miami Dolphins during a game at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are off to a hot 3-0 start to the 2026 season, securing wins over the Los Angeles Rams, Miami Dolphins, and Arizona Cardinals. So far, it’s been their offense that’s been the story, as the 49ers have excelled behind Brock Purdy, playing mistake-free football and ranking first in the NFL (by far) in EPA per play. Their passing offense has especially come out strong, as Purdy looks like an MVP candidate, but we’re also slowly starting to see the run game built out with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. It isn’t a surprise that the 49ers offense has looked good. Many have under Kyle Shanahan, but this unit has looked quite elite through three weeks, and it isn’t just Purdy and the skill position players. The offensive line has also played quite well, holding up in pass protection, while the run blocking is also starting to play out. According to Ben Baldwin’s formula, which takes into account PFF grades, blown block percentage, and pass-block win rate, the 49ers rank first in the NFL in pass protection rankings currently. Pass protection ratings pic.twitter.com/l4WuVTlpW7 — Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) September 29, 2026 They lead the NFL in both PFF grades and blown block percentage through three weeks, and they also haven’t given up a sack. What has the coaching staff seen from that unit so far? “I think they’ve been really good,” offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said. “We knew who four out of the five would be, I think, in general, but as far as the guard competition, we felt really good. Whoever ended up starting was going to be the right guy and play good for us. These guys have done a heck of a job through three weeks. Obviously, no sacks, but I look at that as a team stat too. “It has a lot to do with, obviously, the O-Line, our tight ends, our backs, our quarterback, our receivers being in the right place. There’s been a little bit of luck involved. Brock’s made some great plays of making people miss. So, it’s really a team stat. It has to do with our offense being efficient and staying on track, and so far so good. Hope to keep that going.” The 49ers are also bringing back that efficiency in the run game after struggling last season. So far, they’re averaging 5.1 yards per carry as a team, with Christian McCaffrey up at 4.7 yards per carry on 35 attempts. What has been the key to being more efficient there? “I felt like we were really efficient running the ball, staying out of long passing situations, second and long, third and long,” Kubiak added. “In this game, it felt like maybe in the second half we got that going a little bit more. Anytime you can be efficient on first down running the ball, it’s going to help. I always talk about staying out of obvious passing situations where the D-Line can tee off, where a play caller might change up their coverages. It just gets harder when you’re in those situations, so the more efficient we can be. “I’ve been real happy with our backs. They’ve had some good runs, but there’s been hard runs that get us four, five, six yards that maybe were blocked for three that keep us on track, get us to second and four and then maybe third and two and we have a better chance of staying on the field. Then you look at the second half last week, Christian [McCaffrey] had a 12-yard run in the fourth quarter. That’s what we’re talking about. Those just efficient grinder runs that keep you on the field and let you keep calling plays, so hopefully we keep that going.” So far, when it comes to protection, Jake Brendel has allowed just one pressure through 163 pass-blocking reps. Dominick Puni has given up just two, while Connor Colby and Colton McKivitz have given up four each, and Trent Williams has allowed five. The 49ers offensive line was a strength last season as well, but the run game never really got going. Now, that unit is looking like a strength again this season, and they’re near the top of the NFL in a couple of metrics so far.

(Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cam Ward had his worst game as a professional last week. He missed a wide-open Carnell Tate in the end zone on one drive and threw an interception in the end zone to seal the game on another drive. If he hits Tate, or if he doesn’t throw that interception, the Tennessee Titans probably get their first win of the season. He gets the chance to bounce back this week against the Baltimore Ravens. Through three games, the Ravens defense is middle of the pack in passing yards allowed, rushing yards allowed, and points allowed. Baltimore has historically been great on defense. The current unit doesn’t rank that way early in the season. Ward doesn’t have to be Superman for the Titans to be good on offense. He just needs to take care of the ball and hit the easy throws that are there. He wasn’t able to do that against the New York Giants. It all starts with his footwork. Paul Kuharsky wrote a great piece this week about the breakdown in Ward’s footwork. We knew it was a problem last year. That was supposed to be the focus of his offseason. Robert Saleh said this week that Ward’s footwork has been better early in games but breaks down as the game goes on. It hasn’t looked that way to me. To me, it looks like there is no consistency in his footwork from play to play at any point in the game. Until he can figure out a way to do it right consistently, we will continue to see the up-and-down play that we have seen through his first 20 games in the NFL. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans will play against Derrick Henry, Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4 . The winless Titans need to be significantly better than they’ve been if they hope to execute an upset. We’ve identified three veteran players the team needs big-time performances from. QB Cam Ward It obviously starts with quarterback Cam Ward. Believe it or not, the sophomore No. 1 overall pick did some good things versus the New York Giants in Week 2, including leading a possession where he completed 8-of-8 passing attempts and threw a touchdown. But Ward made two glaring red-zone errors that cost the Titans 14 points in a five-point defeat. The fanbase is beginning to sour on Ward. Sunday’s showdown with the Ravens will be his 21st career start. The Titans can’t admit defeat on a top-pick quarterback this quickly, but progress needs to start becoming evident. DE Jermaine Johnson II The offseason trade that sent T’Vondre Sweat to the New York Jets for defensive end Jermaine Johnson II is starting to age terribly. Sweat has made an instant impact in East Rutherford. Meanwhile Johnson doesn’t have his first sack with the Titans. All the advanced metrics (Pro Football Focus) say Johnson has been Tennessee’s least efficient pass rusher. Playing against Lamar Jackson and this Ravens offensive line is always a challenge. The Titans need way more from Johnson. CB Alontae Taylor PFF has Titans cornerback Alontae Taylor allowing 13 receptions on 15 targets for 116 yards. That’s a completion percentage of 86.7%. He also doesn’t have an interception or a pass breakup yet. Taylor has been serviceable on tape, but the Titans need more from their $19 million per year cornerback. Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers has been excellent through three weeks. Taylor will probably draw the coverage assignment on Flowers.

title: Who gets credit for Commanders upset of Seahawks? – survey results
summary: Sunday’s 33-31 upset over the Seattle Seahawks did a lot more than just put a mark in the win column. It gave Commanders fans a collective sigh of relief and brought back an energy that seemed completely sapped just seven days earlier. In this week’s Reacts survey, we dug into two key areas: our regular […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Players of the Washington Commanders pose for a photo during the second half against the Seattle Seahawks at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday’s 33-31 upset over the Seattle Seahawks did a lot more than just put a mark in the win column. It gave Commanders fans a collective sigh of relief and brought back an energy that seemed completely sapped just seven days earlier. In this week’s Reacts survey , we dug into two key areas: our regular check-in on fan confidence, and an evaluation of which unit deserved the lion’s share of the credit for pulling off the home upset. Here is how the votes shook out and what our community had to say. Question 1: Are you confident in the team’s direction? The rollercoaster ride continues. After opening at 70% in Week 1 and ticking up to 80% following Week 2, the bottom fell out in Week 3 at a dismal 20%. One week and one signature upset later, that number has bounced right back up to 76%. Whether this jump represents genuine long-term faith or simply immediate postgame relief following the win in the home opener vs the Seashawks, the mood around the fanbase has clearly turned back toward the positive. Still, a few regular commenters were quick to separate game-day emotion from long-term trajectory. Others are keeping their guard up. By the way, here are this week’s results of the confidence question from the other NFC East teams: Question 2: Which phase of the game was most instrumental in the Commanders win over the Seahawks on Sunday? Visit our partners at FanDuel Nearly half the votes went to the offense with just over a third to defense, but reading through the comments, our community wasn’t ready to let David Blough take a solo victory lap. Defense: The reality is that Sunday was a clinic in complementary football. Daronte Jones’ defense repeatedly bailed out the team by clamping down on Seattle’s ground attack and generating 3 critical takeaways—none bigger than the second-half pick-six that completely flipped momentum. Game-winning INT 40 snaps into his career 🤯 Kain Medrano’s already making game-changing plays for the @Commanders . pic.twitter.com/T7cNOSDBHd — NFL Films (@NFLFilms) September 30, 2026 Offense: At the same time, when Blough’s offense had to have a drive in the fourth quarter, Marcus Mariota settled down, shook off that rough 1-for-11 third-down mark, and led a clutch scoring march that drained the clock and sealed the win. Rachaad White with the big run to keep the drive going! @SEAvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8miKbMKu7c — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Special Teams: Then there is the third phase that often gets forgotten: special teams. In a game decided by just 2 points, rookie kicker Drew Stevens was dead-eye reliable on 3-pointers. He nailed both of his field goal tries under immense pressure (we won’t talk about the missed 48-yard PAT following the penalty on Frankie Luvu, who wasn’t even playing in the game). Without Stevens doing his field-goal kicking job cleanly, all the defensive takeaways in the world might not have been enough. DQ: The 19% of respondents who gave their vote to Dan Quinn probably may have been onto something: nobody carried this team across the finish line alone. When a team plays together and comes away with a win in difficult circumstances, the head coach has to get some credit for that, right? Wrapping up the thought When a squad is banged up and leaning on backups in critical spots, winning doesn’t come down to a single playcaller having a stroke of genius. It requires all three phases covering for one another when things go sideways. Daronte Jones’ defense provided the short fields and the splash plays, David Blough’s offense capitalized with a clutch, clock-killing touchdown drive when it mattered most, and Drew Stevens quietly put 6 points on the board to make sure no offensive drives that crossed midfield prior to the 2-minute warning were wasted. That is textbook complementary football, and fostering that kind of buy-in across the roster is ultimately the head coach’s job. Next up: a Week 4 international showdown in London against Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts Holding onto the team’s collective resilience will be vital as Washington packs its bags for London. With a quick turnaround, international travel logistics, and an Indianapolis team eager to turn Daniel Jones loose against his old NFC East rival, the Commanders won’t have the luxury of relying on just one side of the ball. If Sunday proved anything, it’s that this team’s margin for error is razor-thin—and their best chance to keep stacking wins is by doing it together. Per Fan Duel, Indianapolis is currently favored on Sunday. full_text: It’s crazy how much different this week fells now that the Commanders have a win. Doom and gloom dominated last week’s narrative, with Washington reeling after a second straight NFC East loss and Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow . Beating the reigning Super Bowl champs will put some pep in your step. Doing so with a backup quarterback in Marcus Mariota only served to validate the effort, which featured some excellent run defense and performance under pressure. Daniels is back and practicing already but won’t play on Sunday, yet the vibes are high around Commanders football after how Mariota performed in his last start . Can Washington keep them going with a win over Indianapolis on Sunday morning (ET) at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London? Here are five key questions heading into this matchup. Answer them for us in the article comments below and we’ll bring the best responses up for posting in the main story by Saturday morning: Question 1: Marcus Mariota will start a second straight Commanders game on Sunday, a week after he didn’t make mistakes but didn’t pile on the yards. What must Mariota improve upon from for Washington to get another win without Jayden Daniels? Question 2: Colts running back Jonathan Taylor versus the Commanders run defense is a good-on-good matchup. Which Washington players must step up to slow Taylor down? Question 3: As you look at the Colts defense and advantageous matchups against it heading into Sunday, who will lead the Commanders in receiving yards and why? Question 4: Bill Croskey-Merritt had a relatively slow start to the season, with inefficient per-carry averages and without explosive runs, save one that a penalty negated. What’s your take on his start to the season? Where’s your level of concern, if any? Question 5: There’s always someone unexpected who steps up and plays an important role in a victory (i.e. Kain Medrano in Week 3). Who will be the unsung hero if the Commanders are to beat the Colts?

full_text: The Commanders didn’t even wait for their formal injury report to announce the return of some key starters. Head coach Dan Quinn said that linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) and tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) will play on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. That’s a huge win for Washington, getting two primary starters back in the lineup. Not everything in the Commanders official injury report was positive. Star receiver Terry McLaurin was designated as questionable with a hamstring injury. He was added to the participation report Friday, announcing the new injury and his limited status. While the severity of the injury was not immediately known, it always raises an eyebrow with someone is added to the report so late. It implies that the injury occurred during that practice or around it. Update from Ben Standig : My understanding is McLaurin is still expected to play against his hometown team. So why the lighter load on Friday? He apparently tweaked his hamstring against the Seahawks and, after participating in Wednesday’s jog-through and Thursday’s full session, the plan leaned toward precaution. Running back Rachaad White was ruled out of Sunday’s game with a shoulder injury, which wasn’t a huge shock considering he didn’t practice all week. Quinn also announced the quarterback Jayden Daniels was ruled out of Sunday contest after returning to practice on a limited basis while recovering from a dislocated left elbow. If you think we’re buried the lede here, we haven’t. Daniels got his own story, which you can read by clicking the link below: ⬇️ The team formally ruled safety Nick Cross (illness) and guard Sam Cosmi (concussion) out earlier in the week, as they weren’t part of Washington’s traveling party for this Week 4 contest against the Colts. #INDVSWAS game status — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 2, 2026 Final practice report for #INDvsWAS . pic.twitter.com/tzC0QsSzFO — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 2, 2026 The Commanders brought newly re-signed running back Austin Ekeler with them to London and it’s possible he could suit up right away despite Washington running a different system than when he was with the team last season. Washington’s thin at that position, with Ekeler and Kaytron Allen as available backups on the active roster. If Ekeler isn’t quite ready, the Commanders could dip into the practice squad (Robert Henry Jr. or Craig Reynolds) for support. summary: The Commanders took the field in their home opener against the Seahawks, reeling from the Week 2 loss of their starting quarterback Jayden Daniels, adding to the injury attrition of key starters including LT Laremy Tunsil, RG Sam Cosmi, S Nick Cross, LB Frankie Luvu and TE Chig Okonkwo. full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders defensive tackle Tim Settle (97) celebrates with teammates after recovering a fumble against the Seattle Seahawks at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Commanders took the field in their home opener against the Seahawks, reeling from the Week 2 loss of their starting quarterback Jayden Daniels, adding to the injury attrition of key starters including LT Laremy Tunsil, RG Sam Cosmi, S Nick Cross, LB Frankie Luvu and TE Chig Okonkwo. The injury concerns were further compounded by the underperformance of secondary players Mike Sainristil, Quan Martin and Jeremy Reaves, combined with growing doubts about leadership of the head coach and new schemes on both sides of the ball being spearheaded by novice coordinators. Around the league, confidence in the Commanders was tanking following the devastating 20-37 Week 2 loss to the Cowboys. The Vegas line had the Commanders as 8.5-point underdogs at home, against the visiting Seahawks. What took place was a reminder of the generally mis-quoted, but nonetheless apt movie line about what can happen “on any given Sunday”. The rag-tag band of injury replacements, disrespected, and underrated players rallied around journeyman backup Marcus Mariota, who led an efficient offense that did enough to capitalize on opportunities generated by the defense, while avoiding turnovers. The defense was strong against the run (9 th fewest rushing yards allowed Week 3), but continued to struggle against the pass (32 nd in passing yards allowed). The key to victory was generating 3 turnovers which led to points, compared to the Seahawks’ 0. Historically, teams with a +3 turnover differential have a 90.7% win rate. That is a tremendous obstacle for an opponent to overcome. As good as Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks’ passing attack may be, on Sunday it was not enough. In Week 3, missing their star QB and key starters on both sides of the ball, against the reigning Super Bowl champs, the Commanders’ offense ranked 20 th in the league in weighted EPA/Play at +0.04, while the defense ranked 11 th at -0.045: Image courtesy of RBSDM.com The upset win was the result of total team effort. Players making that kind of effort, in the face of the type of adversity the Commanders were facing, points to coaching and leadership perhaps being better than was widely appreciated. While the overall game left plenty of room for improvement, there were some standout performances on both sides of the ball, as well as continued struggles from players who have underperformed, and another key loss to injury. As the Commanders seek to carry the momentum with them to London, let’s take a look at who stepped up, who struggled and where everyone played in the biggest upset of the 2026 season so far. BIGGEST PLAYS OF THE GAME These plays had the biggest impact on a team’s scoring potential on a drive, as quantified by Expected Points Added (EPA).
